Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a quiet suburban scene with large wooden villas set back from a road. There is an open grassy area in the foreground, simple fencing, and several utility poles. The architecture appears early 20th‑century Northern European. A printed caption in a serif font appears along the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a large European city square showing a military parade. Hundreds of soldiers with rifles and bayonets march in formation across a broad cobbled plaza with tram tracks in the foreground. On the right stands a large, ornate civic building with columns, arches, and a steep roof, while on the left and in the background are multi‑story 19th‑century townhouses and commercial buildings lining the square.

A monochrome vintage postcard showing the courtyard side of a large Renaissance-style hunting palace with several gabled wings, ivy-covered façades, and a central archway. There is an open gravel courtyard in the foreground and a large tree near the right side. At the top in red Gothic-style script is a brief caption identifying the building.

Monochrome postcard showing a narrow rocky gorge with steep cliff faces. At the bottom center a loaded pack animal and a person stand on a rough road or path. Stone walls and simple structures are visible near the foreground. Printed captions in French and Greek identify the place as Castalie Gorge at Delphi, and a web address appears at the bottom.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a bustling scene in Piazza San Marco. People in early 20th‑century clothing stand and feed pigeons in the square. On the right is the ornate facade and domes of the Basilica di San Marco, while on the left are the surrounding historic buildings and the clock tower. Large flags hang prominently in the foreground. Printed text in Italian appears at the top describing the view.

Black‑and‑white image of a steam cargo vessel at sea or on a river, viewed in profile. The ship has a single funnel with a logo, a central mast with rigging, and the name "ELLEN" with the home port "BOOT" (or similar) painted on the bow. A small national flag flies from the stern. The shoreline is faintly visible in the background under an overcast sky.

Sepia-toned photographic postcard showing a seated woman in an elaborate 18th‑century style gown and large hat, posing thoughtfully on an ornate chair. The text identifies her as Margarethe Siems in a role from the opera "Rosenkavalier." At the bottom right is a photographer's credit with location and date.

A tinted vintage postcard showing several people riding camels on a desert road in front of large domed mausoleums and minarets. The architecture is Islamic, with multiple domes and a tall slender minaret in the background. There is handwriting at the top and printed caption text at the bottom in French.

Black-and-white vintage street view showing a broad cobbled market square lined with multi‑storey townhouses and shops. A tall, slender tower with a clock or observation platform rises prominently in the center background, likely attached to a historic town hall. People walk along the sidewalks, and a bicycle is parked by the curb. The caption at the bottom reads "Löwenberg i. Schl. – Marktplatz," and a small printer's logo appears in the lower right corner.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a small Alpine town nestled in a valley with surrounding mountains. In the foreground are clustered buildings with tiled roofs and a prominent church tower rising above the town. Fields and terraced hillsides extend into the distance. At the top of the card there is printed text identifying the view and its altitude in Italian.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing an old stone canopy structure with four columns and a domed, ornamented roof. Through the arches, a large mosque complex with prominent domes and tall minarets is visible in the background, along with other buildings of a historic cityscape. Handwritten ink text appears at the bottom over the image. Printed caption text at the bottom identifies the view as a tomb in Cairo.

A color postcard showing a panoramic view of the city of Graz with a prominent green hill (the Schlossberg) rising above the historic center. Buildings with red-tiled roofs surround the hill, and a river with embankments and bridges runs through the city to the right. In the background are distant mountains and a broad valley. Printed text at the top left reads "Graz, vom Rainerkogel," and there is cursive handwriting across the upper right.

Colorized vintage view of a harbor with piers, sailing ships, small boats and waterfront buildings. The image shows a river or canal opening into the sea, with a lighthouse or beacon on a spit of land at the right. Printed red text in multiple languages appears at the upper left, identifying the place as Windau/Wentspils and describing it as a fishing harbor.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a long, two‑storey school building with many uniform windows and a tiled roof. In the background are onion‑domed towers and a tall clock or bell tower. Leafless trees line the front of the building. The top left bears printed red text identifying the location and institution, and above the main entrance the word "Gymnasium" is visible.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a rural landscape with a dirt road in the foreground bordered by a low stone wall and large trees. Open fields and wooded hills stretch into the distance. Printed text in the upper right area reads "Uddevalla, Gamla landsvägen till Gustafsberg".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a cobblestone square framed by historic buildings. At the back stands a large Baroque-style building with an arched passageway. On the left is a tall spiraling Marian column. In the background, on a wooded hill, a clock tower rises prominently. The printed caption at the top left reads in red letters "Graz - Karmeliterplatz".

Sepia-toned panoramic view over a dense European town with tightly packed, gabled-roof buildings and a few taller industrial chimneys in the background. The vantage point appears elevated, likely from a church tower, overlooking the central part of the town and surrounding countryside. At the top of the image, printed in German, is the caption identifying the location and viewpoint.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a stone lookout tower with crenellations and a flagpole, attached to lower stone buildings with arched windows and tiled roofs, set in a lightly wooded landscape with a narrow path leading toward the structure. Printed German text appears in the upper left corner.

Sepia-toned postcard showing several naval vessels in a calm bay, with a line of buoys or anti‑submarine nets stretched across the water near the harbor entrance. Low hills and coastline are visible in the background. Printed captions in Greek and French appear at the top, and a website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears at the bottom.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard view over a park and waterfront street with trams, cars, and boats. Large multi‑story buildings line the left side, while a harbor or river with several docked vessels appears on the right. The image is titled at the top in Swedish: "Stockholm – Utsikt från Operaterrassen" (Stockholm – View from the Opera Terrace). The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century cityscape.

A vintage black‑and‑white photograph printed with a wide white border, showing a rural farm scene. A young barefoot girl in a light dress stands on grass, watching a group of piglets feeding together. A dog stands behind the piglets, looking toward the camera. In the background, there is a simple dirt yard with wooden fencing, a bucket, and the lower half of an adult person in work clothes and boots. The overall style resembles an old real‑photo postcard from a European farm.

Sepia-toned historic postcard view over the rooftops of a small European town set in a hilly landscape. In the foreground are narrow houses with steep tiled roofs and a small, fenced garden or courtyard with pillars and ornamental plants. In the middle distance, more compact buildings form the old town, and in the background a church tower with a bulbous spire rises above the rooftops. Smokestacks and open countryside can be seen further back. Printed German text appears at the top of the card.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard featuring a studio-style photograph of two young boys in traditional Chinese clothing standing side by side and holding hands. The boys wear long tunics, loose trousers, cloth shoes, and round caps. The photo is centered with a wide light border. Printed captions run vertically along the left and right margins, with a title at the bottom and a handwritten number in pencil in the lower right.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a canal or narrow harbor basin flanked by stone buildings with balconies and shuttered windows. A small bridge or gate-like structure spans the water in the background, with hills visible beyond. Greek handwritten text appears in the lower left, and the year 1918 is printed nearby. A modern website watermark, "www.elia.org.gr," is overlaid across the lower right.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a small domed Byzantine-style Orthodox church with ornate brickwork and a cross on top, located along a street with a fence and adjacent multi‑storey building with balconies. In the street there is a horse‑drawn or early motor tram with several people around it, and other small houses and trees in the background. Greek text captions appear at the bottom, along with a website watermark.

Colorized historic postcard view of a large multi‑storey school building with red roofs, small towers and decorative gables, seen from a distance across a garden or park. In front of the building is an open courtyard with a fountain. At the top in red Gothic-style letters is printed the location and name of the building.

A black‑and‑white vintage view of a small rural railway station labeled "ESPEN" on the station building. Curved train tracks run through the foreground toward a water tower and a house in the distance. Trees and low hills surround the line. In the top left corner in red letters is the caption "Espen St." and in the lower left corner there is a handwritten‑style date, likely "1908".

Sepia-toned vintage street scene showing a cobblestone street lined with two‑ and three‑story historic buildings. On the left is a building with flower boxes and a sign reading "Hotel Goldenes Lamm" above an arched entrance, with flagpoles extending from the façade. Similar old town buildings continue down the street. The caption at the bottom of the image identifies the town and street.

Black‑and‑white image showing a woman in a long dress standing on an ornate, decorative footbridge over a small pond in a lush, landscaped garden. The bridge has elaborate wrought‑iron railings with floral scrollwork and a gentle arch of brick or stone. Surrounding the scene are dense trees, shrubs, and water plants, giving a romantic park or estate‑garden atmosphere. There is no visible printed caption or border text on the image side.

Black‑and‑white view of a European town square or main street. On the right stands a substantial two‑storey civic building with a steep tiled roof, dormer windows, and a small tower; it resembles a town hall or administrative office. A stairway with a gabled porch leads to the main entrance. In the foreground to the left is a tall stone monument or war memorial topped by a large eagle sculpture with wings partly spread. The base of the monument carries multiple plaques and inscriptions. Behind it a tree‑lined street recedes into the distance with several smaller traditional houses. The lower edge of the image shows torn paper, consistent with an old postcard or photographic print. Some faint German text appears on the monument but is not fully legible.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large military barracks complex with long, multi‑storey buildings lined with many identical windows and dormer roofs. In the foreground is a fenced entrance with gates and low pillars, opening onto a cobblestone street leading between the barracks blocks. Handwritten red numbers appear in the top right margin. Printed caption text in German runs along the bottom edge.

Black‑and‑white view of a European riverside town with a large hilltop cathedral complex and adjacent castle-like buildings dominating the skyline. In the foreground a broad river flows from left to right; a long low cargo boat moves along the water. Two bridges span the river: an older arched stone bridge and, in front of it, a metal truss bridge on stone piers. On the right, a riverside embankment road with tram tracks curves alongside a rocky cliff with trees and houses above. People are walking and cycling along the promenade. The overall look suggests an early‑20th‑century cityscape. No text is visible on the image.

A monochrome illustrated postcard showing a harbor scene with a small arched bridge in the foreground, quayside buildings and sheds, moored sailing vessels, and in the background a church or town hall tower with a clock. The style is early 20th‑century engraving or lithograph. The lower margin bears titles in German, including the place name and harbor, and the artist's signature.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a cobblestone street lined with multi‑story historic buildings. On the right is a long arcaded façade; further down the street stands a decorated building with four corner turrets and patterned walls. On the left corner is a shop with a sign bearing the name "Adolf" and another word. People are visible on the sidewalk and looking out of an upper‑floor window. The printed caption at the top reads "Kamenz i. Sa. - Kirchstraße".

Sepia-toned photograph of a grave monument surrounded by abundant flowers and foliage in a wooded cemetery. The tall, dark headstone has a cross-like shape with a name plate reading "J. Rennit" and a larger inscription below in Estonian. The background shows trees and a simple metal fence.

Black-and-white aerial photograph of a small residential town surrounded by dense coniferous forest. The settlement consists mainly of detached houses with pitched roofs, gardens, and tree-lined streets. There are no prominent monuments, churches, or tall buildings visible, just a grid of quiet suburban roads cutting through wooded terrain.

A monochrome panoramic view of a small rural village with several traditional half-timbered houses, farm buildings, and narrow paths crossing fields and gardens. The landscape is gently hilly and appears leafless, suggesting late autumn or winter. At the bottom, printed in red German text, it reads "Gruss aus Röhrsdorf." Below in smaller type is the printer's credit and date.

Black‑and‑white illustrated wartime scene showing French soldiers in an intense bayonet charge against German troops wearing spiked pickelhaube helmets. Smoke and explosions fill the background, and the foreground is crowded with bodies and close‑quarters combat in a trench or on a battlefield. At the bottom, printed text reads "LA FURIA FRANÇAISE" with a small publisher's mark and the word "PARIS"; there is also cursive handwriting in ink across the lower margin.

Black-and-white panoramic view of a small European town along a river with a weir or low dam in the foreground. There are tree-lined paths, fields, and a park-like riverside area, with a compact town center beyond, including a church tower, residential houses, and an industrial complex with a tall smokestack. Rolling farmland and forested hills extend into the distance. In the bottom-left corner, white caption text reads "Wurzen a. d. Mulde".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with red printed captions showing a street lined with wooden villas behind lattice fences and trees in a forested, hilly area. The main house in the foreground is labeled "Villa 'Stadthütte'", and another house further along the street is labeled "Villa 'Friedenshain'". At the top is a caption indicating the place name, and at the bottom left is the printer's imprint.

A black‑and‑white view along a wide stone walkway lined with white balustrades and potted plants leading toward a traditional Chinese gate with a tiled roof. Beyond dense trees rises a large white Tibetan-style stupa (dagoba) on a hill, with a dark niche on its front and a small structure at its base.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a hillside covered with trees and scattered villas. In the center stands a large multi‑storey sanatorium building with decorative turrets and a central clock. Above it, on the hilltop, there is a round tower and a smaller pavilion. Text identifying the site is printed over the image and along the bottom border.

Black‑and‑white image of a large, three‑storey, late‑19th‑century building seen from across a small park or garden. The facade has regularly spaced tall windows, rusticated ground floor, and more ornate upper storeys with pilasters and decorative gables above the central and left sections of the roof. Dormer windows project from a steep, dark roof with chimneys. Leafy trees and bushes partly obscure the lower part of the building, and a simple metal fence runs along the front, with fallen leaves on the ground suggesting autumn. There is no clearly legible printed title on the image, only some small, vertical markings along the right border that look like a handwritten or film-edge notation.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a riverside town with dense trees in the foreground, a winding river through the center, industrial chimneys and factory buildings near the water, and a compact historic town with churches and multi‑story buildings on the hills beyond. The layout and printing style are typical of early 20th‑century European picture postcards. Red handwritten numbers are visible on the top, and printed titles in German appear along the top and left margin.

Black‑and‑white view over a small European town at the foot of a wooded hillside. In the foreground there is a fenced public or private garden laid out with curving flowerbeds and young trees along a path. Behind the garden stand several late‑19th‑ or early‑20th‑century houses and small apartment buildings with steep gabled or mansard roofs, stucco or brick facades, and simple ornamentation. A broad unpaved or lightly paved street with utility poles runs at the right edge. On the distant ridge are terraced slopes, scattered houses, and a small chapel‑like building on the hilltop.

An old, colorized postcard depicting a large medieval castle complex on a hill with high stone walls and a prominent round tower on the right. In the foreground there are gardens, paths, and small buildings. The structure appears fortified, with a long rectangular wing and small windows. The card shows signs of age with creases and worn edges. At the top left, text states the location.

Black‑and‑white view of a cobblestoned town square in front of several historic European buildings with steep tiled roofs and dormer windows. A church or town-hall tower with a clock and weather vane rises at the right. In the middle of the square stands an ornate multi‑globe streetlamp and a circular flowerbed. People, including children, are walking and gathering in small groups. Signs on the right-hand building read like German commercial or municipal inscriptions.

A monochrome postcard view of a medieval castle complex with a prominent cylindrical tower and surrounding walls, set against a mountainous backdrop. In the foreground are rocky terrain and a few low buildings, while higher on the left are houses and walls overlooking the castle. At the top of the postcard the printed caption reads "TRENTO. Castello".

A sepia-toned postcard showing a large Neo-Gothic city hall building with a tall central clock tower and multiple pinnacles. In the foreground is a circular fountain with a high water jet and landscaped gardens with people walking around. Leafless trees frame the scene. Handwritten-style captions appear at the bottom margin.

Vintage black‑and‑white winter street scene in a European mountain town. Snow covers the rooftops and a large bare tree; people in early 20th‑century clothing are skiing and standing in groups along a main street lined with multi‑storey houses and shops. At the bottom left there is printed white text with the place name, and shop signs are visible on the buildings.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a quiet semi‑rural road curving through a small town. On the right are simple wooden houses with pitched roofs and fenced gardens; a few bicycles are visible by the roadside. A small 1930s–1950s style car drives away from the camera along the paved road, which has streetlamps and telegraph poles. On the left is an open grassy area leading to water or wetland, with a bench and low fencing. In the distance, beyond trees and low buildings, rises a church with a tall, narrow spire. The sky is wide and lightly clouded. There is no visible printed caption or handwriting on the image side.
Vintage portrait postcard showing an older man in formal ceremonial robes and cap (academic/judicial style). The reverse bears museum/archive stamps and a handwritten name and inventory number.

Color lithographic postcard with two vignette views labeled in German: one shows the medieval gate with four sharp spires (Catherine's Gate) and another view marked Waisenhausgasserthor, both from Kronstadt (Brașov). A floral motif decorates the front along with a handwritten German message. The address side reads "Levelező-lap" in Hungarian and bears postmarks from Nagy-Szeben, addressed to Frau Friederike Fitsch in Hermannstadt, Siebenbürgen.

Sepia postcard showing a long, four‑storey Austro‑Hungarian military school building with a gated entrance and a few soldiers standing by the gate. Tram tracks run along the street in the foreground. Multilingual caption identifies it as the Infantry Cadet School. The reverse lists the city in Hungarian, German and Romanian and uses the Hungarian postcard heading.

Old monochrome postcard with a panoramic view of the city labeled Hermannstadt, showing church spires and town towers against distant hills. Printed caption and publisher credits appear on the front; handwritten German message overlays the lower margin. The reverse reads LEVELEZŐ-LAP and bears a pink Austrian stamp with a clear Wien postmark dated 15 Aug 99, plus an address written in German.

Vintage b/w postcard showing a town square with horse‑drawn carriages and a long Austro‑Hungarian infantry barracks building. The caption reads about Hermannsplatz and the k.u.k. infantry barracks in Hermannstadt. Address side bears Hungarian heading 'Levelező Lap', a 5 fillér stamp with postmarks, and an address written in German.

Sepia studio portrait of a middle‑aged man in a suit and tie. The card has deckled edges and typed Romanian captioning beneath the photo, plus handwritten inventory numbers. The reverse shows divided‑back postcard layout with a purple museum stamp reading "MUZEUL JUD. Bv." and various pencil notations.

Tinted lithographic postcard with two views labeled in German: the entrance to the town hall and the town hall courtyard. The scenes show medieval buildings with a gate, tower, and ivy-covered walls. The top reads "Gruss aus Hermannstadt." Publisher and printer credits appear along the left margin. The reverse is a divided back printed in Hungarian with "LEVELEZÖ-LAP."

Black‑and‑white real photo postcard showing a rural scene: two cows wading through a shallow stream or ford on a dirt track, trees along the banks, and a small wooden hut with a steep metal roof in the background. The photo has a wide white border. The reverse has a multilingual 'postcard' heading and pencil notations.

Sepia street view postcard showing Strada Mitropoliei in Sibiu with pedestrians, shop signs and, in the distance, the twin-towered church. The caption lists the city in Romanian, German and Hungarian. The reverse has Romanian stamps and postmarks, an address written in pencil, and the printer's imprint from Sibiu.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large industrial building with many workers posed in front of it. The caption identifies it as the glass factory in Avrig. Romanian text appears on both the image side and the address side.

Colorized winter scene showing a large Neo-Renaissance palace with snow-covered trees and a square filled with people and horse-drawn sleighs/carts. Printed caption in German identifies the view as the Bretterpromenade with the Habermann Palace. The reverse bears the Hungarian header 'LEVELEZÖ-LAP.' with address lines and a collector's stamp.

Vintage multiview lithographic postcard with vignettes of the city and surroundings: a panoramic view of Hermannstadt (Sibiu), the Großer Ring (Grand Square), the Natural History Museum, Michelsberg (Cisnădioara) hill/fort, and Salzburg (Ocna Sibiului). Front bears the printed title "Gruss aus Hermannstadt Salzburg Michelsberg." with handwritten German message. Reverse shows Hungarian 'Levelező-lap' layout, a Magyar Kir. Posta stamp and Nagy-Szeben postmarks, addressed to Vienna (Hernals).

Black‑and‑white winter scene of an outdoor market in a large European square. Snow covers the roofs of Baroque townhouses. Numerous stalls and striped awnings fill the square, with many people in winter clothing. At right stands a statue/fountain on a pedestal; an early automobile is parked nearby. The verso bears museum and director stamps and pencil notes.

Tinted black‑and‑white view of a central square with the old town hall and clock tower, people walking, and an ornate streetlamp in the foreground. Handwritten message appears across the lower margin on the front; the reverse has an address area, a red postage stamp, and a long handwritten note.

Vintage sepia postcard showing the ornate interior of the Orthodox cathedral in Sibiu, with a large central dome, a massive chandelier, colonnades and galleries. A printed caption appears below the image. The reverse reads "România — Cartă Postală" and lists the Sibiu/Hermannstadt publisher.

Sepia-toned view of a grand neoclassical school building along a street, with a fenced yard and large trees. Several Romanian tricolor flags hang from the facade. The caption at the bottom reads the city and the institution's name. The reverse says Romania and Carte Poștală with the publisher imprint dated 1925.

Sepia panoramic view of a historic town with multiple church towers and domes, backed by snow‑covered mountains. Printed Hungarian captions on the front read "Nagyszeben" and "Látkép." The reverse shows handwriting in Romanian, a green charity/revenue stamp reading "TIMBRU DE AJUTOR 5 BANI ROMANIA," and Hungarian publisher/price markings.

Vintage collage postcard showing a river-bathing and open‑air sports establishment with wooden cabins, lawn and deckchairs. Three inset photos are labeled for the river bath, the men's section, and the women's section. Floral/water‑lily decoration frames the images. Printed German text identifies the place and address and includes a greeting from Hermannstadt.

Colorized street scene showing a lively boulevard with shopfronts and striped awnings, pedestrians in early‑20th‑century attire, a horse‑drawn carriage, and a tramcar. Caption at top reads "Hermannstadt — Nagyszeben — Heltauer Gasse."

Sepia-toned postcard showing the interior of a large beer hall with arched windows, many wooden tables and chairs lined in rows, and ceiling light fixtures. Caption in German at the bottom names the venue. The back bears Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP', a printer's credit from Hermannstadt, and a collector's stamp.

Sepia photograph of a church with multiple spires and a clock tower behind a gated arch and tile‑roofed houses, set against wooded hills. The front caption lists the city in Romanian, Hungarian, and German. The reverse has Romanian handwriting and address lines, three Romanian stamps (including an aviation stamp and a blue 'Pentru Cultură' stamp), and postmarks dated 30 July 1932. Printed text on the back identifies the scene as St. Nicholas Church.

Hand‑tinted street view showing Brașov's main street with the corner building signed "CAFE KRON" and the Hotel Coroana/Hotel Krone. Multilingual captions (Hungarian, German, Romanian) identify the place. Reverse side bears Romanian stamps and an address written in Romanian.

Monochrome postcard showing a long, low building with an arched veranda and a central pedimented section bearing the inscription 'CERCUL MILITAR'. Captions in the image read 'Brasov' and 'Cercul Militar'. The reverse is a divided-back postcard printed in Romanian with 'România' and 'Cartă Postală', guide lines for the address, and small pencil marks.

Colorized street scene with outdoor café tables under large awnings in front of ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. Caption on the picture reads "Brașov, Brassó, Kronstadt," indicating the city in Romanian, Hungarian, and German. The reverse has Romanian postal cancellations, a Romanian stamp, and handwriting addressed to Bucharest. A printed caption on the back mentions the Prefecture with the Transylvania Café.

Color lithographed multi‑view greeting postcard with floral motifs reading "Gruss aus Kronstadt". It depicts two scenes from the city: a neoclassical 'Concerthaus' (concert hall) and an ornate mansion labeled 'Villa Schuller'. People stroll in front of the buildings. Publisher credit appears on the right margin. The reverse side is a blank address layout in Hungarian ("Levelező‑lap", "Czim").

Old sepia/black‑and‑white postcard showing two children posing outdoors. The girl wears a bonnet and light dress with a muff; the boy wears a beret, cape coat and boots. A handwritten caption appears on the front margin. The reverse has the classic divided back with the preprinted Hungarian word "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP," blue handwritten notes in Romanian, a museum stamp, and inventory numbers.

Sepia street view of a historic town with low, tiled-roof houses and shutters, a telegraph pole, and a square medieval-looking tower in the distance. The caption at top right reads "Mediaș — Mediasch." The reverse is a Romanian postcard layout.

Colorized early-20th‑century postcard showing a grand historic villa labeled "Villa Kertsch" in Brașov, Romania. The multi‑storey building has a corner tower, bay windows and an iron fence with a garden in front. Pedestrians and a horse‑drawn carriage are visible on the street. Small shop signs include one for a dentist and another reading HOTEL. The reverse is a divided back printed in Romanian, with the publisher credit and a 1925 date.

Old, monochrome postcard showing a large neoclassical barracks building with soldiers and horses standing in snow in front. Printed bilingual captions at the top read the Hungarian and German names of the city and the site. The reverse is a used Hungarian postcard form (LEVELEZŐ-LAP) with a green stamp, address to Johann Farkas, and a handwritten German message.

Colorized view of a broad urban square with a grassy foreground, a long neoclassical building with arcades on the left, a plain three‑story building with a red roof on the right, scattered pedestrians and a small tram in the distance. Printed captions read "Nagyszeben" and "Hermann-tér — Hermannsplatz"; a blue handstamp reads "SIBIU." The reverse has bilingual headings "CARTE POSTALA" and "LEVELEZŐ-LAP," a dotted stamp box and a Budapest printing credit dated 1918.

Old black‑and‑white street view postcard showing a sloping cobblestone street lined with shuttered houses and arcaded buildings, pedestrians and horse‑drawn carts. A stairway descends at right. The caption at the top is trilingual and identifies the place as Nagyszeben / Hermannstadt / Sibiu and the street as Burgergasse / Burger‑utca / Strada Ocnei. The reverse is a Hungarian-format postcard (LEVELEZŐ‑LAP) with a green 5‑fillér stamp canceled in Nagyszeben and addressed to Brassó (Kronstadt), with a handwritten German message.

Vintage tinted postcard view of a long three‑storey military barracks with a hipped roof in Sibiu. Pedestrians and a horse‑drawn cart are in the foreground. The caption is printed in Romanian, German and Hungarian. The reverse says România / Cartă Postală and credits publisher Jos. Drotleff, Sibiu–Hermannstadt.

Sepia photographic postcard showing a studio portrait of a middle‑aged woman wearing a dark, floral-patterned blouse. The card has scalloped edges. On the front margin there is an oval studio stamp. The reverse reads 'CARTE POSTALE' and bears a purple museum stamp and a studio imprint.

Green-tinted aerial view of a hillside settlement with a church featuring a clock-tower and a terraced cemetery. Caption at the bottom names Brașov and identifies the scene as Holy Trinity Church (Tocile) and the Heroes' Cemetery. The reverse reads "România – Carte Postală" with printed date 1928 and a handwritten address mentioning București, Gara de Nord.

Sepia real‑photo studio portrait showing a seated woman in a white, elaborate dress and hat beside a man wearing a long clerical cassock and collar. A handwritten Romanian caption with the priest's name appears on the image. The reverse carries a long Romanian message and is addressed to the Albina Bank in Nagyszeben (Sibiu), with a Romanian green stamp postmarked Dragomirești.

Black‑and‑white real photo postcard showing a side‑profile portrait of a woman in traditional Transylvanian folk costume (white blouse, long embroidered skirt/apron, tall cylindrical headdress) standing by a building with block‑patterned wall cladding. The reverse is a divided back with pencil notes including the word "Dedrad," a date-like note, and an Agfa paper mark.

Vintage Romanian postcard featuring a sepia studio portrait of a mustachioed man in 19th‑century attire, standing with one hand on a pedestal. The front is captioned with the name "C. Negruzi." and the series title "Colecția scriitorilor români" with the number 37. The back bears Romanian postcard markings, the publisher line, a museum stamp, and several handwritten inventory numbers.

Hand‑tinted street view showing a row of historic buildings along a broad cobbled street. Caption at top reads "Hermannstadt" and "Mühlgasse." People and horse‑drawn carts are visible; architecture is late 19th‑century Austro‑Hungarian style. The reverse has a Hungarian postcard layout and a green 5‑filler Hungarian stamp with 1908 postmarks.

Colorized townscape seen from a church tower, showing red‑tiled roofs in a valley beneath a forested mountain. The front caption reads "Zeiden vom Kirchturm." The reverse is a Hungarian postcard layout with a green 5 fillér stamp, postmarks, address lines, and publisher credits.

Real photo postcard: a black‑and‑white studio portrait of a WWII-era German/Austrian soldier in uniform, standing full-length against a painted backdrop. The reverse has a divided back with German handwriting in pencil and blue ink, dated 20.11.43, names Lederer Elisabeth and Lederer Andreas, and an address on Königsgasse. A faint purple photographer's stamp runs vertically along the left edge.

Color lithographed street view of the old town with an iron-railed bridge leading into a square. A clock tower rises over tiled roofs; ornate Baroque façades flank a lamppost. Captions read "Kleiner Ring" and "Alt‑Hermannstadt," with artist credit "gez. v. Trude Schullerus." The reverse is a divided back marked in Hungarian "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP," with a purple circular stamp from Brukenthal's Museum in Hermannstadt and a date stamp 7 JULI 1917.

Black-and-white postcard showing a rural procession of men on horseback wearing traditional Romanian folk costumes, riding along a dirt street lined with simple houses and wooden fences. The back has Romanian handwritten notes, a number, and archival marks.

Sepia photograph of a large school dormitory building with arched windows and a carved entrance. A group of men and boys pose in front of the fence. The facade bears an inscription in Romanian. Bottom-right caption lists the city name in Romanian, Hungarian, and German. Hills are visible in the background. The reverse side is a Romanian postcard template.

Sepia real-photo postcard showing a large Gothic hall church dominating a historic townscape. The church has tall pointed-arch windows, exterior buttresses and a hefty square tower with a circular clock, topped by an octagonal lantern and a short spire. Tiled roofs of old houses fill the foreground, and a steep, forested mountain rises immediately behind.

Black-and-white postcard showing a grand Neo-Baroque/Beaux-Arts courthouse with a large central dome and symmetrical wings. A sign above the main entrance reads "PALATUL JUSTITIEI." There is a landscaped square with paths and trees in front, and hills visible in the background. The back is printed with multilingual captions identifying the view and has a stamp box marked 018.

Sepia postcard showing a large city gate with one tall central arch and two small side arches. Several people stand near the entrance. Caption at the bottom reads "Kronstadt — Brassó Waisenhausgässer-Tor." The reverse has German handwriting, a purple "BRASOV Cenzurat" stamp, a penciled 1920 date, and the publisher credit along the left edge.

Vintage black‑and‑white real‑photo postcard showing a rural parade or fair: villagers in Romanian folk costumes ride an ox‑drawn cart decorated with fir branches and a large cooking cauldron, with wooden houses behind. The reverse has a divided‑back layout with Romanian handwriting and a purple archive stamp from Muzeul Brukenthal, indicating museum cataloging.

Sepia postcard showing a traditional Saxon house with large shingled roof and fenced garden on a small town square. People in period dress stand in the square near a kiosk/pillar. Caption in German names the scene in Mediasch (Mediaș). The reverse has Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP' layout and the publisher credit printed vertically.

A black‑and‑white vintage street scene showing pedestrians on a cobblestoned lane lined with historic Central‑European buildings. A printed caption at the top right reads "Herrmannstadt — Fleischergasse." The reverse bears Hungarian postcard wording and a printer's mark.

Multi-view black‑and‑white postcard with floral frames showing a fortified church complex with towers and a gate, captioned in German. The reverse has a Hungarian header, a 4 fillér Magyar Kir. Posta stamp, and a Nagyszeben/Sibiu postmark with handwritten German message.

Colorized view of early skyscrapers and a church spire surrounding a leafy urban park. The caption at the top reads about West Grand Circus Park in Detroit, Michigan. One rooftop sign reads "HOTEL STATLER." The reverse has a printed description of Grand Circus Park, ornate "POST CARD" lettering, and typical stamp/address boxes.

Sepia-toned portrait postcard showing an older woman in a dotted headscarf and dark dress holding light-colored flowers, standing beside a child wearing a dark outfit with a large bow. They are outdoors in a leafy garden or yard with wooden structures behind them. The card has a white border with rounded image corners. The reverse is a divided back with handwritten notes.

Vintage photo postcard showing people rowing boats on a tree-lined lake with a small pier and pavilion in the background. The caption printed on the front names the city in Romanian, German, and Hungarian and identifies the lake. The reverse bears Romanian postage stamps and a 1928 postmark, plus a Sibiu printer's imprint.

Vintage monochrome street scene labeled in Hungarian and German, showing a bustling avenue with shops, pedestrians, and horse‑drawn carts. A prominent baroque church tower with a clock rises above the street. Title at top reads "Brassó — Kronstadt / Kolostor-utca — Kloster-Gasse." The reverse carries the heading "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP."

Colorized early 20th‑century view of a park fountain surrounded by dense trees; a woman and a child stand near the basin. Caption at top appears in Hungarian and German. The reverse bears Romanian stamps, a Bucharest postmark, and a short Romanian message and address.

Vintage monochrome view of a long, single‑story villa set against a forested hillside. A white picket fence, garden paths and a bench appear in the foreground. The reverse carries multilingual captions and Romanian postcard layout.

A multi-view vintage postcard titled in red "Gruss aus Kronstadt." It shows four photographs of Brașov/Kronstadt: the town hall with a clocktower and a busy market scene (captioned "Rathaus"), the main marketplace ("Marktplatz"), a building labeled "Villa Kertsch," and a panoramic view of a hill labeled "Schlossberg." Publisher credit along the left reads "Wilh. Hiemesch, Buchhandlung, Kronstadt." The front is filled with a handwritten German message dated from Bistritz. The reverse is a Hungarian 'Levelező-Lap' with a green Magyar Kir. Posta stamp and postmarks, addressed to Hermannstadt (Nagyszeben).

Color-tinted panoramic view of a valley with mountains, a river and a railway line leading toward a village. Small houses dot the hillsides. Captions at the top read "Iacobeni" and "Intrarea în Iacobeni." The reverse has Romanian postcard layout with the heading "România – Cartă Postală" and a publisher line dated 1925.

Sepia postcard showing a large, early‑20th‑century school building with a mansard roof and many dormer windows, bordered by a concrete fence; a ruined watchtower rises on the hillside to the right. The reverse is a divided back with Hungarian header and bilingual city name indicating the subject is the Honterus-Gymnasium in Kronstadt/Brassó.

Vintage multiview postcard with an Art Nouveau oak-tree frame. Left inset shows a grand building labeled "Schützenhaus"; right inset shows a tree-lined moat/canal and medieval walls labeled "Graft-Parthie." The city name "Kronstadt" appears on the front. The reverse reads "Correspondenz-Karte" with dotted address lines.

Black‑and‑white real photo postcard showing a large group portrait in front of a building. Many young women wear traditional embroidered Romanian blouses and headscarves; seated in front are older women in 1930s-style coats and hats, with several men in suits standing behind. Scalloped postcard borders; the reverse has a studio stamp and pencil notes.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a town nestled in wooded hills, seen from an elevated lookout framed by dark tree silhouettes. The reverse is printed in Romanian with state-publisher marks and identifies the view as a general view of Brașov.

Colorized postcard showing the corner façade of the grand Hotel Europa with people and an early automobile in front. Title at top reads in three languages: Hermannstadt – Nagyszeben – Sibiu. The reverse has a Hungarian 10 fillér stamp, handwritten German message and address, and a publisher's imprint from Hermannstadt. Dated 1916.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large group portrait of youths and girls in traditional Romanian dress. A printed caption at the top reads about the Romanian Greek‑Orthodox youth and girls' society of Marpod. The reverse has address lines, the printed Hungarian word "NYOMTATVÁNY," a museum stamp from Sibiu and various handwritten notes.

Colorized postcard showing a curving railway and a village in a valley with a large mountain behind it. The printed caption names Kronstadt and the Schuler mountain. Publisher's imprint appears on the left margin. Handwritten German message surrounds the image. The reverse is a Hungarian 'Levelező-lap' with a Magyar Kir. Posta stamp and BRASSÓ and NAGY-SZEBEN postmarks.

Tinted blue-and-white view of a large two‑storey historic building with a central pointed-arch doorway and Gothic windows, set behind a garden. Printed greeting text appears at top right and a caption under the image identifies the building as a Protestant church seminary. Publisher and printer credits run vertically along the left edge. The reverse shows the Hungarian word for postcard, "Levelező‑lap.", with dotted address lines.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing an ornate, late‑19th/early‑20th‑century building labeled as the Romanian National House, seen from the street with bare tree branches in the foreground. Printed German caption reads "Gruß aus Hermannstadt" and "Rumänisches Nationalhaus." Publisher credit appears at the bottom. The reverse side uses the Hungarian postcard header "Levelező‑Lap." and bears a purple ownership stamp.

Colorized early-20th‑century view of a large Gothic church with a tall central clock tower and steep spire, flanked by multiple gabled roofs and lancet windows. The reverse bears multilingual captions identifying the place and a Romanian 'CARTĂ POSTALĂ' header.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the Black Church of Brașov in the foreground with the forested Tâmpa Mountain rising behind. The caption in Romanian is printed along the lower front margin. The reverse carries Romanian stamps, circular postmarks, a printed publisher credit, and a handwritten address to Bucharest.

Vintage street-view postcard showing a tram, carts, and pedestrians on a busy historic street lined with late-19th/early-20th‑century buildings. Title at top names the city in three languages and the street. Addressed side bears a Hungarian stamp and handwritten German text.

Sepia real-photo postcard showing a young woman in traditional Romanian (Transylvanian/Pădureni) costume standing in profile in a rustic yard before a wooden gate and fence. The back is printed with multilingual captions and Romanian postcard layout, indicating it was issued by the Ethnographic Museum in Cluj.

Sepia postcard view of a medieval gateway and stair street descending through an arch beneath a roofed building. The caption reads "Sagstiege" with the bilingual city name "Hermannstadt — Nagyszeben." Photo credit "Phot. Dr. V. Roth" appears on the front.

Vintage divided-back postcard with three black‑and‑white views of military buildings labeled in German: the officers' mess, the barracks, and the canteen. The captions include the place name Hermannstadt. The reverse has Hungarian postal text (Levelező‑lap) and a green 5 filler Hungarian stamp postmarked around 1914, addressed within Hungary. Printer credit reads Jos. Drotleff, Hermannstadt.

Black-and-white real photo postcard with scalloped edges showing a group of about a dozen men posing on building steps beside a large round column. Two accordions and a brass horn are visible, suggesting musicians. The reverse has a vertical divider and handwritten notes.

Colorized view of a hillside in Brașov with late‑19th/early‑20th‑century villas and a tree‑lined green foreground. The front bears the trilingual city name: Romanian, Hungarian, and German. The back shows Romanian postage and a Romanian postal layout with handwritten message and address.

Colorized street view with a church and spire along a sloping road lined with small houses. Printed caption at top right reads in Hungarian and German. The reverse is a Hungarian postcard layout (LEVELEZŐ-LAP) with a 1916 postmark from Nagyszeben and handwritten field‑post address (Feldpost).

Monochrome vintage postcard showing the tall spires of Saint Nicholas Church rising above trees and old tile‑roofed houses, with wooded mountains in the background. A small gatehouse and archway stand in the foreground. Caption at bottom reads "Brașov — Biserica Sft. Nicolae — Piața Prundului." The reverse bears Romanian stamps, a 1933 postmark, handwritten message and address, and the publisher imprint "Editura Librăria Cooperativă, Brașov."

Sepia-toned photo of five people posing on a weathered wooden pier by the sea. The group includes a man in a light suit, two women in dresses and hats, an older woman in dark clothes, and a boy in a vest and tie. The reverse has penciled names, an inventory note, and an oval stamp reading "FOTO MAMAIA 1934."

Sepia photograph of a grand Baroque palace with a steep tiled roof and ornate façade on a city square. Ground-floor shops include a sign reading "C. MULLER" and "APOTHEKE." People are gathered on the street. The reverse side is a divided back with multilingual captions naming the Brukenthal Museum in Hermannstadt/Sibiu and a 1932 copyright notice.

Colorized view of a grand Beaux‑Arts courthouse with a red tiled roof and central clocked dome, set behind a landscaped square with a vintage bus and pedestrians. The front is titled "Brașov – Palatul Tribunalului." The reverse is a divided back with Romanian text and a local publisher imprint, plus a purple library stamp and a red handwritten number.

Sepia postcard showing a medieval gatehouse with four slender spired turrets and adjoining buildings around a small courtyard. Title at the top reads "Katharinentor – Katalinkapu," referring to Catherine's Gate. The reverse lists the city in three languages and bears a Hungarian stamp and 1916 postmarks with an address written in German.

Sepia photograph of a grand baroque-eclectic palace behind a wrought-iron fence on a wide, tree-lined street with tram tracks and overhead wires. Caption at the bottom identifies the building and the city in German, Hungarian, and Romanian.

Color-tinted postcard view of Huet Square in Sibiu, showing the Evangelical Lutheran Cathedral of Saint Mary on the right, surrounding historic buildings, and a central statue within a fenced area. The caption appears in Romanian, German, and Hungarian. The back is printed "România – Cartă Postală" with multilingual city names and a Sibiu publisher credit.

Sepia postcard depicting a Romanian girl in traditional costume standing on a dirt road before stone, thatched-roof houses; villagers in folk dress gather near a house. Caption identifies her as from Gyalár. The reverse has a divided back with the Hungarian word for postcard, the printer's credit to Jos. Drotleff in Hermannstadt dated 1917, and a Brukenthal (Sibiu) museum stamp.

Sepia postcard view of a bustling central square with many horse-drawn carriages and pedestrians. A large Gothic church with flying buttresses and a small spire dominates the left side, while rows of merchant houses with shop signs line the square. The reverse lists the city name in Romanian, German and Hungarian and a German-language publisher credit.

Colorized postcard showing a grand early-20th‑century hotel with red-tiled roof and arched windows amid trees. The caption on the image reads "Hotelul Statului." The reverse lists the spa resort names in Romanian, German and Hungarian and has Romanian postal instructions.

Multi-view vintage postcard with the printed caption 'Gruss aus Kronstadt.' showing four small images: the Rathaus (town hall) with a busy market, the Marktplatz, 'Villa Kertsch', and 'Schlossberg'. Publisher credit 'W. Hiemesch, Kronstadt.' appears on the left. The reverse has Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP' and a Budapest postmark dated 98.VII.18, addressed in German to a recipient in Hermannstadt.

Sepia-toned street scene showing an early electric tram on Strada Turnului in Sibiu. Low gabled houses and shops line the street, and the tall spire of the Lutheran Cathedral of Saint Mary rises in the background. A trilingual caption is printed beneath the image.
Sepia/black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural Roma couple with a donkey in front of huts and wattle fences in a mountainous landscape. The German caption "Zigeunerpaar" appears in red at the bottom.

Sepia postcard showing a photograph of a framed painted portrait of a 19th‑century gentleman with a mustache, wearing a dark coat and white cravat, his right hand tucked into his coat. A wide white margin surrounds the image and the number 153 is handwritten at the bottom. The reverse is a divided postcard back with pencil and ink notes and a purple museum stamp.

Sepia photo postcard showing a long, multi‑storey infantry barracks with an arched gateway and a small towered roof. In front is a square with a horse‑drawn carriage and a few soldiers. Caption reads "Hermannnstadt – Infanteriekaserne – Hermannsplatz." The reverse bears the Hungarian word for postcard and a local publisher credit.

Tinted view of a Lutheran church complex with white plaster walls and steep red roofs. A central tower with a pointed spire stands above adjoining buildings facing a quiet street. Printed German captions read "Hermannstadt" and "Ev. Johanniskirche." The reverse is a divided back with a vertical publisher credit.

Colored view of a broad, tree‑lined boulevard with ornate late‑19th‑century buildings and café awnings on the right and several pedestrians in the street. A church spire rises in the distance. The caption at top reads the city's names in Hungarian, German and Romanian and identifies the boulevard. The reverse is a divided back headed LEVELEZŐ-LAP with a green 5 Filler Magyar Kir. Posta stamp and German cursive message addressed to Herr Gustav Grüber in Hermannstadt.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a landscaped park with paths and a circular fountain in the foreground, and a long classical building behind it. The front caption reads the city name in three languages and identifies the site as the Erlenpark and the k.u.k. Garrison Hospital.

Vintage postcard with a monochrome panoramic view of a city nestled among hills. A hilltop citadel/fortified complex appears on the right, with dense rooftops and a large open square in the center. The caption on the image reads "Brașov — Kronstadt." The reverse side is printed "România — Cartă Postală" with address lines and a small printed letter "E"; there is also a red hand-stamped number "1237."

Monochrome street view showing a corner building with ornate façades and a small rooftop cupola, identified as a branch of the Austro‑Hungarian Bank. Tram tracks curve along the street and an early electric tram is approaching. Leafless trees line the sidewalk. The caption is printed in German and Hungarian.

Black‑and‑white village scene showing a man in traditional Romanian costume (sheepskin coat) on a white horse, surrounded by villagers in folk dress along a dirt street. It appears to be a ceremonial gathering. The reverse bears a purple museum stamp from Sibiu and handwritten Romanian notes mentioning the unveiling of a Heroes' Monument in Jina.

Colorized early 20th‑century postcard showing the Catholic Upper Gymnasium in Brassó (Brașov), Transylvania. The school complex with a church steeple stands before a wooded park, with a mountain and hilltop fort behind. Reverse side has the Hungarian heading 'LEVELEZŐ‑LAP', a green 5 fillér Hungarian stamp cancelled 'BRASSÓ', and an address to Hermannstadt/Nagyszeben; the picture side bears a handwritten German message.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a grand neoclassical school building with arched loggia and columns on a corner. The printed caption at top right reads in German 'Hermannstadt – Ev. Knabenvolksschule.' Handwritten message overlays the image. The reverse has 'LEVELEZŐ LAP' (Hungarian for postcard), a Romanian 'Timbru de Ajutor' 10 bani stamp, and an address to Cluj University.

Tinted divided-view postcard showing two steep old-town stairways labeled 'Fingerlingstiege' (left) and 'Sagstiege' (right). Narrow houses with green shutters line the steps; an arched passage and a tall clock/bell tower rise in the right image. Caption in German reads 'Gruss aus Hermannstadt'. The back is a Hungarian-format postcard ('LEVELEZŐ-LAP') with a green 5 FILLER stamp and handwritten German address/message.

Colorized view of a steel truss bridge over a river with the city skyline behind it. Caption reads in German and Hungarian naming Hermannstadt/Nagyszeben, the Zibin Bridge and the Honvéd barracks. On the reverse there is a Hungarian 10 fillér "Magyar Kir. Posta" stamp and a German-addressed message.

Sepia-toned street view of a large neoclassical public building lined with trees. Printed captions in Romanian at top read "Făgăraș" and "Palatul Prefecturii jud." The reverse is a divided back with "România – Cartă Postală," a bookseller credit, and a faint purple stamp.

Black‑and‑white real photo postcard showing a large group of young people sitting on a grassy hillside. Many wear Central/Eastern European folk costumes (embroidered blouses, vests, dirndl‑like dresses, knee socks), others wear casual 1930s clothing and caps. Trees and shrubs form the background. The reverse has a divided back with handwritten German text and the date 1935.

Sepia studio portrait of a young man in a military uniform standing beside an ornate table with a vase of flowers and a carved chair; draped curtain and framed picture in the background. The reverse has a divided-back layout with a handwritten name/number.

Colorized panoramic view of Brașov taken from a hillside lookout with a wooden fence in the foreground. The skyline shows red-roofed houses and the clock tower of the Council House in Piața Sfatului; on the left a white medieval tower on the slope. Reverse side bears Romanian stamps and handwriting addressed to Bucharest.

Sepia panoramic view of a spa resort with saline lakes, wooden boardwalks and pavilions, arched bath buildings and a smokestack, set among hills with a church spire in the distance. The caption on the image reads "Salutări dela Băile Ocna-Sibiului" and "Lacurile Horia, Cloșca și Crișan." The reverse is printed in Romanian, German and Hungarian and lists the publisher in Sibiu.

Tinted view of a large late 19th–early 20th‑century school building in Brașov, with a wrought‑iron fence and small groups of people along the street. The title and captions appear in Romanian, Hungarian and German. The reverse is a divided back with 'CARTA POSTALA' and a faint overprint of the Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐLAP', plus a printed stamp box.

Tinted vintage postcard showing the Baroque Brukenthal Palace on a square, with shops at street level and a sign reading APOTHEKE. Printed multilingual titles at the top identify the city (Sibiu/Hermannstadt/Nagyszeben) and the palace (Brukenthal) with reference to its picture gallery and library. The reverse has a divided back and a publisher credit.

Hand-tinted panoramic view of a town nestled among wooded hills. A large Gothic church with a tall tower dominates the center, and red-roofed houses spread across the valley. Printed title at top reads "Brașov Vedere generală — Látkép."

Colorized view of a spa complex with several connected white bath buildings and arched colonnades around salt lakes. Wooden piers and a pavilion sit over the water, with a large villa at left and a church spire on a hillside in the distance. Title printed in red at the top reads "Lacurile Horia, Cloșca și Crișan." The reverse states Romania and gives trilingual locality names, with the printer credited in Sibiu (Hermannstadt).

Colorized street view labeled "Hermannstadt – Fleischergasse," showing a cobbled lane lined with historic houses and pedestrians. In the distance rise two red‑domed towers of the Orthodox Cathedral. The reverse has a Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐ' postcard layout, a Romanian handwritten message, and two Serbian 15‑para stamps.

Vintage divided‑back postcard showing the Evangelical Lutheran church with a tall central spire and four smaller corner spires. Caption at top reads "Hermannstadt - Nagyszeben - Sibiu Evangelische Pfarrkirche." The reverse has a green Hungarian stamp and cancellation, printed publisher credit along the left edge, and a purple collector's stamp.

Color-tinted postcard showing a tall column with a statue of Árpád on a hill, surrounded by vegetation and mountains. Red caption at top reads the German and Hungarian city names and the monument name. The reverse has Hungarian text, a green 5 filler Hungarian stamp, and postmarks.

Sepia postcard showing the interior of a traditional Romanian peasant room filled with stacked textiles, plates on a high shelf, icons on the wall, wooden benches, a table with a woven cloth, and a cradle. The front bears the printed greeting "Salut din Sibiu!" and a bilingual caption identifying the scene. The reverse has bilingual postal headings, a Romanian orange 50 BANI stamp with cancellation, publisher and printer credits from Hermannstadt (Sibiu), and a collector's stamp.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large Gothic church with a clocktower dominating a square. Caption at the bottom reads 'Brașov - Brassó - Kronstadt'. The reverse side carries multilingual captions naming the Black Church and mentions Romania with address lines.

Sepia view of a European historic square with old gabled houses and a tall church spire with a clock. A tram kiosk or pavilion stands in the foreground with people in the square. Caption at the front bottom reads "Kleiner Ring — Kis-placz." The reverse has bilingual heading "Hermannstadt — Nagyszeben," Hungarian postcard text and a 10 filler Magyar Kir. Posta stamp dated 1917.

Real-photo postcard showing a studio portrait of six young male musicians in formal suits, holding violins and a double bass. Handwritten numbers mark each person on the front. The reverse has a handwritten list of names corresponding to the numbers and a note identifying them as a high school orchestra with the year 1916. There is also a museum stamp reading MUZEUL JUD. Bv. and an accession number.

A sheet with about a dozen vintage postcards showing people in traditional folk costumes, wedding couples and families posed indoors and outdoors. Most are black‑and‑white with one colorized card. The captions under the images are in German and refer to Transylvanian (Siebenbürgen) ethnic costumes, including Saxon bridal attire with tall cylindrical hats.

Vintage multi‑view chromolithographic postcard with German captions, titled "Gruss aus Hermannstadt." It shows the Großer Ring (Grand Square), the Evangelical Lutheran Cathedral, a theater with fortification towers, and a city panorama. The reverse reads "Correspondenz‑Karte" and bears a green Austro‑Hungarian stamp, addressed in German to Fräulein Marie Wegenstein in Temesvár (Piaristenstrasse).

Antique divided‑back postcard with a monochrome drawing of a fortified town surrounded by walls and mountains. A prominent city gate with a bridge leads into the town; small figures walk and ride horses in the foreground. Caption in German identifies it as Old Kronstadt and specifically the Klostergasse Gate before the great fire of 1689. The back bears Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐ‑LAP' and the publisher line.

Chromolithographed multi‑view postcard with floral decoration. Main view is a panoramic cityscape labeled "Kronstadt v. Schlossberg." Two inset scenes show "Schutzhütte am Schuler" and "Schützenhaus." The front has bilingual greetings in German and Hungarian. The reverse reads "Levelező‑lap." with address lines and bears a purple circular stamp of the Brukenthal Museum in Hermannstadt.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a bustling market square with many horse‑drawn carriages and townspeople. A large Gothic church dominates the background; mountains rise behind the townhouses. Red captions in German and Hungarian identify the place as the main market square of Kronstadt/Brassó.

Sepia-toned panoramic city view labeled "Brașov – Vedere generală," showing the historic center of Brașov with the rounded White Tower in the foreground and the wooded Tâmpa hill rising behind. Reverse side reads "România – Cartă Postală."

Divided-image postcard. The front shows two black‑and‑white views: at top, the main building of the Berlin University (today Humboldt University) with people, horse carriages and early automobiles on the street; at bottom, a panorama of Hermannstadt (Sibiu) in Siebenbürgen/Transylvania with church spires and snow‑covered mountains behind. The back bears German text announcing a 27 Feb. 1914 trip to Siebenbürgen organized by a Berlin group, with the word "Postkarte" and address lines.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a crowded market day in the central square of Agnita/Agnetheln, Transylvania. Horse‑drawn carts and townspeople fill the muddy piața in front of a row of two‑story houses. Signage notes Hotel "Comunal" and Hotel "Agnetha". The caption is bilingual Romanian–German, identifying the market square.

Sepia photograph of a large three-story military barracks building with a hipped roof and a small cupola, seen from a corner in an open square. Pedestrians and a horse-drawn cart pass by in the foreground. Caption at top lists the city name in Romanian, German, and Hungarian and identifies the building as the Mihai Viteazul Barracks. The reverse side is a divided back printed in Romanian with the publisher credit and a handwritten name.

Sepia-toned street view with ornate late‑19th/early‑20th century buildings along a wide boulevard at the foot of a wooded hill. Printed bilingual captions in red at the top read the German and Hungarian names of the city and the location. The reverse has the Hungarian word for postcard and a divided-back layout.

Sepia photo postcard showing a stately late‑19th‑century villa and a small round fountain with a statue in front. Printed bilingual caption at top reads in Hungarian and German, indicating a street view. The back is a Hungarian 'Levelező‑lap' with an address written to Marosvásárhely.

Vintage real-photo postcard showing a long, low hall-like building with a metal roof and several small roof vents. A line of young trees and a footpath run along the facade; a grassy field with a few people is in the foreground. A slender church spire is visible behind trees at the left, and low mountains/hills form the background. Overhead power lines cross the scene. The reverse has a divided back with penciled notes and a small serial number.

Vintage real-photo postcard: a studio portrait of a seated woman in rural/folk dress with a polka-dot headscarf, patterned skirt and lace-up boots, beside a small table with a vase of flowers. The reverse has a divided-back layout with dotted address lines and a stamp box, plus remnants of album paper and a small inventory sticker.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing an ornate villa and nearby spired buildings along a tree‑lined street. The caption on the front reads "Brașov" and "Livada poștei." The reverse is a divided‑back Romanian postcard labeled "România — Cartă Postală" with a local publisher's imprint from Brașov.

Album page holding a dozen vintage postcards that show people in traditional Transylvanian Saxon and Landler costumes: wedding couples, families, groups and interiors. Most cards are sepia; one is hand‑tinted. Captions printed under the images are in German (examples include phrases like "Sächsisches Brautpaar" and "Sächsische Frau mit Mädchen"). A round stamp on the mounting sheet reads Brukenthal Museum, suggesting collection ties to Sibiu.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of Brașov seen through trees, with the Gothic skyline including the Black Church and the clock‑tower of the Council House rising over the old town. The reverse has a handwritten Romanian message and address, printed "Vedere din Brașov", "Editura Meridiane", "C.P.C.S." and price, plus a blue 55 BANI R.P. ROMINA postage stamp (tractor motif) with Romanian postmarks.

Bilingual Austro‑Hungarian postcard with a monochrome panoramic view of an industrial complex labeled as the Czell factories at Dârste near Brașov, set against mountain scenery with chimneys and horse‑drawn carts. The reverse reads "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP" and bears BRASSO postmarks dated Sep. 20, 1902, a Hungarian stamp, and an address to Kronstadt (Brașov).

Two-sided vintage postcard. Front: a sepia portrait of a bearded man with the printed caption "DOMN AURELIU VICTOR MURESIAN (1884.)". Reverse: printed header in Romanian/German/Hungarian reading "ROMÂNIA – CARTA POSTALĂ – KORRESPONDENZ-KARTE — LEVELEZŐ-LAP", a green 5 FILLER stamp cancelled with a postmark reading "BRASSO", a purple handstamp "MUZEUL JUD. BV.", a short handwritten greeting in German, and an address to a recipient in "Kronstadt, Rossmarkt 2".

Collage-style, green-tinted postcard with three vignette views labeled in German: the city Concert House facade, St. Nicholas Church with a dome and spires, and the ornate Villa Schuller. Decorative floral border and a handwritten German note on the image. Publisher credit on the left margin. The reverse is a Hungarian-address format 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP' with a Magyar Kir. Posta 4-filler stamp and a Brassó postmark, addressed to Kronstadt.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a snowy street in Agnita (Transylvania) with the Casa Comunală (Town Hall) building and adjoining shops. People and an ox-drawn cart are in the street. Caption is bilingual Romanian–German. The reverse is a Romanian divided back printed with "România – Cartă Postală" and credits to a local photographer.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large group of workers, including men, women and children, posing in front of an industrial courtyard with long plastered buildings, a picket fence and an external stair. Caption at the bottom reads "Avrig – Fabrica de Sticlărie." The reverse is a divided back with "România – Cartă Postală," address lines, and the publisher credit "Editura Gh. Maxim, Avrig," plus an archival stamp and pencil notes.

Tinted/hand-colored street view of a grand corner hotel with a mansard roof and arched ground-floor windows. The entrance canopy reads "HOTEL EUROPA," with people gathered outside and an early automobile parked at the curb. A tree-lined boulevard and benches are in the foreground; a neighboring building bears the word "VOLKSBAD." Printed captions identify the scene as in Sibiu and also give German and Hungarian city names.

Colorized street scene showing a narrow, gently curving lane lined with two‑story houses with red tile roofs. People stroll along the street and shopfronts are visible. The caption on the image reads "Hermannstadt – Burgergasse." The reverse side is printed with "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and credits the publisher "Chromophot. v. Jos. Drotleff, Hermannstadt," with a purple ownership stamp.

Multi-view postcard showing interiors and exterior of a spa/sanatorium complex called Sanatorium-Volksbad in the Stadtpark. Images include the main facade, dining hall, reading room, guest rooms, and therapeutic bathing facilities such as an electric tub. The text is in German with a bilingual city name (Hermannstadt–Nagyszeben), and the postcard back bears the Hungarian heading for postcard.

Vintage postcard showing a crowd gathered in front of a railway-station building with shuttered windows. The façade bears station name boards and signage. Printed captions at the top read in Romanian and Hungarian. The reverse is a divided back labeled România / Cartă Postală with address lines and a numeric hand-stamp.

Vintage divided‑back postcard with five b/w views: several suburban villas and a turreted public building around a park, plus a long barracks‑like complex labeled as the Imperial and Royal Infantry Cadet School. Caption in Hungarian sends greetings from the Erlenpark villa colony of Nagyszeben.

Colorized vintage street view captioned "Hermannstadt – Harteneckgasse (Stadttheater)". A neoclassical theater building with a balcony and colonnaded porch stands on the left; along the street to the right are medieval city-wall towers with red conical roofs. A few pedestrians are visible; the card shows age spots and a mailed back.

Colorized panoramic postcard showing Brașov seen from the hill, with Parcul Ferdinand and its promenade fountain in the foreground. Caption appears in Romanian and Hungarian. The reverse has Romanian postage stamps and a Brașov postmark, addressed to Făgăraș.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a church with multiple spires and a clock tower at the foot of a mountain, with tiled-roof houses, a gate, and a couple of figures and a cart in the foreground. Caption at the bottom reads "Brașov  Biserica Sft. Nicolae." The reverse is a standard divided back with printed "România" and "Cartă Postală" with address lines.

Hand‑colored panoramic postcard showing a general view of Brașov with the red‑roofed old town in the foreground and the forested Tâmpa Mountain rising behind. Tree‑lined avenues and parks are visible, with scattered churches and civic buildings. The front bears the printed Romanian title "Brașov – Vedere generală." The reverse has Romanian postage stamps and a Brașov postmark, with an address written in Romanian.

Sepia postcard showing a street‑promenade scene in Brașov: a broad avenue with trees and benches on the left, cafés and ornate buildings with awnings on the right, and a church with a tall slender spire in the background. The reverse has a Romanian layout, a Social Assistance postage stamp, several 1927 postmarks, and a handwritten message addressed to Galați.

Hand‑tinted view of a spa complex with white secession/neo‑Romanian buildings, arched colonnades and red‑tile roofs set around landscaped gardens. A village with a church steeple and low hills appears in the background; a pergola and paths are in the foreground.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a fortified city gate and adjoining tower with crenellations and a steep roof. A walled enclosure and arched entrance are visible, with people and a horse-drawn cart in front. Caption in German identifies the scene as the Schmiedgässer Gate in Mediasch. The reverse reads "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and bears a vertical publisher credit and a purple stamped number.

Vintage divided card showing a large open square with horse-drawn carts, a long public building and a distant church spire. The image is captioned in German "Der Hermannsplatz" with a greeting "Gruss aus Hermannstadt." Publisher credit reads "Jos. Drotleff Hermannstadt." The address side bears the Hungarian heading "Levelező-Lap" and is addressed to Herrn Prof. Julius Kootz in Mühlbach (Szász-Sebes), with a Hungarian stamp and a Dec. 31, 1898 postmark.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a long line of villagers in traditional dress in front of a fortified church with a tall square tower. The front carries bilingual greetings in Romanian and German. The reverse reads "România — Cartă Postală," with address lines, a German-language publisher credit from Agnita/Agnetheln, and a purple archival stamp.

Sepia-toned portrait postcard showing a bearded man in 19th‑century Central/Transylvanian attire with a frogged jacket and chain fob. The reverse has bilingual postcard markings and a purple museum stamp.

Colorized panoramic view over a historic European city nestled at the foot of forested mountains. In the center stands a large Gothic church with a steep roof (the Black Church) and nearby a clock/bell tower rising over the main square; 19th–early 20th century buildings line a curving street. The top caption reads "Brassó - Kronstadt - Brașov." The reverse is a divided back with printer marks and the date 1913/14.

Vintage multi‑view postcard with three grayscale images framed decoratively: left shows a cobbled path and canal with arches labeled 'Hinter der Graft'; center shows a hillside with two defensive towers labeled 'Schwarzer und weisser Thurm'; right shows a spired city gate labeled 'Katharinenthor'. The printer credit appears at the bottom. The reverse bears Hungarian 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP.' with address lines and a stamp box.

Vintage green-tinted postcard view of an elegant late‑19th/early‑20th‑century villa with ornate façades in a tree‑lined area, with a spired building in the background. The caption on the front reads "Brașov" and "Livada poștei." The reverse is a Romanian divided back printed "România — Cartă Postală," with a long handwritten Romanian message, Brașov postal cancellations, and an address to a painter/professor. Publisher imprint from a Brașov bookshop on Strada Hirscher is visible.

Real-photo postcard showing a large outdoor celebration with women in Romanian folk costumes forming a circle in a cobbled square, watched by a crowd. A banner reading in Romanian is visible in the background and a church spire rises at right. The reverse has a Romanian handwritten note referencing Brașov and the year 1927.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a street of ornate villas and townhouses with eclectic architecture. Bilingual caption at front left reads 'Brassó / Kronstadt' and at bottom right 'Fellegvár sor a Beer villával / Schlossberg-Zeile mit Villa Beer'. The reverse has 'Levelezö-lap', a Hungarian 10 fillér stamp, Brasso postmarks dated July 1907, a German handwritten message, and an address to Bucharest.

Colorized view of a European town square labeled in three languages as King Ferdinand Square. In the center-right stands a long Baroque Roman Catholic church with an onion-domed bell tower; a lamppost rises in the square and early automobiles and horse-drawn carts are visible. On the left is an ornate Art Nouveau corner building. A tree with posters frames the foreground. The reverse names the city in Romanian, German, and Hungarian and carries Romanian postal instructions and the publisher/date.

Antique blue‑tinted postcard showing a large two‑storey academic building with a central arched entrance and Gothic‑style windows. People stand in the garden in front. Printed greeting at upper right reads in German, and a caption below identifies the building as the Evangelical regional church seminary. Publisher and printer credits run vertically at left. The reverse bears the Hungarian word for postcard, dotted address lines, and a purple round stamp of the Brukenthal Museum in Hermannstadt (Sibiu).

Colorized view of a rural spa resort set on grassy hills with paths, benches, a small wooden bridge and several pavilion-style buildings, with forested hills in the background. The front caption is trilingual. The reverse reads "România – Cartă Postală," indicating a Romanian postcard back.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a huge crowd gathered around the equestrian Matthias Corvinus Monument in a central square, with the Gothic façade of St. Michael's Church to the left and a domed corner building to the right. Flags and people are on the monument, suggesting a public celebration. The reverse has address lines and handwritten notes dated 1918.

Sepia postcard view over a tree-lined meadow and villas at the foot of wooded hills. The printed caption reads "Kronstadt. Postwiese — Schlossberg." In the distance is the hill with the citadel area. The reverse is a Hungarian 'Levelezö-Lap' with a 5 fillér stamp, Brassó (Brașov) postmark dated 1913, and a handwritten message and address.

Colorized panoramic view of a historic European town nestled at the base of a forested mountain. The red‑roofed old town spreads across the foreground with a tree‑lined square and rail/road in front. A summit pavilion or lookout sits atop the mountain. Tri‑lingual caption appears along the lower margin.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large Neo-Byzantine Orthodox cathedral with a central dome and two tall striped towers, seen from an elevated street view. A Romanian caption is printed under the image, and the publisher's credit appears at the bottom. The back has Hungarian preprinted postcard text.

Color-tinted view of a Central/Eastern European city with a tall slate spire and clock tower rising above a tree-lined boulevard and park, hills in the background. The reverse is printed in Romanian, shows an imprinted stamp of R.P. ROMINA (40 bani), and the caption reads "Vedere din Orașul Stalin".

Sepia postcard showing a richly decorated exhibition pavilion labeled "Kunsthalle," with wreaths and garlands on a symmetrical wooden hall. Foreground has urns and a small landscaped area. Printed German caption at the bottom references the Hermannstadt trade exhibition; printer credited. The reverse bears Hungarian text for postcard format.
