Monochrome postcard showing a large decorative fountain in a tree‑lined city park with benches and visitors. Red printed captions identify the place in German, Hungarian and Romanian. The reverse is a Hungarian postcard form with a green Magyar Kir. Posta 5 fillér stamp and Brassó postmark.

Colorized view of a Catholic high school complex labeled in German and Hungarian, with a church beside it and a wooded park in the foreground. A steep green hill with a small structure on its summit rises behind the town. Handwritten message runs along the right edge. The reverse is a Hungarian postcard back with green 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP', Hungarian stamp and postmarks.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a one‑story school building with a gabled entrance and balcony, flowerbeds in front, and a sign above the door. Printed Romanian captions at the top read "Școala Normală de învățători" and "Făgăraș." The reverse side says "România – Carta Postală" with address lines and the imprint "Editura I. Hațegan, Făgăraș."

Colorized panorama postcard showing the city of Brașov nestled at the foot of a forested mountain (Tâmpa). Tiled-roof houses and a tall church spire rise among trees. The front caption reads in Romanian, and the reverse is a divided back printed with 'România Cartà Postală' and the publisher 'Editura Librăria Cooperativă, Brașov', plus a purple archive stamp and a red inventory number.

Sepia panoramic view taken from a hillside looking over a Transylvanian town with rows of low tiled-roof houses, a church with a tower in the right mid‑ground, and a small hilltop citadel visible in the distance; mountains fade on the horizon. The back carries trilingual city names and a German-language publisher line.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a zeppelin flying above the rooftops of a Central/Eastern European city; a flock of birds crosses the sky. The reverse has German handwriting dated 16.10.1929 and multiple stamps, including the Brukenthal Museum in Hermannstadt and the studio mark of a court photographer. Agfa Photo postcard stock.

Colorized street-view postcard showing a bustling old European street labeled in Hungarian and German as Mészáros-utca — Fleischergasse (Butchers' Street). People walk along the sidewalks and a horse-drawn cart stands at left. A church tower with a green spire rises at the end of the street. The reverse is a divided back with bilingual heading and Hungarian publisher imprint dated 1917.

Colorized panoramic view over a town nestled beneath forested mountains, showing red-tiled roofs, courtyards, and several church steeples. Romanian caption at the bottom reads "Brașov – Vedere generală."

Sepia photographic postcard showing a busy market in a small historic square surrounded by old houses; in the background rises a tall Gothic church tower with a clock. Printed captions read "Gruss aus Hermannstadt" and "Kleiner Ring." The reverse bears the Hungarian heading "Levelező-lap" and is addressed in German to a recipient in Graz.

Sepia ethnographic postcard showing three women in richly embroidered Transylvanian Saxon folk dress inside a rustic interior with shelves of pottery. A bilingual German–Hungarian caption appears beneath the image.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a narrow cobblestone lane with medieval brick arches and old houses. Several pedestrians walk beneath the arches. The back side carries a multilingual caption identifying the street in Sibiu and Romanian postal instructions, along with a 1933 publisher credit and a collector's stamp.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a neoclassical building with columns and a balcony, identified in the caption as the Natural History Museum. People stand near the entrance behind a fence; trees line the street. Printed German caption and publisher credit appear on the front, with handwritten greetings. The back bears Hungarian postal text and an address.

Hand‑tinted studio postcard showing a smiling young woman wearing a hat made from newspapers with the words "Neueste Nachrichten" visible, and a sheet of paper pinned to her chest. She holds a small stick with a bow. The reverse has a green Hungarian stamp and a circular postmark.

Vintage green-tinted street-and-square view showing arcaded houses with shop awnings, pedestrians in early 20th‑century dress, gas lamps, and a domed church tower at the edge of a large cobbled square backed by a wooded hill. Printed caption at top reads "Brassó — Kronstadt / Búzasor — Kornzeile." The reverse is a Hungarian "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP" with a BRASSÓ postmark and a handwritten message and address to Budapest.

Colorized panoramic view of a town at the foot of a forested mountain, dominated by a large Gothic church with a square clock tower and red roof. The caption 'Brassó.' appears at top left. The reverse is a divided-back postcard with Hungarian publisher credit and a stamp box.

Monochrome postcard showing the interior of a sanatorium reading room: Art Nouveau–style furniture with a round central table and wooden chairs, high-backed armchairs, patterned rugs, a bookshelf with books on the right, hanging lamps, and a curtained window centered on the far wall. The reverse bears printed captions and publisher information.

Vintage postcard showing an outdoor restaurant garden with round tables covered in white cloths under leafy trees. Waitresses in aprons and several guests pose for the camera; a man who appears to be the proprietor stands at right. The reverse has printed German and Hungarian text, including a caption naming the venue and street, the word for postcard in Hungarian, a vertical credit line, a Vienna address written in pencil, and a purple collector's stamp.

Colorized view of a central square in Brașov showing the historic city hall with a tall clock tower and red roofs. People and an early streetcar are visible on the square. Captions in Romanian and German identify the city and the building. The reverse side reads "România – Cartă Postală" and gives the publisher from Kronstadt (Brașov).

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large mountain lodge (Cabana Poiana) with dormer windows and a stone ground floor, set against dense conifer forest and hills. The back bears a Romanian People's Republic 38‑bani stamp and printed titling mentioning Poiana Stalin (the communist‑era name of Poiana Brașov).

Vintage monochrome street-view postcard captioned "Hermannstadt – Mühlgasse," showing a cobblestoned street lined with 19th‑century townhouses and a few pedestrians. The reverse reads "LEVELEZŐ-LAP," bears a green 5 fillér "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA" stamp with a circular postmark of NAGYSZEBEN dated 1908, and contains a German handwritten message addressed to a Fraulein.

Sepia postcard view of a tree-lined promenade/park with two ornate civic buildings facing each other, horse-drawn carriages on unpaved streets, and a wooded hill in the background. Caption on the front reads "Kronstadt — Brassó."

Sepia Easter greeting card showing a walking hare carrying a large egg tied with a ribbon and using a walking stick. Handwritten holiday greeting at the bottom. The reverse has a multilingual "Postkarte" back, a Swedish 5 öre green stamp, Göteborg postmark, and is addressed to a family in Göteborg.

Color postcard with a romantic illustration of a young couple kissing in a wooded setting; a hen and an egg appear in the foreground. Caption in Swedish at the bottom reads "En puss i påsk." The reverse shows a multilingual 'Postkarte — Carte postale' layout with a green Swedish 5 öre stamp, Gothenburg museum archive stamp, and a handwritten address to Soffia Thorn on 4th Long Street.

Color postcard showing a tall, pink stone obelisk-like monument on a stepped base set in a landscaped park with flowers in the foreground and trees and low buildings in the background under a blue sky. The reverse has Romanian text identifying the site and publisher details.

A multiview Romanian postcard titled ANINA, showing chalet-style cabins, a panoramic view of a mountain town, a villa with arcaded terrace, the building signed Cinema MINERUL, and a forested lake with boats. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian postage stamp, and an address to Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a neoclassical museum building with a columned portico and arched windows, seen through trees and a landscaped garden with flowers and potted palms. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian 40-bani stamp, and postmarks dated 1970.

Black‑and‑white street view showing a domed Roman‑Catholic church with a grand neoclassical portico and statues, and a tall obelisk with a radiating sun symbol in a square along a busy boulevard with pedestrians and a storefront sign reading "Magazin Uni…". Caption at top reads "ARAD – Pe b-dul Republicii".

Color view of a grand neo‑classical building with a pediment labeled "PALATUL CULTURAL," flanked by turrets and set beside a river with a bridge in the background. The reverse shows Romanian handwriting, a Romanian 40‑bani stamp, a Bucharest cancellation dated 28.III.72, and the printed caption identifying the site.

Color postcard showing the grand neoclassical Cultural Palace (Palatul Cultural) in Arad with its central tower, columned portico, and red-tiled wings, set beside a river and a small bridge amid greenery. The reverse has Romanian text and a printed Romanian stamp.

Color postcard showing a panoramic cityscape of Arad, Romania, with late‑19th/early‑20th‑century buildings along a broad boulevard and a distinctive onion‑domed corner turret in the foreground. The reverse bears a Romanian airmail stamp with an airplane, circular ARAD postmarks dated in the early 1960s, printed headings, and handwritten Romanian message and address.

Color postcard showing a formal city park with striped flowerbeds, stone balustrade and urns, and in the background a cream-colored administrative building with a clock tower. The reverse is printed in Romanian and names Arad with a note that it is a view from the park.

Color photograph of a large civic square with historic buildings. On the right is a grand neoclassical/eclectic building with an arched loggia and a tall clock tower; in front a wide boulevard with marked lanes, a blurred car and a tram at far left. The reverse side has Romanian address fields and publisher info.

Multiview color postcard showing scenes from Arad, Romania: at left the State Theatre (Teatrul de Stat) illuminated at night with the city coat of arms above; at top right a modernist high‑rise labeled Hotel Astoria; at bottom right an outdoor public pool/strand with curved bridges and bathers.

Multi-view color postcard showing four scenes from Arad County, Romania: a general view of the town of Sebiș with flowerbeds and low historic houses; the rustic interior of the Dezna Inn with carved wooden chairs and a brick fireplace; the exterior of chalets by the water at Dezna; and people rowing boats on a tree-lined lake at Moneasa.

Color postcard showing a landscaped city park with patterned flowerbeds, tree-lined paths and people strolling; historic buildings with towers and a modern mid‑century block appear in the background. Reverse side has Romanian printed caption, publisher credit, two Romanian stamps, a 1975 postmark and a German handwritten message addressed to a camping site in Mamaia, Constanța.

Color postcard showing a modernist spa hotel with multiple floors and continuous balconies, labeled as Hotel Parc in Buziaș. Several 1970s–1980s Eastern‑bloc cars line the driveway. The reverse has Romanian handwritten text, Romanian address form fields, a blue stamp reading ARTA POPULARĂ 2L POSTA ROMÂNĂ, and a circular BUCUREȘTI postmark dated 1988.

Color postcard showing a modernist spa and hotel complex bordered by large trees and a landscaped boulevard with flowerbeds. Reverse side is a Romanian Poșta Română template with a 2 LEI stamp carrying the socialist emblem, Bucharest postmarks dated 30.08.82, and a handwritten Romanian message; the printed caption states BUZIAȘ: Vedere – Vue.

Color postcard showing a landscaped park with a central fountain, flower beds, large urn‑shaped topiary planters, and tall trees on a sunny day. The reverse side has Romanian text and a Romanian stamp, with the printed caption indicating Buziaș and a park view.

Color view of a leafy public park with benches, ornamental hedges and lamp posts. In the foreground is a sculpted fountain with fish/dolphin heads at the base and a wide mushroom‑shaped bowl with thin water jets. Vintage look typical of mid-20th‑century Eastern European postcards.

Color postcard showing a wide street in a small Romanian town with socialist‑era apartment blocks and a modern department store on the corner. The store carries a vertical sign reading "SUPER" and the script word "magazin." A blue Dacia car is parked at the curb; concrete flower planters line the sidewalk. The back is printed in Romanian with areas for address and sender, a gold "POSTA ROMANA" stamp, and a cancellation from Buziaș. Caption at bottom left reads "BUZIAȘ. Magazinul universal."

Color postcard showing a busy outdoor thermal swimming pool with bathers and a diver in mid‑air, surrounded by leafy trees and wooden changing cabins. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian socialist-era 40 bani stamp, a circular postmark, and the printed caption naming Buziaș and the thermal pool.

Color postcard showing a lush green park with flowerbeds, a central fountain jet, and a small octagonal pavilion/gazebo amid tall trees. The reverse has Romanian text, a Romanian stamp and postmarks, and a printed caption identifying the view.

Color postcard showing a formal garden and pedestrian square bordered by ornate late‑19th/early‑20th‑century buildings. The most prominent building has a steep roof with small corner turrets and a tall spire; people stroll along paths and flowerbeds under a clear sky. The reverse side has Romanian text, stamp and postmark.

Black‑and‑white view of a tree‑lined path in a park, with tall poplars casting shade. A few people walk along the alley; a small pavilion/house is visible at right. The reverse side has Romanian printed headings and handwritten message, with postal cancels from Caransebeș and Oradea and a red "40" postage marking.

Multiview Romanian postcard titled "caraș severin". It shows four scenes: a meadow and forest in the Cernei Mountains; a large modernist administrative building in Reșița; the spa resort of Băile Herculane with Hotel "Hercule"; and a panoramic view over Reșița's Bârzava meadow with apartment blocks. Bordea; code 3783/82; price 3,50 lei.

Color postcard showing a rustic hilltop complex with steep wooden shingle roofs and a central tower-like building, surrounded by small A‑frame cabins on a grassy slope with trees and a blue sky. The reverse contains Romanian mailing fields and publisher details.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view of a heavy‑industry steelworks with multiple smokestacks, blast furnaces and a gas holder in the foreground, and a town nestled among low mountains in the background. The reverse side identifies it as a panoramic view of Reșița and bears Romanian handwriting, stamps, and 1963 postal cancellations.

Multi-view color postcard with six framed photos from the city of Reșița: a modern school building, Lake Secu with forested hills and the "Constructorul" hotel, a wide plaza/steps area, the stalactite interior of Comarnic Cave, a landscaped park in front of the administrative palace and the "Semenic" hotel, and a city square with a tall modern building. The word RESITA appears vertically in red on the front. The back shows Romanian postal layout with 'POSTA ROMANA', 'CARTE POSTALA', an imprinted 40 BANI stamp with the socialist coat of arms, address lines, and a bilingual Romanian–French caption list describing the views.

Color postcard of a lakeside lodge with red-tiled roofs on a grassy hill by a calm lake, steps leading to a small pier with two boats, and wooded hills under a blue sky. The reverse has Romanian text, a 40 B POSTA ROMANA stamp (Densuș), and circular postal cancels reading LUGOJ TRANZIT dated 30.5.72.

Color postcard showing a lakeside hotel with red roofs on a grassy hillside by a calm lake. The reverse side has Romanian text, publisher line, price, and a Romanian stamp reading POSTA ROMANA with a 40 B value and the word DENSUS. Address lines and the heading CARTE POȘTALĂ are printed.

Color view of a modernist open‑air cinema with curved brick and stone walls, a colonnaded canopy, broad terraced steps, mid‑century lampposts, planters, and flowerbeds. Three people are walking up the main stairway under a bright blue sky.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing people on a seaside promenade looking toward the art‑nouveau casino building on a rocky pier by the Black Sea. The reverse is printed in Romanian with spaces for address, bears a green stamp fragment, a circular postmark, and handwritten message and address.

Color postcard showing a low, stone-built complex with tiled roofs by the seaside, viewed over a stone wall with trees and lampposts; the Black Sea fills the background. The reverse reads CARTE POȘTALĂ with Romanian publisher details and identifies the site as the Archaeology Museum in Mangalia.

Color postcard showing a tall stone obelisk with reliefs at its base, rising above red‑tiled roofs and green hills in the background. In the foreground is a close-up of a sculptural group. The view looks toward the Horea, Cloșca și Crișan Obelisk in Alba Iulia.

Color postcard showing a formal park with long striped flowerbeds, stone balustrade and an urn planter in the foreground. In the background stands a historic civic building with a tall clock tower, consistent with Arad City Hall. Reverse side has Romanian postcard layout printed in blue.

Color postcard showing a large European square with tram tracks, cars and buses from the 1960s. The square is lined with Secession/Art Nouveau palaces; a wedge‑shaped, richly decorated pink building dominates the corner. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, Romanian postage (40 Bani) and Bucharest postmarks from 1967.

Colorized historic street scene showing a grand neorenaissance theater building on a central square with an early electric tram and horse-drawn carriages. The image is framed by an orange border. The reverse has Romanian and German text describing Timișoara's Victory Square/Opera Square and the theater palace.

Vintage postcard showing a black‑and‑white view of the State Theater building in Constanța, Romania. The reverse bears bilingual printed captions (Romanian and Russian), a green 38‑bani Romanian People's Republic stamp with agricultural motif, Bucharest cancellation dated April 1955, a handwritten short greeting, and an address in Bucharest.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a hilltop fortress with towers and walls, identified by the caption as Castelul Bran. The foreground has trees and grazing sheep. The reverse has Romanian text, a purple airmail stamp, a Bucharest postmark, and address lines.

Color postcard showing a broad river winding through a steep, forested mountain gorge with rocky slopes (summer scene). People are relaxing on the grassy riverbank; a wooden telephone pole and dense trees line the left. The reverse bears Romanian text and an imprinted stamp.

Color view of a hilltop medieval castle with red tile roofs and a central tower, surrounded by dense forest and framed by pine branches. The reverse side is printed in Romanian with "CARTE POSTALA" and fields for address, plus a printed stamp and notes indicating Bran Museum in Brașov County.

Colorized vintage postcard with scalloped edges showing a hilltop castle with red-tiled towers and walls (Bran Castle) above a wooded slope and a stream in the foreground; small figures and a car are visible near houses below. The back has Romanian-language printing indicating the location and publisher.

Vintage multi-view black-and-white postcard titled "Oradea – Băile Felix," showing the Băile Felix spa resort near Oradea: crowded outdoor thermal pools, timbered spa buildings with steep roofs, landscaped gardens, and a small footbridge over water. The reverse has a handwritten Romanian message dated July 13, 1968, a Romanian 40 bani postage stamp (Aniversari Culturale – Aron Pumnul), postal cancellations, and an address.

Tourist postcard showing the interior of a limestone cave with stalactites and stalagmites, lit by artificial lights. Visitors walk on a railing path inside the cavern. The back has Romanian address fields and notes indicating it depicts Peștera Urșilor near Chișcău, Bihor, with an ONT Carpați imprint and the code 1265/84.

Multiview color postcard of the Romanian spa resort area Oradea–Băile Felix. It shows an outdoor thermal pool with an A‑frame pavilion, a tall modernist hotel, and landscaped parks with paths, flower beds and water‑lily ponds. A yellow title band on the front reads "Oradea‑Băile Felix." The reverse is in Romanian with address fields, publisher credits, a price in lei, and a stamp box numbered 16924.

Multi-view color postcard showing the Băile Felix spa resort: a hotel in a leafy park, the famous lotus lake with pink water lilies, landscaped gardens, and the modernist A‑frame Apollo swimming complex crowded with bathers. The back has Romanian handwriting, a 40 bani Poșta Română stamp, and postmarks from BAILE FELIX and BUCURESTI.

Color postcard showing a wooden spa pavilion with steep shingled roofs and small dormers, approached by a double staircase. Tall poplar trees stand behind it; a lamppost and garden beds appear in front. The image depicts a building in the Băile Felix spa complex.

A multiview color postcard featuring landmarks of Sibiu: central image of a medieval defensive tower with a steep conical roof and machicolations, flanked by scenes of ornate historic buildings, an old-town street, parked vintage cars, and a park lake with a rowboat. The front has a red band labeled "SIBIU." The reverse shows a standard Romanian layout with price and publisher marks.

Multiview color postcard showing the Romanian spa resort Băile Felix near Oradea: modernist hotels, thermal outdoor pools crowded with bathers, and a lotus pond. The front title reads "ORADEA – BAILE FELIX." The reverse has a handwritten Romanian message dated 3 Aug. 1978, a 40 B "POSTA ROMANA" stamp (DENSUS) and a Bucharest circular postmark dated 05.08.78. Addressed to a family in București. Publisher imprint Editura Meridiane with price 1,50 lei and photo credits.

Color postcard showing a modernist hotel building set among trees with a large rooftop sign reading 'HOTEL NUFĂRUL'. The reverse side is printed 'CARTE POȘTALĂ', bears a green 'POȘTA ROMÂNĂ 40 BANI' stamp with a BĂILE FELIX postmark dated 29.VII.72, includes printed details 'BĂILE FELIX – Hotel "Nufărul"', price 'Lei 1,90', and a handwritten Romanian message and address to București.

Color postcard showing a modernist hotel with three floors of recessed balconies and an outdoor terrace with umbrellas. Large rooftop signage reads "HOTEL" and, in cursive, "Nufarul." The reverse has Romanian printed fields ("CARTE POSTALA") and a handwritten message dated "Felix 21 nov. 1973," plus a Romanian stamp (POSTA ROMANA 40 BANI) and an address to Focșani.

Color photo of a modernist hotel complex with a sign reading 'Felix' on the facade and 'restaurant' on the lower building. A vintage car with plate 1-BH-4273 is parked in front, with terrace seating and landscaped greenery. The reverse has Romanian text, a Poșta Română stamp and address fields.

Multi-view color postcard bordered in brown showing a busy spa resort with crowded outdoor thermal pools and conical shingle-roofed pavilions, an indoor/outdoor bath complex, a modernist hotel building, and a general aerial view of the resort grounds. A pink lotus flower is inset at center, a symbol of the thermal lakes. The reverse is a Romanian postcard with postage and handwritten Romanian message.

Color postcard showing a large outdoor thermal pool complex crowded with bathers, terraced sunbathing areas and a modern multi‑story hotel surrounded by forest. The back has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp (POSTA ROMANA), and postal cancellations from Băile Felix and București dated June 1982. Printed caption credits the image to the Băile Felix spa near Oradea.

Color postcard showing a very crowded outdoor thermal pool with children and adults swimming and playing around a white concrete slide with round holes. The scene is surrounded by tall poplars and willows, suggesting a spa park. The reverse side has Romanian handwriting, Romanian printed postal text, a printed stamp of Poșta Română, and circular postmarks reading BĂILE FELIX.

Color postcard showing a crowded outdoor swimming pool surrounded by trees at the Băile 1 Mai resort near Oradea. The reverse has a Romanian handwritten message, a Romanian 40 bani stamp, a BĂILE 1 MAI postmark dated 1967, and a multilingual printed caption describing the swimming pool.

Vintage Romanian postcard. Front: a black‑and‑white view of a castellated mansion with towers, seen from a park with a large circular fountain, benches and trees; people stroll and sit around the fountain. Back: Romanian 40 BANI blue stamp (POSTA ROMANA) with cancellation marks reading BALC BIHOR, handwritten Romanian message and address. Printed caption at the bottom mentions a sanatorium.
Color photograph of several llamas standing in a fenced paddock, likely inside a zoo. The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard in Romanian, titling the image and giving the animal's name.

Color postcard showing a large yellow Baroque palace with a red-tiled roof and a domed central pavilion, seen across an ornate iron balustrade. Two seated lion statues on pedestals flank the approach. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp, and a Bucharest postmark.

Color photo postcard showing the central square of Oradea, Romania: a wide square with an orange tram, the yellow Biserica cu Lună (Moon Church) with its dark spire, the Oradea City Hall clock tower in the distance, and ornate historic palaces around the square. Color postcard showing the Cozia Monastery church with an arcaded porch and domed roof topped with crosses, set in a rose garden within a monastic courtyard against forested hills. The reverse has a multilingual caption identifying the site and a handwritten date, with a divided back for address.

Multiview color postcard showing the exterior terrace and interior dining rooms of mid‑century restaurants. The back is a Romanian divided back labeled CARTE POȘTALĂ with a printed price and caption listing restaurants in Tulcea County.

Color postcard showing an aerial view of Tulcea on the Danube River: the waterfront with passenger boats, the modernist Hotel Delta, communist-era apartment blocks around a central square, streets and greenery along the quay. The reverse has Romanian text, a blue 1 leu Poșta Română stamp (Curtea de Argeș), a Tulcea postmark dated 1981, and is addressed to a county committee in Craiova.

Color postcard showing the facade of a mid‑century modern hotel with stacked balconies, a landscaped walkway and flowerbeds leading to the entrance, a few 1970s cars parked, and people walking in front. The back is in Romanian and includes a printed stamp with the socialist coat of arms.

Color postcard showing a modernist cultural building with deep eaves and geometric window balustrades. A low pedestrian bridge with flowerbeds crosses a small canal in the foreground; a 1970s Eastern European car passes on the road. Tree-covered hills rise behind the building. The reverse has Romanian text, a Romanian stamp, and Baia Mare postmarks.

Color postcard showing a socialist‑era central square with a circular fountain set in a landscaped lawn. Behind it are a mid‑rise hotel with a rooftop sign reading "Hotel Moldova" and rows of apartment blocks. Many pedestrians are visible. The reverse side is a Romanian postcard template with a 40‑bani Poșta Română stamp and postmarks dated 10.6.69, along with printed caption "BACĂU – Vedere."

Color postcard showing an autumnal park scene with tall trees, a calm pond and arched pedestrian bridges. Several people stand on the main bridge, whose reflection forms a circle on the water; a wooden fence lines the path in the foreground. The reverse side bears Romanian text identifying Botoșani and the publisher, with a stamp box and address lines.

Color postcard showing a modern alpine-style hotel building surrounded by dense coniferous forest and visitors in front; the reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp and Bucharest postmark. Printed caption identifies the scene as Hotelul "Durău" in the Durău mountain resort, Neamț County, Romania.

Front shows an ornate early‑20th‑century cultural building with a large arched window, green doors, and decorative reliefs; a bust statue stands on a pedestal in the square before it. Black‑and‑white view of a round fountain with a small sculptural group (putto with fish) in a tree‑lined public park. Paths and benches appear in the background with a few pedestrians. The reverse side is printed in Romanian and has a handwritten message, address, postmarks, and a Romanian stamp.

Black‑and‑white street view with people walking along a wide avenue in Galați. On the right is a long arcaded building with a sign reading "Restaurantul". Trees line the sidewalk and mid‑century streetlights are visible. The back bears Romanian text and a purple airmail stamp of the Romanian People's Republic with circular postmarks.

A multiview color postcard with a blue border and a yellow ribbon reading "Salutări din Galați." It shows modernist civic buildings, a park with a fountain, a boulevard lined with apartment blocks, and another red‑brick institutional building. The reverse has Romanian text, a 40 Bani 'Posta Română' stamp with the socialist coat of arms, and handwritten message and address.

Color postcard showing a large saucer-shaped fountain in a leafy park with red flowerbeds and a child in a stroller in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian text, a vertical "EDITURA MERIDIANE" imprint, caption lines naming Galați and "View of the park" in multiple languages, price in lei, and a Romanian 40 BANI stamp reading "POSTA ROMANA" with a socialist coat of arms and postmark.

Color postcard showing a bronze statue of a man (Costache Negri) on a stone pedestal in a manicured park with flowerbeds and trees. People walk along paths around the monument. Color postcard showing the river passenger terminal in Galați on the Danube. A long white building with a small tower bears the sign NAVROM, with moored boats and a Romanian flag in the foreground. Verso has Romanian handwriting, a blue 2 lei Poșta Română stamp (Arte Populară), and a București postmark.
