The postcard front shows a busy street lined with historic multi‑story buildings in a European city. The central focus is an ornate late‑19th‑century facade with balconies and decorative stonework; on its pediment is the inscription "NÁDOR SZÁLLÓ". Pedestrians, cars, and delivery trucks move along the street, and shop signs are visible at street level. Hills rise in the background behind the buildings. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with printed address lines and information about Hotel Nádor in Pécs, Hungary.

A color aerial view over a mixed urban landscape: in the foreground are older, low-rise houses with red-tiled roofs and tree-lined streets, while behind them stand mid‑ and high‑rise apartment blocks typical of socialist-era architecture. In the distant background an industrial area with tall chimneys and factory buildings is visible across open fields. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with space for a stamp and address, printed captions, and credits.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square with a cobblestone street and stone balustrade in the foreground. On the left stands an equestrian statue on a high pedestal. Behind it are historic multi‑story buildings with ornate facades and tiled roofs, and a tram with carriages runs through the busy square filled with pedestrians. Tree branches frame the top of the image. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with Hungarian text printed in the upper left and along the vertical center.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an elevated view of a large central square with a monumental column in the foreground and a domed church/mosque-like building with a tower in the center-right. Surrounding the square are multi‑storey buildings and a hilly cityscape with a prominent multi‑towered cathedral in the distance. The lower left corner of the image is captioned "Pécs" and the lower right corner "Széchenyi tér." The reverse side has a Hungarian postage stamp, postmark, and handwritten address lines, with a small printer's mark at the bottom.

A color postcard showing a historic Ottoman-era stone mosque with a large gray dome and a tall, slender minaret, situated between later residential buildings along a street. The back of the postcard contains multilingual captions (Hungarian, German, English, Russian) identifying the site, along with standard postcard layout for address and stamp, printer and photographer credits, and a printed price in Hungarian forints.

The postcard shows a tall concrete television tower with multiple circular observation and equipment decks, some highlighted by red bands, rising above a densely wooded hillside with autumn-colored trees under a blue sky with clouds. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with multilingual captions identifying the site as a television tower in the Mecsek hills near Pécs, Hungary, plus publisher and price information.

Vintage monochrome postcard depicting a broad street lined with large institutional buildings. The main structure on the right is a multi‑storey university building with a corner tower and classical detailing; other similar blocks recede into the distance. A few small figures walk along the sidewalks. The caption at the bottom front identifies the location and institution in Hungarian. The reverse side is blank except for standard postcard address lines and a small Hungarian publisher's imprint at the lower left.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large, ornate multi‑storey building with corner pavilions and a central entrance, set behind a landscaped garden and low fence. Curved paths and an open square or park occupy the foreground, with hills visible in the distant background. The reverse side has divided postcard layout, printed Hungarian text and the publisher name.

Color postcard showing a slightly inclined street lined with mid‑20th‑century cars and historic buildings, leading toward a green hill dominated by a tall television/observation tower on the summit. The reverse side has printed multilingual location text, publisher details in Hungarian, a handwritten address, and price information.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large European-style public square with formal gardens, benches and a central columnar monument surrounded by a fountain or plinth. Historic multi‑storey buildings with ornate façades line the square, including a tall clock/bell tower on the left and a domed-roof corner building. Cars, a bus and pedestrians are visible, suggesting a mid‑20th‑century scene. The reverse side has printed and handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp and address lines.

Multi‑view color postcard showing Turkish art monuments in the city of Pécs, Hungary. The front side is divided into several photographs: a 16th‑century mosque with a tall minaret, an ornate interior mihrab or prayer niche, a small round stone türbe (grave chapel) with a red tiled roof in a green setting, excavated stone ruins and historic houses along a street, and a broader cityscape of Pécs with a central former mosque topped by a large dome in a town square and hills in the background. The reverse side has multilingual descriptive text (Hungarian, German, English, Russian), standard postcard address lines, stamp boxes, a publisher credit from Budapest, and the printed price.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy urban square with a decorative stone fountain or monument in a circular flowerbed in the foreground. Around it are pedestrians, bicycles and early/mid‑20th‑century buses. In the background stand multi‑storey buildings and, prominently, a large domed building. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text indicating it is a greeting from Pécs and standard postcard layout for address and stamp.

The postcard shows a modernist concrete restaurant building with large glass windows and a wide outdoor terrace lined with tables and chairs. A broad exterior staircase leads up to the terrace. On top of the building is the sign "MISINA" in stylized letters. A tall concrete tower structure is visible behind the restaurant. In the foreground there is a curved road, a streetlamp, some parked cars, and a parking sign indicating 150 meters. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with multilingual description and publisher information printed along the left and center.

Black-and-white postcard showing a decorative fountain with carved human figures around its central drum, spraying water into a circular basin adorned with floral motifs. Behind the fountain stand the stone ruins of an old building or fortification, surrounded by trees and a park-like setting. The reverse side has Hungarian text printed and handwritten, a Hungarian stamp and a postmark from Pécs dated 1971.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a long, modernist multi‑storey building along a street, likely a socialist‑era public clinic. The facade has repetitive vertical window bays and a glassy ground floor. People walk on the sidewalk and a small car is parked on the street, suggesting a mid‑20th‑century scene. The back of the postcard has multilingual printing describing the building as the ambulatory clinic of the trade unions in Pécs, and attribution to photographer Ripely Imre.

Multi-view color postcard showing exterior and interior views of a domed former mosque, now a church. The main exterior image depicts a large stone building with an Ottoman-style green dome situated on a public square with gardens and a monument in front, against a hilly backdrop. The interior views show the Christianized mosque with an altar, crucifix, pews, arched windows with circular lattice openings, and striped arches in red and white. The reverse side has printed multilingual captions identifying the site and standard postcard layout for address and postage.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque‑style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcaded façade, fronted by a broad square with trees and a central statue. Hills and town buildings lie in the background. The reverse side is printed as a divided postcard with Hungarian heading "LEVELEZŐ LAP", a Hungarian stamp and postmark, multilingual caption identifying the view, and handwritten Hungarian text and address.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a long, formal dining hall with two rows of tables covered with white tablecloths, set with plates, cups, and bread rolls. Vases with flowers stand on the tables, and a carpeted runner leads toward the far wall, where a crucifix, small religious pictures, and double doors are visible. The room has tall windows along one side and simple hanging lamps from the ceiling. Handwritten-style text at the bottom of the image identifies the location. The reverse side has standard postcard address lines and printed Hungarian text, including a publisher imprint and a commemorative seal.

Black‑and‑white aerial view over a Central European city with tiled roofs, a church with a tall spire in the mid‑ground, and a tree‑filled park in the foreground featuring a statue on a pedestal in a circular flowerbed. Rolling fields and low hills extend in the background. The reverse side is a divided back printed in Hungarian, indicating the scene shows Pécs and the Szepessy statue near a convent church.

Two-sided vintage postcard. The front shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a large, multi‑storey collegiate building with inner courtyards and a formal garden featuring paths and a circular flower bed in the foreground. Hills and other city buildings are visible in the background. Below the image there is Hungarian text describing the Maurinum at Erzsébet University and listing accommodation fees. The reverse side is a typical divided‑back layout with address lines and stamp box, printed in Hungarian, and a caption describing the southern façade of the Pécs University Saint Maur College with garden and sports field.

Vintage Hungarian postcard. The front shows a monochrome sketch of a narrow street with tall buildings leading toward a Baroque-style church with a tower and dome; pedestrians are visible in the foreground. Below the image is the caption "EGYETEMI TEMPLOM." The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp box, printed in Hungarian, and a heading indicating Pécs Lyceum Church and the artist's name.

The postcard shows the richly decorated apse of a cathedral, with a large fresco of Christ in Judgment seated on a throne, surrounded by saints and angels in a golden semi-dome. The reverse side includes multilingual descriptions (Hungarian, German, English, Russian) identifying the scene as the sanctuary apse of the Pécs Cathedral and crediting the fresco to K. Andreas. It has standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp box.

Vintage black‑and‑white Hungarian postcard. The front shows a pencil drawing of a narrow street lined with simple houses, with a hill densely covered by more buildings and a small chapel on top in the background. A few small figures walk along the street. The artist's signature and the year 1922 appear in the lower right corner. The reverse side is a classic divided back with address lines and a stamp box, printed entirely in Hungarian, mentioning Pécs, Puturlu Street and the Havihegy Chapel, and crediting the artist and printer.

Sepia-toned industrial scene showing a large mining or factory complex with multi‑storey administrative buildings, a very tall smokestack on the left and a massive elevated water tower on the right. The foreground contains fenced yards, rails and construction materials; wooded hills rise in the background. The reverse side is printed and handwritten in Hungarian, mentioning the 'Gróf Széchenyi István' mine shaft at Pécsbányatelep and a 1927 consecration.

Black-and-white postcard showing a modernist school complex in a hilly, rural landscape. The main building has long rows of windows and a flat roof, with additional block-like wings nearby. The foreground is filled with trees and cultivated land, and low mountains or large hills rise in the background. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating the view of the general school in the Mecsekalja district of Pécs, and publisher/pricing information.

A sepia-toned panoramic photograph taken from an elevated vantage point, showing a mining settlement and industrial landscape in a valley surrounded by rolling hills and distant mountains. A pine tree frames the left side in the foreground, while mine buildings, spoil heaps and chimneys are visible below. On the front, handwritten-style text identifies the view as the coal mining colonies of Pécs. The reverse side is a classic divided-back postcard layout printed in Hungarian, commemorating the First National Credo Day held in 1929 in the free royal city of Pécs, with a vertical credit line to an engineer-photographer and a small serial number at the bottom.

The postcard shows a small red diesel locomotive pulling open passenger cars along a narrow‑gauge track through a lush green forest. People are seated in the cars, and the scene appears to be part of a recreational or park railway. The reverse side has Hungarian text printed at the top left and the usual postcard layout for address and stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a Central European city with hills in the background. In the middle distance stands a large Romanesque‑style cathedral with four tall square towers. In the foreground is a long, three‑storey school or institutional building facing a street with small figures walking. At the bottom left of the image the caption reads "Pécs" and at the bottom center "Látkép a Cisztercita reálgimnáziummal." The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address, a brown Hungarian postage stamp, postmarks and a small publisher's logo labeled "WEINSTOCK".

A vintage Hungarian postcard. The front side shows a monochrome pencil drawing of a sloping street with small houses, tiled roofs and a distant view of two church towers on the skyline. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text identifying the scene, a green Hungarian postage stamp, cancellation mark, and handwritten Hungarian message and address lines.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a street scene in the city of Pécs. A large, monumental brick building with stone base and ornate roof dominates the view; in front of it stands a war memorial. A tramcar and several early‑ to mid‑20th‑century automobiles are on the street, and pedestrians walk around the square. Trees and a church tower with a tall spire are visible to the left. The caption beneath the image is in Hungarian. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address to Budapest, a Hungarian postage stamp and the printer's imprint.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing an outdoor swimming pool complex with many bathers, surrounded by tall poplar trees and a grandstand with tiered seating and changing facilities below. The front caption reads "Pécs" on the left and "Strandfürdő" on the right. The reverse side has a green Hungarian postage stamp, handwritten Hungarian text, and a Budapest address.

Colorized photographic postcard showing a large corner building complex with red roofs and light-colored walls, identified as a university children's clinic. People are visible on the unpaved street in front of the building. The caption at the bottom front is in Hungarian. The reverse side is a standard divided back postcard layout with printer information in Hungarian.

Sepia-toned divided postcard with two photographs on the front. The upper image shows an industrial mining complex with a prominent tall shaft or tower-like building surrounded by ancillary structures and rail tracks leading toward it, captioned in Hungarian "Szent István akna." The lower image shows a broad street or open field with a large, multi-storey institutional building with balconies and a small tower or dome, captioned "Mecsekszabolcs. Legényotthon." The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, printed Hungarian publisher information, an address to Budapest, and a green Hungarian postage stamp cancelled at Pécs.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows a crowded outdoor swimming pool with waves, surrounded by bathers, umbrellas, and buildings in the background. At the bottom front it is captioned in Hungarian with the city name "Pécs" and the site name "Hullámfürdő" (wave bath). The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, printed address lines, a Hungarian stamp depicting the Budapest central railway station building labeled "KÖZPONTI PÁLYAUDVAR BUDAPEST" and "MAGYAR POSTA", and a circular postmark. The lower center shows the printer's mark "FOTO WEINSTOCK" and the code "2833/30. SZ."

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a modernist, elongated hotel or resort building on a wooded hillside. In the foreground there is a bench and a rocky wall, while the background reveals a sloping, tree‑covered landscape. The printed captions on the image side read "Pécs" at the lower left and "Üdülőszálló a Mecseken" at the lower right. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a Hungarian postage stamp with the Holy Crown, a circular postmark from Pécs dated 1941, and a publisher mark "FOTÓ WEINSTOCK".

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large modernist multi‑storey building on a hill surrounded by trees and landscaped grounds. A winding road or driveway with a white fence curves in front of the building. Pine branches frame the view from above. The lower left of the image has the printed word "Pécs" and the lower right "Üdülő szálló". The reverse side shows dense handwritten text, address lines, a Hungarian stamp and postmark, and the printer's mark "FOTO WEINSTOCK".

Color photograph of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcaded façade, seen from a broad paved square with steps and a central statue in front. The reverse side shows a standard divided-back postcard layout with printed multilingual caption and publisher information.

Color postcard showing a richly detailed church fresco depicting the Baptism of Jesus by John the Baptist in a river, surrounded by angels and other figures with golden halos. Below the scene runs a Latin inscription on a decorative band. The reverse side has multilingual captions (Hungarian, German, English, Russian) identifying the artwork, along with standard postcard address lines, stamp boxes, price, and publisher details in Hungarian.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large, symmetrical historic building with arched windows and a stone lower level, fronted by a garden or small park with people sitting and children playing. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, printed location text, a Hungarian stamp, address lines, and a pencilled year "1965".

Multi-view color postcard with four photographs of city landmarks separated by red borders. The upper-left image shows a central square with parked cars and a large domed former mosque with a tall column monument in front. The upper-right image depicts a neoclassical building facade with arched windows and a sign above the entrance. In the center is a small city coat of arms and the word 'PÉCS' on a blue strip. The lower-left image shows a church-like building with a tower and cross in a quiet street. The lower-right image presents a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers partly obscured by trees and a stone retaining wall in the foreground. The reverse side is blank with standard postcard layout lines for address and stamp.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy town square with tram tracks, horse‑drawn carts, pedestrians and trees. Dominating the scene is a large domed church with a cross on top and an attached bell tower, along with a tall column or monument in the center of the square. The caption at the bottom names the place and the church. The reverse side is a typical divided postcard back with address lines and a printed indication of rights and the year 1927 by the Budapest publisher Barasits.

A printed color illustration of a neoclassical building with a strong row of tall columns and many rectangular windows, seen from an oblique street view. A green street lamp hangs on an ornate bracket in the foreground, and a few pedestrians walk along the sidewalk. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard with printed Hungarian and German text and no handwriting.

A color postcard showing the front view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with two tall square towers and a green roof, framed by trees and a landscaped park in the foreground. People are visible near the main entrance. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, and printed information identifying the subject as the cathedral in Pécs, plus the photographer's credit.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a modernist building complex with bold, angled facades and large awnings, identified as the Olympia Restaurant. The scene includes curved roads with buses, pedestrians, streetlights, landscaped areas, and low hills in the background. The reverse side has Hungarian text, a vertical publisher line, printed price, and standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp box.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a European city square with mid‑20th‑century cars. On the right stands a large domed former mosque with a cross on top and a spacious paved square in front, containing a tall Baroque plague column or monument with sculptures. On the left is a long, ornate classical building lining a tree‑planted street. The reverse side shows printed multilingual captions identifying the scene, handwritten Hungarian text, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Black-and-white postcard showing a Romanesque cloister courtyard with stone arches in the foreground and the apse and tall bell tower of a large cathedral in the background. The reverse side is an unused divided-back postcard with Hungarian text identifying the location and the publisher.

The postcard shows a sepia-toned panoramic view over a historic European city filled with dense low-roofed houses and church towers. The photo is taken from an elevated hillside with rocky foreground. On the right side, a large crucifix with the figure of Jesus dominates the foreground, overlooking the city below. The back of the card has standard postcard layout with address lines, stamp boxes, and printed caption text in Hungarian and English.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the interior of a small Catholic chapel with wooden pews, an ornate altar with statues and candles, and religious wall paintings. The lower front caption identifies the location as in Pécs and describes it as the chapel of the episcopal seminary. The reverse side is blank except for printer information and dividing lines for address and message.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a central square with a large domed church/mosque-like building featuring a cross-topped dome and an attached bell tower. In the foreground stands an ornate plague column or monument in the middle of the square, surrounded by steps and open space. Cars, horse-drawn carriages, and pedestrians line the adjacent street with multi‑story buildings on both sides. Hills rise in the background. Handwritten text at the bottom labels the scene, and the reverse side shows typical divided-back postcard layout with printed Hungarian text.

Color postcard showing the front view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall square towers and a row of arches and statues on the façade. In the foreground there is a plaza with flower beds and a central statue on a pedestal. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with multilingual caption identifying the cathedral in Pécs, Hungary, plus printer and price information.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over a hilly landscape near the city of Pécs, Hungary. In the foreground there is a terrace filled with tables, chairs, and people enjoying the view; a road curves just below the terrace where a bus is passing by. The back side shows Hungarian handwriting in red pencil, a green Hungarian postage stamp, printed Hungarian publisher information, and address lines filled in red.

Illustrated postcard showing a grand Baroque-style building with a central clock in the pediment, tall windows with shutters, and an ornate stone staircase leading up from the foreground. An obelisk-like monument with a cross on top stands to the left of the staircase. A few figures in early‑20th‑century clothing walk or stand near the stairs. The reverse side contains handwritten text and printed Hungarian captions identifying the scene and publisher information.

Colored vintage postcard showing an ornate Neo-Baroque theater building with multiple domes and elaborate sculptural decoration. The front top caption reads in Hungarian, and the back has handwritten Hungarian text, a green postage stamp, and typical postcard address and message layout.

Vintage-style postcard with a monochrome drawing of an old stone ruin overgrown with vegetation. The structure has arched doorways and partially collapsed walls. At the lower left, the word "Tettye" is written, and at the lower right appears an artist's signature with the date 1987. The reverse side shows a typical divided-back postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, but no printing or handwriting.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square framed by an arch. Prominent is an ornate historic town hall with a tall clock tower and baroque details, facing a row of 2‑storey buildings and a busy street with pedestrians. At the bottom front side, Hungarian captions identify the scene as Pécs and Széchenyi Square with the town hall. The reverse side has handwritten correspondence, an address to Czechoslovakia, a Hungarian postage stamp and a small printer's mark from Budapest.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the southern façade of a large Romanesque cathedral with four tall square towers and an open square with a central statue in the foreground. The reverse side has printed multilingual captions describing the view, handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp, and postal markings.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard with six photographs of landmarks and streets from the city of Pécs. The top left shows a large Romanesque‑style cathedral with four towers and a statue in front (Pécs Cathedral). Other views show civic buildings, a domed former mosque on a central square, a grand railway‑station‑like building, a clock‑tower on a street with a tram, and a square with a central statue and surrounding historic houses. The front caption, in Hungarian, reads "Üdvözlet Pécsről!" (Greetings from Pécs). The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp labeled "Magyar Posta 40 f", and printed credits for the publisher in Budapest along with the words "Pécsi részletek."

Color postcard showing an ornamental fountain with sculpted human figures on its central drum, set in a park with trees and benches. Behind the fountain stand stone ruins and an arched wall from the 16th century. The reverse side contains multilingual captions identifying the location and the fountain, along with standard postcard address lines and stamp boxes.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcade façade. The church stands above a town with low houses and wooded hills in the background. Hungarian captions are printed below the image. The reverse side is blank with standard postcard address lines and a small printer's logo.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a European town seen from a hillside with blossoming trees and a small shrine or monument in the foreground where a cloaked figure stands. In the middle distance are church towers and a large domed church, with a wide valley and fields stretching to distant hills. The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, a red Hungarian stamp, and printed caption information.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an outdoor terrace café crowded with people sitting at tables, many playing chess or chatting, on a hill overlooking a sprawling town with low houses and, in the distance, a prominent church with twin towers. The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, printed Hungarian captions, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Vintage sepia-toned multi‑view postcard. The picture side shows four small photographs: an elegant central European street with large classical buildings and a fountain or monument in front; a large modernist building on a hillside; a hillside landscape with a multi‑story building at the top and two men walking on a road in the foreground; and a garden or park scene with a small house or pavilion reached by steps among trees. At the bottom is printed Hungarian text reading "Üdvözlet Pécsről" (Greetings from Pécs). The reverse side has a handwritten message in blue ink in Hungarian, address lines, a red Hungarian stamp showing 'CSEPELI POSTAHIVATAL' and 'MAGYAR POSTA', and a circular postmark with 'VASAS'.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a scenic view over a city with a four‑towered Romanesque cathedral in the background. In the foreground, on a terrace framed by flowering tree branches, there are decorative stone balustrades covered with abundant fruit: a pile of large round fruits (likely peaches) on a tray atop a patterned cloth, and bunches of grapes arranged on a stone ornament. The reverse side is printed in multiple languages, identifying the cathedral in Pécs and laid out in the typical divided‑back postcard format.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque cathedral with two tall western towers, viewed from across a series of cascading pools and fountains in a formal park. Trees frame the building and small figures walk on the steps leading up to the church. At the bottom of the image, printed captions in Hungarian read "Pécs" on the left and "Székesegyház" on the right. The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, address lines, a partial circular postmark, a missing stamp area, a small publisher logo reading "L. F. WEINSTOCK" and a printed serial number "3268/17. sz."

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a large modernist stone-and-concrete building on a hillside surrounded by trees, with people standing along the terrace; in the foreground there is a railing and part of a stepped structure. The caption at the bottom identifies the location as Pécs and mentions a holiday resort in the Mecsek mountains. The reverse side has handwritten text in blue ink, Hungarian postage stamps, and an address in Budapest.

Color postcard showing a modernist building complex with angular concrete facades, large windows shaded by red awnings, landscaped lawns and paths in the foreground, and low hills in the background. The reverse side contains printed multilingual text identifying the place as the Olympia Restaurant in Pécs, handwritten Hungarian message and address, a green 40 fillér Hungarian postage stamp, and Pécs postmarks.

Color postcard showing a stylized street map of a city with Hungarian street names. Overlaid in the center is an illustration of a tall TV tower with red and white antenna segments and a circular observation/restaurant level. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with printed text indicating the location and publisher.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a circular fountain with sculpted reliefs and water jets in the foreground, set in a park. Behind it stand the stone ruins of a 16th‑century structure, partially covered by trees. The reverse side has multilingual printed text identifying the site as the ruins of Tettye in Pécs, Hungary, with standard postcard address lines and publisher information.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped park with tree‑lined paths and the stone remains of an old structure featuring large arches and walls. In the foreground a woman and a child walk along a curved path. The reverse side includes printed multilingual captions identifying the location as the Tettye ruins in Pécs, Hungary, along with handwritten Hungarian text, an address, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a newly built residential district with several four‑storey apartment blocks, balconies, fenced green areas and paths in the foreground, and a prominent streetlamp on the left. The reverse side contains printed multilingual text identifying the view as a new district of Pécs, along with a Hungarian postage stamp and handwritten Hungarian message and address.

Old sepia postcard showing a bustling market square filled with people in early‑20th‑century attire, horse‑drawn carriages, and surrounding low buildings. A larger, ornate building stands in the background. The reverse side has a green postage stamp, circular postal cancellations, and printed Hungarian text such as "Levelező-Lap" and address lines.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard. The picture side shows a broad view of a hilly landscape with vineyards and terraces, with prominent stone ruins in the foreground and scattered buildings at the edges. At the top it is captioned in Hungarian "Pécs–Tettye" and "A fennsík teljes látképe". The reverse side has a green Hungarian stamp, dense handwritten text in Hungarian, and printed heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" with the address written to Budapest.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a hilly, wooded landscape with a winding road in the Mecsek mountains. In the foreground there is a tall street lamp, a railing along the road, and a vintage bus parked at a viewpoint or terrace. The reverse side contains printed Hungarian text indicating the view is from the terrace of the Mecsek SZOT holiday hotel in Pécs, handwritten Hungarian message, address lines, a Magyar Posta postage stamp and a circular postmark.

A color postcard showing a bright, sunny view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and a greenish roof, fronted by an open square with flower beds, a statue on a pedestal, trees, benches, and surrounding historic buildings. The lower front margin bears the caption "PÉCS". The reverse side is mostly blank except for printed publisher information and the title of the scene.

Vintage colorized postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and a green roof, fronted by a circular garden and statue. The caption at the top left reads "PÉCS Székesegyház". The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, address lines, and a circular postmark.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a historic building with a domed roof and a slender Ottoman‑style minaret rising above it, crowned by a crescent. In front of the structure are bare trees and an iron fence. At the bottom margin of the image, handwritten-style text identifies the location. The reverse side is blank, laid out in the classic divided‑back postcard style with printed publisher information along the right edge.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over the city of Pécs from a hillside. In the left foreground stands a tall, pyramidal stone monument with a statue on top, overlooking the city and surrounding landscape. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a Hungarian stamp, and printer information.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a long, modernist clinic building with tiled facade, stone base and a colonnade of round pillars along the front. Large horizontal windows run across the upper floor, with some open blinds. A 1950s–60s style station wagon and a bus are visible in the foreground, suggesting a hospital or institutional entrance area. The reverse side has printed multilingual text identifying the place as the clinic in Pécs, Hungary, space for address and message, and publisher/pricing information.

Color postcard showing a stone ruin of a 16th‑century structure surrounded by lush trees. In the foreground there is a circular orange fountain decorated with reliefs of dancing figures and water jets spraying inward and outward. The back side contains multilingual captions identifying the site as the ruins of Tettye in Pécs, Hungary, plus publisher and price information.

Color postcard showing large stone ruins with thick, crumbling walls from a 16th‑century structure surrounded by grass and some trees under a clear blue sky. The reverse side is a standard divided-back layout with multilingual caption and Hungarian publisher information.

Color postcard showing a stone lookout or refuge building with a small tower and adjacent tall metal lattice observation/telecommunication tower on a hilltop. People walk toward the building and others sit on red benches under large trees. The reverse side has divided back layout with printed Hungarian and Cyrillic text identifying the place as Pécs, Misina-tető, publisher details from Budapest, and the photographer's credit.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The image side is divided into three vertical panels: on the left, a former mosque with a tall slender minaret and domed roof set among trees; in the center, a broad terraced garden with fountains leading up to a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers; on the right, a monumental statue of a standing man atop an ornate pedestal with seated figures around the base, located in an urban square. The message side shows handwritten Hungarian text, a green 40f Hungarian postage stamp labeled "MAGYAR POSTA" and "SIMONTORNYA", and an address in Budapest.

Colored postcard showing a tall, pointed‑spire church with brick and white façades along a tree‑lined street. At the top is printed the caption "PÉCS, Ref. templom". The reverse side has a green 5‑fillér Hungarian stamp, postmark, address lines, and a handwritten Hungarian message covering the lower half.

Two-sided vintage postcard. The front side is divided into four black‑and‑white photographs showing city views and religious interiors. The upper left image depicts a large square with the domed former mosque of Pasha Qasim in the center of Pécs. The upper right shows a panoramic view over the city with the four-towered Pécs Cathedral prominent on the skyline. The two lower images show interiors of a church or converted mosque with striped Moorish-style arches, an altar, pews, and religious decorations. The reverse side has Hungarian printed text, handwritten message and address, a green Hungarian postage stamp featuring the castle of Tata and marked "MAGYAR POSTA", plus a circular postmark.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a modern hillside hotel building partly hidden by pine trees. In the foreground there is a stone terrace and stairway with a reclining nude female statue placed on a low stone wall. A person walks up the steps toward the hotel. The reverse side contains printed Hungarian text identifying the location and sculpture, a green Hungarian postage stamp, a Pécs postmark, and handwritten Hungarian correspondence and address.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The front shows four photographs: a modern building complex on a forested hillside; a central city square with a large domed former mosque and an equestrian statue; a panoramic view over a hilly town with people sitting on a slope in the foreground; and a stone lookout platform with railings overlooking rolling hills. The back side has handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, printed publisher information, a PÉCS postmark, and an address field.

A color multi-view postcard featuring landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front shows four images: a medieval stone fortification, the tall TV tower rising above trees, an ornate fountain in front of a large building, and a large panoramic view of the main square with a domed former mosque and surrounding historic buildings, statues, cars, and people. The word "PÉCS" is printed prominently in white on a black strip in the center. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp, postmarks from Pécs dated 30 May 1978, and printed publisher and price information.

A round multi-view color postcard bordered in orange, featuring four photographic scenes of the city of Pécs. The upper-left shows a historic cathedral with multiple towers above a hillside of houses. The upper-right shows a central square with a domed former mosque and surrounding buildings, cars, and a large paved plaza. The lower-left image shows a modern, terraced hotel or public building. The lower-right shows a broader cityscape with modern high‑rise blocks set against green hills. In the center front is a white label with bold black text reading "PÉCS". The reverse side has standard postcard layout printed in Hungarian, with areas for stamp, address lines, and price information.

A multiview color postcard showing several landmarks of the city of Pécs. The central circular image features a tall telecommunications tower rising above green trees. Surrounding it are four rectangular views: an old chapel on a grassy hill, a domed former mosque in a busy square with many cars, a modern multi‑storey building complex set among trees, and a large Romanesque cathedral with two tall towers flanking its façade. The front has a turquoise sky background with a yellow band containing Hungarian text. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with space for address and stamp, and small printed text in Hungarian and Cyrillic.

A multi-view color postcard featuring exterior and interior views of a historic mosque with a tall stone minaret and domed roof, along with surrounding city walls and buildings. The front has three photos and a beige background with the word "PÉCS" printed below the images. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with space for address and message, red stamp boxes, and printed captions in multiple languages describing Jakovali Hassan's Mosque and its minaret.

Multiview color postcard with an orange border, featuring four oval photographs of buildings and historic structures from the city of Pécs. The upper two images show modern mid‑20th‑century multi‑story buildings, likely a hotel or commercial center and another institutional building. The lower left image shows a round medieval stone tower and fortification wall. The lower right image shows an Ottoman‑style mosque with a dome and minaret behind a stone wall, flanked by historic buildings. In the center is a white label with the word "PÉCS". The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard layout with lines for address and space for a message, printed multilingual greetings from Pécs, publisher information from Budapest, price in forints, and boxes for postage stamps.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcade façade, fronted by a statue in a circular park. Flanking the cathedral are historic buildings and tree-lined paths. Printed Hungarian captions read "Üdvözlet Pécsről" (Greetings from Pécs) and "Székesegyház" (Cathedral). The reverse side has the Hungarian heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP", handwritten Hungarian text and address lines, a PÉCS postmark dated 1914, and a small printed publisher line at the bottom.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a large Catholic cathedral, focused on the high altar and ciborium with multiple steps, pulpits, arches and ornate ceiling. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text at the top and bottom and handwritten correspondence, address, and postmark.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a sloping walkway with trees and stairs leading down toward a small city. In the background, a large church with four Romanesque towers dominates the skyline, with hills visible beyond the town. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a green Hungarian postage stamp, printed text indicating the view is of Pécs, and the recipient's address.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a formal city park with walking paths, statues, and a small domed pavilion on the left, and a large historic building with arched gateway on the right. Many people, including what appears to be a marching band or troop, walk along the path by the building. The front bears red printed captions "Pécs" and "Sétatér". The reverse side is a divided back with Hungarian text, a green Hungarian stamp marked "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA", and handwritten message and address.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a lively European square with a domed former mosque and church tower on the left and an ornate multi‑story historicist building with shops and striped awnings on the right. A tram runs through the square among horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians. The front is labeled in red with the place name and the square's name. The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, address lines, and a purple Hungarian postage stamp denominated in korona.

A multi‑view color postcard with an orange border showing several scenes from the city of Pécs. The main images include a panoramic view of the city with a TV tower on the nearby hill, the central square with the mosque‑church with a large green dome and surrounding historic buildings, a view of the ornate City Hall, a pedestrian street lined with old houses, and a church with a tower and a small square in front. In the center there is a city emblem with a stylized bastion, red star and other symbols. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines, stamp box, and Hungarian text indicating the publisher and photographer.

Color postcard showing a stone castle barbican with high rough masonry walls, a wooden staircase leading up along the right tower, and a cobbled courtyard. In the background is a building with a light-colored plastered façade and a steep hipped roof with a small spire. The reverse side has multilingual printed text identifying the place, publisher details, price, address lines, and stamp boxes.

A multi-view color postcard. The front shows three main images of Pécs: on the left, the large domed mosque‑church on the main square with a monument and flower beds in front; in the middle, a circular inset of a tall modern TV tower; on the right, the Romanesque cathedral with its four towers seen from the square. The word "PÉCS" is printed vertically on a black strip on the right. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address section, a Hungarian stamp with 'MAGYAR POSTA', and printing details.

A round, multi-view color postcard. The front shows several photographic scenes from the same city arranged in a circular collage: in the central circle is a tall red‑and‑white striped TV/radio tower on a hill overlooking the landscape; the surrounding segments depict a large modern square with a monument, modern hotel or apartment blocks with zigzag balconies, a hillside park with a large statue, and historic multi‑storey buildings with domes. The back is printed like a standard postcard with address lines, stamp box and price, all in Hungarian, and includes the word "PÉCS".

Round multi‑view color postcard with an orange background and four photographic views of a historic Hungarian city. The images show old fortress walls and towers, a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers, and a central square with historic buildings and a domed structure. In the middle is the city coat of arms featuring a stylized castle wall with a red star and an emblem below. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines and stamp box, printed mostly in Hungarian.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a modernist stone church with a tall bell tower bearing a cross, arched windows and arcades, situated on a hillside at a road junction. The reverse side is printed in Hungarian and includes handwritten Hungarian text, two Hungarian stamps, and a postmark.

A sepia-toned historic view of a broad European square with tree‑lined streets, horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians. In the center stands an ornate Marian or Holy Trinity column on a stepped pedestal, surrounded by a low fence. Behind it rises a domed church with a tower and cross, flanked by long, classical multi‑story buildings. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, and printed captions identifying the scene and publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand central square with historic buildings. A large eclectic-style city hall with a tall clock tower dominates the left side, while other multi‑story buildings and a church frame the square. People and shop awnings are visible around the plaza. The caption at the bottom of the image reads "Pécs" on the left and "Széchenyi tér" on the right. The reverse side has standard divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian instructions about postage and the publisher's mark "Foto Weinstock".

A color postcard showing a large abstract bronze Liberation Monument sculpture rising behind a tall concrete wall on a green hillside. In the background are modernist buildings surrounded by trees under a clear blue sky. The reverse side has Hungarian handwritten text, address lines, two Hungarian stamps, and printed multilingual caption information about the monument in Pécs, plus publisher and price details.

The postcard shows a color photograph of a large, modernist concrete hotel building with terraced balconies and prominent white diagonal supports along the front. Several 1970s–1980s style cars are parked in front on a curved access road, with two pedestrians walking on the pavement. The back of the postcard is printed with Hungarian text identifying the location and hotel, a pre-printed 2 Ft Magyar Posta stamp, address lines, and publisher/photographer information.

Color-tinted postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers and an arcade of arches along the façade. In front of the church is a circular lawn with a statue on a pedestal in the center and paths with benches around it. The caption at the top reads "Pécs. Székesegyház." The reverse side has printed Hungarian text indicating a correspondence card, handwritten message and address, a red Hungarian postage stamp, and postal marks.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a drawing of a large Romanesque cathedral with multiple towers and an arcaded façade, viewed through bare tree branches from a park-like square with benches and a tall column or obelisk. The reverse side contains handwritten text in Hungarian, an address, a purple Hungarian postage stamp and a circular postmark.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall corner towers, fronted by a formal garden and statue. The building is set against low hills with surrounding city structures. The front bears printed Hungarian text "PÉCS" at the top left and "Székesegyház" at the top right. The reverse side has divided postcard layout lines, handwritten Hungarian address/message, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and a printed card number along the edge.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over a hilly, partly forested landscape with a town spread across the valley in the foreground. The reverse side is a standard divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating the view is from the Flóra rest area in Pécs.

A multi-view color postcard. The front shows five images arranged on an orange background: four photos of ornate ceramic vases and pitchers, and in the center a photograph of a decorated fountain set in an urban square with historic stone buildings and traffic in the background. Below the collage, the caption "PÉCS" is printed. The reverse side is a standard divided back with address lines, stamp boxes, price information and publisher details printed in Hungarian.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view over a town nestled among rolling hills and agricultural fields, taken from an elevated lookout. The reverse side is a classic divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating the view is from the Flóra rest area in Pécs, along with publisher information and the printed price.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over the city of Pécs from an elevated, tree‑framed vantage point. The foreground has a large tree and bushes, while the middle and background show dense rooftops, church towers, and the outline of Pécs Cathedral's towers on a hill. The back side is divided with Hungarian text, handwriting in pencil, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and a 1915 postmark.

Old black‑and‑white postcard showing a domed Ottoman‑style building with a tall, slender minaret rising in front of adjoining houses and a garden with benches in the foreground. In the upper part of the image there is red printed text reading "Pécs" on the left and "Török minaret" on the right. The reverse side has a divided back with printed Hungarian text, a circular postmark, handwritten message and address.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a modernist residential and commercial complex with flat‑roofed apartment blocks and a distinctive low angular building with deep concrete fins and terraces in the foreground. Two-sided postcard. A black‑and‑white postcard showing the facade of a large Romanesque‑style cathedral with four tall towers and a central nave, seen from a square with steps, benches, trees, and a statue in front of the building. The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian notes dated 1935 Oct 6 and printed Hungarian text indicating rights reserved and the photographer/publisher in Pécs.

Multi-view color postcard with four photographs separated by black borders and a small city emblem in the center. A multi-view color postcard with an orange border featuring landmarks of the city of Pécs. A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard featuring several landmarks of the city of Pécs. Multi-view color postcard with several landmarks of the city of Pécs. The central upper image shows the façade of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four towers and a statue in front. A multiview color postcard with a magenta background featuring five photographs of landmarks from the city of Pécs. The reverse side contains Hungarian handwritten text, a Pécs postmark dated 1971, a red MAGYAR POSTA stamp, and printed publisher information in Hungarian.

A color postcard showing a large round medieval stone bastion in the foreground, part of the city walls, with crenellations and small openings in the masonry. Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a large statue of a man in a cloak standing on an ornate pedestal in a city square. Vintage sepia postcard showing a grand Neo-Renaissance style building with arched windows and ornate roofline, seen from a cobblestone street with horse-drawn carriages and small trees lining the sidewalk. Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers rising above a tree‑filled square and surrounding buildings. Color postcard showing the ornate Zsolnay Fountain in an urban street setting. Multiview postcard with a brown border. Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing an industrial mining complex with tall brick chimneys, power‑house style buildings and surrounding yards in a hilly landscape. Posta stamp, handwritten message and address, and a printed publisher line at the bottom.

Old monochrome industrial-view postcard showing a factory complex with tall chimneys and adjoining buildings, bordered by bare trees and a dirt road. The reverse has the word "LEVELEZŐLAP" (postcard in Hungarian), handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp, and postmarks.

Colorized historic view of an ornate red-brick railway station building with towers and arched windows. In front are people with handcarts and horse-drawn vehicles on a wide square. Color postcard showing a lush park scene framed by a large stone arch, likely a remnant of an old wall or aqueduct. Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing an aerial view of a modernist, multi‑storey hotel complex on a curved mountain road surrounded by dense forest. Black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a historic Central European city with hills in the background. Vintage monochrome postcard showing a grand Romanesque-style cathedral with two tall western towers and a long nave façade, viewed from across a series of terraced pools and fountains. An old monochrome postcard showing a hilly landscape with scattered houses and a church standing prominently on a hilltop. A vintage divided-back postcard with Hungarian text. Vintage black‑and‑white Hungarian postcard. A black-and-white postcard showing the medieval Barbican (Barbakán) of Pécs, a round stone defensive tower and wall surrounded by grass and trees, with a statue standing on a pedestal in front of the fortifications. A color postcard showing a round, richly ornamented stone mausoleum with arched decorations, circular windows, and a cross on top, photographed from the front at dusk. A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large, ornate, multi‑storey historicist building with a central entrance and two corner pavilions. Black-and-white postcard showing a socialist-era residential district with several mid-rise apartment blocks in front of a tree-lined green area, with hills in the background. An old sepia-toned postcard showing a street scene with a large historic building complex. Old sepia-toned industrial scene showing a large factory complex with multiple tall chimneys emitting smoke, surrounded by buildings and bare trees. Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with Hungarian text. Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a group of women and children in traditional folk costumes standing on a simple wooden footbridge in a rural setting. Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a panoramic view of a large European public square lined with multi‑storey historic buildings, trees, pedestrians and horse‑drawn vehicles. Two-sided illustrated postcard. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with address lines, a stamp box, and Hungarian text giving contact information and opening hours for the Mecseki Kultúrpark in Pécs, plus publisher information.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a central European square. In the foreground stands a large statue of a man in a cloak (Lajos Kossuth) on a high pedestal decorated with wreaths. To the left is a long, ornate historic building, and to the right is a grand façade with a large round window and arched entrances, likely a public or religious building. People are gathered around the monument and along the paths. The caption at the top reads: "Pécs – Majláth-tér és Kossuth szobor". The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian and printed address lines.

A vintage divided-back postcard. The front shows a monochrome street scene with ornate late-19th/early-20th‑century villas and shops along a wide avenue. There are trees lining the street, two children with a cart in the foreground, and a horse‑drawn wagon on the right. In the distance is a large decorative building or gate. Printed red captions read "Pécs" and "Schlauch-villatelep". The reverse side has Hungarian printed text, a green 5 filler stamp, a circular postmark, and handwritten Hungarian cursive addressed to Budapest.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large multi‑storey academic building along a broad street. The architecture is late‑19th/early‑20th‑century with ornate façades, high windows, and a towered central section. The reverse side includes Hungarian handwriting, an 8‑fillér Hungarian stamp, and printed Hungarian text identifying the building.

Colored view of a small European town with red‑tiled roofs and green fields. On a hill in the background stands a white church with a tower and spire, surrounded by trees and scattered houses. The reverse side shows handwritten text in Hungarian, an 8 fillér Hungarian stamp, postmarks, and printed postcard layout text.

A multiview color postcard featuring various landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front shows several photographs bordered in red and yellow: the Pécs Cathedral with its four towers, a domed mosque, historical buildings and a public square with statues, city panoramas with tiled rooftops, a section of medieval walls and towers, a statue on a balcony, and an interior church mosaic of Christ and saints. The top of the front side has the large title "PÉCS". The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines, stamp boxes, barcodes, and multilingual greetings from Pécs, along with the logo and details of the publisher Ars Una Studio from Budapest, Hungary.

Color-tinted postcard showing a small round stone lookout tower with a wooden pavilion and railings on top of a hill, with a figure standing on the terrace and grassy, rocky surroundings. At the bottom edge, printed Hungarian text identifies the view and sends greetings from Pécs. The card front and margins contain handwritten cursive notes. The reverse side has the heading 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP', a green Hungarian stamp, postal cancellations from Pécs dated 1906, and an address written in pencil.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a pavilion complex in a landscaped exhibition ground. There are ornate historicist buildings with gabled facades and tall, leafless trees in the background, and a timbered structure with a tall, pointed roof on the left. The caption in red Hungarian text appears at the top left and top right. The reverse side is a typical divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian wording for postcard and a publisher's line at the bottom.

Vintage divided‑back postcard printed in Hungarian. The front shows a monochrome pencil drawing of a long Baroque/Classicist civic building along a gently rising street lined with trees. A lone figure stands on the sidewalk and a small guardhouse or sentry box is visible near the entrance. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines, a boxed area for a stamp, and printed Hungarian captions indicating the subject and the publisher.

Multi-view color postcard with four photographs of landmarks in the city of Pécs. The upper-left shows an ornate historic building on a street with several 1970s–1980s Eastern Bloc cars parked in front. The upper-right image depicts a central square at dusk with a domed former mosque, a tall column, an equestrian statue, and parked cars. The lower-left shows greenery with trees and a round stone ruin or tower. The lower-right image features a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four towers and a prominent statue in front, surrounded by flower beds and old buildings. In the center of the front side, on an orange band, is the caption "PÉCS". The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a Hungarian stamp, postmark, and printed publisher information.

A multi-view postcard showing several religious buildings and interiors around the city of Pécs. The upper left view is a small historic church in a rural setting. The upper right view shows a city square with a prominent domed former mosque (now a church) surrounded by older buildings and parked cars from the socialist era. The central image depicts the interior of a traditional church with a Baroque-style altar. The bottom left view shows a modern white church with angular, minimalist architecture, while the bottom right view shows the interior of this modern church, including a white balcony decorated with abstract reliefs and a simple altar. The reverse side has standard postcard address lines and Hungarian-language publishing information.

A multi-view color postcard with an orange border showing landmarks of the city of Pécs. The front is divided into six photographs: an ornate historic building with a fountain, a city street with café terraces and red Coca‑Cola umbrellas, a large synagogue-like building, a tall baroque column in a square, the four-towered Romanesque cathedral, and a close-up of a decorative bronze ram's-head fountain spout. The word "PÉCS" appears prominently at the bottom. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with lines for address, a barcode, and the word "KÉPESLAP".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural scene with a stone well or spring structure in the foreground identified as Idris baba's well. A person stands drawing water with buckets. A cobblestone road curves past simple houses and fences, with a grassy hill and small column-like roadside shrine bearing a cross on the left. Trees and low hills are in the background under a cloudy sky. The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp, and typical postcard address lines.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a small domed building with a cross on top and, behind it, a slender turret-like minaret with windows and a pointed roof. Leafless trees and an iron fence stand in front of the structure, suggesting a winter or early-spring scene. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard layout with printed Hungarian text identifying the place and a date note from 1933.

Black-and-white postcard showing a richly decorated baroque altar inside a church. The altar features marble-like columns, ornate carvings, religious paintings, and statues of saints on either side. A cloth-covered altar table with candlesticks stands at the front. The caption in Hungarian is printed along the bottom margin of the image. The reverse side is blank except for standard postcard dividing lines and small printed Hungarian text, plus a handwritten date.

A multi-view color postcard with a yellow border showing various street scenes, squares, monuments, and buildings of the city of Pécs, including historic facades, a statue of a rider on horseback, and a cathedral-like structure. The word "Pécs" is prominently printed in red letters on the front. The reverse side features a faint background image of a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers (the Pécs Cathedral), standard postcard address lines, stamp boxes, barcodes, and greetings in multiple languages.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a stone monument on a rocky hillside above a city. The monument is a tapered, obelisk‑like structure with a statue on top, standing on a pedestal surrounded by low vegetation and pines. In the distance, a broad panoramic view of the city and plain below is visible under a hazy sky. At the bottom of the image there is printed Hungarian text identifying the scene. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a Hungarian postage stamp and postmark, and a printed publisher's mark.

A vintage, hand‑tinted postcard. The front shows a green lawn at the foot of rocky hills, with scattered groups of women and children walking or playing, many in long skirts or traditional dress. Behind them are trees and a few buildings, including a tower‑like structure and pavilions, all set against a rocky hillside under a blue sky with some clouds. The caption is printed in Hungarian at the top left, with additional handwritten Hungarian text across the sky. The reverse side is divided for address and message, densely filled with handwritten Hungarian text. Numerous Hungarian stamps marked "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA" are affixed, each denominated in fillér, and postmarks are visible.

Vintage sepia postcard showing the ornate main gate and façade of a large historic academy building. The entrance gate has brick pillars with decorative lamps and an iron arch, with uniformed figures and civilians standing in front. The upper part of the image is overlaid with handwritten text. Printed captions in Hungarian read "Pécs" in the upper left and "Hadapród iskola főbejárata" in the upper right. The reverse side contains dense handwritten correspondence in German, address lines, postal markings, and a vertical imprint of the Budapest publisher dated 1917.

Two-sided vintage postcard. The address side is plain with Hungarian headings "Levelező-lap." and "Czim" and a boxed area for a stamp. The picture side shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a church with a dome and bell tower and, in front of it, a large Baroque plague column/statue in a town square. Below the image are bilingual captions in Hungarian and German indicating the location as the inner-city church on Széchenyi Square in Pécs (Fünfkirchen).

A multi-view color postcard featuring various landmarks of Pécs, Hungary. The front side is divided into several photographs: an observation deck with scenic views, historic buildings and streets, a TV transmission tower amid greenery, the four-towered Romanesque cathedral, ornate church interiors with mosaics and frescoes, a grand square with a plague column, and a large white civic building. The word "PÉCS" is prominently printed in large white letters in the center. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines, barcodes, and multilingual greetings from Pécs, with a faint background image of the cathedral's façade.

A vintage colored postcard showing a large military barracks complex with multi‑storey buildings with red-tiled roofs surrounding an open yard lined with young trees. A row of uniformed soldiers stands in formation along one of the buildings. The front side bears the printed caption "Pécs — Frigyes főherceg laktanya". The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a red 10 fillér Hungarian postage stamp with a postmark, sender and recipient addresses, and divided sections for correspondence and address.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a tall stone lookout tower with a balcony at the top and an attached one-story building at its base, standing on a hill with a path leading up to it. Two people are visible near the entrance. The front has printed text at the top identifying the location. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and printed publisher information along the left edge.

A multi-view color postcard showing several landmarks and street scenes from the city of Pécs. The central images feature a main square with a column and statues, and a green-domed former mosque. Other panels show ornate historic buildings, a cathedral with twin towers, statues, and a tourist train. At the top right, large lettering spells out "PÉCS" next to a small outline map of Hungary filled with the national colors. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with space for a message and address, plus publisher details.

A color postcard with a burgundy border showing the four towers and façade of a large Romanesque-style basilica rising above green trees and red rooftops. At the top, in an oval cartouche, is the name "PÉCS." The reverse side has standard postcard address lines, a barcode, publisher info, multilingual greeting, and a caption identifying the basilica and photographer.

Color postcard with two views of a historic Ottoman mosque and its tall slender minaret, surrounded by trees and adjacent buildings. The reverse side has multilingual printed captions identifying the site, along with standard postcard layout for address and stamp.

Color postcard showing a massive round stone barbican tower and adjacent fortification walls of a medieval castle. A person in a red shirt walks along the road in front of the structure. In the background is a hilly landscape with a TV tower, and on the right stands a multi‑story historic building with a tower and steep roof. The reverse side has multilingual printed captions describing the view and standard postcard layout for address and stamp.

Color postcard showing two views of a large stone domed building on a square, with flowerbeds, benches, steps and parked 1960s-era cars. The structure is the former Gázi Kászim Pasha mosque in Széchenyi Square, Pécs. The back has multilingual captions identifying the place, standard postcard address lines, and credits.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a richly carved Renaissance-style altar or tabernacle inside a chapel. The structure features an arched top with a relief of a bearded figure flanked by angels, intricate floral and figurative carvings on the sides, and several standing saints or allegorical figures around a central panel. The altar table below has ornamental reliefs and candles placed on either side. Behind it, patterned wall decoration and faint mural paintings are visible. There is handwritten text in pencil beneath the image on the front and a short note in Hungarian on the divided back of the postcard.

Multi-view color postcard with five images of landmarks from a European city. The top left shows a charming pedestrian street lined with historic buildings, cafes, and outdoor seating. The top right depicts a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers and a statue in front. The center right shows a stone mosque-like building with a prominent green dome. The bottom left has a monumental fountain or statue group with a central standing figure and two seated figures. The bottom right shows an ornate baroque/neo-baroque theater or opera house with domes and decorative facades. The word "PÉCS" is printed in large green letters across the lower left image.

Color postcard with a collage of three photographs on an orange background. The largest circular image shows a central square of a historic city with a domed former mosque, surrounding Baroque buildings, a column-like monument in the square, parked cars, and hills in the distance. Two smaller rectangular photos show modern high‑rise apartment blocks and a commercial building in a newly developed district. The word "PÉCS" is printed on the front. The reverse side has handwritten text in blue ink, address lines, postage area with a Hungarian stamp featuring peaches and the inscription "MAGYAR POSTA 2 Ft", and printed publishing information.

Multiview color postcard showing sights of the Hungarian city of Pécs. The upper images depict sections of medieval stone fortifications with round towers and an arched entrance. The lower left image shows the front of the Romanesque Pécs Cathedral with its four towers and a large statue standing in the square before it. The lower right image shows a full‑figure bronze statue of a man in a coat in a park setting. The reverse side has standard postcard address lines and Hungarian printing information, including the city name PÉCS and publisher details.

Multi‑view color postcard with an orange border featuring five photographs from Pécs: landscaped gardens with modern sculptures, a colorful geometric outdoor sculpture in front of a stone building, a tall TV/observation tower on a forested hill, and two modernist multi‑storey buildings surrounded by greenery. The back includes handwritten text, a Hungarian stamp showing fruit and labeled "MAGYAR POSTA 2 Ft", printed information in Hungarian, and address lines.

A multi-view color postcard with a blue border. The front features three main photographs and one small circular inset. The top image shows a modern terraced concrete building on a hillside. The middle image presents a central square with formal flower beds and paths; in the background stands a large stone building with a green dome (the former mosque in the main square), surrounded by historic facades and a statue. The bottom image shows a large modern housing or civic complex with white façades and multiple stories, set behind a landscaped park. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with address lines and stamp boxes, printed text identifying the place and publisher details.

A monochrome postcard showing an exhibition ground with long pavilions, a small octagonal kiosk with a tall pointed roof in the foreground, rows of empty chairs along wide avenues, a few people standing, and hills in the background. The printed caption in Hungarian at the top right mentions the Pécs national exhibition and its machine hall and ceremonial hall. The reverse side is a classic divided-back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating 'postcard', a circular stamp dated 1907 referring to the same exhibition, and a photographer's credit at the bottom.

Old black‑and‑white postcard showing a group of pavilion-style buildings with ornate wooden gables and fences, set behind a lawn planted with small conifer trees and with hills in the background. Red Hungarian captions at the top read about a domestic industry exhibition and the national exhibition in Pécs. The reverse side is a typical early‑20th‑century divided back with Hungarian text, a 1907 postmark and stamp, and a circular cachet mentioning the Pécs national exhibition.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing an ornate exhibition pavilion with arched windows and decorative rooflines, set in landscaped gardens with trees, shrubs, and lampposts. A tall flagpole with a long vertical flag stands in front. The red printed Hungarian captions at the top read "Pécsi országos kiállítás" and "Közoktatásügyi pavillon." The reverse side is a typical divided back with the heading "LEVELEZŐ LAP" and a credit line at the bottom.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing pavilion‑style exhibition buildings in a landscaped park with paths and flowerbeds, set against low hills. The wooden pavilions have tall, ornate towers and spires. Two women in long skirts and hats walk on a path in the foreground. Red printed Hungarian text appears at the top, and the reverse side has a typical divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian wording.

Vintage sepia postcard with Hungarian text. The front shows a pavilion‑like exhibition building with multiple tiered roofs and an entrance gate, likely a temporary structure on exhibition grounds. People stand at the entrance; the surroundings are open grounds with paths and some construction materials. The reverse side has a typical divided‑back layout with Hungarian headings and space for address and stamp.

Black-and-white panoramic view over a historic European city with dense low rooftops in the foreground and a large Romanesque cathedral with four tall square towers and spires prominently visible on the right side. At the bottom left the caption "Pécs" appears, and at the bottom right the word "Látkép" (Hungarian for 'view'). The reverse side shows a divided-back postcard layout with Hungarian handwriting, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and the printer's mark "Barasits Budapest".

A vintage-style advertising postcard featuring an illustrated woman with long dark hair wrapped in a red garment, standing next to a bar of soap shown in perspective. The background is beige, with bold black and red lettering in a decorative early‑20th‑century style. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with place for a stamp and address, and a short printed caption in Hungarian at the bottom.

Color postcard showing a dramatic sunset behind four dark church towers with spires topped by crosses, framed by a thin border. The word "Pécs" appears at the top of the image. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with address lines on the right and printed information about the publisher at the bottom.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy central square with horse-drawn carriages, trees, and prominent historic buildings. A tall clock tower and ornate domed town hall dominate the skyline, with a column or monument and a church-like structure in the background. The caption at the bottom identifies the view as Pécs and Széchenyi Square with the Town Hall. The reverse side is blank, divided for address and message, with a small printer's mark.

Front: A vintage postcard with a large Hungarian tricolor flag (red‑white‑green) on a flagpole against a dark red background. Inside a rectangular inset is a black‑and‑white photograph of a bustling town square with market stalls, crowds of people, multi‑story historic buildings, and a church or town‑hall tower at the right.
