Under the photo is Hungarian text indicating greetings from Pécs and identifying the square as Széchenyi tér. Back: a typical undivided‑back style postcard layout with printed Hungarian text indicating it is a postcard and the name of the printer/publisher.

Color postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a church that was formerly a mosque. The view is toward the altar with a white marble altarpiece, crucifix, and arched windows framed by alternating red‑and‑white voussoirs reminiscent of Islamic architecture. Large wall murals depict Christ and religious scenes with soldiers, clergy, and nuns. The back side has multilingual printed text identifying the place, address lines, and stamp boxes.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a busy town square with horse‑drawn carriages, pedestrians, a central monument and surrounding multi‑storey buildings. Two church towers or clocktowers rise above the square. The caption at the bottom reads "Széchényi tér", and at the top right "Üdvözlet Pécsről". The reverse side bears the printed word "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and address lines, with a blank stamp box.

Fold-out postcard with a printed map of the Pécs Zoo (Állatkert) and surroundings in Pécs, Hungary. One side shows a colorful illustrated plan of the zoo with animal drawings (tiger, snake, birds, bison, deer, otter, wolf, etc.), paths, buildings, enclosures and labels for features such as the aquarium, terrarium, education room, entrance and nearby streets. The reverse side has typical postcard layout with address lines, stamp boxes, printed ticket information and opening hours for the zoo and adjacent amusement park, along with the location name 'Mecseki Kultúrpark, Pécs'.

The postcard front shows the façade of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with two tall square towers flanking a long nave with a greenish copper roof. In the foreground are trees and a stepped plaza with people walking. An inset image at the top center depicts a richly decorated golden reliquary resembling a miniature Gothic chapel. The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard layout with multilingual printed text describing a national display of the Holy Right Hand at the cathedral in Pécs in 1988.

Multi-view black-and-white postcard showing scenes from the lakeside resort of Fonyód-Sándortelep at Lake Balaton. The front is divided into several photographs: a long stone pier (móló) crowded with bathers leading into the lake; a large building labeled as the Erzsébet girls' orphanage holiday resort; an oval central view of people sunbathing along the pier; a children's holiday camp of the city of Pécs; and a harbor scene with a steamship and small boats at the kikötő (port). The reverse side has printed Hungarian and German text naming Bad Fonyód-Sándortelep and a slogan 'Nyaraljon Fonyódon!' with a Hungarian postage stamp and handwritten Hungarian message and address.

A monochrome printed postcard showing a line drawing of a church complex in a valley landscape. The church has a tall, narrow bell tower with a pyramidal roof topped by a cross, and an attached basilica-style nave with a large circular window above the entrance. In front is an arcade of rounded arches. A road curves around the complex, and low hills or mountains rise in the background under large, stylized clouds. In the lower corners are small handwritten elements, including what appears to be a year and a signature.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a garden walkway lined with large statues of robed apostles set on a high terrace wall beside a historic building. Several people, likely seminarians, sit and stand along the shaded path below the statues. Handwritten Hungarian caption appears at the bottom of the image. The reverse side has a Hungarian postage stamp, postmark, printed Hungarian text, and a handwritten message and address.

Vintage multi‑view postcard with ornate floral borders. The front shows three black‑and‑white photographs: a central square with a large domed church labeled "Belvárosi székesegyház" (downtown cathedral), a city street scene labeled "Király uteza" (Király Street), and a church or convent building labeled "Zárda." At the top left is the Hungarian greeting "Üdvözlet Pécsről" and at the top right a German banner "Gruss aus Fünfkirchen." The right side contains a handwritten message in brown ink. The reverse side reads "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA. LEVELEZŐ‑LAP." with address lines filled in German cursive, including an address in Vienna, and several postal cancellation marks.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large, ornate corner palace-style building with mansard roof and rich Neo-Renaissance/Neo-Baroque details, labeled as Dr. Löwy's palace. Trees and a paved street surround the building. Hungarian text appears below the image and along the left margin. The reverse side is blank and printed with Hungarian words for postcard and address lines.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy city square with a circular flowerbed and an ornate stone fountain in the foreground. People walk and cycle around the square, and buses are visible on the street. In the background stands a large domed building that was formerly a mosque, fronted by surrounding historic buildings with shops at street level. The reverse side has standard postcard address lines and printed Hungarian text indicating greetings from the city of Pécs.

Black-and-white postcard view of a central square with broad stone steps, flower beds and people sitting around. On the right stands a large, ornate multi‑storey hotel building with balconies and an inscription on the pediment reading "NÁDOR SZÁLLÓ" topped by a star. To the left is an older church-like building. The reverse side of the postcard has printed Hungarian text identifying the scene, space for a message and address, and an outlined box for a stamp.

A commercial postcard front showing a colorful historic square with ornate buildings, a tall clock tower, and a large baroque-style column monument with statues. The right half of the front is a grey design panel with printed text indicating it is a Pécs postcard collection by Ars Una Studio. The back side is a standard unused postcard layout with space for a message and address, marked with the city name Pécs and publisher details.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square with wide stone steps, low walls built of rough stone blocks, and a landscaped public area with benches and people sitting and walking. In the background stand several multi‑storey historic buildings with ornate façades; one has an inscription on its pediment and a five‑pointed star on top, indicating the socialist era. On the left edge part of an older church‑like building and a monument with a statue are visible. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with Hungarian text identifying the view and the publisher, plus a printed price.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the interior of a small Catholic chapel with wooden pews facing an ornate altar. The altar is richly decorated with statues, framed religious images, flowers, candles, and patterned drapes. Above the altar are several angel figures along the upper wall. The reverse side has printed and handwritten Hungarian text, with printed description at upper left and purple ink handwriting covering much of the card.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and an arcaded façade, set in a town with hills in the background. Handwritten-style caption at the bottom reads "Pécs-Székesegyház." The reverse side is a typical divided-back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating rights reserved and the publisher's details.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a large cathedral with vaulted ceilings, ornate arches, frescoes, and an elaborate high altar approached by several stairways. At the bottom left of the front image is a printed caption. The reverse side shows typical postcard layout with Hungarian text, a Hungarian stamp, postmark, address lines, and handwritten message.

The postcard front shows a tall lookout tower surrounded by green trees under a clear blue sky. The lower part of the tower is a rough stone cylinder that spirals upward, topped by a smoother concrete shaft and a green-roofed, enclosed observation deck. The back of the postcard is blank aside from standard postcard layout elements and a printed caption along the left edge.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large multi‑storey academic building complex on a street corner. The architecture is early‑20th‑century, with stone base, plastered upper floors, and a towered section further along the street. Trees and lampposts line the road. At the bottom of the image the words "Pécs" and "Központi Egyetem" are printed. The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, a Hungarian postage stamp, a circular postmark, and printed postcard layout elements.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-storey stone and brick institutional building with arched windows and a central entrance framed by trees and a landscaped square. The image is bordered in white with handwritten-style captions at the bottom. The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, address lines, a printed instruction box about postage, and a publisher mark from Budapest.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing stone ruins on a hill surrounded by vegetation, with two small human figures near an arched opening. The front caption at the bottom reads "Pécs" on the left and "Tettyei romok" on the right. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address, and a magenta Hungarian postage stamp marked "MAGYARORSZÁG 8 FILLÉR", with a circular postmark from Pécs dated November 24, 1928. Printer information "Barasits Budapest" and a copyright line with the year 1927 appear at the bottom.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows the hall or lounge of a hotel with armchairs and tables, large windows with lace curtains, potted plants and a wall‑sized pastoral mural depicting trees, water and swans. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text identifying the location, publisher information from Budapest, a price in forints, and handwritten Hungarian correspondence and address, along with a partially visible postmark and stamp area.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large neo‑Gothic/neo‑Romanesque school building with an attached church or chapel and prominent tower. In the foreground a group of uniformed boys or scouts march in formation along the street. The caption at the bottom identifies the location as Pécs and the institution as the Pius Gymnasium. The reverse side is a typical divided postcard back with Hungarian text, printer's mark, and a note about postage.

A multi-view color postcard featuring various landmarks and street scenes from the city of Pécs. The front shows a collage: a road with a railing and the towers of a cathedral in the distance, historic buildings around a central monument in a square, garden views with sculptures and the façade of a cathedral, an Ottoman-era mosque with a green dome, outdoor cafés, and a decorative close-up detail. At the top is the word 'PÉCS' over a tricolor background resembling the Hungarian flag and the outline map of Hungary. The back is a standard unused postcard layout with a vertical publisher imprint and a barcode.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a two‑storey, U‑shaped barracks building surrounding a bare yard. The structure has a tiled roof with several chimneys and a continuous arcade on both levels, with arched openings. Leafless trees and a simple wooden structure stand in the yard, and a few people are visible. At the lower left of the image side the word "Pécs" is printed, and at the lower right "Fejérváry laktanya" is printed. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address area, a green Hungarian postage stamp, and a circular postal cancellation.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows a panoramic view over the historic center of Pécs framed by tree branches, with church towers and a dome rising above old city walls and rooftops; hills and fields appear in the distance. At the bottom of the image there is a Hungarian caption printed in white. The reverse side has a green Hungarian postage stamp, circular postmark, printed address lines, a typed address to Dr. Fábry Lajos in Budapest, and a handwritten Hungarian message.

A sepia-toned historic street scene showing a large ornate late‑19th‑century bank or savings building on a city square, with horse‑drawn carriages, pedestrians, trees, and a sculpted column or monument in the foreground. The façade of the main building bears Hungarian inscriptions, and printed captions at the bottom identify the location and the institution. The reverse side is a blank divided-back postcard with Hungarian text for 'postcard' and the publisher's line along the left edge.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a long, tree‑lined avenue leading towards the center of a town with hills in the background. On the right side stands a prominent church with a tall spire and arched windows, surrounded by low buildings and fenced open ground covered with circus posters. A horse‑drawn carriage and a few pedestrians are visible on the wide street. The front has printed captions at the top reading "Pécs" on the left and "Látkép" on the right. The reverse side is a divided back postcard in Hungarian, labeled "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP," with address lines and a small imprint of the publisher at the bottom.

Color postcard showing an ornate stone fountain with a tall, richly decorated central pillar topped by a small roof-like structure. Around the base are four bronze animal heads (likely oxen) spouting water into a circular basin. The fountain stands in a flower bed in front of a historic building with arched windows and doorways. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, an orange Hungarian postage stamp, and printed caption information along the edge.

Color postcard showing a busy central square with a decorative Zsolnay fountain in the foreground, featuring ornate ceramic details and animal heads. Surrounding it are flower beds, 1960s-era cars, buses, and pedestrians. In the background stands a domed former mosque on a hill-facing square with additional statues and buildings. The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, a red Hungarian stamp, and printed captions indicating the subject of the card.

Black-and-white historic postcard showing an ornate multi-storey neo-baroque/neo-renaissance bank building on a large square with people walking, a horse-drawn cart, and a monumental fountain or statue group in the foreground. Hungarian text is printed below the image and along the left edge, identifying the scene as the savings bank palace in Pécs.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard. One side shows a rural landscape with hills and trees in the background, and in the foreground a traditional well with a long wooden sweep (draw‑well) beside low stone walls; Hungarian postage stamps are affixed in the lower right corner. The other side contains handwritten correspondence in Hungarian, an address written in French to a recipient in Paris, and a blue airmail label reading "LÉGI POSTA PAR AVION." The correspondence side is dated 1931 and mentions Pécs, Hungary.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand historic city hall building with a tall clock tower dominating a public square filled with horse‑drawn carriages and people. Smaller buildings and a church‑like structure frame the square. The front has the printed captions "Pécs" at the upper left and "Városháza" at the upper right. The reverse side is a standard divided‑back postcard layout with vertical Hungarian text along the left indicating a Budapest publisher and a small boxed logo with the letters "K. R." near the bottom.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large, ornate multi‑storey institutional building with Baroque Revival elements, a central entrance, and two prominent end pavilions. A fence and sidewalk run along the front, with a few pedestrians visible. The caption beneath the image is in Hungarian. The reverse side is blank except for pre‑printed Hungarian text and address lines.

Vintage black‑and‑white panoramic view of a broad, tree‑lined avenue in a European city, with church spires and historic buildings on both sides and hills in the background. At the top corners are printed words in red, and there is a handwritten date. The reverse side is a classic divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating it is a correspondence card published in Pécs.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a garden scene at a girls' gymnasium boarding school run by nuns. In the park, schoolgirls in dark uniforms and nuns in habits sit at outdoor tables reading or writing, while others stand or walk along a curved path bordered by flowerbeds and trees. The reverse side is laid out as a divided back postcard, printed in Hungarian, with space for address and message.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over a hilly mining landscape with scattered houses and industrial buildings in a valley, likely a coal‑mining settlement near Pécs, Hungary. The reverse side is printed as a divided postcard with Hungarian text and small sections for address and message.

Vintage divided‑back postcard with embossed floral Art Nouveau border. The front shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a grand, multi‑storey historic building framed by decorative blue flowers and green stems. At the bottom of the image and in the margin there is Hungarian text indicating greetings from the city of Pécs. The reverse bears standard multilingual postcard headings of the Universal Postal Union era.

Multi-view black-and-white postcard showing several landmarks of a city: a large Romanesque cathedral with four towers and a terraced fountain in front, panoramic views over a hilly city with a prominent cross on a rocky outcrop, modern public buildings and squares, a curving road around a hillside complex, a lookout tower in a wooded area, a decorative urn in a park, and a large outdoor swimming pool. At the bottom front, Hungarian text reads "ÜDVÖZLET PÉCSRŐL." The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text in red ink, a Hungarian stamp, postmark, and printed publisher details.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a broad, almost empty street flanked by large institutional buildings with classical facades and a central tower-like structure in the distance. The printed caption at the top identifies the location as the Royal Elizabeth University of Sciences in Pécs. The reverse side is an unused divided back with space for address and message, and a vertical imprint naming the publisher.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a wide street lined with low houses and taller buildings, with hills in the background. People are walking and standing in the middle of the street. On the right side a building bears a large painted advertisement and a tower-like structure. The front is filled with handwritten text in Hungarian above and below the image. The caption below the picture reads "Indóház-utczа." and also "Kiadó Fischer Ferencz Pécsett." The reverse side has multi‑language headings for "Post Card" and an address written in ornate script, including the name "Szilágyi János" and place "Hidvég".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a monumental statue complex in a square. A tall pedestal supports a standing male figure in a long coat, with additional seated figures around the base. Behind the monument are low, traditional buildings with tiled roofs. The front of the card has red printed captions at the top identifying the location and subject in Hungarian. The reverse side is blank except for printed Hungarian text and layout lines typical of early 20th‑century postcards.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a simple, long interior corridor with tiled floor and rows of tall white cupboards or wardrobes on both sides, leading toward a window with a potted plant and small tables at the far end. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text describing the scene and a standard divided‑back layout for address and stamp.

Vintage colored postcard showing a grand multi‑story historicist building with ornate façades and red-tiled roofs, looking over a tree‑filled area and several surrounding buildings. The sky is softly tinted blue and pink. Hungarian text identifying the scene appears at the top right of the image. The reverse side is blank except for printed Hungarian heading and dividing lines typical of an early 20th‑century postcard.

Colorized view of stone ruins standing alone in an open grassy park, with a curving dirt path in the foreground. Trees and a few hillside houses appear in the background, along with a small pavilion-like building to the right. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text indicating the location and publisher, laid out in the typical divided-back postcard format.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a formal park with a large oval reflecting pool bordered by low stone walls and manicured shrubs. Tall poplar trees and other greenery encircle the water, and a low modern-style building stands in the background near the far edge of the pool. The reverse side has Hungarian printed text indicating the location, a handwritten message and address, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a long, ornate multi‑storey historic building behind a fence and young trees. Two small figures walk along the street in the foreground. The caption at the bottom reads "Pécs Hadapród iskola." The reverse side has a green Hungarian 5 fillér stamp, handwritten Hungarian text, and an address in Budapest.

A vintage multi-view postcard showing four black‑and‑white photographs of an outdoor bath and park complex with pavilions, pools and landscaped walkways. The main building has a domed central rotunda and surrounding wings; other views show a large swimming pool, stone balustrades, and people walking in the bath grounds. At the bottom of the picture side the captions read "Pécs" and "Strandfürdő". The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, a Hungarian postage stamp labelled "MAGYAR POSTA", a pink propaganda cachet, and the Budapest-based publisher imprint MONOSTORY / KALANTAY.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a grand brick railway station complex with ornate facades, arched windows, and a central entrance pavilion topped by steep roofs and small towers. The words "Pécs" and "Indóház" are printed on the image side. The reverse side has Hungarian handwritten text, a green postage stamp labeled "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA 5 FILLER," postmarks, and the printed heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP."

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a street scene in front of a one‑storey neoclassical building with the name "MEISENZAHL" on its façade. Several men stand with horses; two are mounted and one holds a horse by the bridle, suggesting a horse‑trading or export business. The printed title text above the image reads in German: "MEISENZAHL PFERDE-EXPORT FÜNFKIRCHEN – PÉCS. Telegr.-Adresse: Meisenzahl, Fünfkirchen." The reverse side is a blank divided back with the Hungarian heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and a small imprint at the bottom right.

Colorized historic postcard showing a central square with a grand town hall building featuring a tall clock tower and green roof, a baroque column or monument in the foreground with horse‑drawn carriages around it, and other surrounding buildings and trees. The caption beneath the image reads in Hungarian. The reverse side is blank with standard postcard dividing line and address lines.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of the city of Pécs with hills in the background and an open field with a few people in the foreground. Prominent church towers rise above the cityscape. At the top it is captioned in Hungarian and German. The lower front margin bears a handwritten greeting and signature. The reverse side is printed as a correspondence card in Hungarian and addressed in elegant cursive handwriting, with a postmark from Pécs and a postage stamp.

Vintage colorized postcard showing a panoramic view over a town surrounded by green hills and cultivated fields. Red-roofed houses are scattered in the foreground, while in the center of the town a large church or cathedral with multiple towers is visible. The sky is blue with light clouds. On the top left the word "Pécs" is printed, and on the top right the word "Látkép" appears. The reverse side is an unused divided-back postcard with green printed guidelines for address and stamp.

A vintage color aerial view of a densely built historic city center with red‑tiled roofs, narrow streets and several prominent public buildings and squares. The reverse side is a divided‑back postcard with multilingual caption and Hungarian publisher information, price and photo credit.

Old sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-storey academic building on a street corner, with ornate façades and many windows. A towered section is visible further back along the right wing. The front of the image has a printed Hungarian caption identifying the building. The reverse side is a standard divided-back layout with printed Hungarian legal notice and publisher imprint.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large multi‑storey institutional building with a central tower-like section and statue in front, set behind a landscaped park or square. Decorative script at the bottom front reads "Üdvözlet Pécsről." The back is blank except for printed Hungarian text indicating the publisher and price, with standard postcard address lines.

Color postcard with a burgundy frame showing a statue in front of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with multiple towers and arched windows, bordered by a flowerbed of red tulips under a blue sky. The word "PÉCS" is printed prominently on the front. The reverse side has space for address and stamp, multilingual greetings from Pécs, a barcode, publisher information, and the word "Bazilika".

Advertising postcard for the Szent György Fogadó (Saint George Inn) in Pécs, Hungary. The front side shows a black‑and‑white photograph of the corner building that houses the inn, alongside a detailed street map of central Pécs with a marked location. At the bottom is an invitation line in Hungarian. The reverse side is a standard blank postcard layout with space for a stamp, address lines, and dividing line for message and address.

An illustrated industrial panorama showing a large leather factory complex with multiple long brick buildings, tall chimneys emitting smoke, smaller administrative houses, and surrounding fields with hills in the background. The factory is enclosed by fences and bordered by a rail or road line. Beneath the image is multilingual printed text in Hungarian, German, and French identifying the factory as the First Pécs Leather Factory joint-stock company, including its trade name "Sopianae" and founding date. The reverse side is a blank divided-back postcard layout with printed guidelines for address and message.

Two-sided vintage postcard. The front shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a large stone college building with arched windows and a central entrance staircase. At the top is the printed caption "EGYETEMI SZENT MÓR-KOLLEGIUM, PÉCS." indicating it is the Saint Maurus University College in Pécs. The reverse side contains handwritten text in Hungarian, a printed emblem of the institution, address lines, a Hungarian postage stamp, and postal cancellation marks.

Vintage color postcard showing stone ruins with a large arched opening and fragmented walls set on a grassy area with tall trees and hills in the background. Several men in early-20th‑century attire stand near the arch. The back side has handwritten text in Hungarian, postal markings, and space for the address. The front caption at the bottom identifies the location as Pécs‑Tettye and mentions details of the ruins.

Black‑and‑white industrial scene showing a large conical spoil tip or slag heap with a long conveyor running up its side, surrounded by factory buildings, smokestacks, smaller houses, and fenced fields in the foreground. The view is partly framed by a metal structure and gauge on the right, suggesting it is taken from within the industrial complex. The reverse side is a divided‑back postcard with Hungarian text identifying the publisher or photographer in Pécs.

Sepia-toned photographic postcard showing an outdoor crucifix on a rocky, possibly snowy hill. A woman in traditional clothing kneels and prays at the base of the cross. Handwritten text in Hungarian appears below the image, and the reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard layout with printed publisher information in Hungarian.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a domed religious building with a large metal-clad dome topped by a cross. The façade has an arched entrance, statues, and a prominent cross in the entryway. Ivy covers parts of the walls. In front of the building there are early 20th‑century automobiles parked on the street. The reverse side is a divided back with space for address and message and a small printer's logo composed of the letters "L K" or "L K S" in a box.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a tall stone lookout tower with a balcony and upper structure, attached to a lower building, surrounded by trees and rocks. The front caption identifies the location as the Misina Riesz József lookout at 534 meters in the Mecsek hills near Pécs. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, an address, and a postmark from Pécs.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over a valley with coal mining facilities, spoil heaps and small settlements, framed on the left by a pine tree. Low, forested hills rise in the background. On the front lower left, handwritten-style text reads "Pécs. Szénbányatelepek." The reverse side is an unused divided postcard back with printed Hungarian text and space for the address.

Sepia-toned photograph of a vintage city bus at a bus stop. The bus has rounded 1960s-style bodywork with twin headlamps on each side and a large front grille. Route number 31 is displayed above the windscreen. A bus stop pole with a timetable is visible in the foreground. The license plate on the bus reads "GC-84-40" and a circular logo with text is painted on the side of the vehicle. Residential buildings with tiled roofs appear in the background.

Vintage divided‑back postcard printed in Hungarian. The address side has the heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and handwritten blue-ink script with a green postage stamp cancelled in 1911. The picture side shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a grand, ornate multi‑storey historicist building behind a decorative entrance gate with lamps. At the bottom of the image the caption identifies the scene in Hungarian.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy, narrow urban street lined with multi‑story historic buildings and shopfronts. Hanging shop signs and pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing are visible. A church with a tower stands further down the street in the center background. At the top of the image, printed in red, are the words "Pécs" and "Király-utca." The reverse side is formatted as a divided postcard with printed heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and handwritten Hungarian text, addressed to someone in Budapest.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard. The front shows a panoramic view of a hilly, wooded area with a winding road, scattered houses and tall trees. In the foreground are prominent stone ruins on an open plateau. At the bottom margin, Hungarian text identifies the location as part of the Mecsek hills near Pécs. The reverse side contains a handwritten Hungarian message, an address in Budapest, a printed Hungarian postage instruction box, and a circular postal cancellation mark.

Vintage black-and-white postcard showing a monumental statue ensemble on a richly decorated pedestal and fountain basin. A standing male figure in a long coat dominates the top, while several seated figures are positioned around the lower part of the structure. Rooftops and a tall tree appear in the background. The reverse side is a standard divided back with printed Hungarian text indicating the subject and publisher information.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over the rooftops of a town toward a large Romanesque cathedral with four tall square towers. Vegetation frames the foreground, while the city and distant landscape stretch into the haze. The caption at the bottom front identifies the view and city in Hungarian. The reverse side is an unused divided‑back postcard printed in Hungarian, with space for address and stamp and a small printer's mark from Budapest.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a busy central square with a large ornate fountain in the middle, surrounded by crowds of people in early 20th‑century clothing, horse‑drawn carriages and a tram. Multi‑story historic buildings with shops and awnings line the square. The captions at the bottom identify the place as Pécs and the square as Széchenyi tér. The reverse side is blank with the usual divided‑back layout for address and message, and a small publisher's logo at the bottom.

Vintage sepia postcard showing an ornate historic theatre building with domes and rich Neo-Baroque decoration. The structure has a large central dome, side domes, grand staircases, arched windows and classical columns on the façade. At the bottom margin of the image, Hungarian text identifies the location and building.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with two photographs on the front: the upper image shows an indoor swimming pool (long narrow hall with tiled floor, railing and large windows); the lower image depicts a school gymnasium with boys practicing gymnastics on apparatus such as a pommel horse and wall bars. Captions in Hungarian label the pool and gym and identify the institution as the Pius College in Pécs. The reverse side is an unused divided‑back postcard with Hungarian printing instructions and publisher information from Budapest, mentioning a Jesuit gymnasium, boarding school and residence.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows three images: on the left a bust of Count Gyula Zichy, in the center the richly decorated main altar of a church with a statue of Christ and ornamental railings, and on the right a bust of Pope Pius X. Hungarian captions identify the figures and scenes, and at the bottom the city name "Pécs" and the institution name "It. Pius-Kollégium" are printed. The reverse has the typical divided postcard layout with Hungarian printing, including a note about domestic postage rates and the printer's mark from Budapest.

Vintage multi‑view postcard showing four interior photographs of a Jesuit boys' college: a grand assembly hall with rows of chairs and a stage, a richly decorated chapel with altar and wall paintings, a recreation room where boys in uniforms play table tennis and other games, and a large classroom with many wooden desks where students are studying. Hungarian captions label each view and identify the institution as the Pius College in Pécs. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back printed in Hungarian, dated 1933 and crediting the Budapest publisher Monostory György.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a broad public square with a large Baroque-style plague column or fountain in the center and an ornate historic town hall building with a clock tower on the right. Several pedestrians stand in the open square. The front bottom margin carries handwritten-style captions that read "Pécs" on the left and "Városháza" on the right. The reverse side is a classic divided postcard back with address lines and stamp box, printed with publisher information in Hungarian.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a hilly, terraced landscape with vineyards and scattered houses. On the upper left stands a large multi‑storey modernist hotel building on the hillside. On the upper right there is a tall monument or statue on a small peak. The foreground shows a road with a rustic wooden guardrail curving along the slope. The reverse side is a divided postcard back with printed Hungarian text indicating Pécs and the Mecsek Hotel, a postmark, and publisher information.

The postcard's front shows an old black‑and‑white photograph of a broad European square bordered by multi‑storey classical buildings. In the center right stands an ornate Baroque column with statues and a sunburst at the top, surrounded by a low fence and steps. Behind it is a large church with a domed roof and a tall, slender bell tower. Horse‑drawn carriages and a few pedestrians occupy the largely unpaved square, with trees and benches scattered around. The reverse side is a standard modern postcard layout, with printed lines for the address and stamp, and printed text identifying the place and publisher.

Colorized historic street view of a European city showing a narrow cobblestone street lined with multi‑story shopfronts and ornate façades. Hanging signs in Hungarian advertise various businesses. In the background stands a baroque church or chapel with twin green domes. The top of the front side bears printed red text identifying the location. The reverse side is blank except for printed Hungarian words indicating it is a postcard and a publisher line at the bottom.

Colorized postcard showing a large, ornate multi‑storey historicist building with red roofs and elaborate corner pavilions, seen behind a red‑brick and iron fence lined with young trees. The sky is bright blue with scattered clouds. At the top left of the image is printed red text in Hungarian: "Pécs.  M. kir. honvéd hadapród iskola". The reverse side has the printed word "Levelezőlap" (postcard) and green side text "Karpf Béla, Pécs", a green Hungarian stamp, postal markings, and handwritten Hungarian message and address dated 1915, including "Pécs" and "Budapesten".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing an aerial or elevated view of a modernist multi‑storey hotel complex on a curved mountain road surrounded by forest. The building has long balconies, a flat roof, and a terrace with rows of deck chairs. At the bottom of the image, handwritten text identifies the place. The reverse side is divided for message and address, written in blue ink in Hungarian, with a Hungarian postage stamp and postmark.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a domed building with a cross on top and an adjacent slender Ottoman‑style minaret rising above trees and nearby houses. The front caption at the bottom reads "Pécs. Török minaret." The reverse side has handwritten text in blue ink in Hungarian, a Hungarian postage stamp, and postal cancellations.

A vintage black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The front is divided into nine small photographs showing various sights of a city: a skyline with a large four‑towered cathedral, civic and university‑style buildings, a church with a tall clock tower, a landscaped lake or pond, a busy swimming pool or bathing beach, hillside buildings, a modernist complex with a tall mast or monument, and a central square with a fountain and a statue. The back has standard postcard layout with space for message, address lines, a dotted stamp box, and printed Hungarian text and publisher's mark.

A vintage divided-back postcard. The front shows a colorized street scene with several multi‑storey buildings and horse‑drawn carriages in front. The central building is labeled as the Nádor Hotel. Bare trees line the wide street. On the message side, there is printed Hungarian text "Levelező-Lap" and a Budapest postmark dated August 20, 1908, along with handwritten Hungarian correspondence and address details.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large historic building complex with an ornate façade and a tall clock/bell tower on a city square. The building has Baroque and eclectic architectural details and houses street-level shops. In the upper left corner the printed word "Városház." appears, and in the upper right corner "Pécs." The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, a green Hungarian postage stamp, postmarks, and the printed heading "LEVELEZŐ LAP" along with a publisher line at the bottom.

A vintage multi-view postcard with a dark border and a central scroll bearing a greeting in Hungarian, surrounded by small black-and-white photographs of notable sites in and around the city of Pécs. Each vignette is captioned in Hungarian, showing buildings such as a mausoleum, hotel, theater, school, church, city square, Roman ruins, and villa-lined street. The reverse side has the typical divided-back layout with the printed word 'Levelező-lap', handwritten cursive message and address lines, and a green Hungarian postage stamp canceled with a PÉCS postmark.

Two-sided vintage postcard with a collage of small tinted photographs of various city landmarks arranged on a dark background. Each view has a red Hungarian caption, such as streets, squares, public buildings, and churches. The reverse side shows Hungarian handwritten text in purple ink, a green 5‑fillér stamp, red printed headings, and address lines.

Color postcard showing a panoramic view of a central square in a historic European city. In the foreground is a large paved square with a column-like monument. On the right stands a distinctive historic building with a large blue-green dome – a former mosque – surrounded by a curved street lined with parked cars from the late 20th century. On the left is a long Baroque-style building with a red-tiled roof, and in the distance a cathedral with four tall towers is visible above the rooftops. The lower border of the card bears the word "PÉCS" in large serif letters. The reverse side is a standard unused postcard layout with address lines, stamp boxes and publisher information.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a lively street scene in a historic European city. On the right are ornate multi‑storey buildings with elaborate facades; at the end of the street stands a large domed building in a square, with hills visible in the distance. People, buses and a tram are in the foreground, suggesting an active urban centre. Below the image is the printed caption in Hungarian, and the reverse side has a Hungarian postage stamp, postmark, printed publisher information, and handwritten Hungarian text and address lines.

Sepia-toned historical image showing a large military parade moving through a narrow city street lined with multi‑story buildings. Soldiers in uniform march in formation, many carrying drums, while dense crowds fill the sidewalks. Numerous flags hang from the façades, prominently including French tricolours and at least one American flag. A shop sign reading "AU BON …" is visible on the right-hand side. The overall look is of an early 20th‑century celebration or victory parade in a French city.

Black‑and‑white historical postcard showing a military parade through a city street. A large open automobile filled with uniformed officers drives past lines of soldiers with rifles and a dense crowd of civilians. Flags are visible among the crowd, and shopfronts with French and German signage appear in the background. A printed caption runs along the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white vintage image showing a group of World War I–era soldiers walking arm‑in‑arm with young women in regional folk costumes along a narrow city street lined with buildings and flags. The mood appears festive, as if celebrating liberation or a victory parade. The scene is photographed from the front, capturing several passersby and hanging flags high above the street.

Black‑and‑white historical postcard showing a crowded street parade with soldiers on horseback and many civilians. Young girls in traditional Alsatian dress walk in the foreground. The background features old timber‑framed buildings with signs, flags, and watching crowds at the windows. Caption text at the bottom identifies the scene as the solemn entry of Marshal Pétain into Strasbourg on 25 November 1918.

A sepia-toned historical postcard showing a French military parade entering a city. In the center, a high-ranking officer (Général Gouraud) rides a white horse, accompanied by other officers on foot and horseback, followed by troops in World War I-era French uniforms and helmets. They march along a street or bridge with tram tracks, lined by balustrades and multi‑story European buildings in the background. Printed caption text in French appears at the bottom, along with the publisher's credit and a date from 1918.

A black-and-white historical postcard showing a large military parade of infantry soldiers marching along a cobblestone street lined with dense crowds. The background is a grand classical building with arched ground-floor windows and circular dormer windows on the roof, heavily decorated and filled with spectators at the windows and on the roof. Flags hang from poles and the building, and the scene is clearly celebratory. Printed French text at the top describes the solemn entry of Marshal Pétain on 25 November 1918 and the infantry parade at Place Kléber in Strasbourg. There is also a small publisher's credit at the bottom.

Illustrated postcard showing the skyline of Strasbourg with the tall Gothic spire of Strasbourg Cathedral rising above the city. To the right, large white storks fly across the sky carrying French tricolor flags with golden fringes and symbols, evoking liberation or national celebration. The dates 1870 and 1918 flank the cathedral, and the word 'Strasbourg' appears in decorative script. A small artist signature is at the lower right.

Monochrome postcard showing a grand military parade passing in front of an ornate neo‑Renaissance stone building. Cavalry officers ride horses along a broad avenue while large crowds of civilians and soldiers watch from the street, the steps, balconies, and windows of the building. The façade features rusticated stonework, arched windows, heavy balustrades, and large sculpted atlantes supporting the balcony. The image is bordered below by a tonal scale and measurement marks, suggesting this is a reproduction of an old postcard.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large military parade passing in front of an ornate neo‑Renaissance stone building. Infantry soldiers wearing early 20th‑century uniforms and helmets march with rifles, while a mounted officer on horseback rides at the front. A dense crowd of civilians watches from the street and from balconies and windows of the grand façade behind them, which features arched windows, heavy rustication, sculpted figures and balustraded balconies. The overall impression is of a ceremonial review or victory parade in a European city.

Black-and-white wartime postcard showing several soldiers walking and standing in a village street with half-timbered houses and farm buildings in the background. Leafless trees and a fenced garden or yard appear on the right side. Printed caption text at the bottom identifies the scene as from the First World War in Alsace and names the village Traubach-le-Bas.

Black‑and‑white historical postcard showing a dense military parade of infantry soldiers marching with rifles along a city street lined with ornate multi‑story buildings and packed crowds of spectators. Several mounted officers on horseback accompany the troops. The scene is urban and celebratory. Printed caption text appears at the bottom in French, identifying the event and location as an infantry parade on Rue de la Mésange in Strasbourg on 22 November 1918.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a large military review or parade held in an open park or parade ground, surrounded by rows of soldiers and spectators. The scene is framed by leafless trees and townhouses in the background. Massed troops form large rectangular and circular formations around an open central area where officers and standard‑bearers are assembled. The postcard includes a printed French caption at the top describing the event in Colmar on 22 November 1918.

Black‑and‑white historical postcard showing a French general in uniform (identified in the caption as General Pétain) receiving a large bouquet of flowers from a young Alsatian girl in traditional dress. Several officers stand around them, with a line of soldiers and a building façade with arched windows in the background. The caption is printed in both French and German at the bottom edge.

Black‑and‑white wartime postcard showing a damaged rural house with a sagging tiled roof and broken wooden walls, likely hit by artillery. Two soldiers in uniform stand in front of the ruined building; bare trees and a muddy, cratered foreground suggest a World War I battlefield landscape. Printed French text appears along the bottom margin identifying the publisher and the location in Alsace.

A monochrome historical postcard showing a large military parade on a cobbled street lined with tram tracks. Horse‑drawn field artillery and mounted soldiers move from left to right while dense crowds of civilians watch from the sidewalks. Leafless trees and park‑like surroundings suggest late autumn or winter. Printed text at the bottom identifies the scene as a parade of field artillery in Colmar on 22 November 1918.

A sepia-toned historical postcard showing a dense street procession of French soldiers and musicians marching through a crowded city street lined with traditional half-timbered houses. Flags hang from the buildings and large crowds celebrate on both sides of the street. The scene depicts the ceremonial entry of Marshal Pétain into Strasbourg on 25 November 1918, shortly after World War I.

A monochrome image showing a dense crowd gathered in a city street in front of an ornate stone building with large arched windows and balconies. The façade and balconies are decorated with multiple French tricolour flags and bunting. People crowd the balcony and entrance, suggesting a political or ceremonial event, possibly a speech or official reception. The scene feels early‑20th‑century, with men in hats and coats and an old-fashioned streetlamp at right. A gray scale and rulers are visible along the bottom edge, indicating later archival reproduction of the postcard.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a large military parade in front of a grand stone building with arched windows and balconies crowded with onlookers. In the foreground mounted soldiers ride horses past a dense crowd lining the street; many people wear early‑20th‑century clothing and military uniforms. The print border is rough‑cut, and scale bars for photographic reproduction appear at the bottom.

Illustrated wartime postcard showing German infantry with bayonets charging across rough ground toward burning village buildings in a mountainous, forested area. Several soldiers lie fallen in the foreground; in the distance a building marked "AUBERGE" is on fire. At the top is a German caption describing a battle near a specific height close to Markirch in Alsace.

A black‑and‑white wartime postcard showing American soldiers marching in formation through a large Parisian square, rifles on their shoulders and a U.S. flag at the front. In the background stands a monumental statue on a pedestal, surrounded by a grand neoclassical building with columns and arched ground floor, likely the Place de la Concorde area. The postcard includes bilingual French and English captions beneath the image, identifying the scene as an American troops parade before the Statue of Strasbourg in Paris on July 4th, 1918.

Black‑and‑white wartime photograph showing three uniformed men standing in front of a railcar or ambulance wagon marked with a Red Cross symbol. The man on the left wears a German-style uniform and peaked cap, the central figure is in a darker coat with rank stripes on the cuffs and a side cap, and the man on the right wears a lighter greatcoat and an Adrian-style helmet. At the bottom of the image there is handwritten text identifying the three men, and beneath the image a printed credit in French to the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire de Strasbourg.

Colorized panoramic view of a historic European city nestled in a valley surrounded by green mountains. The town shows dense red‑roofed buildings, church spires, a clock tower, and a large open square or field in the foreground. At the top of the image the caption reads "Brașov" and "Vedere generală" (General view). The reverse side is a classic divided postcard back printed with "România – Cartă Postală" and address lines, plus a purple rectangular stamp impression on the left.

Multi-view black-and-white postcard with five photographs of urban and landscaped scenes and a central vertical title. The largest central inscription on the picture side reads "BRASOV" in stylized letters. The images show grand classical and neoclassical buildings, a large formal park with paths and a central monument or fountain, panoramic views of a city set among hills or low mountains, and residential blocks. The reverse side contains handwritten text in blue ink in Romanian, postal cancellation marks, a stamp box, printed words indicating it is a postcard, and the publisher name "Editura Meridiane".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a central town hall building with a high clock tower topped by a bulbous dome and small lantern. The ground floor has shops and arcades, with a horse‑drawn cart and several pedestrians in the square in front. Printed captions in three languages at the bottom identify the building and town; handwritten message in ink covers part of the lower margin. The reverse side has the typical divided postcard layout with Hungarian text "LEVELEZŐ-LAP", address written in cursive, postage stamps and postmarks.

Colored postcard showing the rear view of a large convent complex with red-tiled roofs featuring distinctive eye‑shaped dormer windows, white and pastel building facades, a small tower with a spire, and lush gardens in the foreground. On the image side, printed titles in German and Hungarian read "Hermannstadt / Nagyszeben" and "Ursulinenkloster (Rückansicht) / Orsolya-zárda (Hátsó látképe)". The reverse side has handwritten text in Hungarian, a divided back with address lines, Romanian postage stamps, and a collector's stamp.

Vintage divided‑back postcard printed in black and white with decorative floral borders. The front shows two images: on the left, a group of people standing on a wooden terrace in front of a wooden building set against a rocky mountainside, labeled in German and Hungarian as the Bethlen Grotte/Bethlen barlang with its altitude; on the right, a tall commemorative column or monument on a hilltop, labeled in German as "Millenium-Denkmal" and in Hungarian as "Millenium emlék szobor." Below is the bilingual city name "Kronstadt — Brassó." The reverse has handwritten text in German, a printed word "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" (Hungarian for postcard), postal cancellations, and a green Hungarian stamp denominated in fillér.

Vintage real-photo postcard showing three people posed on a terrace or balcony: a seated man in a wicker chair wearing a suit, a younger man in a military-style uniform standing behind him with arms crossed, and a woman in a dark dress standing to the side. There is a railing with trees visible beyond it and a small table with potted plants against the wall. The reverse side has the typical divided-back layout for address and message, plus handwritten numbers and notes in pencil.

Colored postcard showing an outdoor scene in front of a one‑storey house with a red roof and a veranda supported by white columns. Several men, women and children sit and stand around tables under large trees, suggesting a rural guesthouse or inn. At the bottom of the image is the caption in German "Gruss aus dem Jungenwalde." The reverse side has handwritten text in German, an address, and a green Hungarian stamp postmarked with a circular cancellation that reads "NAGYSZEBEN".

Colorized panoramic view of the city of Brașov surrounded by hills. The foreground shows dense urban buildings with red roofs, while in the background a large green hill with structures on top dominates the scene. The caption "Brașov" appears below the image. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard layout with printed Romanian text indicating it is a postal card from Romania and a small line of publisher information dated 1930.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a cobblestoned square bordered by 2–3‑storey houses with shutters and shopfronts, large chestnut trees in bloom, and townspeople in late‑19th/early‑20th‑century dress. A horse‑drawn cart stands in the foreground. The caption at the top reads "Hermannstadt. Dragonerwache." The reverse side is printed with "LEVELEZŐ-LAP." and address lines, plus a small publisher line at the bottom and a purple ownership stamp.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a busy central square with many horse-drawn carriages and pedestrians. On the left dominates a large Gothic church with buttresses and a high roof; in front and to the right are multi-story townhouses with shops at street level bearing German-language signs. The reverse side has a divided back with printed trilingual heading "Brașov—Kronstadt—Brassó" and the publisher credit "Verlag H. Zeidner."

Colorized historic postcard showing the massive round White Tower (Turnul Alb) of Brașov with crenellated walls and a small red‑roofed annex. In the foreground, people in early‑20th‑century clothing stroll and sit on benches along a tree‑lined promenade; in the background appears part of the town and surrounding hills. The front caption names Brașov and the tower in multiple languages (Romanian, Hungarian, German). The reverse bears the bilingual heading for postcard/cardă poștală in Romanian and Hungarian.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a tree-lined boulevard with café tables and chairs arranged on a wide sidewalk in front of ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. People in early 20th‑century clothing stand near an open automobile, and more pedestrians walk along the street. In the background rises a tall church tower and other civic buildings. The caption at the bottom reads "Kronstadt. Rudolfsring." The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard with a purple oval stamp reading "LAZAR ERHOVITZ GALAȚI" and small vertical publisher text in German along the left edge.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a statue of a robed man standing on a pedestal in front of a large Gothic stone church wall with arched windows. Low railings and shrubs surround the monument. The front caption indicates it is the Honterus monument in Kronstadt (Brasov). The reverse is largely blank with a vertical publisher's imprint in German.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a fortified medieval church with a tall clock‑tower and steep roof, surrounded by the roofs of an old town and backed by forested hills. To the left stands a separate ruined stone tower on a grassy slope. The caption beneath the image names the place in Hungarian and German. The reverse side contains a green stamp, a circular postmark, printed Hungarian text, and handwritten German correspondence and address lines.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a broad, unpaved street lined with low townhouses in an old European town. A horse-drawn cart stands to the left and a few pedestrians walk along the right side near arched gateways. The image caption and city name are printed in German, Hungarian, and Romanian. The reverse side bears the Hungarian word for postcard "Levelező-lap" with dotted address lines and a purple postal stamp.

Vintage sepia-toned group photograph of dozens of schoolgirls and two adults posed outdoors in front of dense foliage. The girls wear sailor-style blouses with dark collars and large bows, and long skirts, while a seated man in a dark suit and a standing woman in a dark dress appear at the center beside a small table with a floral arrangement. The reverse side bears a purple studio stamp from "Atelier Diujanski 'Foto Arta' Blaj" and handwritten Romanian text noting the class, names, year 1924, and a note about a reunion in 1934.

Vintage sepia postcard with two photographic views of an outdoor restaurant/beer‑garden set among large trees. The left image shows rows of tables with white tablecloths and folding chairs, with a few staff or guests standing. The right image shows the veranda of a villa‑like building with ornate iron columns and railings, where many people pose around tables. Handwritten cursive text in German covers parts of the front. Printed captions identify the place as the "Drei‑Eichen" (Three Oaks) restaurant of Kovács, and the printer as being in Hermannstadt. The reverse side has the word "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP" (Hungarian for postcard), a Hungarian postage stamp marked "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA" and a circular postmark, along with an address written in German.

Vintage illustrated postcard showing a large multi‑winged institutional building with a chapel and bell tower on the right, set behind a fenced garden and tree‑lined street. The facade has three stories, gabled central sections, and numerous windows. Below the image is printed red text with the place name and a Hungarian caption about the institution, and the lower portion is filled with handwritten Hungarian correspondence. The reverse side has the heading 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP', address lines written in Hungarian, postal cancellations and a stamp from the Austro‑Hungarian period.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a cobblestone street lined with historic multi‑story buildings, shop signs and pedestrians with a cart in the foreground. At the end of the street rise two tall church towers. The caption at the top lists the city name in several languages and identifies the street. The reverse has typical postcard dividing lines and the Hungarian phrase 'LEVELEZŐ-LAP'.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large central square with a fountain in the middle, bordered by grand historic buildings. On the right is a long Baroque church or monastery with a tall tower topped by an onion dome; to its left stands an ornate multi‑storey corner building with elaborate façades and a pointed spire. The reverse side is printed with lines for address and the heading "România – Cartă Postală" along with the locality "Sibiu / Hermannstadt – Nagyszeben" and publisher details.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing multiple framed views of a fortified church complex. The upper images are labeled as the north and south sides of the church, with a tower and surrounding wall visible in a rural landscape. At the bottom left is a tall gate tower with a portcullis and people standing nearby, and at the bottom center is a close view of a Romanesque‑style church entrance. Floral graphics decorate the montage. The title at the top identifies the site as the fortified church of Holzmen­gen.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a bustling town square with horse-drawn carts and carriages in front of multi‑story historic buildings with shops at street level. Large neoclassical façades with columns line the right side; smaller houses and commercial buildings frame the left. The caption at the top reads "Mediaș – Mediasch". The reverse side carries the printed heading "România / Cartă Postală" and publisher information at the bottom.

Colorized street view of a grand boulevard lined with stately 19th‑century buildings and trees, with hills in the background. A prominent stone mansion with ornate façade and balcony stands on the right behind an iron fence. Pedestrians walk along the wide unpaved road. The front text at the top reads in German and Hungarian: "Kronstadt. — Brassó." and on the right "Rudolfring. — Rezső-körút." The reverse side shows handwritten correspondence in German, Hungarian postal markings and the Hungarian word for postcard "Levelező lap", addressed to Frl. Mausi Stenzel in Hermannstadt, Siebenbürgen.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a broad square with horse‑drawn carriages in front of a long, two‑storey barracks‑like building with a towered roof. Smaller townhouses and a defensive tower are visible in the background. The front text identifies the view as Hermannnsplatz with the imperial and royal infantry barracks and sends greetings from Hermannstadt. The back has printed lines for address and the Hungarian heading "Levelező-Lap."

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large, ornate late‑19th/early‑20th‑century courthouse or justice building on a city street. The multi‑storey structure has elaborate facades, steep roofs with dormers and finials, and arched windows; trees without leaves line the sidewalk and a few pedestrians walk along the street. The back of the card has typical divided postcard layout and printed captions in multiple languages.

Colorized historic street view showing a central square with a tall clock tower rising from the middle of attached buildings, surrounded by two‑ and three‑story houses with tiled roofs and shopfronts. Small groups of people stand in the cobbled street. The caption at the top lists the city name in Hungarian, German, and Romanian, and identifies the street. The reverse side has handwritten correspondence in German, a green postage stamp from the Kingdom of Hungary, and the printed word "Levelező‑lap."

Colored lithographic postcard showing a cobbled street lined with multi‑story historic buildings. Children and a few adults stand in the middle of the street. In the distance rise two tall church towers with onion‑shaped domes. A sign on the right reads "Foala Poporului." The captions at the bottom read "Hermannnstadt." and "Fleischergasse." A vertical imprint at the left margin credits the publisher and printer. The reverse side is blank except for printed Hungarian text "LEVELEZŐ-LAP" and standard address lines.

Vintage sepia-toned studio portrait of a young man in a military-style uniform with shoulder rank stripes, buttoned jacket, white shirt, and dark tie. The photo has softly faded edges. The reverse side is laid out as a classic divided-back postcard with a handwritten message in a Romance-language script and spaces for address, showing stains and aging.

Two-sided illustrated postcard. The picture side shows three small monochrome photographs framed with floral decoration: at left a tree‑lined path along a fortification labeled "Graft."; in the center a city gate and wall scene labeled "Waisenhausgässer‑Thor."; at right a canal with houses and trees labeled "Tömös‑Kanal." Beneath the center photo is the printed caption "Gruss aus Kronstadt." The card is heavily overprinted with handwritten German text and dated 4.VI.1909. The address side has the printed Hungarian word "LEVELEZŐ‑LAP." at the top, a green 5‑fillér Hungarian stamp, multiple postmarks, and handwritten address to "Fräulein Mathilde Hebbel" in "Hermannstadt".

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a mountainous, forested landscape. In the foreground, three people sit or recline on a grassy meadow looking toward densely wooded hills and higher rocky peaks in the background. The photo is mounted on a card with wide margins. On the front margin, handwritten text reads a date and location. The reverse side has the typical divided-back postcard layout printed with vertical dotted address lines and the small word "Agfa" at the center.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a large historicist building with steep tiled roofs and ornate gables. People in early‑20th‑century clothing stand in front of the arched entrance. Printed German captions identify it as the new post and telegraph office in Hermannstadt. The left margin lists the publisher, and a handwritten message runs vertically on the right side. The reverse side has Hungarian text, a green "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA" 5‑fillér stamp, postal cancellations, and the printed heading "LEVELEZŐ-LAP."

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a bustling central market square with horse‑drawn carts, cattle, vendors, and rows of 19th‑century townhouses surrounding the square. The front is captioned with the town name and the name of the main square in Hungarian, German, and Romanian. The reverse is a classic divided‑back postcard layout with Hungarian text indicating "postcard" and the publisher's imprint.

Colorized panoramic view of a historic town nestled in a valley surrounded by green mountains. The town has dense blocks of buildings with red roofs and several prominent church towers and large public buildings. The caption at the top identifies the view in Hungarian and German. The reverse side shows a divided back with Hungarian text layout and a small crest or emblem.

Old color-printed postcard with two architectural views of a historic town hall complex. The left vignette, titled "Eingang zum Rathaus.", shows people walking through an arched gateway leading into a courtyard surrounded by buildings with red-tiled roofs. The right vignette, titled "Rathausshof", depicts the inner courtyard of the same town hall, with ivy-covered walls, wooden balconies, and a tall corner tower. At upper right is printed the greeting "Gruss aus Hermannstadt." in red. The front is densely covered with handwritten script in German. The reverse side is a divided postcard back printed with the Hungarian word "LEVELEZŐ-LAP.", address lines filled in cursive, a postal cancellation, and Hungarian stamps.

A colorized postcard view of a historic European town square surrounded by red‑roofed buildings. The square is busy with people, horse‑drawn carts, trees, market stalls and parasols. On the right rises a large clock tower overlooking the rooftops, with hills visible in the distant background. The caption at the top names the city in three languages and identifies the square. The reverse side is a standard divided-back layout labeled as a Romanian postcard, with printer information at the bottom.

Sepia-toned postcard showing the interior of a neatly furnished bedroom with strong Central/Eastern European folk decor. There is a double bed with embroidered linens, several wooden chairs, a small dining table covered with an embroidered tablecloth, a dresser with a mirror, and a daybed. On the wall above the bed hangs a large embroidered wall piece with German text. Along the right margin of the image, printed vertically, is German advertising text referring to Sächsische Leinenstickereien and a tapisserie shop in Sibiu/Hermannstadt.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a tall stone clock tower attached to an ornate historic building in a town square, with a mountainous, forested backdrop. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk in the foreground. The bottom margin bears printed Romanian text identifying the place.

A multi-view color postcard showing modernist cityscapes. The left panel features a tall telecommunications tower with red-and-white bands rising above a green landscape and city in the distance. The upper-right panel shows a broad plaza with flowerbeds, pedestrians, and modern high-rise hotels and office buildings. The lower-right panel depicts a wide avenue with mid-20th-century cars parked along the street, large buildings on one side, a modern hall with a distinctive sloped roof, and landscaped lawns and flowerbeds. Across the middle, there is a title band with the word 'DRESDEN' and a German subtitle.

A sepia-toned panoramic view over a small town in a hilly, vineyard-like landscape. Numerous villas and houses with steep roofs and ornate facades fill the foreground and middle ground, surrounded by many trees. On the hill in the background stands a prominent building complex labeled as a mountain guesthouse, likely with a tower or lookout. German text identifying the location and the guesthouse is printed at the top of the image.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a city street with a central fountain in the foreground and historic multi‑story buildings lining the street. A tall baroque church tower with a clock dominates the right side. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the street and around the square. Printed caption text at the top left reads "Graz. Herrengasse".

A vintage black‑and‑white/sepia postcard showing a gently rising urban street lined with multi‑storey masonry buildings on both sides. On the left stands a large, ornate school‑like building partly obscured by trees behind a brick wall and fence. Several people, including pedestrians and someone with a pram or cart, walk or stand along the unpaved street and sidewalk. Decorative street lamps line the right side. The caption text in red at the top identifies the town, the type of school, and the street name.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a harbor scene with several large sailing ships moored at a wooden quay piled with timber. A man is sitting among the lumber in the foreground. In the distance low buildings line the waterfront. In the upper right corner there is printed text in two languages identifying the location as the harbor of Rauma/Raumo.

Black-and-white panoramic view of a small European town in a valley surrounded by forested hills. In the center stands a large stone church with a tall nave, steep gabled roof, and tower, slightly elevated on a hill above compact rows of masonry houses. The town has orderly streets, multi‑story buildings with steep roofs, and a river or road curving through the valley. No visible printed caption or handwriting appears on the front.

Black-and-white winter scene showing a small alpine-style chalet with a snow-covered pitched roof and shuttered windows, set at the edge of a dense forest of tall fir trees heavily laden with snow under an overcast sky. No visible writing or caption appears on the image side.

Black‑and‑white photograph showing a rock cliff with cave dwellings and small whitewashed monastic buildings built into the rock face, surrounded by some trees in the foreground. The lower border contains captions in Cyrillic and German describing the Aladzha Monastery near Varna.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a rural scene with a woman in traditional dress filling metal jugs at an outdoor water source. In the background stands a two‑story plastered house with small windows, chimneys on the roof, and a wooden balcony extension. The caption at the top is in French and English, identifying the setting as Salonique and describing the villager fetching water. A small website watermark appears at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white image of a small wooden church with a tall, narrow steeple. The church stands behind a white picket fence and is framed by leafy trees on both sides. Over the entrance there is an arched sign with text that appears to end in "KIRKA" or "KIRKAEN," suggesting a Scandinavian word for church. The overall look is that of an early 20th‑century photographic postcard.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the Kasr El Nil Bridge in Cairo. At the entrance to the bridge stand two large lion statues on pedestals. People in traditional clothing and a camel are in the foreground, with the bridge and lampposts stretching into the distance. The title is printed at the top, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

A vintage black‑and‑white (sepia-toned) view over a small town with many trees and pitched-roof houses. On the left stands a prominent church with a baroque-style tower and onion dome. To the right are larger institutional-looking buildings along a main street. The title printed in red at the top reads "Großröhrsdorf. Mitteldorf." indicating the central part of the town Großröhrsdorf.

A monochrome blue-tinted coastal landscape printed within a thin rectangular border. It shows a wide sandy beach and calm sea curving into the distance, with low cliffs or headlands on the horizon. Trees and shrubs frame the view on the left and right edges. Along the lower margin of the card, beneath the image, there is a short handwritten inscription in a cursive script that appears to be in Cyrillic.

Black‑and‑white street scene showing a tramcar numbered 5 on cobblestone Aleksanterin katu/Aleksandersgatan. People in early 20th‑century clothing stand near the tram, and horse‑drawn vehicles move along the tree‑lined avenue. Buildings and overhead tram wires recede into the distance toward a large arched structure.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over a small European town set in hilly countryside. In the foreground are sheds or greenhouse roofs and gardens. Behind them stand neat, steep‑roofed houses with dormer windows, surrounded by many trees. Dominating the middle distance is a large church with a tall Baroque-style tower and spire rising above adjoining buildings that resemble a monastery or large institutional complex. Rolling hills form the backdrop under a clear sky. There is no visible printed title or caption on the image.

A black‑and‑white photograph of a mid‑20th‑century cargo steamship sailing in a harbor. The ship has a single funnel with a large letter "S" painted on it and two cargo masts with booms. Smoke is coming from the funnel. The vessel's name, likely "SELE", appears on the bow. In the background is a coastal city with low hills, industrial buildings, and a waterfront, suggesting a working port.

Colorized vintage view of a town by a river with a bridge leading into the settlement. On the far side of the bridge are low buildings and trees, with a church steeple rising above the rooftops. The river curves along the town, with grassy embankments in the foreground. Printed captions appear in the lower margin of the image area.

Sepia-toned postcard showing an elevated view of a grand semicircular colonnade enclosing an open square. People are strolling in the plaza, which is surrounded by elegant classical buildings. Forested hills appear in the distant background. French caption text is printed along the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a dense coniferous forest in hilly terrain. In the foreground are tall fir trees and undergrowth; in the background a rounded mountain rises above the forest under a cloudy sky. A printed German caption appears in the lower margin.

Sepia-toned vintage street scene showing a narrow village road lined with single- and two-story buildings with verandas and arcades. People are walking and standing along the sides, some goods or crates are stacked near the buildings, and an animal (likely a donkey) is visible in the middle distance. At the bottom of the image there is printed caption text indicating the location and description of the scene, and a website watermark is overlaid across the image.

A monochrome (blue-tinted) vintage postcard showing a cobbled street passing under a large arched gate in a traditional medina. Whitewashed buildings with small windows and wooden doors line the narrow lane; hanging lanterns are visible. Several figures in traditional North African clothing walk away from the viewer through the arch. Printed captions identify the scene as a street in Tétouan named El-Mexuar, and a vertical note at the left margin indicates the publisher.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a symmetrical country manor house with a tiled roof and central balcony. In front of the entrance stands a pedestal with an armillary sphere surrounded by a circular flower bed and gravel courtyard. Trees frame the building on both sides. White caption text is printed at the lower left and a publisher/photographer credit at the lower right.

A black‑and‑white view of a formal public garden with wide gravel paths, neatly edged flower beds full of blooming plants, trimmed lawns and vine‑covered pergolas with white wooden benches. A woman in early 20th‑century clothing, wearing a long dark skirt and light blouse and holding a hat, stands beside one of the flower beds.
