Color postcard showing a small wooden boat with people paddling through a narrow water channel surrounded by tall reeds in a wetland under a clear blue sky. The reverse side has multilingual captions and Romanian postcard layout with price and publisher.

Color view of a town center with a landscaped park and round modernist fountain in the foreground, older low-rise houses and a church spire to the left, and a tall socialist-era high‑rise hotel or apartment block to the right. Several 1970s–1980s Eastern European cars are parked along the street. The reverse has address lines and multilingual caption identifying the scene as the central park of Covasna.

Color postcard showing the beach resort of Mamaia on the Black Sea with a crowded sandy shore, bathers, and a line of modernist seafront hotels. A tall tower block with the sign "PERLA" stands prominently on the left. The reverse is a Romanian address side printed by Editura Sport‑Turism with price in lei.

Color postcard showing a modern seaside resort with a low-rise hotel complex and a nearby high-rise, set beside a lagoon/lake with the Black Sea in the background. The reverse reads "CARTE POȘTALĂ" and credits Editura Sport-Turism; caption identifies Jupiter resort's Lake Tismana and Hotel Tismana.

Multiview color postcard showing Black Sea beaches, seaside hotels and resort facilities of the Jupiter resort; the word "JUPITER" is printed prominently on the front. The reverse is a Romanian postcard template by Editura Sport-Turism with multilingual caption and a printed price.

Vintage black‑and‑white view showing wooded hills and a resort settlement, likely a spa area. The reverse has Romanian text printed with the header "Republica Populară Romînă – Călimănești — Vedere," a 40 bani Romanian stamp, multiple Călimănești postmarks dated 9.4.58, and a handwritten message in blue ink addressed to Craiova.

Color postcard showing a busy urban intersection with mid‑century buildings at Piața Romană in Bucharest. A large rooftop billboard reads "Rumarta," and a tall hotel tower in the background bears the name "Hotel Dorobanți." Buses and cars circulate around the square.

Color postcard showing a steep brick passage with arches and pedestrians, known as the Stairs Passage, with the tall spire and four corner turrets of a clock‑faced Lutheran cathedral rising above tiled-roof houses under a bright blue sky. The reverse has printed publisher and location notes in multiple languages.

Color postcard showing a crowded sandy beach on a sunny day. A boy stands in the shallow sea in the foreground while many sunbathers fill the beach. Behind them rise two modernist, multi‑story seaside hotels with stacked balconies. The reverse side has Romanian address fields and identifies the scene as Mamaia — Hotel Lido and Savoy.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a multi‑roofed villa/spa building surrounded by tall conifer trees with hills in the background. The reverse has two pink Romanian stamps of 20 BANI marked "R.P. ROMINA POSTA," a circular postmark, printed "CARTE POȘTALĂ" and "LIBRĂRIA NOASTRĂ," and handwritten Romanian text mentioning Covasna with an address.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a snowy forest scene with tall conifer trees and a lone skier/walker in the distance. The back is printed in Romanian and Russian and reads that it depicts the Bucegi Mountains – Diham, a winter landscape. It bears the phrases REPUBLICA POPULARA ROMINA, CARTE POŞTALA, the publisher LIBRARIA NOASTRĂ, number 13, and a handwritten date Mai 1955.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a mountain spa resort with several large villa-style buildings among coniferous forest. A path with two people walking is in the foreground, with fences and utility poles leading toward the complex. The reverse side carries printed Romanian and Russian captions identifying Borsec and a CCS rest house, a Romanian postage stamp, a 1957 cancellation, and a handwritten message and address.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped park with circular basins/fountains and tree‑lined paths leading to a multi‑arched spa building, likely in a mountain valley. The reverse has Romanian text printed for the People's Republic period, a long handwritten message in blue ink, two red 20‑bani Romanian stamps, postal cancellations, and an address to a public office in Câmpina.

Color postcard showing a modernist seaside hotel with many balconies beside a calm water canal or pool. In front is a low pavilion with an outdoor terrace full of tables and parasols and people relaxing. The back has Romanian text and a Romanian stamp.

Color postcard showing the Church of Cozia Monastery with striped brick-and-stone walls, a domed roof with a cross, gardens in the foreground and forested mountains behind. The reverse has a Romanian 40 BANI POSTA ROMANA stamp canceled in Călimănești, Vâlcea, printed caption about the Cozia Monastery in multiple languages, publisher details, and a handwritten greeting and Bucharest address.

Color postcard showing a seaside scene: a stone terrace with lanterns overlooks a crowded sandy beach with umbrellas by a calm sea. The reverse has Romanian text and address, a blue ROMANIA postage stamp, and publisher details. Printed caption indicates Eforie Nord. The handwritten message is dated 15 August 1969 and addressed to Ploiești.

Color postcard showing the bus station (Autogara) of Buzău: a low modernist building with parked intercity buses, a yellow Dacia car, pedestrians and a roadside with greenery. The reverse has Romanian printing and price details.

A color postcard showing a modernist seaside resort with curved hotel buildings and high‑rise blocks, landscaped lawns, and people walking. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp featuring I. Slavici, and address lines. Printed identification at the bottom reads "MANGALIA NORD – VENUS."

Color postcard showing a red aerial cable car crossing a steep, forested gorge with rocky cliffs in the Bucegi Mountains. The back has Romanian handwriting and address fields, a Romanian stamp and Bucharest postmarks. Printed caption at bottom left reads "MUNȚII BUCEGI. Valea Jepilor."

A museum art postcard reproducing a dramatic Baroque marine painting showing ships in a storm near rocky cliffs and a fortress. The back is printed in Romanian with address lines, a stamp box, and price.

Sepia postcard showing a street corner with a large three‑storey building featuring steep roofs and small towers, typical early‑20th‑century Central/Eastern European architecture. Pedestrians walk along the sidewalk; power lines and trees line the street. The reverse bears Romanian text, stamps of the Romanian People's Republic, and a message and address.

Front shows a color reproduction of a Baroque painting of a violinist (The Sense of Hearing) attributed to Gonzales Coques. The reverse reads "CARTE POSTALĂ", gives the title in Romanian and French, credits the Brukenthal Museum in Sibiu, and shows a printed price of Lei 1,50.

A multiview color postcard with a blue border showing alpine-style spa buildings and landscaped lawns in a forested mountain setting. The title BORSEC appears on the front. The reverse has handwritten Romanian text, an address to București, Romanian postage and cancellations.

Museum postcard reproducing an oil painting: a half-length portrait of a 17th‑century man with long hair and a buttoned coat, hands posed near the wrist, against a dark background. A white margin appears at the bottom. The reverse lists the artist Gonzales Coques and the title in Romanian and French, and notes the Brukenthal Museum in Sibiu with a printed price in lei.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a general view of a mountain valley settlement framed by two tall fir trees. A village with a church steeple sits below steep, forested slopes of the Carpathians. The reverse prints the caption 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMÂNĂ – POIANA ȚAPULUI – Vedere generală' (also in Russian), has two 20 bani Romanian People's Republic stamps, cancellation marks, a vertical imprint 'LIBRĂRIA NOASTRĂ', address lines to Ploiești, and a handwritten Romanian message.

Color view of Regensburg on the Danube: the Stone Bridge with its bridge tower in the foreground and the twin spires of Regensburg Cathedral rising behind. The reverse shows German postage (50 Deutsche Bundespost) with a cancel promoting blood donation and a printed caption identifying the view. Addressed in blue ink to Bucharest, Romania.

Sepia photo postcard showing a general view of a mountain valley framed by two tall fir trees, with scattered villas and chalets below and rugged peaks in the background. The reverse has printed Romanian and Russian captions, a blue Romanian R.P.R. 7.50 lei stamp with postmark, purple handwritten message and address lines.

Color postcard showing people rowing small boats on a lake with a central fountain, framed by blossoming trees and spring foliage. It depicts a lively scene in Cișmigiu Gardens, a central park. The reverse includes multilingual captions, publisher details, and a price in lei.

Vintage Romanian postcard showing the richly carved wood dining room of Peleș Castle (Peleș Museum) in Sinaia, with a long banquet table and chandeliers. The reverse has Romanian handwriting in blue ink, a 40 B POSTA ROMANA stamp (DENSUS), 1976 postmarks, and a multilingual printed caption.

Split-view vintage postcard. Left: a white Orthodox monastery with a tall spire set against forested mountains, captioned for Sâmbăta de Sus and framed by an arch. Right: a modernist civic building and landscaped square in the town of Victoria, captioned 'ORASUL VICTORIA – vedere'.

Color postcard view of Red Square showing the onion domes of Saint Basil's Cathedral and the Spasskaya Tower of the Moscow Kremlin. Soviet-era cars and buses are visible in the foreground. The reverse side has Russian text with a printed USSR postage imprint and publishing details.

Collage postcard with five photos of exterior‑painted Orthodox churches/monasteries surrounded by a purple border. The center bottom has the word "Suceava," and at the top a label reads "Monumente Istorice." The reverse is written in Romanian with a Suceava postmark and a green Posta Română 40 bani stamp.

Vintage color postcard showing the white wooden double-leaf drawbridge Magere Brug spanning the Amstel River with traditional Amsterdam canal houses in the background under a blue sky. The reverse has printed text at top-left, dotted address lines on the right, a stamp box marked "ST 1/42," and a vertical divider ending with a windmill icon.

A multiview tourist postcard showing mountain resorts, hotels, alpine scenery and the famous Neo‑Renaissance Peleș Castle in the center image. The title on the front reads "VALEA PRAHOVEI" in red, indicating the Prahova Valley in the Carpathian Mountains of Romania. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a red POSTA ROMANA 55 BANI stamp, and printed multilingual captions.

Sepia-toned portrait postcard of a high-ranking Romanian military/royal figure in formal uniform with many medals and a large star insignia. The reverse shows a classic UPU postcard layout printed in Romanian and French with a Bucharest publisher imprint and a handwritten 1914 date.

Sepia-toned portrait of a bearded man in a decorated military uniform, framed with illustrated laurel and palm leaves. A French caption beneath the portrait reads "CHARLES Ier, ROI DE ROUMANIE." Small imprint text appears along the border. The reverse is a classic French-language postcard back with an address-only side and a 10‑centime stamp box.

Vintage Romanian postcard. Front: a sepia decorative card with floral border and an oval portrait of a woman; printed Romanian caption reads "Poetii si Autorii Români" and the name "Carmen Sylva – Reine de Roumanie," with publisher credit along the left margin. Handwritten message in French appears at the bottom with a date. Back: UPU layout headed "ROMANIA CARTE POSTALE" with a red 10 BANI Romanian stamp canceled "BUCURESCI 7 MAI," transit/arrival marks, and an address to La Haye (The Hague), Netherlands; a blue library stamp from Zaltbommel is also present.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large spa complex with mansard roofs, dormer windows, and a central portico with columns, set against forested hills. People stroll along a landscaped promenade and a canal/terrace in front. The reverse has Romanian printed text identifying the place as Slănic Moldova – Băile Centrale and a handwritten message with an address.

Sepia studio postcard showing a young boy in a sailor suit seated on a decorated stool. The caption on the image reads "A.S.R. Prinţul Nicolae." Publisher marks include "Edit. C. Sfetea, Bucuresti" and "Colectia Mandy. Reproductia interzisa." The reverse is printed in red with "ROMANIA Carte poştală," an address layout, a stamp box, and the same publisher credits.

Sepia-toned studio portrait of a small blond child in an embroidered Romanian-style shirt, barefoot and holding a bowl. German title is printed at the top; at the bottom left appears the photographer/publisher credit with place and year, and a small number at bottom right. The reverse is a divided back with red guidelines and a dotted stamp box.

Sepia studio portrait of a young child; the caption at the top reads "A.S.R. Prințesa Ileana." Publisher and series information appear at the bottom. The reverse has red printing with "ROMANIA – Carte poștală," address lines, stamp box, and publisher credit.

Vintage postcard with a monochrome, blue-tinted studio portrait of a young noblewoman seated on an ornate throne-like chair with a leopard-skin drape. She wears a tiara and long pearl strands. Large white lilies are arranged beside her and an equestrian knight statue stands on a pedestal in the background. The reverse shows a divided back with multilingual 'Postkarte – Carte postale – Postcard' headings and address lines.

Sepia-toned photo postcard showing a woman and two children in Romanian folk costumes standing in a forest. A Romanian caption runs along the top and a small series number (13) appears at the lower right. The reverse is a divided back reading 'ROMANIA CARTE POȘTALĂ', with publisher credit 'Editura "CARTEA ROMÂNEASCĂ", București'.

Divided‑back Romanian postcard. The image side is a sepia studio portrait of a seated woman looking up at a small child standing on a draped pedestal, the child wearing a simple white garment and a cross necklace. A Romanian caption appears on the image, with publisher credits at the bottom. The address side is printed in red with 'ROMANIA Carte poștală', a stamp box, address lines, and publisher/series information.

Sepia-toned studio portrait of two children in soft light. The German caption at the bottom reads 'Prinzessin Marie und Prinz Nikolaus von Rumänien.' with a small publisher imprint 'Verlag A. Gimm Gotha' and the number '133'. The reverse shows a standard divided-back postcard layout with a dotted stamp box and address lines; a small handwritten '101e' appears near the stamp box.

Sepia photograph of a woman and two boys in traditional Romanian folk dress standing in a wooded landscape. Romanian caption appears at the top, and a Bucharest publisher credit at the lower left. The reverse is a divided back printed with ROMANIA and Carte postala, red side text, a Dutch handwritten message and address, a Netherlands 2½ cent stamp, and a postmark from 's‑Gravenhage dated 1913.

Color-tinted ethnographic postcard showing a Romanian folk group of Călușari dancers and musicians in traditional costume, one holding a red flag, posed outdoors. The reverse bears a Romanian stamp and Bucharest postmarks, addressed in French.

Vintage sepia postcard showing the ornate interior of the Florentine Hall at Peleș Castle: large crystal chandeliers, carved wooden furniture, an elaborate marble fireplace, paneled walls with paintings, and a coffered ceiling with an allegorical painting. The reverse has address lines, a stamp box, and Romanian captions.

Old sepia postcard showing a blue-toned photograph of a castle nestled among pine-covered mountains, viewed from a road with a railing. The back carries Romanian stamps and a Bucharest postmark dated 23 Aug 1929, plus a handwritten message and address. Printed title reads "Castelul Peleș."

Sepia-toned vintage postcard. Front shows Peleș Castle surrounded by forested hills in Sinaia, with a person working in the foreground. Red captions read "Castelul Peleș" and "Sinaia." The reverse has printed heading "UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE – ROMÂNIA – CARTA POSTALA" with dotted address lines.

Colorized view of a hilltop fortress with multiple red-roofed towers above a village and forested slopes at dusk. People in traditional clothing walk near a wooden bridge in the foreground. Captions read "Bran" and "Castelul Regal." The reverse is a Romanian divided back with address lines, the heading "România," postal-rate note, publisher credit from Bran, and the year 1933.

Sepia-toned coastal view showing the ornate Art Nouveau Constanța Casino on the Black Sea promenade, with a statue on a tall pedestal at left (Carmen Sylva). The front has a small printed caption near the bottom; the reverse has a Romanian caption and two brown 100 LEI ROMANIA stamps.

Vintage colorized street scene of a grand hotel façade along a broad, tree‑lined boulevard at dusk. Caption reads "Bucuresti. Palace Hotel. - Bulevard Elisabeta." The reverse shows Romanian handwriting, postal cancels from Bucuresti, two red 1 LEU Romania stamps, and an address to Bulgaria.

Tinted night view of a central boulevard in a large city, with tram tracks and streetlights running down the middle, cars and pedestrians along the sidewalks, and mid‑rise interwar buildings with illuminated windows and signage (including a rooftop sign reading "CREDITUL MINIER"). The border is scalloped. Caption at the bottom identifies the scene as Brătianu Boulevard at night in Bucharest. The reverse side reads "ROMÂNIA CARTĂ POSTALĂ" and lists the publisher.

Color postcard showing a large modernist domed exhibition hall with glass walls, broad plaza, flower beds, and crowds. Tall light poles and vertical flags (including the Romanian tricolor) frame the scene. The back has a printed multilingual caption and the Romanian National Tourism Office imprint.

Color postcard showing a large carved wooden gate leading into a traditional wooden homestead, with shingled roofs and floral carvings, typical of Romanian village architecture. Two visitors stand under the porch. Bright blue sky and greenery surround the scene. The back identifies the site in multiple languages and bears the Romanian national tourism office imprint.

Color postcard showing a grand multi‑story spa hotel with a central tower (Hotel Cerna) in a mountainous, forested setting. Several 1960s cars are parked on a cobbled square. To the right stands a small striped Orthodox church with a dome. People are gathered on the hotel steps. The reverse has Romanian text, address lines, stamps and postmarks.

Color postcard showing a grand multi‑story hotel with a central turret (Hotel Cerna) in a forested mountain spa town. To the right is a small domed Orthodox-style church. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a 40 BANI Posta Romana stamp, Bucharest postal cancellations dated 30.9.68, and a printed caption referencing Herculane – Hotel Cerna.

Color postcard showing a large modernist beachfront hotel with repetitive concrete balconies set among trees. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a 40 Bani Romanian stamp and postmarks, and a printed multilingual caption identifying the site as Hotel Europa in Eforie Nord.

Black-and-white seaside view of the Mamaia resort on the Black Sea, with modernist beachfront hotels and people on the beach and in shallow water. The image carries the caption 'Vedere din Mamaia'. The reverse side reads 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMÎNĂ' and 'CARTE POȘTALĂ', with publisher 'Editura Meridiane', price 'Lei 1', number '8160', and a handwritten Romanian message addressed to a family in Bucharest.

Vintage black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard labeled "Iași," showing several landmarks of Iași: the Palace of Culture, the façade of the National Theatre, the Golia Monastery bell tower, a statue in a city square with a tram, and a Moldavian‑style Orthodox church. The reverse side has Romanian People's Republic printing and address lines.

Black-and-white postcard showing a close-up detail of the marble statue of the goddess Fortuna from the statue group Fortuna and Pontos. The reverse lists the museum and work information in Romanian, Russian, French, and German, with standard postcard address lines and stamp box.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a resort street lined with alpine-style buildings and tall pines, with crowds walking along the road and forested hills in the background. Caption at lower left reads "SOVATA— Cantina." The reverse bears Romanian text indicating a state-issued postcard.

Black-and-white view of mushroom-shaped rock formations on a mountain plateau under dramatic clouds. Caption on the image reads "MUNTII BUCEGI – Babele." The reverse side says "REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMINĂ," "CARTE POȘTALĂ," includes a stamp box with number 2582, and price line "C.P.C.S. Lei 1."

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a riverside rest house with a small tower and arched loggia, set among dense forest on the bank of the Olt River. Caption at the bottom names Călimănești and describes the house. The reverse reads "REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMINĂ," "CARTE POȘTALĂ," a printed price/issuer line, and a numeric box.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the arched gate/bell tower of the Negru Vodă Monastery, with arcaded decorations and a domed roof. Caption at the bottom identifies the location as Cîmpulung‑Muscel and the tower of the Negru‑Vodă monastery. The back reads "Republica Populara Romina" and "Carte Postala," with price noted as C.P.C.S. Lei 1 and number 1114.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a whitewashed, pavilion-like stone fountain with a shingled roof and an inscription band under the eaves. It stands in a grassy yard with a wooden fence and trees in the background. The structure matches the famous well associated with the legend of Meșterul Manole in Curtea de Argeș, Romania.

Black‑and‑white view showing a broad urban staircase lined with multi‑globe street lamps, with Neo‑Romanian style civic buildings on both sides and a few pedestrians. Caption at top right reads "PIATRA NEAMȚ—Vedere". The reverse bears state and postal inscriptions typical of mid‑20th‑century Romania.

Black‑and‑white seaside panorama titled "EFORIE — Vedere generală," showing a coastal promenade with modernist resort buildings, curving paths and gardens, and the Black Sea to the right, viewed from behind balcony railings. Reverse has printed Romanian postal layout and price.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a small lake ringed by conifer forests with a pier, boathouse and several rowboats; a person rows in the foreground. The front caption reads "TUȘNAD – Cu barca pe lac." The back has a standard divided layout with Romanian text, stamp box, and price.

Black-and-white postcard showing an elevated view over a round crater lake surrounded by forest, with a few hikers in the foreground. Caption at top right reads "TUȘNAD LACUL SF. ANA". The reverse side has Romanian text: "REPUBLICA POPULARA ROMINA", "CARTE POSTALA", a price line "C.P.C.S. Lei 1", and number "2328".

Sepia/black‑and‑white postcard view of Bucharest's Palace Square showing the newly built domed Sala Palatului surrounded by landscaped roundabouts, modernist apartment blocks and a few pedestrians and cars. A printed caption appears at the top right. The reverse bears standard postcard layout and pricing.

Sepia postcard showing a medieval Moldavian church with blind arcades and a steep tiled roof, captioned in the image as the church of Stephen the Great in Piatra-Neamț. The reverse reads in Romanian with a stamp box, price and the legend of the People's Republic of Romania.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing Constantin Brâncuși's stone ensemble "The Table of Silence" with a large circular table and twelve hourglass stools arranged around it in a park setting. The reverse reads "CARTE POȘTALĂ," has address lines, publisher "Editura Meridiane," a stamp box with number 7343, and a multilingual caption identifying the work.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a close-up studio photograph of a small seated terracotta figurine in a contemplative pose, known as "The Thinker." The reverse gives multilingual museum captioning and postcard imprint details.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a narrow rocky gorge with a waterfall and wooden ladders/walkways (the 'Seven Ladders'). The reverse says 'CARTE POȘTALĂ', has a stamp box marked 6171, price Lei 1, and publisher 'Editura Meridiane'.

Sepia-toned landscape photo showing a broad river running through a steep, forested mountain gorge with bright rocky cliffs; tree branches frame the top. No people are visible. The reverse carries Romanian text identifying the view.

Black-and-white postcard view of a mountain valley with the Olt River curving through fields and small houses, a truss bridge crossing the river, and a road/rail line running along the riverbank. Foreground tree branches frame the scene. The back reads in Romanian with a stamp box, address lines, price and publisher.

Vintage Romanian postcard showing a black‑and‑white winter scene in the Făgăraș Mountains: snowy ridges and peaks with a small mountain hut nestled in the valley (Podragu Hut). The back side bears Romanian text identifying the location and publisher, with a price and card number.

A black‑and‑white aerial view of central Bucharest focused on Palace Square, with the domed-roof Sala Palatului in the middle, flanked by the former Royal Palace, the Central University Library, and the Romanian Athenaeum visible nearby. The reverse reads CARTE POȘTALĂ with a stamp box and multilingual caption, price, publisher, and photographer credit.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a dramatic diagonal close‑up of the modular rhomboid forms of Constantin Brâncuși's Endless Column reaching into the sky. The reverse reads "CARTE POȘTALĂ," lists a price and publisher, and identifies the subject in multiple languages as Brâncuși's Infinite Column in Târgu Jiu.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a lone hiker sitting on a rocky ridge above a sea of clouds, with jagged mountain peaks stretching into the distance. The reverse is printed in Romanian, mentioning the People's Republic of Romania and the Făgăraș massif, with publisher credit and a price.

Black-and-white postcard showing a narrow medieval stepped passage with brick arches and old houses, populated by pedestrians. The reverse reads 'CARTE POȘTALĂ' and a multilingual caption identifying the scene as the Stairs Passage in Sibiu, with publisher and price information.

Black-and-white postcard showing a central square with trees and historic houses, dominated by a tall Gothic church tower with a clock and a steep patterned spire. The reverse has Romanian layout text, a stamp box with the number 148, and printing credit.

Black-and-white postcard showing extensive seaside archaeological ruins with low stone walls and foundations; the reverse lists the site as the Histria ruins under the Museum of Archaeology in Constanța, in multiple languages.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the ruins of a medieval stone fortress, viewed through a rocky archway. Crumbled towers and arched doorways are visible with a dirt path in the foreground. The reverse is printed in Romanian, indicating the image is of the ruins of Neamț Citadel and listing the publisher and price.

Divided‑back Romanian postcard. Front shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a statue of a man holding a flag (Tudor Vladimirescu) atop a rocky pedestal with a lion relief, set in a landscaped square with shrubs and a streetlamp, buildings in the background. Back has printed Romanian headings, address lines, and a stamp box numbered 6020.

Vintage Romanian postcard showing a black‑and‑white photograph of a steep‑roofed wooden‑shingled house behind a fence and fir trees. A sign on the house reads that it is the Avram Iancu Memorial House. The back is printed in Romanian with headings indicating the Romanian People's Republic, Apuseni Mountains, and postcard layout with price and publisher.

Vintage Romanian postcard showing a large spa-sanatorium building with arcades and a pitched roof. On the façade are socialist slogans including "TRĂIASCĂ PARTIDUL MUNCITORESC," and atop the roof the letters "PMR" beside a star. The reverse bears Romanian and Cyrillic printed headings, blue handwritten Romanian text and an address to Bucharest, with Bucharest postmarks dated 1954.

Sepia postcard showing a view through a ruined stone arch toward a towered fortress building among trees. Reverse side has Romanian text and address lines, a blue stamp of the Romanian People's Republic, multiple postmarks, and the printed caption indicating Râșnov citadel.

Vintage Romanian postcard printed with "Republica Populară Romînă – Valea Jiului." The picture shows a monochrome view of a mountain river cutting through a forested gorge with a narrow road built along a stone embankment. The reverse has blue handwritten Romanian text, a 40‑bani blue stamp, and a București circular postmark dated 22 Oct 1957.

Sepia-toned Romanian postcard with a small photo of a forest lodge labeled "Șimleu Silvaniei – Cabana Brădet," in Sălaj County. The right half has preprinted Romanian address fields and a preprinted 30 bani stamp with the socialist coat of arms. Layout typical of mid-20th-century Romanian postal stationery.

Reverse side of a vintage Japanese postcard. The back is blank aside from manufacturer marks and light stains, with small handwritten magenta marks and a date. No address lines or stamp box are present.
Color postcard showing a lakeside park with abstract stone sculptures in the foreground, a chain-lined promenade by the water, and low houses and greenery on the opposite bank under a clear blue sky.

Color postcard showing socialist-era apartment blocks with pastel yellow and green facades and colorful balconies around a landscaped courtyard; low hills in the background. The reverse reads in Romanian with a stamp box and address lines.

A multiview night postcard with a blue patterned border and the yellow title "Bucuresti." It shows five Bucharest scenes: the Miorița Fountain, Otopeni Airport's domed terminal, the neoclassical Romanian Athenaeum, the tall Hotel Intercontinental with cars below, and a wide illuminated boulevard/roundabout. The reverse is a Romanian postal template (Posta Romana) with address lines and a caption list of the pictured sights in Romanian and French, plus a printed price.

Night view of a domed neoclassical concert hall with Corinthian portico, illuminated and photographed from a square with several 1960s–70s cars parked in front. The inscription on the entablature reads ATENEUL ROMAN. The reverse shows the Romanian postal template with POSTA ROMANA and fields for address.

A Romanian state postcard. The front shows a color view of a large modernist hall with tall vertical white piers and two triangular roof wings, approached by a long bridge over a lake within a landscaped park. Small figures stroll along the paths. The reverse bears the Romanian postal layout with the printed stamp and the caption naming the site.

Sepia Romanian postal card with a printed stamp and address fields. The photo shows the arched brick fortification known as the city bastion in Timișoara, with pedestrian paths, a road with vehicles, and 1960s–70s apartment blocks in the background. Caption beneath the image identifies the site. Top right reads 'CARTE POȘTALĂ' with a pre-printed 'ROMANIA / POSTA ROMANA / 30 BANI' stamp.

Multiview color postcard showing the Black Sea resort Neptun: beaches with sunbathers and flagpoles, a lake with pedal boats and sailing, modernist seaside hotels and resort buildings, and an entrance gate. The word NEPTUN appears prominently on the front.

Color postcard showing a sunny Black Sea beach with children playing on a large metal gymnastic frame with rings and ropes. Colorful beach tents and umbrellas dot the sand, and a thatched parasol stands to the right. Clear blue sky and calm sea. The reverse has multilingual captions and Romanian publisher details.

Color postcard showing a broad intersection along Strada Horea in Cluj, lined with ornate historic buildings with tall spires. Buses and pedestrians fill the streets. The reverse has Romanian text including 'CARTE POȘTALĂ', publisher Editura Meridiane, price in lei, and photographer credit Al. Mendrea.

Color postcard showing a winter ski scene at a large chalet-style mountain hotel. Snow-covered roofs, evergreen forest background, and crowds of people; in the foreground two children in bright ski outfits play in the snow. The building is identified as Hotel Sport in the Poiana Brașov ski resort.

Color postcard showing a snowy winter scene at a mountain resort. A multi‑story modern hotel building (Hotel Teleferic) stands amid tall fir trees with snow-covered slopes and many people in winter clothing walking in the foreground. The reverse reads 'CARTE POȘTALĂ' with address lines, a stamp box marked 5637, and publisher/credit lines in Romanian and Russian.

Color postcard showing a winter scene of a historic building with a clock on its gable and a red-tiled roof, identified as the Central Post Office in Brașov, Romania. Snow covers the ground and rooftops; bare trees frame the view under a blue sky. The reverse has the Romanian postal layout with a printed 40 bani indicium bearing the socialist coat of arms, address lines, and publisher/price details.

Color street view of a modernist city center with 1970s automobiles and pedestrians. At left stands a cylindrical building with a large vertical sign reading MODAROM (the city's fashion house). To the right is a mid-rise slab hotel with CAPITOL signage on the roofline. Mountains rise in the background. The reverse identifies the scene and publisher in multiple languages.

Color postcard showing a spa/resort complex with a long white building with red-tiled roofs set in a green park with tall conifer trees; people are strolling and sitting on the grass. The reverse reads in Romanian with printed headings "CARTE POȘTALĂ," publisher "EDITURA MERIDIANE," and a caption "BORSEC," plus price and credits. There is a handwritten Romanian message and an address to a soldier in Câmpina, Prahova.

Color postcard showing a striking late‑modernist/Brutalist seaside restaurant-bar with deep white concrete cantilevers, large windows and patterned parasols on terraces. A roadside sign reads "BAR". The reverse is printed in Romanian (and also French, English, German, Russian) and lists the location as Neptun.

A Romanian pre-printed postal card with a blue monochrome photograph of the hospital building in Negrești-Oaș, Satu Mare County. The right side has address lines and a printed blue stamp of Poșta Română with value 30 bani. Text fields for sender and recipient are in Romanian.

Multi-view color postcard showing five Bucharest scenes. Top: the Arcul de Triumf. Left middle: Aleea Trandafirilor in Herăstrău Park, with rose beds. Right middle: the Dr. M. Minovici Folk Art Museum, a white Neo-Romanian house by a broad boulevard. Bottom left: Piața Națiunilor Unite with a fountain and surrounding buildings. Bottom right: the courtyard of Hanul lui Manuc filled with café umbrellas. The front bears the word "Bucuresti." The reverse has Romanian postal layout and a bilingual caption listing the views.

Color postcard showing a Secession/Art Nouveau building with steep gables and shingled spires behind a blue fence, photographed on a clear day. The reverse has Romanian text, publisher details, a price in lei and a stamp box.

Color postcard showing a brick Orthodox church with three cross-topped domes and arcaded windows, set behind a low stone wall and flowerbeds. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian 40B postage stamp (Posta Romana) and a Pitești postmark. The printed caption identifies the church as St. George's Church in Pitești.

Color postcard showing a monument with a bust of the Roman emperor Trajan atop a tall pedestal dated 1906, with additional bronze figures beside it, set in a landscaped square/park with trees and passersby. Reverse side is a Romanian divided-back with preprinted stamp and Romanian address fields.

Multiview color postcard showing several medieval painted churches and monasteries of Bucovina in Suceava County, Romania. Panels depict Moldovița, Humor, Voroneț (center roundel with blue exterior frescoes), Putna church, Dragomirna, Arbore, Sucevița and Bogdan-Vodă. A yellow caption block reads "MONUMENTE ISTORICE ȘI DE ARTĂ din județul SUCEAVA." The reverse says CARTE POȘTALĂ, lists the monuments with their centuries, and shows the publisher Editura Meridiane and price Lei 3.

Sepia-toned Romanian postcard showing giant waterlily pads inside a greenhouse. Caption identifies the scene as the botanical garden in Cluj-Napoca. The right side has the printed heading 'CARTE POȘTALĂ', a Poșta Română 30 bani imprinted stamp, and standard Romanian address fields.

Color view of a Carpathian town with a walled complex featuring a tall stone bell tower with a steep roof and an adjacent church with a red tiled roof, surrounded by landscaped gardens and paths at the foot of a forested hill.

Color view of a mountain reservoir with forested slopes and a concrete dam visible in the distance. The back identifies it as the Bicaz storage lake. Multilingual captions and Romanian publisher details are printed.

Color postcard showing a modernist two‑storey white post office with the PTTR (Poșta/Telecom) sign and the entrance marked POSTA. A small red CTS sign is on the wall. Trees line the street and three men stand talking on the sidewalk. The reverse has Romanian layout 'CARTE POSTALA', a Romanian 40 BANI stamp (Poșta Română) canceled 'CÂMPINA 13.11.72', price printed as Lei 1,90, and a caption indicating the subject is the PTTR office in Amara.

Color postcard showing a small white fairytale-like clock tower rising above a lush park with tall fir trees and flowerbeds of bright red blossoms. The reverse is laid out in Romanian as a standard "CARTE POSTALA," with a blue handwritten message and address, a Romanian 40 bani stamp (POSTA ROMANA), and postal cancellations. Printed caption at bottom left references Vatra Dornei.

Color photo of a forest campground with multiple small A‑frame tents in bright colors and a 1960s Eastern‑bloc sedan among trees; two campers are visible. The reverse has Romanian text, a stamp and postmark, and a printed caption indicating the campsite.

Color postcard showing a wooden mountain lodge surrounded by tall evergreens and patches of late snow. The reverse has Romanian layout text "CARTE POSTALA," a 40 BANI Romanian stamp, a blue postmark reading "SINAIA," and a purple circular cancel. Addressed in blue ink to Câmpina, Prahova, with a short handwritten message at left. The caption at bottom left reads "CABANA BOLOBOCI."

Multi‑view color postcard showing Târgu Mureș, Romania: a tall modernist high‑rise labeled Hotel Grand; a modern plaza identified as Theatre Square with low white buildings and flowerbeds; an aerial view of the central area with the clock‑towered Administrative Palace and the Culture Palace near Roses Square; and a broad boulevard with apartment blocks and a statue. The reverse has Romanian stamps and postmarks and handwritten Romanian message dated 1982, addressed to Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a wide sandy beach crowded with sunbathers in front of modernist high‑rise seaside hotels. The reverse has Romanian printed text, a 40‑bani Romanian stamp, and postmarks from Mamaia and București dated 1964.

Color postcard showing a picturesque pavilion-like building with red tile roofs beside a small pond, reflected in the water and surrounded by dense coniferous forest. The reverse has Romanian handwriting and address, a blue 40 Bani "Posta Română" stamp (industrial cranes), and printed caption crediting the photo and publisher. Caption identifies the view as 'Sinaia. Foișorul.'

Color postcard showing a modernist, high‑rise hotel tower with a long low annex set in landscaped gardens beside water, under a bright blue sky. A woman walks along a paved path in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian printing and handwriting; it includes the word "MAMAIA," indicating the seaside resort.

Color postcard reproducing a Renaissance painting of the biblical Return of the Prodigal Son by Bernardino Licinio: figures in rich 16th‑century dress gathered in a courtyard with arcades and a landscape beyond. The reverse has museum credit lines in Romanian, French, German, and English, a Romanian stamp (Beethoven 1770–1970), and a handwritten French poem with an address in Romania.

A multiview color postcard showing several town scenes: apartment blocks and flower beds, a forest lodge with the word "CABANA" on its facade, historic civic buildings, panoramic views of the town center and main square with gardens and streets. A bold yellow title on the front reads "GHEORGHENI". The reverse side has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp marked "POSTA ROMANA 2 LEI", and postmarks dated 1982.

Color postcard showing the ornate facade, tower and terrace statues of Peleș Castle with a flower garden in Sinaia, Romania. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Bucharest postmark, and a Romanian airmail stamp featuring cosmonaut A. Nicolaev.

Color postcard showing a medieval brick passage with arches and a cobbled, stepped lane where people are walking. The reverse has Romanian text, a Romanian stamp, postmarks dated 1966, a printed caption identifying the scene, and a handwritten message and address.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a busy ski slope with many skiers at Predeal–Clăbucet, looking across forested hills to distant snowy mountains (Piatra Craiului). The reverse has Romanian address lines and publisher markings.

Multi-view color postcard labeled "CLUJ," showing landmarks of Cluj-Napoca: the Napoca Hotel, a panoramic city view, St. Michael's Church (central diamond), the National Theatre/Opera building with the surrounding square, and the Dormition of the Theotokos Orthodox Cathedral.

Color postcard showing a snowy winter scene at a mountain resort: a stone-and-wood alpine hotel with steep roof, balconies and tall fir trees. People and a 1970s Eastern Bloc car appear in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian text and a 40 B 'posta română' stamp (red poppies, dated 1975) with Brașov postmarks and a printed caption identifying Poiana Brașov and the hotel.

Vintage Romanian postcard showing the ornate interior of Sala Unirii (Union Hall) in the Alba Iulia citadel: a long arched hall with chandeliers, stucco decorations, marble columns and display tables; flags are visible along the right wall. The reverse has Romanian printed captioning, a brown 55 B Posta Romana stamp, a Zlatna (Alba) postmark, and a handwritten message addressed to Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a grand neoclassical building with a circular dome and a colonnaded portico on a corner square with tram tracks, a red tram, an obelisk-like monument, pedestrians, and mid‑century cars. The back has Romanian text, stamp, and postmarks.

Color postcard featuring a studio photograph of gladiolus flowers in red, white, and pink against a neutral background. The reverse side has Romanian handwriting, a blue 55 BANI postage stamp depicting a swimmer, circular postmarks, and printed lines for address.

Color postcard with a close-up photo of Christmas tree ornaments: two red glass baubles with white floral motifs and a small orange figurine ornament, with warm bokeh lights. The reverse is in Romanian, formatted as a standard addressable postcard with handwritten New Year greetings and a recipient's name.

Color view of a grand Beaux‑Arts building with corner domes at a large urban intersection, busy with pedestrians, crosswalks, trolleybus wires and several 1960s–70s cars. This is the University of Bucharest building at University Square in central Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a panoramic view of a mountain town with socialist‑era apartment blocks and pine‑covered slopes, framed by fir branches. A county coat of arms labeled with Maramureș appears on the image. The reverse has Romanian address fields and a handwritten message dated 11 May 1980.

Color postcard showing a TAROM jet airliner on the apron with its tail bearing the Romanian flag and TAROM logo. In the background are the terminal building with the sign "BUCUREȘTI–OTOPENI" and the control tower of Bucharest's Otopeni Airport.

Color postcard showing tourists walking among the stone walls and standing columns of an ancient seaside ruin under a bright blue sky. The reverse has Romanian publisher information, a multilingual caption identifying the site, two POSTA ROMANA 20 BANI stamps, a handwritten message and an address.

Color postcard showing a crowded beach with rocks and gentle surf. In the background are 1970s–1980s modernist, terraced hotel blocks forming a stepped pyramid silhouette. Sunbathers, swimmers, and a beached boat are visible. The reverse has Romanian text, printed caption 'AURORA. Plaja – The beach' and postal markings with a Romanian stamp.

Multiview Romanian postcard promoting Tulcea: views of the Danube Delta with waterlilies, boats at sunset, and a fisherman with a large fish. Two modern socialist-era buildings are shown, including the Casa de Cultură and the 'Diana' universal store. Front title banner reads 'Tulcea.' The back has Romanian handwriting, an address to Bucharest, a 'POSTA ROMANA 40 BANI' stamp with the socialist coat of arms, and Bucharest postmarks.

Color postcard showing a rocky Black Sea shoreline with clear turquoise water and, across the beach, a line of large stepped, terraced modernist hotel blocks. The back has Romanian text and a Romanian stamp with postmarks from Mangalia. Printed caption identifies the scene as Stațiunea Aurora (Aurora Resort), part of the seaside resorts near Mangalia.

Color postcard showing a mountain inn complex with steep shingle roofs set against dense forested hills. A rocky riverbank is in the foreground, and two 1970s–1980s coaches and a couple of cars are parked on the road; one bus has the word ROMANIA on its side. A sign on the left building reads AGAPIA. The reverse has Romanian text and a printed caption identifying the place.

Color New Year postcard. Front shows a lit candle and a large red ornament with snowflakes on a blue background and a round photo inset of children in Romanian winter folk costumes celebrating in the snow. The text at top reads "La mulți ani!". The back is a Romanian postcard with preprinted green 'România Poșta Română 40 bani' indicium, Romanian address lines, cancellation marks, a handwritten holiday message, and address to Câmpina, Prahova.

Winter-themed Romanian greeting postcard. The front shows red-white script reading "La multi ani!" above a lit candle on a decorative holder set over fir branches and snowflakes, with an inset photo of a child in traditional Romanian winter dress holding a bouquet of colorful flowers. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp, postmarks, and an address to Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a broad boulevard and landscaped square in Cluj, with the Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral on the left, the National Theatre/Opera building with rooftop statues on the right, and 1960s cars on the street. The reverse is in Romanian, with a 40 Bani Poșta Română stamp and a handwritten message dated 18.07.1969. The card is printed with "CLUJ — Piața Victoriei."

A multiview seaside postcard showing scenes from Constanța, Romania: a modernist building and landscaped boulevard, fishermen on a lagoon with high-rise hotels in the distance, a landscaped park with cars, a crowded sandy beach with resort hotels, and a large neoclassical theater facade labeled "TEATRUL DE STAT." The design includes a nautical anchor emblem. Reverse has a Romanian handwritten message, a Romanian 40 bani stamp with the socialist coat of arms, and a postmark reading Constanța-Litoral.

A multi-view color postcard with five photos of the famous painted churches/monasteries of Bucovina, each showing exterior frescoes and steep wooden roofs. The front has a dark teal border with the title in pink 'MONUMENTE ISTORICE' and the script 'Suceava' at the bottom. The reverse is a Romanian postal template with a printed 2 LEI stamp and captions listing the featured monasteries.

Color postcard showing the central square of a Romanian town with landscaped flower beds, benches and socialist‑era apartment blocks. A rooftop propaganda sign praises the Romanian Communist Party. Reverse side has a long handwritten Romanian message, an address in Bucharest, and three Romanian stamps (a train, the Endless Column of Târgu Jiu, and a Suceava folk costume). The printed caption identifies Hațeg and says it is a view from the center.

Color postcard showing a landscaped park with manicured lawns, flowerbeds and trees. At the center stands a white stone war memorial depicting Romanian soldiers raising a flag on a high pedestal with reliefs. The reverse bears Romanian handwriting, a Romanian stamp and the printed caption naming the monument.

Color postcard showing the Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral in Timișoara, with its patterned green-tiled roofs and tall central spire, seen from a tree-lined boulevard with flower beds and overhead tram wires. The reverse side has a Romanian 40 bani stamp, Timișoara postmarks, and a handwritten Romanian message, addressed to Bucharest.

Multiview color postcard showing landmarks associated with Suceava, Romania: an equestrian statue of Stephen the Great on a tall plinth, the 16th‑century Moldovița Monastery church, a modern roundabout and the 'Moda' complex, and the House of Culture of Trade Unions with landscaped squares and socialist‑era apartment blocks. Reverse has Romanian handwriting dated 31.05.81, a 'POSTA ROMANA' 40 bani stamp, Suceava/București postmarks, and an address to Bucharest.

Color view of a mountain spa resort set among forested hills. A large terraced modernist hotel dominates the center-right, with older villas with red-tile roofs and lush greenery in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, Romanian postage and cancellation marks, and printed caption information.

Color postcard showing a symmetrical view of the Heroes' Monument with bronze figures and eagles atop a tiered stone structure surrounded by trees. The reverse has Romanian layout fields (Carte poștală), a 40 bani Posta Română stamp and postmarks, handwritten greeting and address. Printed caption at bottom identifies Drobeta Turnu‑Severin and the monument.

Color postcard showing an oblique aerial view of a fortified monastery complex in a green valley with forested hills. The complex has high stone walls with corner towers and a central painted church—this is the Sucevița Monastery. The reverse side has Romanian address lines and a printed caption identifying the site.

Oblique aerial view of a seaside resort with modernist hotels and a low pavilion with colorful vertical panels in the foreground, landscaped pools and parking areas, the Black Sea shore to the left and a large lagoon/lake to the right. The reverse has Romanian printing with address lines and publisher details.
Color postcard showing an ornate carved wooden spiral staircase inside a lavish historic interior. The reverse side is laid out for mailing and printed in Romanian.

Color postcard view of a lush mountain valley dotted with wooden-roof houses and fenced fields, likely a rural village. Conifer-covered hills rise in the background, and a stream runs through the green meadows. Out-of-focus pink flowers frame the foreground.

Color postcard showing a winter scene in the mountains above Sinaia. A large modernist hotel/cable-car station stands on a snowy slope with a red cable car cabin and cables crossing the building. Forested ridges and snow-covered peaks of the Carpathians are in the background. The reverse side is in Romanian with address fields and publisher/pricing info.

A color postcard showing a white marble statue group of Fortuna and Pontos against a solid red background. At the bottom it reads "MUZEUL DE ARHEOLOGIE CONSTANȚA." The reverse has multilingual captions, Romanian postal headings, and publisher/price details.

Color postcard showing a winter scene at a mountain resort surrounded by dense fir forests and distant snow-capped peaks. In the lower left stands a large modern multi-story hotel complex. The reverse has Romanian address fields and publisher information identifying the location as Predeal and the hotel as Hotel Orizont.

Color postcard showing a small Orthodox roadside chapel built into a rocky cliff, reached by stone steps, with a steel railway bridge above and a road in the foreground. The back is printed in Romanian with 'CARTE POSTALĂ' and 'POSTA ROMÂNĂ' and identifies the site as Piatra Scrisă near Armeniș, Caraș-Severin County.

A multiview color postcard showing the Iron Gates hydroelectric and navigation complex on the Danube: dam, spillways, locks for ships, road across the dam, and electrical substations with pylons. The front has Romanian captions in yellow panels. The reverse is a Romanian postal back with printed stamp and price.

Color postcard showing a large concrete arch dam and blue reservoir in a rocky mountain gorge. At right is a modernist observation tower with switch‑back stairs and a person in an orange top on a balcony. Clear blue sky. Reverse has a multilingual caption identifying the hydropower station on the Argeș River, address lines in Romanian, price in lei, photo credit to Al. Florescu, and publisher Editura Meridiane.

Color postcard showing a seaside holiday resort with low modernist bungalows, lawns and paths, and the Black Sea in the background. A woman is seated on a balcony. The reverse has Romanian handwriting and postal marks; printed elements include 'CARTE POȘTALĂ', 'COSTINEȘTI', publisher and price details.

Color photo postcard showing a modernist building with a wide glass facade, cantilevered roof and a sculptural stage tower, surrounded by landscaped flowerbeds and paths. People walk on steps in a plaza under a bright blue sky. The back caption identifies it as the National Theatre in Craiova.

Color postcard showing a sunrise over the sea, viewed from a seafront terrace with ornate iron railings and vintage lamp posts silhouetted in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian address fields and a multilingual caption identifying Eforie Nord and describing the scene as the sea at dawn.

Color postcard showing a modernist alpine hotel with many balconies, fir trees around it, benches in front, and a person seated. The building has signage reading HOTEL and a vertical PREDEAL. The reverse side is a Romanian postcard template with mailing fields, publisher credit, and a printed price.

Color postcard showing a lively mountain resort town with a tree‑lined main boulevard, mid‑century hotels and villas, pedestrians and 1970s-era cars, all set against forested hills. The back is a divided Romanian address side with a stamp box and publisher details.

Two-view color postcard from a Romanian seaside resort. The top image shows a modernist high-rise hotel with balconies and a ground-floor sign reading "COMPLEXUL U.G.S.R."; people, a horse-drawn carriage, a car and a yellow bus are in front. The bottom image shows a crowded Black Sea beach with breakwaters. The reverse has a Romanian printed template from the trade-union tourist network, a green 10 lei Posta Romana stamp, Bucharest postmark from early November 1972, and a handwritten Romanian message addressed to Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a tree-lined seaside promenade and beach on the Black Sea, with modern hotels/buildings and people walking. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, printed caption "ROMANIA – MANGALIA — The cliff", a blue "POSTA ROMANA" stamp, and Bucharest postmarks. Addressed to Bucharest.

Color postcard showing a statue group in a garden — the monument of Farkas and János Bolyai — set before a neo‑Gothic building with a red tiled roof and ornate windows. The reverse has Romanian layout fields, a Romanian stamp commemorating 22 Decembrie 1989, and a Bucharest cancellation. Printed caption names Târgu Mureș.

Color postcard showing a tranquil mountain lake with pine-covered hills in the background. People are rowing a small white boat and swimming; a toy sailboat floats in the foreground. Lakeside lamps and cottages line the shore. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a Romanian 40 Bani stamp (Poșta Română), and postmarks reading TUSNAD and BUCUREȘTI.

Color postcard showing a detail of the famous "Ladder of Virtues" fresco: a monk climbing a golden ladder while a demon pulls him down. The reverse side has Romanian text giving the subject and price, with space for address and stamp.

A multi-image postcard featuring Secu Monastery and its ecclesiastical treasures. The central photo shows the fortified Romanian Orthodox monastery complex with white church walls and conical towers against forested hills. Surrounding images display a carved cross, a gilded gospel cover with medallions, silver censers and chandeliers, and an embroidered epitaph. The front title reads "MÎNĂSTIREA SECU." The back lists the depicted items in Romanian, French, German, and English and credits the Metropolis of Moldavia and Suceava in Iași.

Color postcard showing the church within Sucevița Monastery, a Moldavian painted monastery with steep shingled roofs and defensive walls, set against a forested hillside. The reverse bears Romanian text naming the site and publisher.

Color postcard showing the painted exterior walls and shingled roof/tower of the Voroneț Monastery church in Bucovina. Back side has Romanian printed layout "CARTE POSTALĂ," a Romanian 40 bani stamp, and cancellation marks from Suceava and București.

Color postcard showing the painted exterior of the Church of Humor Monastery, a Moldavian Orthodox church with a large shingled roof topped by crosses, frescoed outer walls, and a porch, set among green trees under a blue sky. The back has Romanian printed text and a handwritten note.

Color postcard showing a young child reaching out to two performing dolphins standing upright in a pool, likely during a show at a dolphinarium. The back carries Romanian text, dolphin graphics, address lines, and a printed price.

Color view of an interior gallery in a military museum displaying mortars, machine guns, ship models, uniforms, photographs, and many Romanian tricolor flags with the socialist coat of arms hanging from the ceiling. It depicts the room dedicated to the 1917 battles of Mărășești, Mărăști and Oituz.

Museum postcard from Romania reproducing an old engraving: a view of Bucharest with a hilltop princely palace complex and church towers above the Dâmbovița River, a wooden bridge with carts and people, watermills on the bank, and figures in period dress in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian address fields and credits the Art Museum of the Socialist Republic of Romania; the image is titled "Palace at Bucharest," engraved by William Watts after Luigi Mayer.

Black-and-white postcard showing an elevated view over a forested valley with the Bistrița Monastery complex: several Orthodox church buildings with onion-shaped domes, a clock on the main church facade, surrounding trees and hills, and a small river and bridge nearby.

Sunset view over a lagoon with reeds and small sailboats moored near the shore. Warm sunlight reflects on the water. The reverse side identifies the scene as Siut-Ghiol at sunset and includes multilingual captions, publisher imprint, price, and photographer credit.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a hillside resort town with many villas among forests and mountains. The reverse bears Romanian text and three Romanian People's Republic stamps, dated 13/9/1949, and is addressed to Bacău.

Color postcard showing a landscaped park with rose bushes and a wide roundabout in the foreground, and a tall Socialist Realist building with a central spire and flanking wings in the background. A statue is visible to the right; modernist street lamps frame the scene. The back carries printed Romanian text indicating it is a postcard.

Black‑and‑white photo of a large alpine-style rest house with shutters and a pitched roof, set among fir trees and hills. The reverse identifies it as a rest house in Covasna and bears a Romanian 40‑bani purple stamp (W. Blake), postmarks, and a handwritten Romanian message and address.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a view through a ruined stone arch. Framed by the arch is a white, tower-like building with a steep pyramidal roof on a wooded hill—part of a hilltop fortress. The reverse has Romanian printed text, a blue Romanian stamp, multiple postmarks, a handwritten message in Romanian, and an address in Bucharest.

Sepia photograph showing a leafy spa town with large hotel-like buildings and hills in the background. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a 38‑bani green Romanian stamp, circular postmarks dated Dec 1953, and printed headings indicating the view is from Călimănești. Addressed to Sighișoara (Regiunea Stalin).

Monochrome mountain view framed by conifer trees with wooden fences and a chalet roof in the foreground. The reverse side is printed with 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMÂNĂ' and 'PĂLTINIȘ — Vedere' and bears a Romanian 55 bani stamp and handwritten Romanian message and address.

Sepia-toned view of a mountain resort town seen through tall fir trees, with scattered villas, a rail line and hills in the background. The back reads in Romanian that it is a postcard from the People's Republic of Romania and labels the view as Predeal looking toward Cioplea.

Sepia photograph of a landscaped town park with curving paths, flowerbeds and benches among tall trees. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard with Romanian text indicating it is from the Romanian People's Republic and titled "Călimănești — Vedere din parc."

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large neoclassical academic building with a mansard roof and landscaped gardens in front. Groups of students are walking down steps and along paths; a lamppost with globes is visible. The back side reads in Romanian that it is from the People's Republic of Romania and identifies the place as the medical‑pharmaceutical institute in Târgu Mureș.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a wooded mountain resort scene: a lane with people walking among tall fir trees, with a large wooden chalet with balconies at right. The reverse is printed with Romanian People's Republic markings and the caption indicating Borsec and the way to the springs, also given in Russian.

Sepia-toned winter street scene in a mountain resort town with alpine-style villas and balconies, snow-laden roofs, conifer forests in the background, and a church-like building on the right. People walk along a snowy road. The back is printed with Romanian and Cyrillic text indicating the location and the issuing period.

Sepia postcard view of a mountain resort town: a grand arcaded building set in a wooded park with the Carpathian mountains behind. The reverse bears Romanian text including the state name of the era and a caption indicating Sinaia and a park view.

Sepia photographic postcard showing a streamlined, ship‑like modernist seaside building with rounded balconies and round porthole windows. The reverse is in Romanian and labels the view as a rest house in Eforie on the Black Sea, with a standard address layout and publisher mark.

Sepia-toned art postcard showing a painted self‑portrait of a man in three‑quarter view with mustache, reproduced from an oil painting. The back bears a bilingual caption (Romanian and Russian) crediting the work and mentions the Museum of Art of the Romanian People's Republic, plus the imprint "LIBRĂRIA NOASTRĂ" and the header "Carte poștală."

Vintage sepia postcard showing a dramatic rocky canyon with towering limestone walls and a strip of sky above—an image of the Bicaz Gorge. The reverse bears printed headings and publisher marks in Romanian and Russian.

Black-and-white postcard view of a narrow mountain road winding into a dramatic rocky gorge with forested cliffs. The reverse has multilingual captions and address lines, including a Romanian state header and publisher mark.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a tree‑filled park in Deva with paths and terraces descending through pines; in the distance stands a large neo‑Gothic/Secession‑style public building with a slender spire. The back is printed in Romanian and Russian, identifying the scene as the park in Deva, and carries standard address lines and a publisher mark.

Sepia seaside view showing gentle waves of the Black Sea, a small wooden fishing boat pulled onto a sandy beach, and a person resting nearby. The back is printed with Romanian and Cyrillic captions indicating the location as Eforie and includes publisher markings.

Sepia postcard showing a fountain with the bronze Statue of Hercules in a spa-town square, with three children standing at the basin. Grand 19th‑century buildings and a church steeple rise behind, with wooded hills in the background. The reverse is printed with multilingual captions identifying the scene and marked "Carte poștală" and "EDITURA DE STAT."

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a turreted stone mountain lodge labeled "Cabana Cheile Turzii," set below dramatic limestone cliffs of a gorge. The reverse reads "REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMINĂ," has a stamp box with the number 780, address lines, publisher credit "Editura Meridiane," price "Lei 1," and the mark C.P.C.S.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a wooden mountain rest house (chalet) in a meadow with a dirt road in front and steep rocky, forested mountains rising behind it. The reverse has printed captions in Romanian and Russian indicating the route to Postăvarul and notes the People's Republic of Romania.

Sepia-toned beach scene with crowds bathing and walking on a pier. An elegant arched footbridge crosses the pier, and a modernist pavilion with a small tower stands on the shoreline. The reverse side is printed in Romanian with sections for address and notes, indicating a state-published postcard.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a mountain chalet-style rest house with steep gabled roofs and shutters, set on a hillside with a wooden fence and conifer trees; misty mountains in the background. The reverse has printed Romanian and Russian captions indicating the location in Predeal and a handwritten date.

Sepia-toned view of a seaside beach with waves and swimmers in the water; people sunbathing on the sand below. The reverse side reads in Romanian and Cyrillic, indicating it is a Romanian People's Republic era postcard and naming the location as Vasile Roaită – Beach.
Sepia photograph of people rowing small boats on a tree-lined lake. The reverse side states it is a view from Cișmigiu in Bucharest, with Romanian and Russian captions and publisher markings.

Sepia postcard view through a massive stone arch framing a narrow ravine with a small stream and a footpath. Beyond is another arched bridge and a medieval conical-roof tower and fortification buildings, likely part of Brașov's old city walls. The back is printed in Romanian with headings indicating the People's Republic era and the city name as Orașul Stalin.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large neoclassical academic building set behind a formal garden. Another colonnaded building appears at the right edge. The reverse is printed in Romanian and Russian and identifies the subject as the medical–pharmaceutical institute in Timișoara; it bears the heading 'CARTE POȘTALĂ'.
Sepia-toned postcard showing a winter mountain scene with snow-laden fir trees on a slope. The reverse has a divided back with address lines and publisher markings.

Black‑and‑white street view showing a grand neoclassical courthouse with a pediment labeled 'PALATUL JUSTITIEI'. Crowds and period cars fill a broad square/avenue. The reverse side carries Romanian postcard headings including 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMINA — CRAIOVA — Vedere' and 'CARTE POȘTALĂ'.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a monastery church with a shingled tower set in tall grass and trees, with the Făgăraș Mountains in the background. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, the printed caption naming the site, publisher details, and a Romanian 40 Bani stamp depicting a lizard (Ablepharus kitaibelii). There are Bucharest postmarks and an address written to a recipient in Bucharest.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing three hikers on a rocky outcrop overlooking a forested valley in the Ciucaș Mountains. A winding track leads to a lone mountain chalet in a clearing. Caption at top left reads "MUNTII CIUCAȘ – Cabana "Muntele Roșu"". The reverse has Romanian printing from the People's Republic era, handwritten message and address, and Bucharest postmarks.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a streetscape in Reghin with ornate late‑19th/early‑20th‑century façades lining a broad central street with planters. Pedestrians and shopfronts are visible, including a sign reading "CASA RUSA." The caption on the image reads "Vedere din Reghin." The reverse bears standard Romanian postcard markings from the communist era.

Multi-view color postcard showing the medieval town and citadel of Sighișoara: panoramic hillsides with red-roofed houses, several fortified towers and walls, cobbled streets and a square seen through an arch. The iconic Clock Tower dominates multiple views. A red banner with yellow letters reads "SIGHIȘOARA" on the front; the back has Romanian postcard layout and publisher details.

Black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard showing landmarks of Târgu Mureș. The main image depicts the Secession‑style Culture Palace facing a landscaped square; other panels show an elevated city view with the large dome of the Orthodox Cathedral, a central street scene with period vehicles and ornate lampposts, and a panoramic landscape outside the city. The front title reads "Tg. MUREȘ." The back has Romanian text, a 1959 Târgu Mureș postmark, and handwritten greetings and an address.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a dramatic mountain gorge with a narrow road climbing in tight hairpin turns (serpentines) between steep, forested limestone cliffs. Caption at the bottom reads "Serpentina de la Cheile Bicazului." The reverse side bears Romanian text, a 40‑bani stamp, 1960 postmarks, and a short handwritten greeting with an address in București.

A black-and-white view of several alpine-style resort villas set among tall conifer forests. The reverse side is printed in Romanian, titled for Borsec and bearing a Romanian postage stamp commemorating the Tokyo 1964 Olympics, cancelled at Borsec (Reg. Mureș). Addressed to București.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large timbered resort building with verandas and ornate wooden details, set on a terraced garden with steps and statues; pedestrians walk along the street in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian text, a 40 BANI stamp marked R.P. ROMÎNĂ, and printed caption "SOVATA. Clubul".

Night view of an airport apron with a TAROM aircraft tail marked YR-IMC in the foreground and the round terminal building with a control tower behind it. A neon sign reading "Bucuresti" glows on the terminal. The reverse bears the TAROM logo and a caption identifying the scene.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large school building with a tall wooden-roofed tower and a long multi‑story wing behind a low fence. Caption at top left reads "TG. MUREȘ – Școala agricolă." The back is a Romanian postcard of the People's Republic era with an airmail stamp and handwritten message and address.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a modernist seaside building with a scalloped roof and open terraces labeled "EFORIE – Restaurantul nou." Patio umbrellas and people are visible in front. The reverse has Romanian text, a 40‑bani Romanian stamp, and postmarks.

Black-and-white postcard view of a large Gothic church with a very steep tiled roof and buttresses, seen above the rooftops of a historic town surrounded by forested mountains. On the reverse there is printed Romanian captioning identifying the site, a 40 bani fish-themed Romanian stamp, circular postmarks, and a short handwritten message and address in blue ink.

Black‑and‑white seaside view showing people walking on a promenade with a balustrade. At the end of the pier stands an ornate Art Nouveau building on the Black Sea shore — the famous casino. Reverse side has Romanian printed headings, a purple Romanian stamp commemorating "zece ani dela eliberare 1944–1954," a Constanța postmark, and a handwritten message/address in Romanian.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a calm lake bordered by reeds and trees, with a small pavilion or hut visible across the water. The back reads 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMÎNĂ' and identifies the view as 'SOVATA Lacul Ursu' with a Russian line as well. Standard address lines and 'CARTE POȘTALĂ' are printed.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a mountain landscape with a river winding through the Cerna Valley, trees in the foreground, and hillsides in the distance. Caption on the front reads "BĂILE HERCULANE – Valea Cernei." The reverse has Romanian text, a 40‑bani airmail stamp of the Romanian People's Republic with 1962 postmarks and a handwritten address.

Front: color postcard with an orange border showing a large stepped modernist spa hotel/sanatorium building set against wooded hills and a blue sky. Back: Romanian trade‑union postcard template with blue printed text, a blue 2 lei 'Poșta Română – Arta Populară' stamp, postal cancellations from Covasna and Brăila dated 1983, a printed description of the Covasna spa, and a handwritten message addressed to Brăila.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a landscaped garden with curving flowerbeds, a promenade with railings, and a multi‑story resort/hotel building with a terrace at the right, set amid trees and low hills. The back lists multilingual captions identifying the view of Sovata and standard postcard address lines.

Tinted sepia photo of a narrow street in a mountain spa town with multi‑story buildings with balconies, steep roofs, and people walking. The reverse has Romanian text and address lines, including the header 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMINĂ' and 'TUȘNAD — Vedere'.

Color view of a small Carpathian town: low-rise apartment blocks and a white three‑story building at the base of a steep rocky, forested hill. A red 1960s–70s sedan is parked at left and a blue‑white bus stands at right on an unpaved street. The reverse bears Romanian postal marks and a printed caption indicating Baia Borșa.

Color portrait of a seated woman with short auburn hair, wearing a dark turtleneck and holding a cigarette, in front of floral curtains and an ornate sofa. The reverse is a blue-printed divided back with a filmstrip logo reading CASA FILMULUI, the printed name ANNIE DUPEREY along the edge, and a printed price lei 2.

Color portrait postcard showing a close-up of a woman wearing a large white hat with a flower, a delicate pearl choker, a ruffled polka-dot blouse, and holding white flowers. The reverse is printed in blue with standard postcard divisions and pricing.

Color postcard showing the seaside promenade in Constanța with the Art Nouveau Constanța Casino on a pier by the Black Sea, a park lawn and a reclining stone statue in the foreground. Reverse side is a Romanian postcard layout with a 40 bani 'ROMANIA – POSTA ROMANA' stamp, postmarks from Mamaia and București dated 1967, handwritten message and address. Printed caption at bottom reads "CONSTANTA — Cazinoul".

Front shows a traditional Romanian embroidered towel (ștergar) with stylized birds and two large facing roosters, geometric borders and lace edging. The reverse is a divided-back museum postcard with Romanian text crediting the Constanța Art Museum's folk art section and a printed price.

Color postcard showing a grand early‑20th‑century academic building with a red tile roof and many tall windows, facing a green square with trees, benches, pedestrians, and a few cars. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, Romanian stamps and postmarks, and a printed caption identifying the place as the Medical Institute in Timișoara.

Color postcard showing a modernist seaside hotel complex with a tall grid‑balcony tower and outdoor swimming pools filled with tourists. The front is labeled "hotel sirena" with a round "SATURN" mark. The reverse has Romanian address fields, multiple POSTA ROMANA stamps, and a Bucharest postmark, plus a handwritten Romanian message.

Color postcard showing a modernist, socialist-era cultural building with a long portico and white columns, seen across a plaza with flowerbeds in the foreground. The reverse has Romanian postal printing (CARTE POSTALA, POSTA ROMANA), a pre-printed 40 bani stamp, a Bucharest postmark, a handwritten Romanian message and an address in Bucharest. Printed caption at lower left identifies the place as the Casa de cultură a sindicatelor in the city of Roman.

Color view of a hilltop medieval fortress with red-roofed towers and thick stone walls, seen from a curving road with houses below. The reverse side is a printed Romanian postcard template with a pre-printed stamp and address fields.

Color postcard showing an elevated view of Sibiu's historic center with dense red‑tiled roofs. Visible are the Council Tower with a clock face and the onion‑domed Roman Catholic (Jesuit) Church on the edge of the main square area.

Color postcard showing the ornate seaside Constanța Casino building with gardens, trees, and people walking on the promenade. The reverse side has a Romanian 40 bani stamp (Poșta Română) with Constanța postmark, address lines to Bucharest, and printed caption 'CONSTANȚA: Cazinoul.'

A commemorative postcard featuring a historic black‑and‑white street scene overlaid with small color photos of landmarks along Calea Victoriei in Bucharest. The caption celebrates 300 years of the street formerly called Podul Mogoșoaiei. Landmarks pictured include the Romanian Athenaeum, the CEC Palace, the former Royal Palace/National Museum of Art, and Kretzulescu Church.

Color postcard showing a mountain resort town with villas and red-roofed houses at the base of steep, rocky peaks and dense conifer forest. Several white apartment blocks stand out in the foreground. The scene matches the Bucegi Mountains rising above Bușteni under a bright blue sky.

Color postcard of a snowy winter scene at a ski resort: a drag‑lift runs past a small chalet amid fir trees, with skiers on the slope and a rocky mountain ridge under a clear blue sky. The reverse bears Romanian postal layout with publisher and multilingual caption.

Color photograph of a narrow brick passageway with multiple arched buttresses and tiled roofs, known as a historic stairway. Several pedestrians in mid‑20th‑century attire walk along the path. The reverse side is a divided-back postcard with Romanian text and multilingual captions identifying the place.

Color postcard showing a long flower-lined lawn and landscaped park surrounded by trees, with spa hotels/buildings in the background; caption indicates Govora.
