A vintage monochrome postcard showing a coastal view with a fortified hilltop complex dominating the background, likely a citadel. Sailing ships are anchored in the calm harbor, and low waterfront buildings and trees line the shore in the foreground. The upper right corner bears printed text in French reading "Souvenir de Corfou." The image has a faded, early-photographic style typical of late‑19th or early‑20th‑century postcards, with some handwritten marks and a stamp impression near the bottom.

Black‑and‑white aerial or elevated view over a small European town with dense low-rise houses, trees, and fields in the distance. A church with a tall tower and onion-shaped spire stands prominently to the right. The sky is cloudy, and the image has a white border with a deckled edge typical of vintage postcards. At the bottom left, printed text identifies the scene as a view from the old water tower in Elsterwerda.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a large, two‑story masonry school building with a raised basement, symmetrical façade, and classical portico supported by two columns. The structure has many tall rectangular windows, rusticated stone at the ground level, and a central entrance reached by broad steps. A ventilator or cupola rises from the hipped roof. Trees frame the scene in the foreground, and a dirt or early concrete path leads toward the entrance, with a simple wooden fence and railing. Several bicycles are parked along the side of the building. The image edge shows a black border and some damage at the top, typical of early photographic postcards.

Sepia-toned vintage street view showing a wide avenue lined with multi‑story European-style buildings with balconies. There are shopfronts on the right, people in traditional clothing walking along the street, and a horse‑drawn carriage in the distance. Large trees and what appears to be a church or large building are visible further down the road. The caption at the top left identifies the location, and a modern website watermark appears at the bottom right.

Colorized vintage street view showing a wide, straight avenue lined with low trees and early-20th‑century buildings. Many people walk along the road, some in groups. At the top is a Greek postage stamp with a circular postmark. At the bottom, there is a French caption beginning with "Avenue de la …". The overall look is that of an early 20th‑century urban development scene.

Colorized view over a calm blue bay framed by dark green foliage and hills. In the foreground, a tiny islet holds a white church with a red-tiled roof and a small pier. Further back, another rocky islet with tall trees and buildings rises from the water. Mountains form the distant background. Handwritten text runs along the bottom and right edges, and printed captions appear near the lower edge.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large, four‑storey brick institutional building forming an L‑shaped courtyard with several 1930s–1940s automobiles parked in front. Framed by pine trees, the structure has many uniform rectangular windows and a simple, functionalist design. In the lower right corner there is a white oval photographer's stamp and printed credits.

A vintage black-and-white postcard with a dark background. Across the center is the large word "TROLLHÄTTAN" in stylized, wavy block letters. Each letter is filled with small photographic scenes, likely showing various views of the city: churches, streets, buildings, waterways, bridges, ships, and surrounding landscapes. There is no other visible text or border decoration.

A colorized vintage cityscape showing a dense cluster of low- and mid-rise buildings with red-tile roofs and several prominent white commercial blocks in the foreground. The scene looks over a commercial district with hills in the background. At the top left, text in multiple languages identifies the location as Varna and the commercial square.

Black-and-white view of a tree-lined street in a hilly town with large late‑19th‑century villas and a church or town‑hall tower in the background. In the foreground is an ornate villa with half‑timbered gables and a tall spire, set above the street behind a fence. Two women in long dresses walk along the wide, unpaved road. The scene suggests a European spa or resort town.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a wide shoreline curving along a body of water, with a small settlement of low wooden buildings and fences stretching along the coast in the background. The landscape looks rural and slightly hilly. There is printed Russian text in the lower margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a mountainous landscape with steep rocky slopes and scattered trees, likely a gorge or valley. A few small buildings sit nestled among the trees in the center. The lower margin contains captions in Greek and French indicating Crete, along with the place name Therisso and a round seal on the left; a web address watermark appears across the bottom.

Black‑and‑white aerial photograph of a dense European port city with a busy waterfront lined with ferries and small ships, curving quays, mid‑rise blocks, and some areas under construction cut into rocky terrain. A large green park with tree‑lined avenues stretches inland, surrounded by blocks of 19th‑ and early‑20th‑century buildings. Overprinted purple text and a red frame line appear on the image, suggesting it is a proof or archive copy of a postcard view.

Old black‑and‑white postcard showing a calm river or canal with a low stone bridge and sluice/lock structure. There are three arches in the bridge and a wooden footbridge or gate on top. On the right bank stands a large white rural building with a dark roof, reflected in the still water. Trees and foliage frame the left side of the image, and there is a small wooden plank or jetty in the foreground by the water. Handwritten notes in dark ink appear over the image, likely in a Central or Eastern European language.

A sepia-toned portrait postcard showing a middle-aged man in a heavily decorated military uniform with epaulettes, medals, and orders. He has a bald head with hair on the sides and a large moustache. The image is vignetted, with printed captions beneath in French and Greek, and a circular stamp-like emblem in Greek at the lower left.

Black‑and‑white divided postcard. The upper image shows the facade of a multi‑story urban building with the sign 'Central‑Schlachthof' and a ground‑floor restaurant; various German inscriptions are visible on signs and windows. The lower image depicts a large interior dining hall with long tables laid with white tablecloths and flowers, and on the back wall hang two flags with swastikas flanking a central portrait. In the middle of the card is the caption 'Meißen a. d. Elbe.'

Vintage monochrome postcard view of a town square with a prominent multi‑story town hall building featuring a clock tower and ornate façade on the left. In front of it is a circular fountain. To the right stands a simpler multi‑story building and further right, among trees, a tall war memorial obelisk. The foreground shows the open marketplace. Printed captions in German identify the place and publisher.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a row of modernist residential houses on a sloping street. The buildings have flat roofs, clean rectangular lines, and a mix of smooth facades with horizontal siding. In the foreground, a few children sit and play near two small bicycles. The scene is quiet and suburban, with sparse trees in the background. Printed text appears at the bottom left of the image.

Black‑and‑white aerial view of an outdoor public swimming pool densely crowded with people. The rectangular pool is surrounded by sunbathers, diving platforms, and a tall metal diving tower on the right side. Long rows of wooden changing cabins line one side of the facility, and low pavilion‑like buildings occupy the foreground. In the background there are mature trees and several multi‑story residential houses with mansard roofs and balconies, suggesting a European urban setting. No visible printed caption or handwriting appears on the image side.

A black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a mid-20th‑century cargo ship at sea. The vessel is shown in profile, sailing from left to right, with multiple masts, cargo booms, and a central superstructure. The ship's name "BRITTA" is painted on the bow. In the lower right corner, there is printed caption text identifying the ship as M/s Britta and giving information about the Swedish shipping company and its location. The sky is filled with dramatic clouds and the sea appears calm.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a wide coastal landscape with a calm bay or gulf surrounded by low, rugged hills and distant mountains. There are small settlements along the shoreline and a boat or small ship visible in the water. Greek text is printed in the white margin beneath the image, along with a web address watermark over the photo.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a cobblestone street crowded with uniformed soldiers and civilians walking between multi‑storey buildings with balconies and flags. The scene is urban and busy, likely early 20th century. Printed captions in Greek and French identify the location as a street in Salonique (Thessaloniki). There is also a website watermark at the bottom right.

Sepia-toned theatrical postcard showing three actors on a stage-like set. On the left, a woman in an ornate dress extends her hand back toward a man in the center in formal evening wear who reaches toward her. On the right, an older man in a suit holds a large candelabrum. Stylized German titles and the actors' names are printed on the image, along with a small publisher's mark and a city and year in the lower right.

Black-and-white panoramic view of a European town seen across treetops, with dense low-rise buildings and, dominating the skyline, a large Gothic-style church or cathedral featuring two very tall, slender spires. Rolling hills rise in the far background. The image has rough, worn edges and some surface damage typical of early photographic postcards. No visible caption or printed text appears on the front.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a grand Baroque/Neoclassical episcopal residence with a formal garden in the foreground. A large statue of a robed figure stands on a high pedestal in front of the building, and there is also an obelisk-like monument to the right. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and sit on benches. Decorative handwritten script covers the lower margin. Printed text near the bottom right reads "Püspöki Rezidenczia," and the word "Pécs" appears in the handwriting at the bottom left.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a crowded grandstand in front of ornate historic buildings during a medieval-style jousting tournament. Two armored riders on horses tilt with lances in an arena separated by a long wooden barrier, while spectators fill tiered seating and flags and banners hang from poles and facades. In the foreground, costumed figures watch the event. Printed caption text and publisher information appear along the bottom margin.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a large Orthodox church with multiple onion domes and a central bell tower, standing on a raised plot of land with stairs leading up. A few small figures are visible in the foreground on an open, bare ground. Printed Russian text appears beneath the image.

Black‑and‑white view of a cobbled courtyard enclosed by Renaissance and Baroque buildings. On the left stands a massive, older-looking structure with a steep gabled roof and small dormer windows, attached to a round tower and ivy‑covered walls. In the center rises a more ornate palace façade with triangular gables and a tall tower with a lantern and spire. On the right is a long arcade-like wing with repeated arched windows and sculpted figures above them, also covered in ivy. Several slender lampposts and simple metal posts line the otherwise empty courtyard. At the very bottom of the image, faint handwritten text appears to read something like a date, possibly "1902," mirrored or upside down.

Sepia-toned panoramic view over a lake with several rowboats in the foreground and a town on a hillside backed by mountains in the distance. A prominent church with twin towers stands out in the town. At the bottom, an Italian caption reads "Levico - Veduta generale e lago," indicating a general view of Levico and its lake.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard divided into four images. The upper left shows a hilltop castle‑like villa with crenellated tower, flag, and long veranda, surrounded by terraced vineyards. The upper right depicts steep vineyard terraces with scattered houses and a small round tower or pavilion at the top of the hill. The lower left view shows a large, ornate timber‑frame hotel or sanatorium building with multiple gables and a tall spire, set on a vine‑covered hillside. The lower right image presents a half‑timbered house with a distinctive rounded corner tower and a courtyard with an old wooden well or press. The card edge has a scalloped border. No printed caption text is visible.

A colorized view over a European riverside town with tightly packed multi‑story houses with red-tile roofs along a riverbank. Above the town, on a wooded hill, stands a large medieval hilltop fortress complex with multiple walls, towers, and buildings. To the right is a tall church with a distinctive Baroque onion-dome tower. The scene is surrounded by green countryside under a lightly clouded sky. No visible printed captions or text appear on the image side.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a river valley landscape with fields and wooded slopes. On the left hill stands the ruined twin-towered fortress labeled "Ruine Saaleck." On the right hill, across the valley, is another castle complex labeled "Rudelsburg - Kösen." Fine print along the right edge credits the publisher. The image has an old, early-20th‑century printed style.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large castle complex and cathedral towers on a hill above a river. In the foreground are riverside houses and boats; above them stand the fortified palace buildings and twin Gothic spires of a cathedral. There is German handwriting-style printed text on the right side identifying the location.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing views of Assisi. The upper part presents a wide view of the hill town with its basilica complex stretched along the slope. To the right is a broader landscape labeled "Panorama" with fields and small figures in the foreground and the town on the hill in the background. At the bottom left, framed decoratively, is a view of a medieval fortress labeled "La Rocca (XIV secolo)". Decorative text and a round stamp‑like mark with the letters "A. C. T." also appear.

A black‑and‑white view of a tree‑lined boulevard with a single pedestrian walking away from the camera. At the entrance to the avenue stand two large stone plinths, each surmounted by a reclining lion sculpture. Behind the right plinth is a villa-like building with a square tower, shuttered windows and a weathervane. The scene appears early‑20th‑century, with no cars present and a simple wooden fence running along the right side. The overall composition and framing resemble a vintage architectural postcard.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a long, tree‑lined avenue with tram tracks running along the center. People stand and walk along the road: a woman with a pram and a child on the left, and a man on the right. Large houses are partly visible behind the trees. The top of the image is arched. Printed captions at the bottom identify the scene as in Nijmegen and label the street as "Berg en Dalsche weg". Handwritten cursive text is visible across the lower margin, and printer information appears vertically along the left edge.

Illustrated postcard with a bold red background showing caricatured couples dancing energetically, accompanied by a man operating a gramophone that is mounted on a chair. The figures are drawn in a satirical, early‑20th‑century cartoon style. At the bottom, in black capital letters on a white band, is the German title 'APACHENTÄNZE!'. A small logo and the words 'OÖ LANDES-KULTUR GMBH' appear in the lower margin outside the image frame.

Black‑and‑white rural view showing a scattered village with wooden houses, barns, fences and open fields in the foreground, with a tree line in the distance. The printed caption at the bottom identifies the place, and a publisher line appears in smaller type on the right.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a large rectangular Renaissance-style palace or castle on a hill above a town. The long multi-windowed building with hipped roofs and dormers dominates the scene, with terraced gardens or walls in front and smaller town houses with tiled roofs below. The caption "Bilin Schloss" is printed in red at the top left, and a vertical red publisher's imprint appears along the right edge.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over a town in a wide valley with fields and scattered houses stretching towards distant low mountains. In the foreground are dense clusters of multi‑storey historic buildings and villas surrounded by trees; further back are railway lines, farms, and small settlements. The caption in German at the bottom margin identifies the view as looking from Freundschaftshöhe toward the town and the Ore Mountains (Erzgebirge). The overall layout and print style resemble a mid‑20th‑century tourist postcard.

An old black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a Baroque or late Renaissance building with ornate stonework. In the foreground there is a balustraded stone terrace partly covered with climbing plants and trees. Behind it stands a two‑storey mansion or palace wing with a steep tiled roof and dormer windows. At the center is an elaborate arched entrance with sculpted decoration and a balcony, suggesting a historic European residence or palace complex. The lower edge of the image is damaged, and handwritten numbers are visible along the bottom border.

A colorized postcard view of a landscaped urban park with a central octagonal bandstand or gazebo surrounded by trees, flowerbeds, white benches, and lampposts. Pathways lead toward the structure from the foreground, where more benches line the walkway. Low buildings with red roofs are visible beyond the greenery. Spanish and English captions identifying the scene and its location are printed in the image border, along with a postcard number.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing the ornate interior of a grand café or restaurant with high decorated ceilings, chandeliers, wall mirrors, wood paneling, and many small tables covered with white cloths and bentwood chairs. A piano is visible toward the back, and a sign reading "Pause" hangs above it. In the lower‑right corner, a caption reads "CAFÉ OPÉRA Unter den Linden 21."

Colorized postcard view of a street corner with a prominent three‑story historic building featuring a towered roof and ornate facade. People walk along the sidewalks and street. Signs on the building read "CENTRAL" and "KÖZPONTI SZÁLLODA" indicating a central hotel. Printed Hungarian captions at the bottom identify the scene and publisher.

Color-printed view of a large white building with arcades and red-tiled roofs, set behind a formal garden full of flowers and walking paths. A small national flag flies atop the central roof. White benches line the garden paths. The image has a vintage, slightly faded print quality and is framed by a white border, typical of mid‑20th‑century postcards.

Sepia portrait postcard of an older military officer in a German-style uniform with large moustache, wearing an Iron Cross at the neck and other high decorations on his chest. The background is plain. At the bottom of the image there is a facsimile handwritten inscription in German, ending with a signature and rank title. The card is bordered and shown against a measurement grid.

Sepia-toned postcard view of a rural road lined with tall trees leading into the distance. On the left side are fields, fences, telegraph poles and a few residential buildings; in the background on a hilltop is a large building complex. Printed German text in the upper left identifies the location as a road from Frankenberg toward Sachsenburg.

A black‑and‑white industrial view showing a large cellulose (pulp) factory complex with long low buildings, tall silos and chimneys emitting smoke. The plant stands behind a river or water channel, framed in the foreground by trees. At the lower right edge, a caption label reads "19. Fabrica de Celuloză".

Monochrome postcard-style print showing a medieval brick city gate and fortification. A round tower with a steep conical roof stands at the left, pierced by small slit windows. An arched gateway leads through the wall, with a couple of small human figures beneath it for scale. High, sloping ramparts or earthworks reinforce the walls on both sides. The scene is rendered in a somewhat artistic, etched style rather than a sharp photograph, and there is no visible caption on the front.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing an urban square with several electric trams, cobblestone pavement, and late‑19th‑century multi‑story buildings. In the background a steel suspension bridge is visible. The title text in red Gothic-style lettering reads "Gruss aus Blasewitz." and "Schillerplatz." The publisher credit appears at the bottom, also in red, mentioning Blasewitz. The tram in the center bears route signage and the number 209.

Colorized vintage view over a small alpine town in a valley, with tiled-roof houses clustered on a hillside and a large white church with a bulbous onion-shaped bell tower on the right. Mountains rise in the background, and trees and a wooden fence frame the foreground. Printed caption text appears at the top right.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a terraced garden path on a steep riverbank. On the right, wooden and stone retaining walls support a slope covered with vegetation and lead up to a large wooden house with decorative latticework balconies. On the left, dense trees and shrubs overlook a wide river or lake stretching into the distance. At the bottom center, the caption reads "Haus Böhme."

A monochrome vintage postcard showing a line of horse-drawn carts and carriages with drivers and pedestrians in a town square or open street, backed by multi‑storey Mediterranean-style buildings with shutters. The scene is bustling with people and appears to depict everyday urban life. There is printed French text at the bottom identifying the view as being from Corfu and describing the vehicles used for transporting food supplies, along with a publisher line indicating Paris.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a hilltop Baroque pilgrimage complex with multiple onion‑domed towers and domed chapels, surrounded by trees and a sloping grassy hillside in the foreground. The building is set on a high stone terrace wall with arcaded openings. There is a handwritten note along the right margin, but most of it is cut off or obscured.

Sepia-toned photographic postcard showing a uniformed guard or soldier standing in front of a chevron-striped sentry box. He wears a pickelhaube-style spiked helmet and holds a short sword at his side. In the upper right corner, a young woman in traditional dress leans out from what seems to be a window or balcony, offering him a flower. The scene appears staged, likely in a studio, and there is no visible printed text on the image side.

Vintage black-and-white postcard showing a small bridge over a calm river or canal, surrounded by trees and greenery in a park. The bridge and its reflection are centered in the composition. Printed captions in German appear at the bottom margin.

Black-and-white postcard showing the interior of a large Gothic church with tall ribbed vaults, slender pillars, wooden pews, a pulpit on the left, and the main altar at the far end. Caption text in German appears at the bottom of the image.

The image depicts a vintage postcard illustration of a corner building with the name 'ANTON SUESS' prominently displayed in large yellow letters across the storefront. The building has numerous display windows with curtains and mannequins or goods inside. Several well-dressed pedestrians from a historical era, possibly late 19th or early 20th century, walk by. There is a small cart in the foreground with the text 'Anton Suess' and 'Graz'. The color palette suggests an antique style.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a small decorative wooden bridge over a pond in a lush botanical garden. Dense tropical and subtropical plants surround the water, with large agaves or similar plants in the foreground. A person is seated on the middle of the bridge. Below the image is a printed caption and descriptive paragraph in Portuguese, and the right half of the card is left blank for writing or an address.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural mountain scene with dense forest, a dirt road with a simple wooden guardrail, and a large timber building labeled as the 'Rehberger Grabenhaus'. A narrow man‑made water channel runs alongside the road, crossed by small wooden bridges. Printed red text at the bottom identifies the place as Höhen-Kurort St. Andreasberg in the Harz mountains. Publisher information appears along the lower edge.

Colorized landscape view over a wooded hilly area with a curving elevated railway or tramway (a bergspoor or mountain railway) crossing on a bridge. A single railcar is visible on the line. In the foreground and background are winding roads and dense green trees under a blue sky. Printed caption text in Dutch appears at the top.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a large, two‑storey historic building with a small tower on the left side, situated beside a body of water and partially obscured by trees and shrubs. The facade bears German text indicating it is a concert and ballroom. Traditional half‑timbered houses stand to the left and right, suggesting a small European town setting.

Black-and-white multi-view postcard showing a large baroque courtyard complex. The top image appears to be an old painting or engraving of the site with carriages and people in 18th–19th‑century clothing. The two lower photographs show the same baroque pavilion wings and richly decorated gate surrounding a fountain basin, with visitors in 20th‑century dress. The architecture features long colonnaded façades with many tall windows, elaborate sculptural ornament, and the distinctive crowned portal of the complex.

Sepia-toned photographic postcard showing a large Renaissance-style hunting palace complex with gabled roofs, a central tower, and ivy-covered walls, set behind trees and an open lawn. Printed caption at the lower right reads "Jagdschloß Wermsdorf."

Sepia-toned photograph with a decorative scalloped border showing an Italian town square. On the left is a mid‑20th‑century apartment block with street‑level shops, including a bank; on the right is a large historic palazzo with small Gothic windows and a projecting balcony. A few pedestrians and a cyclist move across the largely empty square.

A black‑and‑white view of a massive stone Neo‑Renaissance/Neo‑Baroque style public building on a corner lot. The façade is richly ornamented with tall Corinthian columns, statuary in niches and on the roofline, decorative bas‑reliefs, and a heavily rusticated ground floor. Several arched entrances with steps lead into the building. In the foreground there is a formal garden or square with paths, low iron fences, and early 20th‑century pedestrians in long coats and hats. The image edges are worn and irregular, suggesting an old photographic postcard or plate.

Tinted historic postcard view of a busy bridge with ornate railings and lampposts, filled with pedestrians in late 19th–early 20th century clothing. The bridge leads into a street lined with multi‑storey buildings and shop signs, dominated by a tall church or tower with a bulbous onion dome and a clock. At the bottom in red Gothic-style script it reads "Graz." on the left and "Erzherzog Ferd. Karl-Brücke." on the right, with a small number "Nr. 537." in the lower left corner.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a cobblestone courtyard framed by old stone buildings and trees. To the left is a large masonry wall with a lantern; ahead stands a multi-storey gabled building with arched entrance; to the right another rough-stone house with steps. The scene is tranquil and mostly empty. German text printed in the bottom margin identifies the location.

The postcard depicts a large, ornate historic building with red-tiled roofs and white decorative elements, located on the bank of a river. The structure is identified as 'Fürstenschule' and is adjacent to a church with a tall spire. Trees line the promenade in front of the building, and a small boat is visible on the river. The sky is clear and blue, and the photograph has the appearance of a colorized image. The words 'Grimma' and 'Fürstenschule' are printed on the front.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a side view of a twin-funnel steamship at sea, with low, hilly coastline in the background. The handwritten-style caption at the bottom left reads the vessel's name and the word "Nautical," suggesting it is part of a ship postcard series.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the front view of a large, three-story civic building with a central tower-like section marked with the year 1896. The structure has a stone ground floor, stucco upper floors, mansard-style roof with dormer windows, and a stairway leading to the main entrance. People stand near the steps and a cart, with large trees framing the scene. Printed German text at the top identifies the location and function of the building, and a publisher line with date appears at the bottom.

Monochrome postcard view of an outdoor beer‑garden or terrace under tall trees, filled with many empty wooden tables and folding chairs. In the background stand wooden and half‑timbered buildings, and behind them a tall, square stone observation tower. The scene appears calm and shaded, with handwritten caption text at the bottom left.

A sepia-toned postcard displaying a river winding through a heavily wooded, hilly landscape. The scene is peaceful, with dense forests and a calm waterway. At the top, printed text reads 'Wechselburg. Muldenpartie'.

A black and white image depicting a picturesque coastal harbor scene with several wooden boats and sailing vessels moored at docks. Small traditional wooden houses line the shore beneath a large, rocky hillside. The name 'HUNNEBOSTRAND.' is printed in the lower left, and a triangular publisher logo with the code 5417 is visible in the lower right.

The postcard features a black-and-white photograph of a park scene with a wooden bridge leading into a lush, tree-filled area. In the background, a large building can be seen above the treetops. There is text in Bulgarian (Cyrillic) and French at the bottom, mentioning Varna and the sea garden.

A vintage postcard depicting a historic, three-story wooden building with prominent bay windows and ornate trim. The corner of the building has a small balcony and several exterior staircases. There is a wooden sidewalk and a telephone pole in front. The text at the top right reads 'Revere House, Albany, Ore.', and handwritten numbers are present on the left side of the image.

A black-and-white (sepia-toned) postcard image showing a central European town square, with prominent older buildings around the edges, two tall industrial chimneys in the background, a fountain or monument in the center, and ornate street lamps. The text "Frohburg i. S. Markt." appears at the top, suggesting the market square of Frohburg is depicted. There are also commercial signs visible on some of the buildings.

The image is a vintage postcard depicting a bustling European city square with ornate historic buildings, a monument with statues in the center, people and horse-drawn vehicles, and a hillside featuring a prominent clock tower overlooking the square. The scene is labeled 'Graz. Hauptplatz.' at the top left.

The image depicts a historical black-and-white photograph featuring an ornate building with glass arches and decorative domes set beside a river, surrounded by thick woodland. The building appears grand and is likely a pavilion or a café, with a picturesque setting. The top of the postcard has text printed in red, reading 'Karlsbad. Café Kaiserpark.'

A monochrome (tinted) historic postcard showing a panoramic view of a hilltop town dominated by a large complex of multi‑storey buildings and towers, including a prominent round defensive tower on the right and baroque‑style roofs and spires in the center. Smaller houses and greenery spread down the slope in the foreground. The caption "Elbogen." is printed in red at the lower left, with the publisher credit "Brück & Sohn, Meissen." and the number "1035" in small red type at the bottom edge.

Color-tinted historic postcard showing a market square bordered by buildings with steep red-tiled roofs and rows of carefully trimmed trees forming an arcade along the street. In the left foreground stands a tall stone column with a sculptural top, surrounded by a balustrade and chains. Two children pose in the open square in the front. The caption at the top reads in German about the market square in Königsberg in the Egerland.

Black‑and‑white photographic postcard showing a young striped antelope (likely a kudu or nyala calf) standing on bare ground and being hand‑fed by a person whose body is mostly out of frame on the left. In the upper right corner are the printed words "Mossamedes" and "Ex-selvagem".

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a broad, unpaved street in a European town. Two- and three‑story houses with steep tiled roofs line both sides. Several adults and many children stand or walk in the street; a man rides a bicycle at right. On the right-hand side is a building with a painted wall sign for a restaurant. In the far distance, centered in the street axis, is a church tower with a dome or baroque-style cupola and cross.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard with two photographs. The upper image shows a large, ornate two‑story building in historicist style with steep gables and the word "TIVOLI" displayed on its facade. It stands behind a fence along a street with some trees visible. The lower image shows the lavishly decorated interior of a large hall set up for a banquet or ball, with very long rows of tables and chairs, folded napkins, and festive garlands and flags hanging from the ceiling. Text beneath the images identifies the location as the concert and ballroom "Tivoli" in Freiberg in Saxony.

A monochrome (black-and-white) postcard view of a grand, multi‑storey station building with a tall clock tower and steep tiled roofs, surrounded by trees and hilly landscape. The architecture is Central European, early‑20th‑century style. Red printed text at the top reads "Karlsbad. Station Helenenhof." The scene looks down over a spa town in a valley.

The postcard shows a historical scene of soldiers disembarking from boats onto a wooden pier. There are several boats in the water and the pier stretches into the sea. The foreground has a lamp post and what appears to be a stone or brick structure. Many people, including armed soldiers, can be seen on the pier. The image is monochrome and has a vintage appearance. At the top, printed text identifies the place and event depicted.

A sepia-toned image showing a small building with a gabled roof, flanked by trees. In front of the building, there is an open-air amphitheater with curved rows of stone benches. The scene is peaceful, set within a wooded area, and the photograph's border is scalloped, characteristic of early to mid-20th-century postcards.

A vintage black and white postcard with a collage of photographs showing panoramic street views, grand hotels, spa colonnades, and ornate architecture surrounded by forested hills. Several famous locations are labeled, such as Mühlbrunnkolonnade, Hotel Imperial, Parkhotel Pupp, and Kurhaus u. Mühlbrunn. The central area has a tower and arcade structure labeled Marktbrunn. The main inscriptions say 'Weltbad Karlsbad.'

A sepia-toned image featuring a historic church with a tall tower in a central European town, surrounded by trees and rooftops, with hills in the background. The printed text at the top identifies the location and church, and there is a publisher's mark on the right side.

The image is a black and white photograph showing a paddle steamer on a wide river, with a grassy riverbank in the foreground and a hilly landscape in the background. There are a few buildings near the base of the hill, and a small tower or ruin is visible at the top of the hill. The scene appears tranquil, with the steamer as the main point of interest. The upper part of the image includes some handwritten text.

A black and white vintage postcard featuring a panoramic view of a historic European town, primarily showing leafy trees in the foreground and a cityscape in the background. Two prominent towers are visible: one belonging to a large church and the other likely part of a municipal or religious building. The text 'Kamenz i. Sa.' appears in the lower right-hand corner.

Colorized postcard view over a town and a large industrial complex surrounded by trees and hills. In the foreground stands a multi‑winged factory building with green roofs and many windows; smokestacks rise from the works. Residential houses with red roofs lie beyond, set in a valley with wooded hills in the background. At the top of the image, German text labels the scene.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing the old National Theatre building and the adjacent square in Bucharest, with a small fountain, trees, and several horse-drawn carriages. Red captions identify the city and subject; publisher information runs vertically along the left margin. The reverse reads "UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE – România – CARTA POSTALA" with address lines only.
Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large historicist courthouse complex bordering a landscaped square, with a German caption printed at the top.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a small stream bordered by grassy banks and leafless or early‑spring trees. In the middle distance there is a low masonry bridge with railings crossing the stream, with village buildings and farm structures behind it. In the foreground several children in early 20th‑century clothing stand and play along the banks of the stream. The caption text is printed at the top in red.

A painted street scene showing a slightly curved, sandy road lined with low two‑ and three‑storey houses with red and grey roofs. There are telegraph poles, a horse-drawn cart, and a few pedestrians walking along the street. The style is early 20th‑century European. In the lower right corner, decorative text identifies the location.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large arched truss bridge crossing a wide river. Boats are visible on the water in the foreground, with low, flat riverside scenery and some trees and buildings in the distance. The caption at the bottom reads "Waalbrug - Nijmegen." The image has a sepia tone and a printed border typical of early–mid 20th‑century postcards.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small railway station with a wooden station building on the left and two trains on parallel tracks. A steam locomotive marked with the number 11 is prominent in the right foreground, while another train with passenger cars stands farther back. Several people are visible on the platform. The lower margin has printed captions, with the left side reading a word that means 'The station' and the right side giving the town name.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard showing a modernist two‑storey building, likely a hotel or roadside restaurant. The main upper panel depicts the full exterior with a flat roof, large ribbon windows, and a central entrance; a few people stand near the entry and several mid‑20th‑century cars are parked to the right. The lower strip contains three interior views: a distinctive circular wooden dining table with tall carved chairs under a heavy ring‑shaped ceiling feature; a cozy café area with wood‑panelled walls, framed decorative motifs, and hanging globe lamps; and a bar with curved stools, elaborate pendant lamps, and garlands or bead strings hanging from the ceiling.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a broad cobblestone market square with several historic buildings. Dominating the right side is an ornate Gothic-revival style town hall with stepped gables, arched entrance, and the word "Rathskeller" on its facade. On the left are simpler townhouses, one bearing the sign "Thüringer Hof". A lone figure stands in the open square. The bottom margin contains printed caption text identifying the scene as the market and town hall of Mügeln, and the publisher information.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a large Renaissance-style brick building with ornate gables, dormer windows, and external stairs leading up to a main entrance. The structure stands on a town square with surrounding narrow row houses. A person is walking in the foreground. Handwritten text at the bottom identifies the place as Nijmegen and the Waag (weigh house).

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large wooden villa-style building set in a landscaped rural area with trees and open fields. Several people stand or sit on benches in front of the house. A tall flagpole with a Scandinavian cross flag (likely Norwegian) dominates the foreground. Printed caption text appears along the bottom edge of the image.

The front of the postcard shows a hand-tinted image of a large neo-gothic church with a tall central steeple and red-brick details, located in a town setting with surrounding greenery. There is text at the bottom that reads 'KYRKAN I SUNDSVALL.' The back features a green stamp from Sweden dated 1910 and is addressed in Swedish in ornate handwriting. The postcard uses multiple languages for 'postcard,' suggesting it was meant for international as well as national mailing.

The postcard consists of two sides: The front features a black-and-white photograph labeled 'Sundsvall. Stadsbacken.', showing a hilly, wooded area with large houses on the slope and a park-like area with pathways, trees, and benches in the foreground. The back contains handwritten messages, a Swedish stamp with a portrait, and address lines, indicating correspondence.

The postcard features a black and white photograph showing a tree-lined path in a wooded park area, with two figures standing in the distance. The top portion of the card is filled with handwritten text. Above the photo are printed words reading 'Hälsning från Stockholms Skärgård' and below the photo, text reads 'Parkinteriör från villaområdet Skarpöborg vid Vaxholm.' The reverse side of the postcard displays more handwritten address information, a Swedish stamp, and postal markings including 'Vänersborg'.

Colorized vintage view of a landscaped city park with tall trees, shrubs, a small pond in the foreground with ducks, and paths and benches in the background. The sky is light blue and there is a telegraph pole among the trees. At the top right, red printed text reads 'NIJMEGEN' with a smaller line below reading 'Hunnerpark'.

A monochrome historic postcard showing a large, ornate corner building with arched windows and balconies in a European architectural style. In front of the building stands an elaborate monument with a central standing figure on a tall pedestal and several seated figures around the base. People in early-20th‑century clothing are gathered around the monument and in front of the building. Printed text in Hungarian appears at the top of the image indicating the city and the name of the building and statue.

The image is of an illustrated postcard featuring a large, historic castle with two prominent towers and an extensive building complex, situated beside a river or body of water. The building rests on a slight hill or elevated area surrounded by trees. At the top, in red Gothic-style script, is the text 'Schloß Rochlitz i. Sa.' The sky is clear with a gradient from blue to a gentle dusk or dawn light.

Black-and-white view of a historic town square with a large Gothic/Renaissance-style town hall dominating the scene. The building has a steeply pitched tiled roof, three stepped-gable façades, a slender central spire, and a clock. On the ground floor is an arched entrance and a sign reading "Rathskeller" above an awning. To the right stands a building with a sign "Hôtel zum" and a horse-drawn carriage in front. On the left, multi-story townhouses line the street, one marked with the vertical sign "F. Richard Fladriz." Several pedestrians stand or walk across the cobblestone square.

Colorized vintage view over a European riverside city. A river flows through the center with tree‑lined embankments and a bridge crossing it. On the right bank stand rows of red‑roofed buildings and a prominent white neoclassical building; on the left are more houses and a broad promenade. A steep hill rises behind the town, topped with fortification‑like structures and a tower. The word "GRAZ." is printed in red at the top left.

A vintage tinted view over cultivated fields toward a small town with several large rectangular buildings, likely civic or school structures, and detached houses. In the background rise pointed church spires. The overall style and coloration suggest an early 20th‑century postcard. The word "Elverum." is printed in the upper left corner.

Vintage black‑and‑white view down a cobblestone street lined with several‑story buildings sporting awnings and shop signs. A woman in dark clothing walks across the mostly empty street while a few other figures stand near shopfronts. At the left foreground is a prominent curved sign for a cigar shop. In red print at the top it says that the scene is of Schmiedegasse in Pirna; small red text is also printed at the bottom edge.

An old black‑and‑white postcard view of a small industrial settlement and surrounding farmland in a hilly landscape. In the foreground and middle distance are several factory or mill buildings with chimneys, large residential houses, smaller village houses, roads and a pond; beyond them lie open fields and a forested ridge. The title "Marienberg i. S." is printed in red at the top left, and a small vertical printer's credit appears on the right edge.

A sepia-toned photograph of a small wooden truss bridge and low dam over a fast-flowing river. The bridge rests on stone abutments and a central stone pier, with water cascading underneath. A few people stand along the rail of the bridge, looking down at the river. The surroundings appear rural, with minimal structures visible beyond the bridge.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a statue of Martin Luther in front of a Gothic church window. The monument stands on a pedestal inscribed in German, and surrounding it are bare shrubs and simple steps leading to a door in the church wall. Printed captions at the bottom identify the location as Dippoldiswalde and the subject as the Luther monument, along with the name of the local publisher.

Vintage black-and-white postcard view of a wooded valley with tall trees on a hillside and several multi‑storey houses with tiled roofs along a road in the foreground. At the bottom, a light-colored text panel contains printed German captions in red, and the number 2274 is handwritten in red ink at the top center.

Old black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a large historic church with a tall tower and spire topped by a cross, a clock on the tower, and a steeply pitched roof decorated with a diamond pattern. Smaller houses adjoin the church, with bare trees, a fenced yard, and a pond or water feature in the foreground. The image edges are worn and damaged, giving it an early-20th‑century appearance.

A monochrome postcard showing a dense coniferous forest in hilly terrain. In the clearing foreground there is a small rustic stone or wooden hut with a pitched roof, a bench and table nearby, and a simple fence. The background is filled with tree-covered hills fading into the distance. The caption in German is printed in red at the bottom.

Colorized historic postcard view of a steel truss bridge leading toward a large fortified castle complex with round and square towers and red-tiled roofs. Soldiers in uniform are marching across the bridge toward the castle. A church tower is visible in the background, and utility poles line the right side. Printed titles in German identify the place as Torgau on the Elbe River and Schloss Hartenfels.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view over a dense European town with steep‑roofed buildings and dormer windows surrounding an open central square. Beyond the town center lie rolling fields, scattered villas, and patches of woodland. Architectural details—tall narrow houses, slate roofs, and orderly facades—suggest a Central European, likely German, small city in the early 20th century. There is no visible caption or border text on the image itself.

Colorized landscape view over a river valley with a railway line, small industrial buildings with a tall brick chimney, and scattered houses amid dense greenery. On the distant hill to the right stands a large castle-like complex. At the top left of the image is printed the caption "Rochsburg i. Muldentale".

Black‑and‑white view of a landscaped city park with tall leafy trees, curving gravel paths, small shrubs, benches, and an ornate multi‑tiered fountain surrounded by a low mesh fence. Several children lean on the fence near the fountain. In the background, partially obscured by trees, is a classical European-style building with large windows. The overall look suggests an early‑to‑mid 20th century urban garden scene.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a wide urban square bordered by a long row of multi‑story buildings with characteristic enclosed glass balconies (galerías). There are trees along the façade and several horse‑drawn carts and pedestrians in the open plaza. Printed captions identify the place as Plaza de Pontevedra in La Coruña. The lower margin shows the publisher's line, and there is a Spanish postage stamp with a handwritten signature on the right.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a town square lined with multi‑storey historic buildings. The image shows the Neumarkt (New Market) in Oschatz, with shops, inns and signage on the façades, a central monument or fountain, horse‑drawn cart, street lamps, and a few people in early 20th‑century clothing. The lower margin contains printed red text describing the scene and the publisher's information.

A tinted vintage postcard showing a pavilion‑like wooden building with ornate decorative trim, set among dense trees and garden greenery. A small child stands on the path at the lower right. The sky is pale blue and the building has a tall central gable with a flagpole. The lower margin bears the printed captions "Lovisa" on the left and "Kapellet" on the right.

Sepia-toned sports postcard showing two male long‑distance runners on an athletics track at the finish of a race. The foreground runner, wearing bib number 797 with a light-colored jersey bearing a small emblem, is crossing or about to cross the finish line ahead of a second runner wearing bib number 800. Spectators fill the blurred background stands. A printed caption in Dutch appears beneath the image.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a richly decorated neo-baroque / historicist theater building on a corner, with arched entrances, ornate columns and balustrades. A few pedestrians stand on the cobblestone street and tram tracks curve in the foreground. At the top of the card, printed text reads "Riga." on the left and "Russisches Theater." on the right.

A colorized historical postcard view of a baroque palace at the end of a wide garden avenue, lined with tall trees and manicured lawns. People in early 20th‑century clothing stroll along the paths; a horse‑drawn carriage approaches the palace. At the top left, printed text in German identifies the scene as a palace in Dresden's royal Great Garden.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large corner building housing the inn and guesthouse 'Einkehrgasthof Strasser'. The multi‑story structure has many shuttered windows, a pitched roof with several chimneys, and ground‑floor awnings with trees and a fenced garden terrace along the street. People can be seen near the entrance. Text identifying the business and address appears on the facade and in the lower right margin.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over a lakeside town with railway tracks and industrial buildings in the foreground, a bus and some houses near the station area, and a hillside densely built with houses across the water. The lake dominates the center and right of the image under a sky filled with large clouds. Swedish text is printed along the bottom identifying the view and the publisher.

The postcard features a vibrant, color photograph of a well-dressed woman standing next to a donkey in a lush garden full of blooming flowers. In the background, there are wide, terraced steps leading up to a modernist building with large columns, above which a sign in Cyrillic reads 'КАЗИНО' (casino). There are fountains, trees, and a few other people visible, suggesting a lively public or resort area.

Colorized landscape view over a forested valley with numerous grand spa-style hotel buildings spread along the hillside. In the background are low mountains under a blue sky. Near the top-left corner, the word "Marienbad." is printed in red.

Black-and-white real-photo postcard showing a bronze bust on a tall pedestal set in a landscaped park with trees, flowerbeds, and a yucca-like plant in the foreground. Printed caption at the bottom reads in Swedish "Vänersborg. Sparrebysten," and a publisher imprint appears at lower right.

Black‑and‑white landscape view of a rural valley with a church featuring a square tower and cross, surrounded by meadows, farm buildings, and forested hills. Swedish captions are printed along the bottom edge.

Sepia postcard showing an industrial cement works at the foot of a hill with multiple bottle-shaped kilns and a tall smokestack. The title at the top gives the city name Brașov in Romanian, Hungarian, and German, and identifies the site as the cement factory at Csigahégy/Schneckenberg. The reverse has printed headings for a postcard in Hungarian and Romanian and a publisher credit.

Sepia postcard showing a large neoclassical hospital building with symmetrical wings and a garden path in front. Captions at the top read 'Făgăraș' and 'Spitalul jud. Făgăraș'. The reverse is a divided back with 'România — Cartă Postală' and a publisher credit from a Făgăraș bookstore.

Black‑and‑white view of a large landscaped central park with tree‑lined alleys, flower beds, and a central obelisk/monument, bordered by a busy boulevard and historic buildings, with wooded hills in the background. The reverse has Romanian text printed 'REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMÎNĂ — BRAȘOV — Parcul prieteniei', a Romanian 40‑bani stamp, postal cancellation, and a handwritten message and address dated 16.VIII.1966.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a fortified church with steep shingled roofs and a tall central tower, framed by silhouetted tree branches. The reverse has a Romanian 40 BANI stamp, multilingual caption identifying the site as the Precista fortified church, and a handwritten Romanian message addressed to the Central Military Hospital in Bucharest.

A sepia-toned vintage postcard depicting a quiet coastal scene. There is a sandy shoreline bordered by tall pine trees, and several wooden rowboats moored along a calm river or bay inlet. The image has an early 20th-century aesthetic. The text at the bottom left reads 'Rujas jūrmala', and at the bottom right corner, there is the word 'Lielupe'.

A multi-view vintage postcard showing several scenes from Meissen on the Elbe River. The central image features the twin-spired Gothic cathedral (Dom). Surrounding views include a panorama of the town and river seen from Albrechtsburg Castle, the state porcelain manufactory complex, the town hall on a large square, and a riverside view with Albrechtsburg Castle and the cathedral on the hill above the town. The captions are printed in German.

A black-and-white photograph showing a passenger steamship named "WAXHOLM III" moored at a wooden pier. Many people stand on the dock and on the ship's decks, apparently boarding or disembarking. A small rowboat is tied alongside the pier, and the scene suggests a coastal or archipelago harbor, likely in the early to mid-20th century.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a small European town with dense traditional houses and a prominent church featuring a tall clocktower at its center. The town is surrounded by fields and forested hills in the background. In the upper left corner, printed text reads 'Oederan i. Sa.'. The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century photographic postcard.

Color tourist postcard showing a modernist high‑rise hotel with many small balconies and a landscaped park in front. A circular county tourism emblem appears at the top right. The reverse side has Romanian handwriting, a black 40 B 'Sfinxul' POSTA ROMANA stamp with Harghita postmarks, and printed identifiers stating the subject is Hotel Bradul in Miercurea Ciuc.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing people rowing boats on a lake with a chalet-style building with two pointed turrets on the shore, backed by dense forested mountains. Caption at the bottom reads "TUȘNAD – Lacul 'Ciucaș'". The reverse side has Romanian text and a 1961 Tușnad Băi postmark from the era of the Romanian People's Republic.

Color postcard showing an ornate Orthodox church with two tall octagonal towers and richly carved stone façades, set against a blue sky with trees and lawn in front. The reverse has Romanian handwriting in blue ink, a Romanian 40 Bani stamp (Poșta Română), postmark, and an address to Baia Mare. A printed caption identifies the church.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Neo‑Renaissance castle with tall spires nestled on a forested mountain slope. The back side has Romanian text, a blue 40 Bani POSTA ROMANA stamp with an industrial motif, and an address written to Sibiu. Printed caption states "SINAIA. Muzeul Peleș."

Color postcard showing traditional Romanian thatched-roof wooden houses in a wooded open‑air setting, likely springtime with yellow blossoms and a stone path and wooden fence in front. The reverse has printed caption and address lines, publisher and price.

A vintage Romanian postcard. The front shows a sepia photo of a large rest-house building with arched windows and a central entrance, set among trees with people sitting in the garden—captioned for Sinaia. The reverse has printed Romanian headings, a blue handwritten message and address, a 40 bani stamp reading "R.P. ROMINA POSTA," and postmarks including "BUCURESTI 70."

A color still-life showing an ornate silver miniature ewer or creamer reflected on a glossy surface, with bright orange roses in the foreground and a warm yellow-green blurred background. No caption on the image side.

Sepia-toned postcard showing two women in traditional Romanian folk dress outdoors; one is breastfeeding a baby while the other stands beside her. A green Romanian 10 bani postage-due stamp is affixed and cancelled on the image. Handwritten message appears along the lower margin. The reverse bears Romanian handwriting, red publisher's imprint, and round postmarks dated 2 NOV 11.

Color postcard showing seaside archaeological ruins with stone foundations and several standing columns, with the sea in the background and a small group of visitors. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a 40 Bani Romanian stamp, a Bucharest postmark dated 1965, and printed captions identifying the site as the ancient city of Histria in Dobrogea.

Black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard of Romania's Black Sea coast showing sailing boats on Lake Siut‑Ghiol, a beach and shoreline, the Constanța seafront with a leaning pine, crowded beaches at Eforie and Mamaia, and a central view labeled Vasile Roaită. Title at bottom reads "Marea Neagră." The back says "REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMINĂ" and "CARTE POȘTALĂ," with a price and code.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing two adjoining, pyramid‑shaped hills with a saddle between them, open meadows and scattered trees in the foreground. The reverse reads in Romanian and includes printed headings and a blue‑ink handwritten message and address. The print identifies the view as from Câmpulung‑Moldovenesc and names the feature "Muntele Adam și Eva." Postmarks show a 1958 date.

Color photo postcard of a leafy city park with a white wooden arched pedestrian bridge over a pond or canal. Stone embankments and two people standing near the water are visible. The reverse has Romanian postal markings and identifies the view as from Mihai Eminescu Park in Botoșani.

Split-image color postcard. The top photo shows children and adults on a sandy beach by the Black Sea, with kids building a sandcastle. A white band across the middle reads "ROMÂNIA • MANGALIA • ROMÂNIA." The bottom photo shows a landscaped resort area with modernist buildings (including the Cazino restaurant), a red 1970s car on a road, and flowerbeds. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a blue 40 bani 'POSTA ROMANA' stamp, and Bucharest postmarks dated 1973.

Multiview postcard featuring Secu Monastery in a wooded valley and several liturgical objects: a 17th‑century chalice, a 19th‑century holy water vessel, a printed homiliary of Metropolitan Varlaam (1643), a 19th‑century paten/plate, and a 19th‑century gospel with ornate cover. Front titles read "MÎNĂSTIREA SECU" and "JUDEȚUL NEAMȚ". The reverse has multilingual captions and the imprint of the Metropolis of Moldavia and Suceava in Iași.

Color postcard showing the Romanian navigation lock of the Iron Gate I Hydroelectric Power Station on the Danube. Two vessels are inside the lock chamber; the river, mountains and an island are visible in the background. The reverse has the usual address lines and stamp box and credits the Iron Gates Region Museum.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the façade of the National Theatre building in Cluj, with statues atop its towers and the inscription "Teatrul National" on the pediment. The reverse is printed with multilingual captions naming the theatre in Cluj and bears Romanian People's Republic postage stamps (35 bani and 5 bani), Bucharest postmarks, a handwritten Romanian message and an address in București.

Vintage sepia postcard showing several chalet-style spa buildings nestled in a conifer forest on a hillside, with two people walking on a path in the foreground. The back reads "REPUBLICA POPULARĂ ROMÂNĂ" and identifies the place as Borsec — Casa de odihnă C.G.M., with publisher "LIBRARIA NOASTRĂ." It bears Romanian People's Republic stamps and Bucharest postmarks with 1950s dates, plus a handwritten address.

Color postcard with a view of a modern seaside resort featuring two cylindrical high‑rise hotels, landscaped roads and roundabouts, green lawns, and several mid‑rise hotel blocks. 1960s–70s Eastern European cars are parked in the foreground under a bright blue sky. The back contains Romanian handwriting, publisher info, and Romanian postal marks.

Museum postcard reproducing a painting by Gonzales Coques showing a young man in a loose white shirt gazing at a small mirror (allegory of Sight). The back reads CARTE POSTALĂ and credits the Brukenthal Museum in Sibiu with a printed price.

Color postcard showing a winding blue river in a narrow, forested mountain valley. In the foreground there is a Romanian roadside milestone painted white with a red top that reads "GURA LOTRULUI – CĂLIMĂNEȘTI 15 Km." The reverse carries Romanian text and a 40‑bani blue Romanian stamp with a postmark from Călimănești.

Color photo postcard showing a calm river bordered by trees with the snow‑tipped Făgăraș Mountains in the background. The reverse has Romanian handwriting, a blue 40 Bani "POSTA ROMANA" stamp (electric pylons), postmarks reading FĂGĂRAȘ, and a printed multilingual caption identifying the Olt Valley and Făgăraș Massif. Publisher line "EDITURA PENTRU TURISM" and code 1140/2 are present.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a two‑storey gabled town hall building framed by trees and shrubs. A bicycle is leaning near the entrance steps. Above the main door there is a long banner with German text. At the bottom border, printed text identifies the location as the Rathaus (town hall) of Neupetershain, district of Calau.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural landscape with rolling meadows, scattered trees, and a forested hill in the background. In the foreground stands a long traditional half‑timbered farmhouse or inn complex with a gabled roof and a veranda. The setting is quiet countryside. At the top of the postcard, printed in red German text, are the location and the name of the building.

A hand‑colored historic postcard showing Pont Adolphe, a large stone arch bridge spanning a deep valley with a river and construction works below. The bridge has multiple arches, with urban buildings, trees, and a large institutional-looking structure in the background. Text in French and German is printed along the bottom margin.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a busy harbor scene with sailing ships and warehouses along the waterfront. A multi‑arched metal city bridge spans a canal or river, carrying a tram and pedestrians. People, carts, and barrels are visible in the foreground on a cobbled quay. At the top of the image, German text reads "Libau" on the left and "Stadt-Brücke" on the right.

Vintage-style printed view of a European city square with a tall Marian or victory column at its center, surrounded by Baroque and classicist buildings. Market stalls line the left side, and people in 18th–19th century clothing walk across the cobbled square. A horse‑drawn carriage and riders move along the streets. The right side features a large, ornate palace-like building with many windows and a central arched portal. The image is monochrome and appears as an old engraving reproduced on a postcard. No legible text is visible on the front.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large curved masonry dam with a roadway along the crest. A man in early 20th‑century clothing stands near the base of the structure. On the right side are terraced construction works, small buildings, and a forested hillside in the background. The printed caption in German at the top left reads "Talsperre Klingenberg i. Sa." and there is a handwritten red number in the top right corner.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-story sanatorium-like building with balconies, set on a hillside surrounded by trees and meadows. German text is printed at the top describing the institution and its location, and a vertical imprint at the right edge names the publisher and the year 1905.

Colorized vintage view of a stone Bismarck tower standing in a landscaped park with lawns, trees, and a flower planter in the foreground. The sky is blue with light clouds. At the top of the image red text labels the location and monument.

A vintage postcard depicting Franziskanerplatz in Graz, Austria. The image shows a square with old European buildings and a prominent church with Gothic windows and onion-domed towers. Horse-drawn carts and people are visible in the cobbled square. There is handwritten text in French at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural forest landscape with a dirt road and small bridge in the foreground. A lone man with a walking stick and umbrella walks along the road toward the camera. Dense coniferous woods and a straight forest track or clearing (Schneise) rise up the hill in the background. Printed red German text appears at the top of the card.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural park-like scene with a straight footpath bordered by trees and wildflower meadows. Two people are walking along the path. On the left side runs a small railway or tram track with a simple wooden railing and telegraph poles. At the top right, in red print, is the caption identifying the place.

The front of the postcard displays a vintage black and white photograph of a grand building with a bridge and a reflective pond in front. The surroundings are lush with trees. The building is labeled 'Pyrmont Schloss.' The image is overlaid with cursive handwritten text in German. The reverse side has a traditional old-fashioned postcard format with 'Postkarte' printed in German, a green postage stamp, official postal marks, further handwritten script, and a marking from a museum in Bad Pyrmont.

The postcard depicts a grand historic building, illuminated at night with lights glowing from the windows. There is a fountain and landscaped garden in the foreground, with a few people standing near the entrance. The building is labeled in the lower text as the Kurhaus, and the text 'Gruss aus Pyrmont' suggests greetings from the town. The reverse side shows German handwriting, a postmark stamp from 1904, a green stamp marked 'Deutsches Reich', and official stamps from Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont.

Humorous Dutch postcard showing a black-and-white dog against a blue background. The dog is behind a circular sign-style design encircled by orange gladiolus flowers and holding a medal ribbon in its mouth. The center of the sign reads "Nijmegen 30 km 4 daagse." Above the dog, curved text says "Op m'n sloffen !!!". At the bottom are a pair of cartoonish slippers shaped like little characters.

A vintage black‑and‑white winter scene showing three deer feeding in the snow around a simple wooden feeder covered with evergreen branches beneath a large tree. Behind them stands a long half‑timbered building with many paned windows and decorative panels along the base. Trees without leaves and a lamppost are visible. Printed red text appears on the right margin of the card.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large round stone tower with crenellations and a flag on top, set by a waterfront promenade with people walking and carts or carriages on a road or tram tracks. Greek text appears at the top right, with a French translation beneath, and a website watermark at the bottom right.

Black‑and‑white view of a European old-town street and square with brick and stone townhouses, shops at street level, and people walking on a cobbled plaza. The central building has a large arched window and ornate gable with the inscription in German script above the window. Shopfront signs in German are visible on the ground floor. In the background rise the tall spire of a Gothic cathedral and, to the right, a large medieval castle tower set on a hill.

Sepia-toned multi-view postcard composed of three photographs. The top and bottom images show interiors of a traditional inn or restaurant with wooden tables and chairs, tiled stoves, mounted antlers on the walls, floral table decorations, framed pictures, and musical instruments such as guitars hanging as decor. The middle image shows the exterior of the property: a fenced rural guesthouse or inn complex with a gabled main building and a long single-storey annex, set along a cobblestone street with trees behind. Over the entrance gate there is an arched sign with faint, almost unreadable text that appears to be in a Germanic script.

Colorized view of a landscaped park with tall trees, flower beds, and a curved path leading to an ornate open-sided pavilion or bandstand with a red roof. In the background are leafy trees, a white building with a steep red roof and tower-like gable, and a large villa. German text identifying the location is printed directly on the image.

Sepia-toned photograph of a low, long, plastered house with a steep clay-tile roof and several chimneys, facing directly onto a narrow street. A well‑dressed man in a suit stands in the open doorway on the left. The windows display household goods or clothing, suggesting a small shop or mixed dwelling-shop. The architecture and street are typical of an early‑20th‑century Northern or Central European town. A handwritten number "6057" appears in the lower left corner; a small oval sign with an unreadable number or letters hangs beside the doorway.

A monochrome vintage view of a wide, tree‑lined street with a few pedestrians and possibly a horse‑drawn carriage. Low buildings and tall trees line the road, with hills or mountains visible in the background. The image is vignetted, and there is Greek text printed near the bottom, along with a circular stamp or seal and a website watermark.

Color postcard view of a grand historic building complex in a European city, showing a neo‑baroque theater or opera house with statues on its domed towers and ornate façade, attached to a more restrained classical administrative building on the left. In front is a circular plaza with patterned flower beds and a small conifer tree, bordered by wide streets with crosswalks, 1960s–1970s style buses and cars, traffic signs, and pedestrians. The scene is framed as a typical tourist view of a major civic landmark.

Black‑and‑white view of a European city with densely packed tiled roofs in the foreground, baroque church towers, and a large wooded hill behind the riverfront buildings. On top and along the slope of the hill are fortification structures and paths, and on the right side stands a prominent clock tower. Printed text at the bottom identifies the publisher and the city.

Black‑and‑white interior view of an elegant museum or gallery room with parquet flooring, ornate ceiling moldings, and tall windows. The room contains multiple glass display cases on light-colored wooden tables showing small artifacts and documents, framed paintings on the walls, and several sculptures, including a prominent standing female statue at the back. On the right stands a large tiled stove or fireplace typical of Central or Northern European interiors. There is some handwritten numbering along the left edge of the image.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard with decorative floral framing. On the left is an oval vignette showing stone ruins with large arched openings, likely from an old cathedral, surrounded by illustrated flowers. Across the upper part of the card is a panoramic view of a town along a waterfront with a church spire and a small sailboat on the water. In the center-right, stylized text reads "Hilsen fra Hamar".

A black‑and‑white historic postcard-style image showing a tall medieval brick tower rising above low houses along a cobblestone street. The tower has Gothic brickwork, narrow arched windows, and a steep roof topped with a richly ornamented spire and flagpole. Horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians move along the street in front of the tower, suggesting a late 19th or early 20th century scene in a European city. Awning‑covered shopfronts sit at the base of the tower, and additional historic buildings appear in the background.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a tall, cylindrical stone tower with a steep conical roof standing beside a street lined with trees and fences. Behind the tower are residential-style buildings and a mountainous landscape under a blue sky. Printed caption text appears at the top of the image.

A black‑and‑white image showing a large crowd of well‑dressed people in early 20th‑century fashion gathered in front of and along a long colonnaded arcade. The building is neoclassical, with repeated arches, Corinthian-style columns, ornate friezes, balustrades, and statues on the roofline. The crowd fills a promenade that runs beside the structure. There are hanging signs on the arcade and another grand building visible further along the promenade.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large villa-like building labeled as a restaurant and bakery with timber-frame elements and a verandah, set behind a wooden picket fence. To the left is a long, lower outbuilding with a chimney. Several men in early 20th‑century clothing stand near the entrance gate. Leafless trees and a wooded hillside rise behind the buildings. Printed red text at the bottom identifies the scene and the publisher.

Color-tinted historical postcard showing a large military barracks complex surrounding an open parade ground. The multi‑storey brick buildings have red tiled roofs and ornate gables, with soldiers and a few figures visible on the drill field. Printed German text at the top identifies the location as the barracks of the Royal Saxon 2nd Pioneer Battalion No. 22 in Riesa.

A color postcard view of the historic center of Strasbourg with rows of steep-roofed traditional houses in the foreground and the tall Gothic tower and façade of Strasbourg Cathedral rising prominently in the background. The sky is bright blue with light clouds, and a white decorative border frames the image. The words "Alsace" appear at the top and "Strasbourg" at the bottom in a cursive script.

A black‑and‑white multi-view postcard divided into four panels. The upper left panel shows a large wooden villa or lodge with a wide veranda, arched brick base, and surrounding greenery. The upper right panel shows a town street lined with two‑ and three‑storey houses; in the distance is woodland, and the printed word "Hamar" appears in the sky area. The lower left panel shows a broad street with early 20th‑century buildings and a few people with a cart. The lower right panel shows another long, straight street bordered by trees and multistory commercial buildings with signage on the facades.

Sepia-toned postcard view of a large wooden-and-masonry mountain inn or lookout building standing on a forested hillside. The multi-story structure has a wraparound balcony, a central gabled roof section, and a square tower. Sparse tall trees surround the building, and a picket fence encloses the property. Printed red text at the top names the site and its elevation; a vertical imprint on the right margin credits the printer and the year 1906.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a stone gate with a pointed Gothic arch and tiled roof leading into a courtyard. Behind the gate rises a round tower with a conical roof and small arched windows. Trees frame the scene. At the very top, German text reads "Brüx. Eingang zur Landeswarte."

A colorized street scene showing a broad sidewalk running alongside a large, two‑story colonial-style building with arcaded verandas and columns. People in early 20th‑century clothing stand and walk along the sidewalk. On the left side of the image runs a street with tram tracks, power poles, and a horse‑drawn or early motor vehicle in the distance. Trees and low fencing line the street. A sign reading "WELCOME YMCA" stands near the tracks. Printed captions in Spanish at the top and in English at the bottom identify the location as Eleventh & Front Street, looking north, in Colón, Republic of Panama.

Sepia-toned historic street scene showing a tram running along curved tracks through a cobbled square bordered by multi‑story townhouses and trees. People are walking, cycling, and standing around the open square. The printed caption at the top reads "Kelfkensch bosch NIJMEGEN".

Black‑and‑white image of a small neo‑Gothic villa or manor house with a crenellated tower on the right side, circular attic windows, and simple rectangular windows on the main façade.
