At the top right, printed French text titles the scene as part of 'Le Cantal pittoresque', identifying the mountain as Le Puy Mary and the nearby pass Pas de Peyrol, as well as the road from Murat to Salers. At the bottom left, there is a boxed poetic caption in French about the road in long zigzags around the mountain.

Colorized historical street scene showing a broad cobblestone avenue lined with multi‑story European buildings, shops, and awnings. Pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalks; a horse‑drawn cart and an early tram or carriage travel down the street. Gas‑style street lamps stand along the road. At the top of the image in red text is the caption identifying the view. A large sign on one building advertises a pharmacy in German.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a large neo‑Renaissance palace‑like public building on a corner by a riverside or canal. The structure has three main stories plus an attic, richly decorated façades, arched windows on the ground floor, pilasters, statues, and a central clock set in a mansard roof with ornate corner towers and spires. In front, horse‑drawn carriages travel along the street beside an embankment wall and an ornate streetlamp, suggesting a late‑19th or early‑20th‑century European city scene.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a spa town nestled in a steep forested valley. Elegant late‑19th and early‑20th‑century multi‑storey buildings line a narrow river or canal, with wooded hills rising sharply behind them. A small pavilion or lookout structure is visible on top of the hill. The scene is framed by tree branches at the top. In the lower left corner there is a caption in a script font reading "Weltbad Karlsbad."

Black‑and‑white postcard showing several men handling a large fishing net on a wooden platform beside a fast‑flowing river surrounded by dense coniferous forest. Rocks line the riverbank and simple wooden structures extend over the water. The scene has a rural, early‑20th‑century feel. The upper left corner of the image bears the printed word "Kotka." and the lower center margin reads "Langinkoski".

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a pastoral field with cows grazing in the foreground and several people walking along a path. In the background lies a small town with factory chimneys, dense roofs, and a prominent tall church spire. The caption in ornate red German script reads 'Gruss aus Geringswalde. Nordseite.' and a publisher line appears at the bottom.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard divided into four photographs of historic buildings and cityscapes. The upper left shows a large ornate institutional building along a broad street. The upper right shows a substantial city hall–type structure dominated by a tall clock tower. The lower left image is a riverfront panorama with stone bridge arches and Baroque church and civic buildings along the opposite bank. The lower right image features an elaborate Baroque pavilion with rich sculptural decoration and large windows, with another domed building visible in the distant background.

Black‑and‑white photograph showing a stone church with a tall clock tower and spire topped by a cross. The nave has a steeply pitched tiled roof and pointed Gothic windows with tracery. The church stands on a low stone wall covered with ivy, with trees and foliage framing the scene, suggesting a European village setting.

Color postcard showing the standing Doric columns of an ancient temple ruin in a rural landscape with a large mountain in the background. At the top there is bilingual text in Greek and French identifying the site as the Temple of Apollo at ancient Corinth. A website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears at the bottom.

Sepia-toned interior view of an old-fashioned domestic kitchen. The room features a large hearth with cooking pots, a wooden table with turned legs, shelves filled with plates on the back wall, and various household utensils. The walls are plain, and light enters from a high window. At the bottom margin there is a handwritten-style caption in German.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small harbor with moored wooden boats in calm water, bordered by a stone quay and seafront buildings. Hills rise in the distance. Greek and English captions appear in the lower margin identifying the location as Piraeus Harbor (Canthos/Canaris Bay). A circular seal and the website address of an archive are faintly visible.

A vintage, lightly colorized postcard view of traditional Dutch windmills standing along the edge of a calm body of water. Several large wooden windmills and adjacent barns or sheds line the waterfront under a pale sky. The scene is printed with captions in the lower margin, including the place name and a short description in what appears to be Dutch or German, as well as a publisher line and date.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a town square with a medieval gate tower and attached church with tall spires and a clock. The image shows cobblestone pavement in the foreground, flanked by townhouses and a bakery on the right. At the top in red Gothic-style type is the location caption, and additional German text labels the tower and church.

An old sepia-toned postcard showing a railway station complex by the water. A long, low station building with a taller central section stands behind a row of train carriages. There are trees around the station and low hills or a shoreline in the distant background. A horse-drawn carriage is visible in the foreground along an empty road. The top left bears red Greek text, and at the bottom right there is a modern website watermark.

Colorized historical street scene showing a broad urban boulevard lined with ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and stand in the street, along with a tram and horse‑drawn carriages. Shop signs in Hungarian are visible on the ground floors, including a café on the right corner building. At the top in red letters it identifies the city and the boulevard.

Sepia-toned, oval-framed image of a three‑story lodging house with balconies and many people gathered in front of it, likely a group portrait of guests and staff. The facade bears a sign with the building's name in German. Under the image there is printed German text identifying the house as a lodging establishment called "Logierhaus grauer Schwan" in Warmbrunn, Silesia.

Black‑and‑white image of a landscaped city park with flowerbeds and trimmed hedges surrounding a central statue. The statue depicts a man in a cloak holding a sword, mounted on a high pedestal decorated with a heraldic shield. Behind the park stand multi‑storey 19th‑century apartment buildings with mansard roofs. The name "Tadeusz Kościuszko" is visible on the base of the monument.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a rocky marble quarry beside a road carved into a cliff. Several men in traditional clothing lead pack animals (likely donkeys or mules) along the road. The scene is mountainous, with rough rock faces on the left and open landscape to the right. Below the image there is printed multilingual caption text explaining that the marble used for the road is extracted and worked on site. A website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears over the lower right part of the image.

Colored postcard showing an evening riverside scene with moored steamships in the foreground and an arched steel bridge spanning a wide river in the background. The sky is softly lit by the setting sun reflecting on the water. At the bottom margin, printed red text reads "NIJMEGEN" on the left and "Riviergezicht bij avond" on the right.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a wide, unpaved main street lined with single‑story buildings with arched windows and doors on both sides. Rows of evenly spaced trees, including some taller palms further back, form an avenue effect, while people in light clothing stand or walk along the street. The image is framed decoratively, with printed captions in red at the bottom and a vertical publisher credit along the left margin.

Black-and-white aerial photograph showing a large rural farm complex surrounded by fields and forest. Several sizable white wooden buildings and barns form a courtyard, with additional houses and landscaped garden areas with trees and circular features such as lawns or flowerbeds. A small road runs along the front edge of the property. The lower left text reads "Berger, Elverum" and the lower right text reads "Flyvefoto: Widerøe & Bjørneby".

Hand‑tinted landscape view of a sandy, grassy beach beside a calm body of water, likely a lake or sheltered sea bay. In the distance are low wooden buildings among trees on the opposite shore, with dense coniferous forest stretching to the right. Several small human figures walk or stand along the waterline. The overall colorization and composition suggest an early 20th‑century tourist or landscape postcard.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a calm lakeside or riverside scene. In the foreground are rocks, bushes, and a small tree by the water; a rowboat with a seated person is tied at the shore. Across the water, gently rolling, wooded hills rise behind a long multi‑storey building, possibly an institution or large house, with a few smaller structures nearby. The sky and water are smooth and reflective. Handwritten text in Swedish frames the image along the top and bottom margins.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a two‑storey country inn with a gabled roof labeled as a guesthouse. People, including adults and children, stand and sit with bicycles in front of the building; trees and a hilly, river‑valley landscape form the background. German text appears above and below the image identifying the Elbe valley and the inn.

Black-and-white postcard showing a large tanker ship sailing through a broad waterway in front of an ornate, white, domed building with arcaded facades on the waterfront. The shoreline behind is densely built with mid‑rise urban buildings. The scene suggests a busy harbor or canal city, photographed from an elevated vantage point.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large two‑towered church building viewed from the street. The tall, plain towers have steep roofs and small arched windows. At the front is an ornate entrance portal with a round window above it, opening onto a town square with a few small figures. At the top in red Gothic-style print is the caption identifying the location and the church.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a hillside town with trees and paths in the foreground and a cluster of multi‑storey buildings and houses on the ridge above. The architecture looks early 20th‑century Central European, with steep roofs and dormer windows. In the distant right stands a round tower‑like building. There is a printed caption along the bottom edge and a red handwritten archive number in the upper right corner.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a large neoclassical institutional building with long colonnaded wings and a central domed section, set in an open, mostly barren foreground with a few palm trees. Handwritten text appears at the bottom identifying the scene and the photographer.

Black-and-white postcard view of a harbor with several steamships and boats moored in the foreground. Behind the waterfront warehouses and low buildings rise a few early high‑rise structures, one being a prominent rectangular tower. The scene shows an urban waterfront area with industrial and commercial buildings. Swedish text is printed along the bottom edge, and a small triangular publisher's mark with the year 1919 appears in the lower right corner.

A black‑and‑white aerial view of a European town showing a large open central square surrounded by multi‑storey buildings and tree‑lined streets. Smaller houses and institutional buildings extend into the background, with some industrial structures including a tall chimney. In the lower left corner the printed caption reads "Uddevalla från flygplan", and in the lower right there is a publisher/photographer credit.

Black‑and‑white landscape postcard showing a broad river with fast-moving water and floating logs, surrounded by forested hills. A small industrial complex or power facility stands on the left bank near rapids or a waterfall. In the foreground is open grassy land with scattered trees and power poles. Printed caption text in Swedish appears along the bottom edge identifying the view, and a photographer/publisher logo is in the lower right corner.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard view of a tree‑lined road and a landscaped park or garden with hedges and small conifers. In the background stands a large, simple, gabled masonry building that resembles a church or historic hall, partly obscured by trees. At the top left, there is red printed text reading "Belgern a. Elbe.", indicating the location near the Elbe River.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a view of Schloss Weesenstein, a castle with a tall tower and clock, standing on a hill above trees and a small arched bridge over a stream in a valley. The image has printed red text at the top left identifying the place.

Colorized vintage image showing a Gothic-style church facade with pointed arches, ornate tracery, and a large central portal, next to a tall bell tower with a clock. A few people stand in the square in front. The sky is softly tinted and there is printed text at the top right identifying the location.

A colorized early‑20th‑century postcard showing a young woman and man in formal clothing standing outdoors. The woman wears a long dark skirt, white blouse with pink sleeves, and a straw hat with a ribbon, holding flowers. The man wears a dark suit with a bowler hat, holding a cane and gloves, leaning slightly toward her. Behind them are garden elements such as plants, stonework, and a balustrade with an urn. Handwritten text in a cursive script appears along the right edge and across the lower margin of the image.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a large, elegant urban building complex with shutters on the windows and a pitched roof, fronted by a decorated wall and small trees. The street is cobbled, and neighboring townhouses are visible on the right. Printed captions beneath the image read "Rorschach." and "Stella maris", with a small number "4971" in the lower left margin.

A black‑and‑white historic postcard showing a small railway station building labeled "STANGE" beside train tracks. A train with a locomotive and cars stands on the right track, while wooden planking covers the platform area in the foreground. The station building is two stories with gabled roof and multiple windows, and people can be seen near the entrance. The text at the top left reads "Stationen, Stange."

A colorized vintage view of a formal garden with palm trees, manicured hedges, and a curving gravel path. In the background stands a neoclassical building with columns. At the top left there is red text in Greek and French, and a website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears at the bottom right.

A black-and-white vintage postcard showing a busy harbor packed with steamships and smaller boats moored along a quay. Cranes and scaffolding are visible across the water where shipbuilding or port construction is underway. The foreground features a large white passenger vessel, while cargo, crates, and sacks are stacked on the dock with workers walking about. Low hills and scattered buildings form the background. Printed text at the bottom identifies the location and publisher.

Color image with scalloped white border showing a large medieval brick city gate with two massive round towers topped by steep blue-grey conical roofs. Between the towers is a richly ornamented Gothic brick façade with multiple arched windows and decorative gables, forming an arched passageway through the structure. In the foreground is a manicured park with lawns, flower beds full of yellow and red flowers, paths, and benches where people sit and walk, suggesting a touristic setting on a sunny day.

A monochrome postcard-style photograph showing a windswept rural road bordered by low vegetation and a large tree strongly bent by persistent wind. Two people riding pack animals (likely donkeys or mules) travel along the road toward the camera. The landscape appears coastal or island-like and largely undeveloped. A web address watermark is visible at the bottom right.

A vintage illustrated postcard with multiple vignette scenes of a historic European city, featuring parks, ruins, a tower, streets with horse‑drawn carriages, and surrounding countryside. Decorative flowers frame the images. Large stylized text reads "GROETE uit NIJMEGEN," suggesting it is a greeting from the city of Nijmegen. Individual scenes are labeled in Dutch, including a ruin, parks, a railway street, and views of nearby areas.

Colorized historic postcard view from a park with a wooden bench and trees in the foreground, looking toward a large multi‑winged barracks complex with red roofs and white walls in the distance. Overhead telegraph poles stand near an open field. Red German text at the top identifies the scene as a view of the barracks of the 3rd Battalion, 12th Infantry Regiment No. 177 in Freiberg in Saxony. At the bottom, small red text notes that it is a hand-colored artist postcard.

Black‑and‑white image showing a richly ornamented Baroque‑revival / historicist city palace on a corner square. The central building has a high mansard roof with decorative cresting, an ornate central portal reached by a broad double staircase, and elaborate window surrounds. On the left is another grand late‑19th‑century façade; behind, several church or public‑building spires rise above the roofs. People in early‑20th‑century clothing walk across a cobbled square in front of the building. No text is visible on the image.

A monochrome postcard showing an inner Renaissance courtyard with arcaded galleries on several levels, a staircase leading up to the first gallery, and ornate dormer windows on the roof. In the courtyard stands a decorative well with an elaborate wrought‑iron cover. Handwritten notes appear at the top and bottom. Printed in red at the upper center is the caption identifying the scene.

Black‑and‑white landscape view of a small village in a forested valley. The scene shows scattered houses, farm buildings, a church with a steeple, winding roads, open fields, and dense conifer-covered hills in the background. In the lower left corner there is a printed caption identifying the place.

Monochrome image showing a Renaissance-style courtyard staircase attached to a substantial stone building. The double-flight exterior stairs have balustrades and are supported by heavy columns with arches beneath. At the top of the stairs stand three slender pinnacles or obelisks. In the background are vaulted loggias with rounded arches and balustrades on the upper floor, and a decorated ceiling in the upper arcade. The scene appears to be an inner courtyard of a historical civic or palace building in a European city. There is no printed caption or visible handwriting on the image side.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a coastal scene with a large round stone tower, crenellated at the top, standing by the waterfront. Small boats float in the foreground near a quay, and low houses line the shore behind the tower. Printed captions in Greek and French identify the location and landmark.

Black-and-white historic postcard view of a city street with a large multi-story museum building in the foreground and a tall, ornate tower rising in the background. Small figures walk across an open square or wide street. The upper left of the card bears the place name 'Bautzen.' and the upper right identifies the scene as 'Museum u. Reichenturm.'

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large group of uniformed soldiers in long coats standing in formation in front of a wooden building with several chimneys and a gabled entrance. A tall ladder leans against the roof. Printed captions in red below the image read "St. Michel." on the left and "Mikkelissä." on the right. Publisher information is printed vertically at the left margin.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view of a small European town in a hilly landscape, taken from an elevated vantage point. A winding road and a narrow river run through the valley lined with two‑ and three‑story houses with steep gabled roofs. To the right stands a large Gothic‑style church with a tall spire; another church complex with towers is visible on a wooded slope to the left. The settlement is surrounded by open fields, scattered farm buildings, and forested hills in the background. There is no visible printed caption or handwriting on the image side.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard view of a cobblestone market square lined with multi‑story townhouses and shops. A church tower with a tall spire dominates the background. Several pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing walk in the street. The caption at the top reads "Aschersleben. Markt," indicating it shows the central market area of Aschersleben. Additional small printed text appears along the bottom margin with the publisher and date.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style image showing a large, ornate historic building with a central pavilion and two symmetrical side wings. The architecture is 19th‑century eclectic/neo‑Renaissance with arched colonnades, decorative facades, and steep mansard-style roofs topped with finials and flagpoles. In front of the building is a formal garden with flowerbeds arranged in decorative patterns, trimmed shrubs, and a circular path. A few people in early 20th‑century clothing stroll along the paths.

Black‑and‑white view of a European town square with a large historicist town hall dominating the scene. The building has a tall clock tower with an onion-shaped dome, stepped gables, and many windows. In front of it, people walk across a cobbled square where small carts and market stalls are set up; a dog is visible in the foreground. The image has wide white margins typical of an old photographic postcard. No visible printed caption or handwritten text can be seen on the front.

Black‑and‑white street view of a European city around the turn of the 20th century. The scene shows a broad, tree‑lined avenue with multi‑storey bourgeois townhouses and corner buildings with domes and small spires. On the left are shuttered windows and shopfronts with striped awnings; people walk on the pavement and a few horse‑drawn carriages and handcarts travel along the unpaved road. Well‑dressed pedestrians in long coats and hats stand near a railing in the foreground.

A monochrome postcard showing an interior view of an ornate building with arches, columns, balconies, and richly decorated walls. The architecture has a historic, possibly Byzantine or Ottoman style. The image is centered on a cream border with printed captions beneath the photo in two languages.

A dusk or early evening waterside scene showing a dense cluster of boats or floating houses in a harbor, surrounded by dark hills and calm water reflecting the fading light of the sky. Neon signs in Chinese characters and English glow on the shore, including one prominently reading "China Motor – Palace," indicating an urban waterfront, possibly a historic Chinese or Hong Kong harbor with a boat-dwelling community.

Black‑and‑white historic postcard showing a large town hall with an ornate façade, central clock‑tower and side turret in a somewhat rural, undeveloped square or open area. At the top in red lettering are the words "Großröhrsdorf." on the left and "Rathaus." on the right.

Sepia-toned portrait of a mustachioed man in light-colored suit, hat, and striped trousers, standing with a walking stick in a studio setting that imitates a rustic outdoor scene with rocks and a wooden fence. French and Greek captions appear beneath the image, along with the name of the editor/photographer and location.

Black‑and‑white street view showing a cobblestone square with a large, ornate early‑20th‑century public building featuring tall windows, decorative panels, and a distinctive domed tower. In the foreground stands a small, simple building with a steep tiled roof. Vintage automobiles and a few pedestrians appear on the right side of the scene. The word "KOTKA" is handwritten at the bottom right of the image.

The image shows the address side of an old German postcard. It has the printed word "Postkarte" at the top left in a decorative font, guiding where to write the recipient's address. A green 5‑Pfennig stamp of the Deutsches Reich is affixed in the upper right corner and is cancelled with a round postmark reading "BAD NAUHEIM" with the date "13.7.04" (likely 1904). The address is handwritten in German cursive and appears to be directed to a male addressee at a university's botanical institute in Heidelberg. At the bottom is preprinted text for the sender's address labeled "Wohnung (Straße und Hausnummer)".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a statue of Johann Georg I standing on an ornate pedestal within a fountain basin in a town square. Behind the monument is a large stone church with Gothic windows; residential buildings line the background on the left. German text printed in red appears in the upper left and at the bottom margin.

A monochrome, old-style printed postcard showing a central European town square. The scene is a drawing rather than a photograph, with baroque‑style buildings surrounding an open cobbled plaza. In the middle stands a small fenced monument or column. To the right is a church with a distinctive large onion dome topped by a star and cross, and an attached porch with arches. Behind it rises a square bell tower with a hipped roof. On the left is a long multi‑windowed building with a small turret and cross, possibly a monastery or civic building, and a vaulted gateway leading out of the square. Low wooded hills form the background. Very small text is printed at the bottom edge of the image, partly readable as dates and words but not entirely clear.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a camp of Blackfoot people on an open plain with several tipis (teepees). Several wrapped figures in blankets stand or sit near the tipis, including two children embracing in the foreground. The scene is printed in a light blue-green tone with red caption text at the bottom and publisher information along the left margin.

An old Russian Imperial postal card with printed red coat of arms at top left and large red Russian text in the center. The card is filled with handwritten cursive in Russian. Several black circular postmarks and a red postage stamp appear on the right side and lower left. There are some stains and age marks on the beige card.

Black‑and‑white aerial photograph of a rural settlement surrounded by fields and forest. A prominent pointed‑steeple church with an adjacent free‑standing wooden bell tower stands near the foreground, bordered by tree‑lined roads and a few detached houses and farm buildings. A main country road curves away through the landscape toward a small clustered village in the distance. The overall style resembles an old photographic postcard of a Northern European countryside parish.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a riverside city scene. A stone bridge crosses the water in the foreground, with small boats moored along the quay. Behind the bridge stand several ornate multi‑storey buildings, including a large corner hotel and a tall clock tower. The overall style is early 20th‑century European urban architecture. Printed caption text at the top identifies the location as Norrköping and mentions Oscar Fredriksbro and Göta hotell.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a vaulted corridor lined on both sides with upright mummified bodies draped in white shrouds. The perspective looks down the long hall toward a bright opening, with a few living visitors visible in the distance. Handwritten and printed captions appear along the bottom margin, identifying the location and photographer.

Black‑and‑white view of a European town square dominated by a tall church tower with a clock and a steep, multi‑tiered spire topped by a weather vane. Around the base of the tower stand 2–3 story houses with steep tiled roofs and dormer windows. Shop signs in German are visible at street level, and a few people in early 20th‑century dress stand or walk in the open square. The upper sky area appears overexposed or masked, emphasizing the tower silhouette.

Black‑and‑white postcard reproducing a historical painting of a battle scene in a mountainous landscape. Soldiers in 19th‑century uniforms, some on horseback and some marching on foot, advance through rocky terrain while artillery and wagons cross a stream or rough road. Smoke and fighting are visible in the distant valley. The lower margin carries an Italian caption identifying the scene as the Battle of Bezzecca with a date in 1866.

Black-and-white postcard view of a small rural village in a gently hilly landscape. Farmhouses and village buildings with pitched roofs cluster in the middle ground, surrounded by fields and patches of forest. The vantage point is from a grassy field looking down toward the settlement, with rolling hills and cultivated land extending into the distance. The caption at the bottom left reads "Polenz bei Neustadt i. Sa." indicating the location depicted.

Black‑and‑white historic postcard showing a cobblestone market square with a main street (Hauptstrasse) in a small European town. On the left are two‑ and three‑story buildings with shops including a cinema (Kino) and a house named Zur Ratswaage. On the right stands a large gabled building labeled Gasthaus zum Goldnen Löwen beside a tree‑lined open square. Several people in early‑20th‑century clothing walk or stand in the street. At the top in red print is the caption identifying the town and location.

Black‑and‑white, vertically oriented street view of a European town, showing a cobblestone main street lined with two‑ and three‑story buildings. At the left stands a tall church tower with an onion‑shaped spire topped by a cross and a clock on its facade. People in early‑20th‑century clothing, including children, walk or stand along the street. Shop signs hang from several buildings, but the resolution prevents reading them clearly. The sky is blank and overexposed, emphasizing the silhouette of the church tower.

A monochrome postcard showing an interior museum view with ancient Greek architecture. In the background there is a reconstructed small temple-like building with a sculpted pediment and two caryatid statues as columns. In the foreground stands a statue of a horse on a pedestal. The space is labeled at the bottom in French and Greek, indicating it is the reconstructed Treasury of Cnidus in the Delphi Museum.

Sepia-toned vintage street view showing a tree-lined avenue beside a long brick building. A horse-drawn carriage with a covered top moves along the street, while several pedestrians walk in the distance. The image has printed caption text at the bottom indicating the location and subject.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a two-part stucco building with tiled roofs and a small clock tower. The left wing has arched arcades and a sign marked "Wache." (guardhouse). Several uniformed men stand in front. The right wing has more formal windows and an inscription on the façade above the central windows, with a coat of arms, indicating an official or court building. The scene shows a cobblestone street and a child near the right side of the building.

Black-and-white landscape view of a coastal rural settlement with scattered wooden houses, open rocky fields, and sparse trees near a body of water. In the foreground is a simple wooden house with a gabled tile roof, surrounded by vegetation and flagpoles. More small houses and dirt roads extend into the background. In the lower left corner is a caption with the place name, and in the lower right is a small triangular publisher logo with a number.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a group of African men working with a grain-winnowing machine outdoors. Sacks and baskets of grain are piled in the foreground, while a large colonial-style building with a veranda stands in the background. The scene appears rural and agricultural. Printed caption text and a small publisher credit appear at the bottom of the image.

A vintage monochrome postcard illustration of a busy European city square with tram tracks curving through the cobblestone street in the foreground. The central focus is an ornate, multi‑story Renaissance building with richly decorated façade and arcades at street level. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and gather around the square. Adjacent buildings have shop signs, including one advertising a ladies' clothing shop (Damen‑Hüte). A handwritten caption at the bottom identifies the scene.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a large historic building in a courtyard setting, likely a palace or manor house. The structure has steep, tiled gabled roofs, ornate Baroque or late‑Renaissance gables, many rectangular windows, and ivy climbing the façade. On the right stands a central clock tower with a domed roof and lantern, topped by a weather vane. An arched gateway appears on the left, also decorated and framed by stone. Trees line the right side of the open courtyard in front of the building. The image is bordered in white like a printed postcard. No legible printed caption is visible.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a large hilltop castle complex surrounded by forested mountains. The fortified walls, towers, and main castle buildings stretch along a ridge above a valley. At the bottom margin there is printed caption text indicating the location and altitude of the castle.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a riverside town with a bridge over the river, several boats and barges along the quay, and red-roofed buildings at the water's edge. A wooded hill rises behind the town, topped by a church-like building. The printed caption at the bottom reads "Gruss aus Meissen. Martinsberg." and there is a red handwritten number "384" in the top right margin. Along the left border is vertical publisher text.

A sepia-toned historic postcard showing a large Renaissance-style castle surrounded by trees and a moat. The building has multiple towers with spires and flagpoles on the roof. At the lower part of the image and into the margin there is dense handwritten script. In the bottom left corner small printed text identifies the place, and in the bottom right corner another printed word appears, likely the name of the castle or town.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a street with several ornate multi‑storey buildings in historicist style. The building on the left has small turrets, circular windows and ivy climbing over an arched gateway. Adjacent façades have gabled roofs and decorative brickwork. Trees line an open square or broad sidewalk to the right. Printed cursive text appears in the bottom margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a small town or village nestled in a hilly, tree‑covered landscape. Several farmhouses and buildings with gabled roofs are visible, along with winding roads and open fields. The printed caption below the image identifies the location as Beek near Nijmegen and states that the view is from the Sterrenberg. There is cursive handwriting in ink along the bottom margin. On the right border there is a vertical printer's credit indicating phototype production in Nijmegen.

Black-and-white aerial view of a large institutional building complex surrounded by forest and fields. The main structure is an elongated multi-storey building with a central tower and courtyard-like spaces, likely a hospital, with smaller auxiliary buildings nearby. At the bottom left, white caption text is printed over the image indicating the name and location of the place, and at the bottom right there is a small printer or photographer credit with a code.

A monochrome historic postcard view of a waterfront canal or river lined with boats and small sailing vessels. On both sides of the waterway stand multi‑story European-style buildings and wooden warehouses. In the distance rises a tall church with a very prominent spire dominating the skyline. The printing at the top reads the place name and a local area name.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a large three-story masonry school building on a street corner, with arched windows, a modest clock or decorative gable on the roofline, and a fenced yard with young trees in front. A smaller residential building stands to the right. The words "Groitzsch." and "Bürgerschule." are printed at the top of the image.

A colorized historical postcard view showing a section of massive stone city walls with multiple round towers, identified as the 'Sept Tours' of Constantinople. In front of the fortifications are several multi‑story houses with red and light roofs surrounded by greenery. The sky is blue with some clouds, and there is printed text at the top and a website watermark at the bottom right.

A vintage monochrome/hand‑tinted postcard showing a calm bay with several small boats on the water, framed by tree silhouettes on both sides. The sky is filled with scattered clouds. Text around the image identifies the view as Spring Park Bay from the porch of Hotel del Otero in Spring Park, Minnesota, and gives the publisher and printing details.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a panoramic view of the city of Graz with the Mur River in the foreground and the Schlossberg hill with its fortress and clock tower in the background. The cityscape is framed by a decorative border of alpine flowers (likely edelweiss). On the right side, there is a Tyrolean-style hat with a feather and a cloth bag tied with a cord, adding an alpine folk motif. The caption in German appears above the view.

Sepia-toned panoramic view over a city seen from a wooded hillside. In the middle distance is a prominent hill with fortification-like structures on top, surrounded by a dense urban area and fields in the foreground. Bare tree trunks and branches frame the image. A caption centered in the lower white border reads "Graz."

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a young Cambodian woman standing barefoot outdoors, holding a baby on her hip. They are in front of traditional thatched and woven-bamboo structures, suggesting a rural setting near Phnom Penh. The lower margin contains printed French text and a publisher's mark.

Colorized view of a grand Baroque palace complex with richly decorated façades and a prominent entrance pavilion topped by a large greenish dome-crown with a golden crown ornament. A wooden bridge crosses a water-filled moat or canal in front of the building, and a flower garden with red blossoms occupies the foreground. The image has the typical printed look and proportions of a vintage tourism postcard. No visible printed text appears on the front.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a large medieval church surrounded by trees and greenery. The church has red-tiled roofs, stepped gables and a tall central tower with a white midsection and darker dome-like top. At the top of the card there is printed German text giving the place and a note that the main church was built around the year 1225.

Black‑and‑white postcard view through an archway into a narrow cobbled alley lined with tall old houses. Signs for small businesses are visible on the walls, and the street curves slightly between the buildings. Beneath the photograph is printed German text identifying the scene as an old lane in Graz and giving publication and demolition dates.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a landscaped city park with lawns, curving paths, and many trees. In the center stands an ornate monument or statue on a multi‑tiered pedestal. In the distance, partly obscured by trees, is a church tower with a clock and spire. At the top of the card, printed in red Gothic-style script, is a caption identifying the location as Frankenberg in Saxony and the specific park as Friedenspark.

Color postcard showing a large crowd of walkers with umbrellas marching along a rural road during rainy weather. People wear raincoats and backpacks, suggesting an organized walking event. The central photo is framed in an oval with two crossed adhesive bandages at the bottom. Around the image are playful texts in English and Dutch and a printed Dutch postage stamp in the upper right corner depicting a large arch bridge over a river, labeled with price and country. The overall style is humorous and festive, referring to a multi‑day walking event in Nijmegen, Netherlands.

A painted illustration of a man standing and playing a traditional string instrument resembling a kora, made from a large calabash gourd with a long neck. The man wears a light-colored hat, loose greenish tunic, wide brown trousers, socks and black shoes. Colored ribbons hang from the instrument. The background is plain and neutral, with no scenery or text besides the artwork itself.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a narrow man‑made canal cut through high rocky cliffs, with a ship passing between them. The sky is pale and the steep rock walls dominate both sides. Printed multilingual captions at the top identify the scene as the Canal of Corinth. A website watermark (www.elia.org.gr) appears across the lower part of the image.

Sepia-toned historical street scene showing a wide unpaved main street lined with low houses and shops. On the left, a half-timbered building houses a confectionery shop, and beside it stands a larger corner house with a shop front bearing the name "Heinrich Noack". People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the street and a man rides a bicycle. The caption at the top reads "Coswig i. S. Hauptstraße." and a small red imprint at the bottom names the publisher.

A vintage black‑and‑white (sepia-toned) postcard showing Yosemite Falls in winter. Snow-covered trees frame a tall, narrow waterfall cascading down a steep rock face. At the bottom margin there is printed red text identifying the location and height of the falls, and an additional red handwritten or stamped number over the snow near the center-bottom.

A black‑and‑white photographic postcard showing a mid‑20th‑century cargo ship at sea, viewed in profile from the port side. The vessel has a long, low cargo deck, masts fore and aft, and an elevated superstructure with a funnel at the stern. Smaller boats are alongside the ship. The ship's name "BREMER HANDEL" is visible on the bow, and "BREMEN" appears on the stern under the name. The sky is clear and the sea is calm.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a panoramic view of a rural town with fields and grazing animals in the foreground and a compact settlement with various houses, industrial buildings, and a church with a prominent tower in the background. Low hills rise behind the town. The caption in German at the bottom describes Seifhennersdorf and nearby localities, and a small imprint at the lower left identifies the printer and the year 1905.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing an equestrian statue of Kaiser Wilhelm I on a large pedestal adorned with several standing and seated figures. The monument stands in a formal urban square, in front of an ornate multi‑story historicist building. Several men in early 20th‑century clothing stand around the monument. Printed red text at the bottom identifies the location and subject, and a small printer's line appears along the lower edge.

Color postcard view over a large neoclassical exhibition building surrounded by extensive gardens and trees, with mountains in the distant background. At the top, red text in Greek and French identifies the scene as the Zappeion exhibition palace in Athens. At the bottom right is a printed web address.

Black‑and‑white winter view of a narrow snow‑covered medieval street running between a high rough stone wall on the right and lower houses on the left. Heavy snow lies on roofs and the roadway where two small human figures walk away from the camera. In the background rises a large round stone tower with a conical roof, part of a city wall. An ornate wall‑mounted street lamp projects over the lane.

Sepia photograph mounted on a postcard showing a small chapel with a simple gabled façade, bell-cote, and round rose window above a double wooden door. Four men stand in front of the entrance on a bare, slightly snowy slope, with leafless trees and a bench visible to the sides. The image is framed in an oval on a white card. Handwritten captions on the card read "S. Lucia presso Fonds." and "1920."

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of an ornate Baroque pavilion opening onto a formal garden. The central building has a richly decorated façade with large arched windows, sculpted figures, and a domed roof topped by a sphere. Curved arcades with repeated arches extend to both sides, enclosing the garden. Manicured paths, hedges, and topiary trees line the foreground, with a few small human figures near the entrance for scale.

Color-tinted vintage postcard showing a formal city garden with manicured lawns, flower beds, hedges and a central statue of a standing female figure on a pedestal. Trees line both sides of the path and a few people stroll through the park. The printed captions at the bottom read "Nijmegen" on the left and "Nassausingel" on the right.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a war memorial column topped with a large eagle in a small European town street. The column stands on a square pedestal surrounded by an iron fence and landscaped greenery. Behind it are traditional gabled houses lining a narrow street. The caption at the top in German identifies the scene as a war memorial and Nikolaistreet in Geithain.

A multi‑view color postcard with four photographs and Swedish text. The upper left shows a scenic rural landscape with forested hills and a lake. The upper right shows a small white wooden church with a steeple surrounded by a graveyard. The lower left shows a rocky shoreline with water and carved figures on the rock surface. The lower right is a close‑up of these rock carvings (petroglyphs). Across the middle is a large greeting text in Swedish, and smaller Swedish captions label the views, including the lake, the church, and the rock carvings.

Black-and-white postcard-style photograph showing a small coastal town beside a bay or inlet, with wooden houses scattered along the shoreline and up low hills. Forested hills surround the settlement. In the foreground are a few larger houses and utility poles; in the distance a church-like building appears among other homes. The words "Ljungkile" are printed in the lower left, and a photographer/publisher credit with a number appears in the lower right.

A black‑and‑white harbor scene showing a busy quay with several steamships and smaller boats moored along the pier. People, early automobiles, and horse‑drawn carts move along a cobblestone waterfront with tram tracks. Across the wide river or harbor are shipyards with large cranes and industrial facilities. On the left hillside a prominent church or cathedral with a tall tower dominates the skyline. On the right, a large building by the water bears the word "GÖTAVERKEN," and one of the closer ships is labeled "GOTA." In the lower‑right corner is a circular printer's mark that reads "ÄKTA FOTO" with stylized initials in the center.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a rural village street. A large two‑storey inn stands on the right side with a gabled facade, several windows and painted signage on the wall. Fenced gardens and trees line the dirt road. A few children stand along the street in front of the fences. Printed German text at the top names the village and describes the street and inn, and signage on the building identifies the guesthouse.

Black‑and‑white image of a high‑altitude landscape with snow‑covered volcanic peaks in the background and grassy alpine terrain with scattered trees in the foreground. Several figures in wide‑brimmed hats and traditional-looking clothing travel on foot and on horseback along a path through the grass, moving toward the mountains. The style resembles an early to mid‑20th‑century travel postcard. No printed caption or writing is visible on the front.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large public building with a tall clock‑tower–like section, arched windows and a broad stairway leading to the main entrance. The foreground has an unpaved cobblestone street and a telegraph/power pole with many wires. The sky is cloudy and dramatic. Printed text in Cyrillic appears at the bottom margin.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a cobblestone street lined with multi‑story townhouses and shops. Horse‑drawn carts and pedestrians appear along the street. In the distance a large church tower with a distinctive spire dominates the skyline. The caption at the top reads "Grossenhain. Naundorferstrasse." Additional German business signage is visible on the right‑hand buildings.

Black‑and‑white view of a small European town square or park with a flower bed in the foreground, a flagpole with what appears to be the Swedish flag waving in the middle distance, and low mid‑century buildings with shops and parked cars along the street. The scene looks like a calm town center captured on a partly cloudy day.

Colorized vintage view of a park fountain. In the center stands a large ornate multi-tiered fountain with water arcing outward in many streams. People in early 20th‑century clothing stroll and sit around the basin, surrounded by manicured lawns, flower beds, large leafy plants, and tall trees. The sky is pale blue with light clouds. At the top left, printed text identifies the scene.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a quiet village street lined with large trees on the left and brick houses with tiled roofs on the right. People, including children and adults with bicycles, stroll along the broad street. At the bottom margin, printed text identifies the scene as a street in Hatert, named Dorpstraat.

Sepia-tone historic postcard showing a neoclassical colonnaded pavilion with arched windows and a central dome, set in a landscaped park with trees and a pathway. Several people stand near the entrance. Printed captions identify the scene as Marienbad and the Waldquelle pavilion, with publishing details at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white interior view of an old pharmacy: shelves lined with jars and bottles, a counter with scales and mortars, and a nun in a traditional habit working behind the counter. Large curtained windows are on the left, a clock hangs high on the wall, and a vase with flowers stands on the foreground counter. The printed caption at the bottom reads "Apotheek."

A black‑and‑white winter scene of a ski resort in the mountains. In the foreground, skiers move across snow-covered slopes with many ski tracks and scattered small fir trees. A chairlift runs diagonally from the lower right toward the upper left, with several chairs carrying people uphill. In the mid‑distance there are a few small chalet-style buildings near the base of steeper slopes, and behind them rises a craggy, rocky peak. The sky is clear and bright, with no visible clouds. There is no visible printed caption or text on the image side.

A colorized vintage view of a wide open square or drill ground bordered by rows of trees, with scattered pedestrians in dark clothing. Behind the trees rises a hillside town with multiple light‑colored buildings and villas, set against a large mountain in the background. The lower white margin contains red printed Italian text identifying the location, and small publisher information in the bottom left corner.

Color illustration of an old European building with arched arcades at street level and richly painted façades depicting animals, horses, and human figures. The upper stories have green wooden shutters and small wrought‑iron balconies. On the left is the rounded apse and dome of an adjacent church. A small fountain with a statue stands in front of the arcades, and a few people are visible in the square. The card has no visible caption or writing on the image side.

A colored vintage postcard view over a coastal town showing a historic Ottoman complex with domed roofs and a minaret near the waterfront. Old stone walls descend toward a harbor with several sailing ships anchored. The sea stretches into the background. Greek and Latin text titles identify the scene as the Imaret of Kavala, and a website watermark appears at the bottom.

A black‑and‑white postcard‑style photograph of a horse-racing track with harness racing (sulky) in progress. Several horses and drivers race along a dirt track in front of a large wooden grandstand filled with spectators. On the left in the distance stands a more ornate building with columns and flags. In the bottom right corner, white text is printed directly on the image reading "VALHALLA HIPPODROME."

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small hillside village with scattered traditional houses bordered by forest. The buildings have steep gabled roofs, typical of Central European mountain architecture. In the foreground are meadows and fields; in the background is a dense coniferous forest under a cloudy sky. The caption in German is printed along the bottom margin.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a large neoclassical basilica with a central dome and towers, surrounded by a cobblestone square and small trees. At the top of the card, in red text, it identifies the location as Budapest and labels the building as a basilica in several languages.

Sepia-toned street view of a European city with a tramcar running along a narrow street lined with multi‑storey buildings and shop awnings. In the background rises a tall Baroque church tower with an onion-shaped dome. People are visible on the sidewalks. Faint printed caption text appears along the top margin, and additional small commercial signs and posters are visible on the right-hand buildings.

Black‑and‑white view over a landscaped park with curving paths and sparse trees in the foreground, facing a row of ornate multi‑storey late‑19th‑century buildings and hotels at the foot of a wooded hill. A small church or chapel stands on the slope. Along the lower border of the image is a black strip with hand‑written white text that appears mirrored, including a word resembling a place name and a number.

Illustrated view of a European town square with market stalls and white umbrellas surrounding a central statue on a fountain. The square is bordered by multi-storey historic buildings with red-tiled roofs and shop signs in German. On the hill behind the square stands a fortified clock tower with a steep roof, overlooking the town.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a large military formation on a wide tree‑lined avenue. Several rows of uniformed soldiers stand in columns, some officers are on horseback at the front, and the road stretches straight into the distance between tall trees. The image is bordered by white margins with printed captions below and along the left edge.

A vintage German postal card with printed green text 'Deutsche Reichspost Postkarte' and pre-printed 5-pfennig stamp. It is addressed in handwritten script to a recipient in Heidelberg, with postmarks including one from Strassburg.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a brick railway station complex with several connected buildings, a forecourt with people standing and a horse-drawn cart, and a tram or streetcar in the right foreground. There is handwritten purple ink text across the sky area. Printed red text at the top left reads "Graz." and at the top right "Staatsbahnhof.", with a small printed serial number at the bottom left.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-storey institutional building with ornate early-20th‑century architecture, arched windows on the ground floor, and a central entrance with decorative stonework. The building is set in a modest garden or courtyard area. At the bottom margin, printed text identifies the place as an obstetrics clinic of Erzsébet University in Pécs.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a narrow street lined with a long, two‑storey classical building with many tall windows and a hanging lantern above an entrance. Several people, including women in long skirts, stand and walk along the street. The scene is overlaid with dense handwritten script. Printed captions at the bottom identify the building and send greetings from the city in both Hungarian and German.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a two-story corner building with a hipped roof, simple stucco façade and rectangular windows. At street level there is a shop with a sign above the entrance reading "MISSZIÓI JELLEGŰ BAZÁR". A few small trees and a lamppost line the sidewalk in front of the building; a lone person stands near the shop entrance. The surrounding area appears to be a quiet, tree-lined street in a town or city.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a large school complex arranged around an inner courtyard, with multi‑storey rectangular buildings and a fenced yard in the foreground. Hills rise in the background under a partly cloudy sky. Printed Hungarian text appears in the bottom margin describing the scene as the interior view of the Cistercian Order's Nagy Lajos secondary school in Pécs.

A tinted early-20th‑century street view postcard showing a wide unpaved road lined with single‑storey buildings and leafless trees. Several men and boys in dark clothing stand or walk along the street. Utility poles run down the center, and fields/gardens extend on the right. Printed Hungarian captions and a handwritten message occupy the lower portion of the card.

A black‑and‑white historic postcard depicting a large, ornate multi‑storey building on a busy square. The facade carries signs in Hungarian, including "Pécsi Takarékpénztár" (a savings bank) and shop signs at street level such as "Neumann M." The square in front is animated with pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing, horse‑drawn carriages, market stalls and small trees. Handwritten cursive text overlays the upper part of the image. Printed captions in red at the top left and right read "Pécs." and "Takarékpénztári palota."

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with three photographic views of the city of Pécs, Hungary. The top image is a panoramic view of the old town with church towers and surrounding hills. The lower left image shows a large cathedral with four towers and a terraced fountain or steps in the foreground. The lower right image depicts a lively public square with a decorative fountain in the center, surrounded by buildings and people. The front caption reads in Hungarian: "ÜDVÖZLET PÉCSRŐL!" ("Greetings from Pécs!"). The reverse side has Hungarian handwriting, printed word "PÉCS." at top left, an address to Budapest on the right, and two Hungarian postage stamps overprinted with the year 1945.

The postcard shows a color photograph of a historic Ottoman-era mosque with a stone dome and a tall slender minaret rising behind it. The mosque is partly obscured by trees and an old stone wall in the foreground, with adjacent multi‑storey buildings framing the scene under a clear blue sky. The reverse side has multilingual printed captions identifying the mosque, standard postcard address lines, stamp boxes, and publisher information in Hungarian.

Color postcard showing a central square with a large domed building, a former mosque now church, in the middle. In the foreground are flower beds, steps, and people walking or sitting. On the left stands a tall Baroque-style column, and on the right an equestrian statue on a high pedestal. The sky is clear blue. The word "PÉCS" is printed in white at the top left on the front. The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard layout with blue address lines and red stamp boxes, and printed information about the place and photographer.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with a view over a central square dominated by a tall Baroque column/monument surrounded by a low fence and steps. Behind the square stands a long multi‑storey building, and in the background rises a church or cathedral with four prominent towers and hills beyond the town. The caption at the bottom reads "Pécs" on the left and "Széchenyi‑tér" on the right. The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, address lines, a Hungarian postage stamp labeled "MAGYAR POSTA," and a small publisher's mark mentioning Budapest.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand Romanesque cathedral with four towers at the far end of a terraced fountain garden and promenade. Many small figures walk or sit along the paths in front of the church. The front caption reads "Pécs" on the left and "Székesegyház" on the right. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, address lines, a circular postmark mentioning "Pécs," and a Budapest printer's mark.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows a long Romanesque cathedral façade with arched windows, colonnades, statues on the upper level, and a tall bell tower with a spire and cross. A decorative street lamp stands prominently in the foreground along a stone-paved street. The lower margin of the image bears Hungarian captions identifying the location. The reverse side has a green Hungarian postage stamp, a circular postmark, printed postcard layout lines, handwritten Hungarian address to Budapest, and a short handwritten message.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing two young men walking on a roadside with a white guardrail in front of a forested hillside. On the hill stands a large multi‑storey resort or sanatorium-type building with balconies, along with some smaller structures. The caption beneath the image is in Hungarian. The reverse side contains Hungarian handwriting in blue ink, a Hungarian stamp, postal cancellation and printed publisher information.

Colorized historic postcard showing a busy central square with a large stone monument in the middle, horse‑drawn carriages, people walking and trading, and a tram. Surrounding the square are multi‑story buildings, including a grand neo‑renaissance style building with a sign on the façade. The printed caption at the top reads "PÉCS. Széchényi-tér". The reverse side contains handwritten text, address lines, the printed Hungarian phrase "Levelező-Lap", printer's mark "N. E. Bpest VIII", and a red Hungarian postage stamp inscribed "MAGYAR KIR. POSTA" and "10 FILLÉR".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with a divided back. The front shows a large public square with a domed former mosque/church on the left, a tall Baroque plague column in the center, and rows of multi‑story buildings with shops and awnings on the right. Several people stand or walk in the open square, with horse‑drawn vehicles in the background. At the top are printed and handwritten captions. The reverse side contains a handwritten message in cursive, an address written to a person in Sopron, Hungary, a Hungarian postage stamp of 1000 korona, and vertical printed publishing information along the left margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard showing several landmarks of a Central European city: a fountain in a busy square, grand historic civic buildings with domes and towers, a hillside hotel or sanatorium surrounded by forest, and stone ruins framed by an arch. The front bears decorative script text in the upper left. The reverse has printed text on the left, a handwritten Hungarian message in blue ink diagonally across the center, pre‑printed address lines on the right, and a green Hungarian postage stamp canceled with a circular postmark.

Color postcard showing the front view of a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and a statue on a pedestal in the foreground square. The sky is bright blue with some clouds and the word "PÉCS" is printed in white at the top left within a rounded rectangular frame. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with blue address lines and red stamp boxes, and printed text identifying the cathedral in multiple languages and the photographer.

A multi-view color postcard with a yellow border showing modern urban architecture in the city of Pécs. The front is divided into four photographs: the upper left shows a large white terraced modernist building with landscaped steps and people walking; the upper right shows a long, low white building with a red-tiled roof on a slope; the lower left and lower right images depict a sizeable commercial complex, with the word "KONZUM" on the facade, a glass-roofed section, parked cars, and pedestrians. The reverse side has standard postcard layout with printed stamp area, address lines, and Hungarian text indicating the city and publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with three small photographs showing newly built multi‑storey apartment blocks along unpaved streets and open ground. The lower center caption reads "Pécs–Meszesi részletek." The back is a standard divided postcard layout printed in Hungarian, including the publisher's line and the price in fillér.

The postcard shows a black‑and‑white photograph of a large Romanesque Revival cathedral with multiple towers and a richly decorated façade featuring arcades and statues. In front of the building there is a garden with benches and people sitting. The reverse side is a standard divided-back postcard layout with printed Hungarian text indicating the subject and publisher, plus a printed price in forints.

Black-and-white aerial photograph of a large, modernist multi‑storey holiday hotel building set in a forested hilly area, with a curved access road and landscaped grounds in front. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with Hungarian text indicating the location and publisher, plus space for a stamp and address.

A black‑and‑white view over a busy central square with a large equestrian statue on a pedestal in the foreground, flower beds and pedestrians around it, and multi‑storey historic buildings with shops and awnings lining the streets. In the background are low hills and more city buildings. The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, printed caption, address lines, and a Hungarian postage stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a tranquil pond in a landscaped city park. Several people are boating on the water in small rowboats and a canoe, while others walk along the curved stone embankment and near wide steps that lead up a grassy slope lined with bushes and trees. The reverse side has multilingual printed text identifying the location and a standard divided‑back layout with space for a stamp and address.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a small Ferris wheel in an amusement park, with people riding in open gondolas and trees surrounding the ride. The reverse side has a green Hungarian postage stamp, handwritten Hungarian text dated 1963, and printed postcard information mentioning Pécs Vidám Park.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a central square with broad terraced steps, a stone balustrade and formal gardens. On the left stands an older church-like building; in the centre background is a statue on a pedestal, with buses and people around. On the right is an ornate late‑19th‑century building with arcaded ground floor, balcony and decorative facade. At the bottom of the image is a printed Hungarian caption. The reverse side shows handwritten Hungarian text, a printed publisher line, and a Hungarian stamp from Magyar Posta.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a large cathedral with Romanesque‑revival arches, painted ceilings, chandeliers and an elaborate high altar and baldachin. The reverse side has Hungarian stamps and printed publisher information, with a caption at the bottom left identifying the view as the interior of the cathedral in Pécs.

Black-and-white postcard showing a grand historic city hall square. A tall clock/bell tower with a baroque dome rises above an ornate, multi-storey building with mansard-style roofs and rich decoration. In front of it stands a baroque plague column with statues and a star-topped cross, plus a statue on a pedestal and terraced steps leading down into the square. Surrounding the square are classical townhouses and another church-like building with a tower in the distance. The reverse side has handwritten Hungarian text, printed location information, and a Hungarian stamp.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a rocky forested ravine with a cave entrance. Two men in early 20th‑century clothing stand at the mouth of the cave, one holding a walking stick, the other holding a hat. The front caption at the bottom reads that the location is in Pécs and identifies the cave. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text at the top, handwritten Hungarian message and address, an 8‑fillér Hungarian postage stamp, and a Budapest postmark dated February 20, 1930. The card is printed by Barasits, Budapest.

Night view of a central square with an equestrian statue in the foreground and the dark silhouette of a large historic church or mosque-like building with a tall tower and domes in the background. Streetlights illuminate shopfronts and people in the square. The back clearly shows postcard layout and printed location information in Hungarian.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an outdoor terrace of a modernist holiday hotel complex in a wooded mountain setting. Numerous people sit at round tables with striped metal chairs under globe lamps, while the multi‑storey building with stone and concrete facades curves along the hillside in the background. The reverse side has multilingual printed captions identifying the location and function of the site, with standard postcard layout for address and stamp.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a pond in a park in Pécs, with people sitting on benches in the shade and others rowing small boats on the water. Behind the pond are steps, trees, and low historic buildings, with a hilly townscape rising in the background and a church-like building visible on the hillside. The reverse side is a standard divided postcard back with printed multilingual caption and publisher information.

Multi-view postcard. The front shows a large stone building with a prominent light-blue dome in a historic cityscape, surrounded by red-roofed houses and hills in the background. Two interior views depict the same building's church-like nave with wooden pews, crucifix, altar, statues, and arched windows decorated with alternating red-and-white stone patterns reminiscent of former mosque architecture. The back is a standard divided postcard layout with multilingual caption identifying the site as the parish church of the city of Pécs.

Black‑and‑white street scene showing a vintage trolleybus or tram stopped in front of benches where several people sit and chat. The vehicle has overhead trolley poles and the fleet number 201 on the side. In the background are older multi‑story buildings with shops at street level and pedestrians walking on a cobbled plaza or street.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a small lookout tower standing on a hilltop, reached by a stone stairway and surrounded by dense trees and bushes. The tower has a tall, narrow base with an external wooden staircase leading to a railed viewing platform and a simple pyramidal structure above it. The reverse side contains handwritten Hungarian text in blue ink, a green 40 fillér Magyar Posta stamp, postmark, address lines, and printed publisher information.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows a large Romanesque-style cathedral with four tall towers and an arcaded façade, viewed from a square with a central statue silhouetted in the foreground. The back has Hungarian printed text, blue handwritten message and address, two green Hungarian stamps, and a circular postmark.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square with a large domed former mosque in the background, an equestrian statue on a high stone pedestal in the foreground, and a tall column with sculpted figures (a plague column or holy trinity column) to the left. Surrounding the square are historic buildings and a street with a bus. The reverse side has printed multilingual caption information, postage area, hand‑written Hungarian text, and a Hungarian postmark.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand neo‑baroque theatre building with a large central dome, side domes, ornate sculptures and columns at the entrance. People are visible on the steps in front. The reverse side has a Hungarian postage stamp, red handwritten message and address, and printed text indicating the location: "PÉCS Nemzeti Színház."

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large historic square with a long Baroque building along one side and a tall sculptural column with religious figures and a star on top in the center of the square. There are 1950s‑era cars and a bus parked nearby, people sitting on the steps and walking, and trees lining the open space. The reverse side is printed as a standard divided‑back postcard with address lines and stamp box, and Hungarian text identifying the location as Pécs, Széchenyi tér.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a European city square with historic buildings. On the left stands a tall clock tower attached to a baroque-style building; in the center of the square there are statues and a fountain surrounded by pedestrians, cars, and buses. The reverse side has Hungarian text, postage stamps, and the printed caption identifying the location.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large central square in a European city. The view looks down over an open plaza with landscaped flowerbeds and a tall Baroque-style column monument in the foreground, and an equestrian statue on a pedestal further back. Surrounding the square are multi‑story historic buildings with pitched roofs; on the left stands a prominent tower with a clock and a domed structure behind it. The reverse side is a divided back with printed address lines and Hungarian text including the city and place name.

Black-and-white postcard showing an interior view with richly carved stone or marble reliefs depicting religious scenes and figures in horizontal bands, likely part of a Christian cathedral museum display. A column and metal rail appear in the foreground, with strong light and shadow across the reliefs.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a city square with a richly decorated fountain in the foreground and a large domed building in the background. The fountain has ornate tile‑like decoration and lion‑head spouts, surrounded by a circular flower bed. The domed building behind it stands on a raised terrace with steps and resembles an old mosque or church in a historic European town. Surrounding multi‑story buildings line the street. On the image border, printed captions read "Pécs" at the bottom left and "Zsolnai kút" at the bottom right. The reverse side contains Hungarian handwriting, an address to Budapest, a Hungarian postage stamp, and a postmark.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a city square with an ornate stone drinking fountain in the foreground, decorated with sculpted lion heads and reliefs, surrounded by a circular flowerbed. In the background stands a large domed former mosque on a raised terrace, with steps leading up from the square and hills visible behind the city. The reverse side has a purple 40 fillér Hungarian stamp labeled "MAGYAR POSTA", handwritten Hungarian text, and printed publisher/location marks including "PÉCS, Széchenyi tér".

Black‑and‑white aerial or elevated view of a European city street lined with two‑ to three‑story buildings and trees. In the distance stands a large cathedral with four pointed towers dominating the skyline. The style of the buildings and the street with pedestrians and telegraph poles suggest a mid‑20th‑century scene. The reverse side is a divided‑back postcard with Hungarian text printed and handwritten, including the word 'PÉCS' and a street name.

Black‑and‑white postcard. The front shows a modernist urban scene with a group of three elongated, stylized human statues standing on stones in a shallow pool, arms raised as if dancing. Behind them are mid‑20th‑century apartment blocks and, in the distant background, a hilly landscape with a church tower or dome rising above lower buildings. The back side has printed multilingual caption text describing a primary school on Móricz Zsigmond Square in Pécs, Hungary, a price line, publisher credit, postal markings, and handwritten Hungarian correspondence and address.

Black-and-white view of a European city square with a cobblestone street and 1950s–1960s cars. On the right stands a large domed stone building with a cross on top, originally an Ottoman mosque later converted into a church. On the left are ornate historic façades with trees lining the street, and in the background rises a church tower. The back side contains printed multilingual text identifying the location, handwritten Hungarian message and address, a Hungarian stamp and postmark.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square with a large domed former mosque on the left and an equestrian statue on a high pedestal in the middle foreground. People are sitting on steps and walking around the square, with multi‑storey historic buildings and a distant church tower in the background. The reverse features Hungarian text, address lines, a green Hungarian stamp, and printed information about the place.

Night view of a large, square stone building with a high greenish dome and small arched windows, illuminated by warm lights. Red light trails from passing cars streak across the cobblestone street in the foreground, indicating a long‑exposure photograph. The back side is a standard divided postcard layout with printed multilingual captions and publisher information.

Black‑and‑white image showing a large domed stone building in a city square, with arched windows and a cross-topped finial on the dome. The architecture is clearly Ottoman but the cross suggests later Christian use. In front of the building is a busy street or square filled with 1950s–1960s European cars, and a row of multi‑storey historic buildings lines the right side of the scene.

A monochrome drawing of an ornate 19th‑century synagogue on a street corner, surrounded by an iron fence and adjacent buildings, with several small cars, a motorcycle, and pedestrians in the foreground. On the back, printed Hungarian text credits the artist Orsós György and references institutions in Pécs and Bogád, with standard postcard address lines and stamp boxes.

Color postcard showing a Romanesque cathedral with four tall towers and an ornate façade, seen from a grassy park with benches, trees and an iron fence in the foreground. The reverse side contains Hungarian handwritten text, a red Hungarian postage stamp, a Pécs postmark, and printed multilingual captions identifying the subject as the cathedral.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Romanesque cathedral with four tall spired towers rising above trees and stone walls. In the foreground there is an open‑air theatre with curved rows of stone or concrete seating. The reverse side has printed Hungarian text at the top left, handwritten Hungarian message in blue ink, a Hungarian postage stamp, and a round postmark dated 1967.

Color aerial-style view over a leafy residential hillside with many red-tile-roofed houses in the foreground and mid‑century apartment blocks behind them.
