Several flagpoles with Nordic flags fly above the buildings. Printed caption text appears at the lower left and a small publisher's logo and number at the lower right.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a large neoclassical palace complex with colonnades and a spacious forecourt with trees and a few walking figures. There is a Greek postage stamp (5 lepta) in the upper left. Decorative borders frame the central photo, and handwritten messages and a date are visible around the image. A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a formal palace complex. The central building has a clock tower or belfry with a spire and is flanked by long symmetrical wings forming a courtyard. Trees frame the image, and at the top is printed the word "GRAVENSTEIN." The overall style is early 20th‑century.

Black-and-white postcard showing a small Catholic chapel surrounded by trees and a meadow. The chapel has a steep roof with a wooden belfry topped by a cross. Coniferous forest rises in the background. Printed caption text runs along the bottom edge of the image.

A black‑and‑white vintage view of a European city street with multi‑story brick townhouses and shop awnings in the foreground. At the end of the gently curving street rises a large neo‑Gothic brick church with multiple steep spires and a very tall, narrow central tower topped by an ornate openwork lantern. Pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the street, giving the scene a bustling urban atmosphere.

A black-and-white aerial photograph showing a manor complex consisting of a central two‑storey main building with a dark pitched roof and small clock/bell turret, flanked by two long one‑storey side buildings. The buildings are arranged around a curved driveway and surrounded by trees and gardens. Printed captions in Swedish appear at the bottom, including the name of the estate and the photo studio in Stockholm.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a historic urban scene with multi-storey buildings featuring steep, tiled roofs and many chimneys and dormer windows. In the foreground is a walled garden and a cobblestone street with pedestrians walking along it. The architecture is late medieval/early modern Central European. Printed captions at the bottom margin read the city name on the left and a description of the building and its construction date on the right.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a tree‑lined promenade with an ornate metal railing overlooking a cityscape. Elegant late‑19th‑century buildings stand on the right, with hills visible in the background. At the top, printed in red, is the caption identifying the location as Budapest's Bástya sétány (Basteipromenade). Small figures stroll along the promenade. A small red number is printed vertically on the right edge.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a large steel arch bridge spanning a wide river. A boat is visible on the water and two small figures walk along the riverbank in the foreground. The bridge rests on massive stone piers. Dutch text is printed in white along the bottom border of the image.

A black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a circular, multi‑story pavilion or exhibition building with a tall, tapering tower at the top. The structure is ringed with balconies, railings, and decorative elements, and flags fly from poles around it. Crowds of people in early‑20th‑century clothing walk on a wet plaza in front of the building. Smaller exhibition halls and booths surround the central pavilion. The overall scene suggests a fairground or international exposition.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing soldiers of a field artillery regiment maneuvering and cleaning cannons in a large military courtyard beside a long stone barracks building with exterior staircases. Trees and additional military buildings are visible in the background. Red printed German text and a handwritten signature appear in the lower margin.

Black‑and‑white photographic postcard showing a small alpine village in a broad valley surrounded by dense conifer forests and dramatic vertical limestone cliffs and plateaus. A church with a tall steeple stands near the foreground, scattered farmhouses and chalets lie along a winding road, and towering rock walls rise behind the tree‑covered slopes. No visible caption or printed text appears on the image side.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a city street with tram tracks passing under a large ancient stone arch (a triumphal arch). People walk along the tree‑lined street, early 20th‑century buildings line both sides, and a tram is visible under the arch. French captions appear at the top and bottom of the card.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a traditional half‑timbered country inn with two attached buildings. In front of the inn stand several people behind a fence, and to the right a horse‑drawn carriage with a driver is visible on a dirt road. Trees frame the scene. The printed title in German at the top identifies the guesthouse and its locality, and a sign on the facade of the building also bears the guesthouse name.

A monochrome vintage postcard showing a broad grassy lawn bordered by trees and bushes. In the distance there appear to be fragments of walls or stone structures partly hidden by vegetation, suggesting ruins. On the left, a few people in early-20th‑century clothing are seated near a path. At the top, there is a printed German caption identifying the view; in the lower right there is a small imprint, likely the publisher's mark.

Sepia-toned historic street view showing a broad, tree-lined avenue flanked by ornate multi‑story townhouses with decorative facades and towers. Period streetlamps and a few pedestrians are visible. Printed script at the top identifies the scene as a street in Frankenberg, Saxony.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a gently curving town street lined with two‑ and three‑story houses. Several pedestrians, children, and a horse‑drawn cart are visible on the street. On the left are commercial buildings with German signs on their facades. In the distant right background stands a tall church with a tower and spire overlooking the town. At the top of the card in red print are the captions identifying the town and the street.

Black‑and‑white image of a large indoor swimming pool crowded with bathers in early 20th‑century swimwear. Spectators sit and stand on an upper gallery that runs around the pool. A slide descends from the gallery into the water on the right. Warning and depth signs are posted on the walls. At the bottom edge of the image there is a caption identifying the scene as an indoor bathing facility at Long Beach.

Black‑and‑white view of a European cobblestone square with ornate historic townhouses on the left and, on the right, a large town hall building with a tall clock tower flying flags. Behind it rises a tall Gothic church tower with a slender spire. People in late‑19th/early‑20th‑century clothing walk through the square and a horse‑drawn carriage stands to the right.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped spa park with a central marble statue group on a plinth, flanked by flowerbeds and paths. Two women in long dresses and wide hats stand on the path. Behind them are dense trees and a pavilion-like building. Printed red text at the bottom identifies the location as Bad Elster and mentions the Hygiea statue and promenade in the spa park.

Black‑and‑white aerial photograph showing a complex of mid‑century modern high‑rise buildings surrounded by forest and open fields. The main complex features several rectangular slab blocks arranged around a curved entrance drive, with a tall chimney or smokestack suggesting a hospital, sanatorium, or institutional facility. Additional residential apartment blocks stand nearby along straight roads, and beyond them are patches of cultivated land and woodland. There is no visible printed caption or writing on the image side.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard view taken from a shaded riverbank or lakeshore framed by large trees in the foreground. Across the water stand dense trees and, slightly right of center, a bright stone tower or castle ruin on a low hill. A small pier or landing with a person and possibly a cart or boat is visible by the shore. The scene is calm and rural. Handwritten script at the bottom left reads a place name, and a credit line to the photographer appears below it.

Black‑and‑white view of a small Gothic-style church standing at a street intersection, with steep tiled roofs and pointed arched windows with tracery. A small open wooden belfry rises from the roof ridge. The church is surrounded by low walls and an iron gate on the left. Several adults and children in traditional rural European clothing stand near the apse, and a few people walk along the cobbled streets. On the right and left are timber‑framed or plastered houses with tiled roofs and vines or trees along the façades. The image has the framing and composition typical of an early 20th‑century picture postcard. No legible printed caption is visible.

Black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard divided into four panels showing a rural town in a hilly landscape. The upper left image is a panoramic view of a valley town labeled "Sohland / Spree." The upper right image shows a central area with houses, trees, and a church near a civic building labeled "Am Rathaus" (at the town hall). The lower left image shows a school building on a slope above scattered houses and fields, labeled "Schule am Frühlingsberg." The lower right image focuses on a large traditional building with dormer windows and a tiled roof, labeled "Volkshaus," with people gathered outside. The edges of the card are scalloped, typical of mid‑20th‑century postcards.

Sepia-toned historic view of a wide market square bordered by multi‑storey townhouses with gabled roofs and a prominent town hall–like building. People in early 20th‑century dress walk across the largely unpaved square, with market stalls and a streetlamp visible. The caption at the top reads "Ostritz i. Sa. — Markt". German text is also visible on a building façade at the right edge.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view of a town at the base of a large, rugged mountain. In the foreground runs a river spanned by a multi‑arch bridge; along the riverbank are mid‑rise apartment blocks and civic buildings in a fairly regular grid. Further back, scattered houses and terraced fields climb the foothills. The mountain dominates the background with exposed rock faces and sparse vegetation. The overall look suggests a mid‑20th‑century photographic postcard of a European town in an Alpine or pre‑Alpine valley.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a small Byzantine stone church with a dome and ornate reliefs on the facade, surrounded by a low metal fence. Larger neoclassical buildings and a narrow street appear around it. Greek and French captions are printed above and below the image, and there is a Greek postage stamp in the upper right corner plus handwritten ink on the left side.

Black‑and‑white riverside view of a European city: a broad river with a paddle steamer and moored barges in the foreground, stone embankment at right, and an arched road or rail bridge crossing the water. On the hill beyond the bridge rises a large medieval complex consisting of a twin‑towered Gothic cathedral and adjoining castle‑like buildings, above a dense cluster of townhouses. Smokestacks in the distance emit smoke, suggesting industrial activity. The image is framed and retouched like an old photographic postcard.

Black-and-white postcard showing a large multi-storey hospital building in a late 19th/early 20th century architectural style, with dormer towers and a hipped roof. In the foreground there is a garden or orchard with flowering trees and a dirt path, bordered by fences. A small figure, likely a child, stands in the grass. Along the bottom-left edge, printed caption text reads "Landkrankenhaus Meißen".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a traditional German half‑timbered building with a steep tiled roof. A sign on the facade reads "Altdeutsche Bier- u. Weinstuben, Vincenz Richter". Several people in early 20th‑century clothing stand at the entrance at the top of a staircase. At the bottom, printed text identifies the location as Meissen and describes the establishment as Vincenz Richter's old German beer and wine tavern near the town church.

Black-and-white vintage photograph of a large Gothic cathedral dominating a town square. The façade shows two tall, ornate spires with intricate tracery and pinnacles, and a central lower structure with a steep roof, rose window, and pointed-arch entrance. Trees and a few people and cars appear in the foreground, suggesting a mid‑20th‑century streetscape. The overall style is late Gothic with dark stone and narrow lancet windows.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a tall wooden lookout / observation tower rising above trees. The tower has an octagonal upper structure with open viewing galleries and a small lantern-like top platform with railings. At the base is a two‑storey wooden building with wrap‑around verandas and decorative railings, with several people standing or sitting on the porch and on the ground. The caption at the bottom gives the name and location of the tower in multiple languages.

Black-and-white colonial-era postcard showing an outdoor market scene with numerous African people seated on the ground beside piles of goods, likely produce, while others stand around. Several loaded camels with handlers are positioned in the middle distance. Palm trees and simple buildings frame the scene. Printed captions in French and Dutch at the top identify the setting as Belgian Congo, Léopoldville, and describe the camels as pack animals.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a rocky shoreline with wooden houses and trees near the water's edge. Several small boats are moored along a simple pier or low stone quay. The water appears choppy and open, suggesting a coastal or large lake setting. Printed text in Finnish is visible at the top of the image, with a handwritten numerical note above it.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a waterfront terrace built from rounded stones, with deck chairs, potted plants, a large parasol, and low stone walls overlooking a calm bay or fjord. In the distance are low wooded hills and a few boats on the water. An arched stone gateway is visible to the left. Swedish text is printed along the bottom identifying the location and photographer/publisher.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a vaulted church with wooden pews, an ornate carved pulpit on the left, and an altar with a decorative window at the far end. The photograph is taken from an elevated position at the rear of the church. Printed caption text appears in the lower right and small photographer credit in the lower left.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a small railway station with a wooden station building beside several railcars or railbuses on multiple tracks. People stand near the front vehicle, and there is a semaphore signal by the building. Printed text at the top left reads that this is Klintehamn railway station in 1946.

A vintage sepia-toned panoramic view of a town nestled in a valley, seen from a field or path in the foreground. Dense clusters of houses, church towers and other historic buildings fill the middle ground, with hills or low mountains in the background. The word "Jena" is printed in cursive in the upper left corner against a blank sky area.

A black‑and‑white photograph of a small roadside stone shrine with a tiled gabled roof topped by a cross. Inside the arched niche stands a statue of the Virgin Mary, likely Our Lady of Lourdes or a similar Marian depiction. The shrine is built from rough-hewn dark stones with lighter stones accenting the arch, set on a stepped stone base along a dirt path, with trees and foliage in the background. The image has scalloped postcard-style edges and two punch holes at the top.

A colorized interior view of a large museum gallery with tall white columns and a high ceiling fitted with round light fixtures. The room is filled with glass display cases containing natural history dioramas, including taxidermy animals such as a dog and other wildlife set in realistic landscapes. Printed caption text appears along the bottom edge describing the scene, and a small credit line is on the right.

Colorized vintage view of a Greek town with red‑tiled roofs spread across a hillside. Above the town rises a rocky hill topped by a fortress and surrounded by trees. At the top of the image there is bilingual text in Greek and French identifying the scene, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a riverside scene in a European town. On the left is a large, ornate multi‑story building with arched windows and trees lining a walkway protected by a metal railing above a stone embankment. On the right side of the river stand smaller residential and commercial buildings closely packed along the water. In the distance, more town buildings rise on a gentle hill. The lower margin contains printed captions identifying the location and the publisher.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view over a hilly European town with dense clusters of pitched‑roof houses, tree‑lined streets, small industrial buildings with chimneys in the foreground, and several prominent church spires rising from the center and upper ridge. The surrounding landscape shows terraced gardens and wooded hills. No visible decorative borders or captioning text appear on the image side.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large spa or bathhouse building with a long, two‑storey façade and steep tiled roof, set behind landscaped gardens and trees. People are visible in the foreground and near the entrance. Printed multilingual captions identify the scene as a spa complex (Curhaus) in Varaždinske Toplice/Warasdin-Töplitz. There is a handwritten date at the top (18. VII. 1905.) and a cursive message across the lower portion of the image.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a wide urban square with landscaped gardens and paths in the foreground, a central statue/monument, and a row of 2–3 story historic buildings and shops lining a broad street. A tower of a church or civic building rises in the middle distance. Horse-drawn vehicles and pedestrians are visible. The caption at the bottom reads "Cluj" on the left and "Piața Unirii — Egyesülési-tér" on the right.

A monochrome postcard reproducing Leonardo da Vinci's mural "The Last Supper." The long rectangular image shows Jesus and the twelve apostles seated at a table inside a refectory with a coffered ceiling and three rear windows. Along the right vertical margin there is printed text in Italian and another language describing the work, mentioning "S. Maria delle Grazie," "Leonardo da Vinci" and dates. The postcard has a simple border and no handwriting on the front.

Color‑tinted vintage street view showing a long, straight avenue lined with two‑ and three‑story colonial-style buildings with balconies. Well‑dressed pedestrians, mostly men in suits and hats, walk along the sidewalks. In the distance stands a clock tower or church tower centered at the end of the street. The caption at the top identifies the location as Calle Sucre in Cochabamba, Bolivia. There is also a hanging commercial sign on the right side of the street.

Color view of a European old town square with historic gabled houses lined along the right side and a green lawn or park on the left. In the background rises a tall, slender medieval tower with a dark spire, characteristic of a town hall. The buildings have red-tiled roofs, stone facades, and ornate details. People are walking and gathering near the base of the buildings. The image has the look of a printed tourist postcard; no visible caption or writing appears on the front.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a modest two‑storey building with shuttered windows and a central doorway bearing a large sign that reads "HOTEL LAVICA". To the right, down a side lane bordered by a fence and trees, another building displays a sign "Restauracija Lavica", in front of which people and outdoor seating are visible. In the distant background on a hill is a round, temple‑like structure with a domed roof. The overall style suggests an early‑20th‑century Central European town scene.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a historic hilltop complex above a riverside town. In the foreground, steam-powered boats travel along a broad river with quays and warehouses on the near bank. Above the town's roofs rises a large castle-like building with towers and, behind it, a Gothic cathedral with tall spires. The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as Meißen on the Elbe River with Albrechtsburg Castle and the cathedral (Dom).

Black‑and‑white photograph showing a fortified stone complex with a tall round tower on the right and a distinctive onion‑domed roof on the left. The scene includes old masonry walls, an arched gate, a path curving through a grassy courtyard, and several mature trees. The print has deckle‑style edges typical of vintage postcards. No visible caption or inscription is present on the image side.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a Catholic church with a tall clock tower and spire topped by a cross. The nave and rounded apse are partly obscured by tall trees and hedges. In the foreground stand two people, one dressed as a priest, in a garden or churchyard. Printed caption text appears along the bottom edge.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a riverside view of a historic European town with rows of brick houses along the waterfront, several church towers rising above the skyline, and sailing barges moored on a wide river in the foreground. Low vegetation appears partially submerged at the water's edge. The printed caption at the bottom is in Dutch red lettering, and there is a small printer's line in fine text.

Black‑and‑white view along a dusty village street lined with plastered and timber houses with steep tiled roofs and vines growing up the walls. A few women and a child carry buckets along the road. At the end of the street rises a large Gothic-style church with a prominent tower and spire. The scene has an early 20th‑century rural Central European atmosphere. No visible printed caption or writing appears on the image side.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a rectangular building with a long colonnaded façade, front steps, ornamental fence, and trees in the foreground. The upper margin reads "EXPOSITION COLONIALE INTERNATIONALE – PARIS 1931," indicating it depicts a pavilion from the 1931 Paris Colonial Exposition. The caption below the image identifies the building as the Musée des Colonies and credits architect Laprade & Joussey.

A vintage German-language postcard with handwritten text on the left and address on the right. The heading 'Postkarte' appears at the top center. There is a purple postage stamp in the upper right corner and a circular postmark overlapping it. The card is faded brown, suggesting age, and the handwriting is in cursive script.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a symmetrical two‑story villa or manor house with a hipped roof, twin chimneys, a central balcony, and a columned entrance. It is fronted by a formal garden with paths and trimmed bushes, framed by large trees. The printed caption at the top left reads "Harg, Ingenjörsbostaden."

A black-and-white postcard view of a harbor with a sailing ship docked alongside the waterfront. In the foreground there is a terraced area with railings and steps, possibly part of a quay or warehouse structure. Across the water, small buildings and houses line the shoreline. Printed text in the upper-left corner reads "Luleå, Norra Hamnen." The overall look is early 20th century.

Aerial view of a coastal town with white buildings and red-tiled roofs clustered along a curving river or harbor opening into the sea. A sandy beach, long breakwater with a small lighthouse-like structure, and historic fortifications by the waterfront are visible. The text "Lagos" appears prominently at the top left, with the smaller word "Algarve" beneath it.

A black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard showing an elegant Baroque riverside palace and its surroundings. The top image depicts a long, low palace building with steep mansard roofs and many dormer windows, standing directly on the bank of a wide river with a bridge or terrace projecting over the water. The bottom‑left image shows monumental river stairs with sphinx sculptures flanking the steps that descend to the river, with boats visible on the water. The bottom‑right image presents a garden view of the same palace complex, framed by trees and landscaped flowerbeds. No printed text is visible on the card front.

Sepia-toned postcard view of a European city with a river in the foreground, a bridge crossing it, and dense historic buildings along the riverbank. Behind the city rises a steep hill topped by a large fortification complex. On the right side of the hill stands a prominent clock tower. Handwritten text at the bottom left reads "Graz, Schlossberg." Additional building signage is visible, including a sign reading "JOS SOGEL."

Black‑and‑white view of a small medieval courtyard framed by old masonry and plastered buildings with steep tiled roofs. Ivy climbs the walls and a few small trees grow near the entrances. At the back rises a taller stone building with a turret, and in the background several church-like spires and a large dome dominate the skyline, suggesting an old European town center.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a massive stone defensive tower with a steep hipped roof, surrounded by trees and a low wall along a street. Part of an adjacent urban building façade is visible on the left. At the bottom margin, bilingual captions identify the city and the tower: in Romanian and Hungarian.

Black‑and‑white (tinted) postcard view of a small-town street lined with two‑ and three‑story buildings. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalks; children stand and play in the street and several horse‑drawn carts move down the unpaved road. The façades show shop signs in German script. At the top, in red print, is the caption identifying the town and district: "Mügeln, Bez. Leipzig."

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a rural valley town with scattered houses, fields, low wooded hills, and an industrial complex with tall chimneys emitting smoke. The printed red caption at the top reads "Ehrenfriedersdorf i. Erzgeb. Blick ins Tal d. Wilisch." indicating a view into the Wilisch valley near Ehrenfriedersdorf in the Ore Mountains.

Colorized historic postcard view of a formal city square with a large ornate fountain in the foreground, featuring seated sculpted figures around a basin and a nude female statue on a tall pedestal at the center. The fountain is set within a landscaped garden with flowerbeds and paths, bordered by decorative metal fencing. Behind it are several grand late‑19th‑century style buildings with elaborate facades and trees lining the street. The caption at the top left reads 'Aussig a. Elbe.' and at the top right 'Monumentalbrunnen.' A handwritten red number is also present.

Black‑and‑white view of a large multi‑storey institutional building complex, likely a school, hospital, or administrative facility. The architecture is early‑20th‑century European with steep tiled roofs, dormer windows, arched entranceways, and tall rectangular windows. Bare deciduous trees line a dirt or cobblestone street in the foreground, with a low stone wall and iron fence bordering the property. Additional similar buildings extend into the distance on the left, and gentle hills or fields are visible in the background.

A colorized panoramic view over a historic European town with red‑tiled roofs, factory buildings with a tall brick chimney, several church towers rising above the skyline, and a large building complex on a hill in the background. Trees and narrow streets weave between the houses. At the top left the printed caption reads "Blick auf Kamenz i. Sa.", indicating the town being depicted.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a European town along a river, seen from an elevated, leafy vantage point. In the foreground is a river with a small weir and a bridge crossing it. The town features clustered houses, factory chimneys, and a prominent hilltop complex with a large tower and castle-like buildings. The caption at the top reads in German: "Zschopau — Blick vom Gensel'schen Park".

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large reservoir with a long dam stretching across the background and low hills beyond. In the foreground stands a small, rectangular stone building with arched windows and a door, positioned right on the water's edge. The caption at the bottom describes the scene in Greek and French and identifies it as the lake and dam of Marathon.

Black‑and‑white view over a small pond with a wooden boathouse in the foreground, its reflection visible in the water. Behind a picket fence and dense trees rises an ornate skyline: a Russian Orthodox church with multiple onion domes and tall central tower, flanked by elaborate late‑19th‑century villas and turreted buildings in eclectic and half‑timbered styles. The scene suggests a spa or resort town with park‑like surroundings.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a street with large trees and a substantial multi-storey school building on the right. The architecture features tall rectangular windows, a central arched entrance with steps, and a slightly mansard-style roof. Further down the street more institutional-looking buildings line the road. The caption at the top left reads in German, indicating this is a view of a public school in Oederan, Saxony.

Sepia-toned street scene showing a mid-rise modernist building on a corner with a large painted advertisement on its side, trams and cars in the foreground, and pedestrians on the sidewalk. The photo has narrow margins and the format and wear suggest it is a vintage postcard photograph.

Sepia-toned image of a richly decorated Baroque church interior, focusing on a monumental pipe organ above the main entrance. The organ case is very tall and ornate, with multiple ranks of pipes framed by carved columns, putti and angels, and elaborate stucco decoration on the surrounding vault. Below it is a balcony with a balustrade over a large arched opening leading to a doorway at the back of the nave, flanked by wooden pews.

Black‑and‑white waterfront scene showing a busy harbor with several steamships and small boats. In the foreground is a quay with pedestrians, early automobiles, bicycles, and kiosks. A moored passenger boat with the name "PRINS …" is visible at left, and various signs and small pavilions line the promenade. Across the water a hilly shoreline is built up with houses, and a tall tower or spire rises in the background. The overall style and vehicles suggest an early‑20th‑century European port city.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a European hillside religious complex. In the foreground is a small chapel or shrine with a gabled façade topped by a cross, beside a stairway with ornate metal railings leading up through a terraced garden covered in ivy. Behind it stands a larger plastered building with a steep tiled roof, small dormer, and round window. In the background, above the trees, there is a tower with a steep, pointed roof and a large clock face, resembling a church or town clock tower.

A vintage black-and-white postcard showing a small whitewashed marabout (saint's shrine) with crenellated parapet near Oujda, Morocco. In front of the building are several adults and many children in traditional robes; at the right a person rides a camel led by another person. Trees and low brush form the background. Printed captions in French identify the scene as the Marabout de Sidi Yahia near Oujda, and indicate the publisher.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a street scene with ornate early‑20th‑century buildings, likely guesthouses or villas, along a gently sloping road lined with young trees and a fence. Overhead power and tram lines cross the view. In the foreground on the right there is a small kiosk or newsstand covered with posters and cards, with a person standing in front. The architecture features gabled roofs and decorative facades. The caption at the bottom left reads "Bad Elster Landfrauenheim."

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over a European riverside town. In the left background, a large hilltop complex with tall Gothic spires and castle‑like wings dominates the skyline, overlooking a dense cluster of townhouses below. A wide river flows through the middle of the scene; a multi‑arched stone and metal bridge with railings and light masts spans the river, carrying pedestrians and possibly a tram or carriage. On the far bank are more houses and villas along a curving embankment. In the foreground there is a grassy slope with a simple wooden fence and leafless or sparsely leaved trees partially obscuring the town. In the foreground is a lush urban park with trees, paths, cars, and a small domed structure. Printed caption text runs along the bottom border.

A colorized vintage postcard showing a wide tree‑lined boulevard receding toward low green hills. Elegant multi‑story European‑style buildings line the left side while lower structures and greenery appear on the right. Tram tracks run along the center of the unpaved street. At the bottom left the caption reads "Salonique – Turquie." and at the lower right "Boulevard Hamidieh." There is additional text at the top in Ottoman Turkish script.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a street corner with a prominent two‑storey traditional European building labeled "Hotel zum Stern". The structure has a steep tiled roof with dormer windows, flower boxes beneath the windows, and signage for the hotel, wine shop, and restaurant on the ground floor. A man in formal clothing stands on the sidewalk near the corner entrance, and an early 20th‑century car is parked in front. The caption at the top reads "Neustadt i. Sa.  Hotel zum Stern".

Sepia-toned photograph showing a flooded rural street with houses partly submerged in water. Leafless trees line the background, and only the upper stories and roofs of several buildings are visible above the flood. At the bottom margin there is printed Dutch text identifying the scene and the photo studio in Nijmegen.

A black‑and‑white image of a single steamship at sea, photographed from the front-left side. The vessel has a dark hull, a central funnel emitting smoke, and two tall masts with rigging. The sea is relatively calm and the background is hazy, with only faint outlines of another ship or structure in the far distance. The name of the ship is faintly visible on the bow.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large stone governmental building with arched windows and classical detailing, identified in red print as the U.S. Custom House in Portland, Oregon. Leafless trees frame the foreground, and a playground with wooden swings and several children is visible on the lawn. Handwritten numbers in black and red ink appear near the top center of the image.

A vintage black-and-white (sepia-toned) street scene showing a gently sloping urban street lined with multi‑story stone and brick buildings on the left and large trees and a substantial institutional-looking building with a cross on top on the right. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the street, and a handcart is visible. At the bottom margin, printed in red, are the words indicating the city and street name.

Vintage postcard with an Italian tricolour flag on the left and a red flag on the right, two oval portraits (a man in military uniform and a woman) above a central photograph of a medieval tower on a street. Floral decorations frame the images. Beneath the tower photograph is the caption "Trento - Torre Vanga," and below that is an Italian verse signed "GAZZOLETTI."

Black-and-white postcard showing the richly decorated interior of a traditional house with Islamic-Andalusian style arches, carved stucco, zellij tilework on floors and columns, and low seating around the walls. A round table covered with a cloth stands in the middle of the salon. The scene is lit by daylight from a window in the background. Printed caption in French appears at the bottom margin.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a hilly vineyard landscape with scattered houses and villas. On the ridge to the left stands a round commemorative tower labeled "Bismarckturm." Farther right on the hilltop is a prominent building labeled "Spitzhaus." At the top right of the image, the settlement name "Oberlößnitz." is printed in red Gothic-style script. The scene is pastoral, with terraced slopes, orchards, and early 20th‑century buildings.

Sepia-toned historic view of a European market square with cobblestone paving. Lined with two- and three‑story townhouses and shops, the square is dominated by two church towers in the background—one a tall Gothic spire with clock faces, the other a shorter tower with a dome and clock. A lattice metal pole with multiple crossarms for telegraph or electrical lines stands prominently in the foreground. Pedestrians, including a man in a suit and several women and children with a pram, are scattered around the square. The printed caption at the top left reads "Wilsdruff — Markt," and several shop signs are visible on the right-hand buildings.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a long, three‑storey brick institutional building with a slate mansard-style roof and many evenly spaced tall windows. Small dormer windows line the roof. The façade is symmetrical, with a central arched entrance on the right wing reached by steps and a gabled end section. There is a spire visible behind the roofline suggesting a chapel or nearby church. A low metal fence and a strip of landscaping run in front of the building, with an open grassy field in the foreground and a few distant buildings and trees to the right. No printed caption or handwritten text is visible on the image side.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an alpine landscape with coniferous trees in the foreground, a small cluster of mountain houses on a slope in the mid‑ground, and snow‑covered peaks in the distant background. Printed Italian text at the bottom describes the view and its altitude.

Color-tinted vintage view of a landscaped town square with curving walkways, lawns, flowerbeds, and small decorative structures or fountains. Low buildings and trees surround the square, and a larger light-colored building stands in the background. The words "Nyköping" and "Jernvägstorget" appear in red text at the top.

A vintage multi-view postcard with the large word 'GROETEN' filled with small colorized images of city scenes, rivers, bridges, streets, and buildings. Below, in bold letters, it says 'uit Nijmegen'. At the top left there is a decorative curled paper scroll with a handwritten name 'Nelly'. The background is dark, making the white and pastel letters stand out.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large hilltop complex with a church tower and castle-like buildings above a steep, rocky, and wooded slope. At the bottom of the hill lie several small houses and a road beside fields. The caption at the bottom reads in German: "Dornburg a. d. Saale. Altes Schloß".

A black‑and‑white view over a calm lake bordered by dense coniferous forest. In the foreground, tall pine trees frame the scene from a hillside. Across the water, on a wooded peninsula or shore, stands a large, light-colored building complex with steep roofs, likely a hotel or institutional building, along with a few smaller structures. A small boat is visible on the lake. Handwritten text along the bottom left reads "Tampere: Pyynikki". The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century photographic postcard.

A sepia-toned panoramic view of a town with dense low-rise buildings, streets lined with trees, and a bridge visible in the left-mid area. The scene is taken from an elevated vantage point looking across the settlement toward open countryside in the distance. Greek text is printed beneath the image, along with a website watermark on the photo.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style image showing a rural street scene with simple wooden houses and bare trees, surrounded by fences. One larger house dominates the right foreground, with a smaller two‑storey house and outbuilding further back. In the top left corner is printed text reading "Parti fra Løiten." The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century Scandinavian village view.

Sepia-toned studio photograph showing a uniformed soldier kissing a woman in traditional rural dress. The soldier wears a pickelhaube spiked helmet, tunic with shoulder straps and belt, tall riding boots, and carries a sabre. The woman holds a rolled paper or letter and stands beside a wicker basket with bread. The background is a painted pastoral scene, typical of early 20th‑century studio postcards. No visible printed text appears on the image side.

Black‑and‑white image showing a winding dirt path through a dense coniferous forest. Tall, straight tree trunks line both sides of the path. Two women in long, early‑20th‑century style dresses stand on the path in the middle distance, accompanied by a light‑colored dog. The scene is calm and natural, with no visible buildings or urban elements. A faint white handwritten numerical mark appears at the bottom edge of the image, as if from an archival or postcard catalog number.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a public square with palm trees, walking paths, and a decorative bandstand or gazebo on the right. Several people in early 20th‑century clothing stand and walk in the square, with arid mountains rising in the background. At the top is printed text in Portuguese identifying the location as a partial view of Praça Nova on the island of São Vicente, Cabo Verde.

Colorized winter scene showing a snow-covered path leading uphill through trees toward a large Baroque church with two onion-domed towers. In the foreground stands a roofed roadside crucifix enclosed by a small fence, and two cloaked figures walk toward a stairway and statue. The caption at the top right reads "Maria Trost im Winter."

Colorized vintage view of a large brick railway station building with ornate gables and a tall spire. Bicyclists ride in the foreground and a horse‑drawn carriage stands near the entrance. The caption at the bottom left reads "Nijmegen. Station".

A black‑and‑white rural landscape view showing several low farm or institutional buildings clustered together on a flat plain, surrounded by open fields and grassland under a wide sky. The scene appears to be taken from a distance, with wildflowers or tall grasses in the foreground and a sparsely populated horizon in the background. In the upper left corner, faint printed text is visible.

Vintage postcard with three colorized photographic panels showing the same older man in different poses in an outdoor colonial-era town setting. The man wears a long patterned wrap skirt and a jacket; in the left image he carries a pole on his shoulder, in the middle he walks in front of a house and wooden fence while other people look on from a doorway, and in the right image he appears to dance or move energetically, with another man and a donkey in the background. The caption at the bottom right reads "S. Thomé." and another caption along the bottom center identifies him as a servant of the firm Salvador Levy & Co.

Colored postcard showing a large ornate fountain in a landscaped city park. The fountain has golden statues and multiple water jets arcing outward into a circular basin, surrounded by manicured lawns, paths, and trees. Handwritten notes are faintly visible across the sky area, and printed caption text appears at the top in German.

A black‑and‑white landscape postcard showing a wide lake surrounded by forested hills and scattered farmland, viewed from an elevated vantage point on a hillside. The sky is filled with scattered clouds. In the foreground are trees on the slope; the lake stretches into the distance between low mountains. White caption text is printed along the bottom left, and a photographer's credit and logo appear in the bottom right.

Vintage black‑and‑white (sepia‑tinted) postcard view of a town street labeled "Kötzschenbroda. Bahnhofstrasse." It shows a row of 2–3‑story buildings with shops, signs, and a hotel along a raised sidewalk overlooking a broad street or square. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk, children play, and a bicycle leans against a railing. In the distance a prominent corner building bears a large sign for a café and billiards. In the foreground stands a cylindrical advertising column surrounded by iron railings.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the interior of a traditional European living room or farmhouse parlor. The room has a wooden beamed ceiling and patterned wallpaper on all walls. On the left stands a tall longcase clock next to a wooden bench with upholstered seats. In the center is a carved wooden table with various small objects on top, surrounded by different styles of wooden chairs. Against the back wall is a corner display cabinet with dishes, and a small casement window with decorative curtain. To the right is a large, ornate tiled or cast‑iron stove with two vertical flue pipes and brick base, accompanied by pottery on the floor and fireplace tools. On the right wall is a wooden sideboard and a rack holding plates. Woven baskets sit on the floor in the front corners. The overall style suggests an early‑20th‑century depiction of a 19th‑century Central or Northern European rural home interior. There is no visible printed caption or handwritten message on the image side.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a traditional Dutch windmill beside a canal. Several small boats are moored along the canal bank in the foreground. To the right stands a brick farmhouse or building with a tiled roof and a chimney. The windmill dominates the central background with its large sails and adjacent outbuildings. Handwritten and printed Dutch text appears at the top of the image identifying the mill and its location.

A colored postcard view of a tranquil pond with rowing boats and swans in the foreground. On the far shore are trees, landscaped flowerbeds, a small half-timbered building with a red roof, and a larger hall-like building on a gently rising hillside. Curved paths run through the park-like setting. Printed German text at the top identifies the location as a gondola pond in the citizens' garden of Döbeln.

A night-time winter scene showing a snow-covered medieval street with stone walls and a large round defensive tower in the background. Warm yellow light spills from windows and a lamp over a doorway, illuminating the snow. At the bottom margin there is printed text with the artist's name and the place depicted.

Black-and-white vintage postcard showing a cobblestone street lined with stepped-gable buildings and shop awnings, leading toward a tall medieval belfry tower in the distance. The caption at the top reads in French that it is a view of La Rue des Pierres in Bruges, and a small printer's credit appears along the bottom margin.

Sepia-toned view of a historic village church with a tall, slender spire and clock tower, likely Protestant, next to a half-timbered building. In the foreground is a multi-arched stone bridge over a river, with numerous people—adults and children—standing along the parapet and on the bank. Bare trees frame the scene, suggesting late autumn or winter. The style resembles an early 20th‑century photographic postcard. No visible printed text appears on the image side.

Sepia-toned waterfront view showing a long arcaded building with elaborate Venetian-Gothic façades and crenellations beside a calm harbor. A square tower with a clock stands further back along the quay. Small boats float in the water in the foreground. The overall layout suggests a historic seaside esplanade with monumental public buildings.

Sepia-toned historical photograph of a two‑storey neoclassical building with a metal roof, arched doorway and tall rectangular windows. Above the entrance and on a corner bay, the word "INCŪKALNS" (printed without diacritics as INCUKALNS) is visible, suggesting it is a railway or public station. A few people stand or sit on the unpaved street and tracks in front of the building. The overall style and wear of the image indicate an early 20th‑century postcard.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a town square bordered by two‑ to three‑storey buildings with gabled roofs and shopfronts at street level. People in early 20th‑century clothing stand or walk across the cobblestoned market square; a lamppost and small monument or fountain are in the center. Red German script at the bottom identifies the view as a market square in Geringswalde, seen from the south side, and a publisher credit appears along the lower margin.

A colorized postcard illustration of the ocean liner 'VATERLAND' at sea, showing a large black-hulled passenger ship with four yellow funnels and extensive deck structures. The ship cuts through choppy water under a pastel sky. At the bow the name 'VATERLAND' is visible. In the upper left a flag with the Hamburg-Amerika Linie (HAPAG) crest is shown. On the right side there is red German text describing the ship's dimensions and capacity.

A sepia-toned postcard view over a town with dense rooftops and trees in the foreground, dominated by a large Gothic cathedral-like church and a castle complex on a hill. A tall tree frames the right side of the scene, and another tower with a dome stands on the far right. At the bottom border of the image there is printed German text identifying the view of Meissen and the Albrechtsburg castle and cathedral.

Black-and-white rural landscape view showing a farmhouse in the foreground and several scattered farm buildings in open fields bordered by dense forest. Tall conifer trees frame the scene. At the bottom is a printed caption in German identifying the location as Steinbach near Johanngeorgenstadt, Eisenganz.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large multi‑storey institutional building complex in a wooded area, likely a sanatorium or hospital. There is open grass in the foreground with simple wooden play structures or frames, and tall conifer trees around the site. The buildings have steep roofs and multiple rows of windows, in a Northern European architectural style. A white border surrounds the image and small printed captions appear at the lower edge.

Color postcard showing a sunlit Italian square with a large baroque fountain in the foreground and a Romanesque cathedral with a central rose window and octagonal drum in the background. To the right is a tall tower with an onion-shaped green dome. Handwritten Italian text appears along the right margin, and printed captions identify the place and publisher.

A sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a curved electric tramway line running through a semi-rural, tree-lined area. There is a small building on the left with a few people standing outside near a fence and tram tracks in the foreground that lead toward a tramcar visible on the right. Overhead power lines and poles run along the tracks. The caption at the bottom reads in Dutch, indicating the scene is in Nijmegen, Netherlands.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a dramatic rock pillar with a monastery complex perched on top, part of the Meteora rock formations. There is a wide valley in the background and another steep cliff on the right. Greek and French captions appear beneath the image.

Black‑and‑white image showing a large alpine-style villa or spa hotel set among tall conifer trees in a forested mountain valley. A narrow river or stream with stone‑lined banks runs in the foreground, crossed by a small wooden footbridge on the left. The multi‑storey building has balconies, wooden verandas, and a small central tower or belfry rising above the roof. No visible printed caption or handwriting appears on the image side.

Black‑and‑white image of a mid‑20th‑century cargo ship at sea, photographed in profile to port. The vessel has a single funnel marked with a star emblem and several cargo masts with booms. The sea is relatively calm and the horizon is low, with no visible coastline. The ship's name is painted on the bow and stern areas.

Black‑and‑white view of a quiet residential street lined with late‑19th/early‑20th‑century houses. On the left corner is a shop with an awning and signage; fenced front gardens border the sidewalk. A woman and a child walk down the pavement toward the distance. On the right, larger, more ornate buildings with decorative façades stand behind fences and trees. The scene is calm and largely empty of traffic, giving an early‑20th‑century European small‑town impression.

Vintage postcard view of a waterfall flowing over a rocky ledge between tree‑covered banks, with small wooden buildings on the cliffs at both sides. A person stands near a hut on the left edge overlooking the falls. The image is partly colorized in brown and green. The lower margin contains printed red text and black handwritten greetings and date.

Black‑and‑white winter scene showing a narrow snow‑covered lane lined with old houses and stone walls. In the background, on a hill above the town, rises a large Gothic church or cathedral with twin towers and spires. Snow covers the rooftops and bare trees frame the view. At the bottom margin, printed text identifies the scene and a small number appears at the lower right.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the courtyard and arched colonnades of a Spanish-style mission complex with tile roofs and a small bell wall topped by a cross. Shrubs and paths fill the foreground. Red caption text along the bottom identifies it as Mission San Juan Capistrano in Orange County, California, and red vertical text along the sides notes it was printed in Germany and published in Los Angeles by M. Rieder. A red number 5731 is printed in the lower right corner.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural riverside landscape with open meadows in the foreground, a winding small river, scattered trees, and a village or farm buildings and forested area in the background. In the top left corner there is printed text reading "Svartån vid Karbenning". The overall look suggests an early 20th‑century photographic postcard.

Color view over a lakeside town backed by high mountains. In the foreground is a waterfront promenade lined with lush greenery and palm trees, separated from the road above by a wall. Across the blue water lies a dense row of old buildings with red-tiled roofs and pastel facades. A notable feature is a square stone bell tower rising above an arcaded white building near the center. There are traffic signs visible on the left side of the road, and the overall style suggests a mid‑20th‑century tourist postcard.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with a pastoral town view. In the foreground are several multi‑story houses beside a street with a tram or railcar and a few people. Behind them are rolling hills and fields. On the left hilltop stands a large baroque church or basilica with twin towers. The lower border contains ornate printed text in German, and the rest of the card is filled with handwritten cursive text in purple ink along the top and right margins. The style is late‑19th‑century.

Sepia-toned vintage view of a broad, cobblestone, tree-lined street flanked by low townhouses and buildings. In the distance stand taller historic structures, including a tower and church spire. Printed title text at the top reads "Mühlberg (Elbe)" with a subtitle "Lindenstraße," indicating the name of the town and the specific street.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a large, two‑storey neoclassical building along a broad, mostly empty street or square. There are a few trees, street lamps and sparse pedestrians. At the bottom left, printed text reads "Karlskrona." and beneath it "Robert Ekecrantz." indicating the subject and publisher or photographer.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a richly decorated church with high vaulted ceilings, wooden galleries, an ornate pulpit, chandeliers, and a polygonal altar area. The image is framed like a vintage postcard, with printed caption text along the bottom identifying the church and the photographer's mark in the lower right corner.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large passenger steamship at sea, photographed in profile. The ship has two dark smokestacks, lifeboats along the sides, and several decks with railings and portholes. Handwritten-style text at the bottom names the vessel, and a small oval logo is printed in the lower-right corner.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a traditional two‑storey wooden log building with a sod/grass roof, set among tall conifer trees. A covered balcony runs along the upper floor on the front façade, with an arched opening over the entrance below. At the bottom edge of the image there is printed text in a Scandinavian language and a small publisher's logo.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a small stone tower styled like a medieval ruin, with crenellations on top and a cannon‑like tube protruding from the wall. In a niche of the tower stands an armored knight figure with helmet and breastplate beneath a small bell. In front of the tower is an outdoor seating area with a round table covered by a patterned cloth and surrounded by folding chairs. Trees without leaves frame the scene. The word "Raubritterturm" appears in script at the bottom.

The image shows the back of a vintage postcard with printed and handwritten text in Estonian. On the left is a printed sender line reading "Eduard Vilde Mälestuse Jäädvust. Kor… Tartu, Aia 19…". In the center-right there is a brown postal form label glued onto the card with printed Estonian text and several handwritten entries, including a location written as "Tallinnas". Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing an ornate neoclassical interior hall with high coffered ceilings, grand arches, columns, elaborate chandeliers, rows of chairs along the walls, and a central statue in a niche. The left side features the photograph labeled at the bottom, while the right side contains dense handwritten text in German script. The word "Graz" appears at the top right in red, and at the bottom center is printed "Universität, Aula."

A monochrome postcard framed by a faux-wood printed border, showing a panoramic waterside view of a large rectangular palace building with classical facades, quays and several boats in the foreground. A church tower and surrounding city buildings are visible to the left. The image is printed in an oval vignette on a light background, with captions beneath it.

Black-and-white studio portrait of an Austro-Hungarian officer in elaborate hussar-style uniform with braiding and fur trim, standing beside an ornate table and chair. He holds a sword and wears several medals. The card has a printed photographer's imprint and coat of arms at the bottom, with decorative script text in Hungarian indicating a Budapest studio.

A vintage black‑and‑white (hand‑colored) postcard showing a large, two‑story school building with a central domed structure on the roof, trees and a dirt street with utility poles in front. The image is bordered by a white margin containing printed red text, including a caption at the bottom identifying the scene as a high school in Pasadena, California, and side text indicating the publisher and that it was printed in Germany.

Sepia-toned portrait photograph of a man in historical costume, with a large mustache and ruffled collar, seated and holding what appears to be a plumed hat. The lighting is studio-style, and handwritten text at the bottom identifies the subject and role in a theatrical production.

A monochrome postcard photograph showing a steamship at sea or in a harbor, viewed from the side. The vessel has a single tall funnel with faint lettering on it and masts fore and aft. The bow on the right side bears the name "MAX." The background shows a low shoreline with industrial structures or harbor buildings. The water in the foreground is slightly choppy. There is handwriting along the bottom edge of the image and postal-cancellation marks across the upper portion.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a bustling outdoor market scene in front of historic multi‑story buildings. Numerous vendors and shoppers, many in early 20th‑century dress, stand among stalls, carts, and large baskets filled with produce under canvas umbrellas. The architecture features Italianate facades with arched windows, balconies, and awnings. A printed caption appears in the lower margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white panoramic view of an old European city with narrow brick houses, tiled roofs, and a canal running alongside a cobbled street. A stone bridge crosses the canal in the middle distance, and several church spires and a tall belfry tower rise above the skyline. At the top of the card it reads "Bruges – Panorama." The overall style and printing suggest an early 20th‑century postcard.

Black‑and‑white streetscape of a European town around the early 20th century. A broad avenue lined with multi‑storey, late‑19th‑century buildings is filled with pedestrians, a horse‑drawn vehicle and an early electric tram. Some shop awnings extend over the sidewalk. On the hill in the background stands a large complex with a central tower, resembling a monastery or institutional building, surrounded by forest. On the nearest corner building a sign on the gable reads "VILLA PETRUSKA", and on the corner building further down the street a sign reads "ALLIANZ". Another shop sign at street level reads "KARL KLOIBER".

A black-and-white image of a medieval stone complex with a square tower in the left foreground and a round double-tower structure in the background. The buildings have steep, tiled roofs, and the nearer tower has a small lantern on top. A stone curtain wall with arched openings runs from the right foreground toward the towers, with a narrow path beside it. Trees and low vegetation surround the structures, giving the impression of a castle or fortified estate on a hill. There is no visible printed caption or text on the image side.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a rocky hillside with a small stone-built cave entrance closed by a metal lattice gate. A few children stand on the dirt road in front of the structure. In the distance on the right, a small church-like building sits on a hill. Printed text at the top reads "Pécs. Barlang".

Sepia-toned photograph mounted on a light border, showing a dusty open area or square with several two‑storey and single‑storey buildings in the background. An early motor vehicle is driving on the dirt road to the left, while a few people, including children, stand or walk in the foreground. The style of the buildings is typical late‑Ottoman / early 20th‑century eastern Mediterranean. Handwritten Greek script appears at the bottom left, and a printed website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' is overlaid on the lower right.

Black‑and‑white view over a hilly European town. In the foreground are plastered two‑ and three‑storey houses with steep tiled roofs, fenced gardens, and a narrow street with a few horse‑drawn carts. Behind them rise terraced grassy slopes with scattered fruit trees and wooden fences. In the hazy distance on a hill stands a large fortress‑like castle complex with towers and a central keep, overlooking the town. The picture has wide borders and the overall appearance of an early 20th‑century photographic postcard.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a baroque-style altar with a realistic crucifix of Jesus Christ at its center, framed by two dark columns and an ornate arch with sculpted decorations above. The lower margin of the card contains printed text in a South Slavic language describing the subject and location, mentioning Visovac on the Krka River.

Vintage monochrome postcard with an Art Nouveau style decorative frame around a photograph of a park-like area with bare trees and buildings in the background. The card is printed in German and includes a New Year's greeting in ornate script on the lower half, along with a small vertical caption near the image and a large printed number at the bottom.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large Ottoman‑style mosque with a central dome, smaller surrounding domes, and a single tall minaret. In the foreground are two men standing by a low wall. The caption at the bottom identifies the view as a mosque in Salonique/Salonica and describes it as a famous or original mosque.

Black-and-white postcard view of a colonnaded hall set within a landscaped park. The long, rectangular building with many columns stands in the background, while trees, lawns, and curved pathways occupy the foreground. There is a handwritten number "32" near the top center. Printed white text at the bottom left reads "Bad Elster Wandelhalle."

Black‑and‑white view down a gently sloping cobblestone street in a European town, lined with multi‑story historic buildings with shuttered windows and shop signs. On the left corner is a shop with large display windows and German signage; on the right are more businesses and houses. A few pedestrians and two boys with a bicycle stand in the street. In the distance rises a tall church tower with a pointed spire and a clock face. The overall look suggests an early‑20th‑century urban scene.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a coastal view with calm water in the foreground, a shoreline with small boats pulled up on the bank, and a town in the background. A tall cylindrical lighthouse dominates the scene, surrounded by low houses and buildings. In the lower left there is a decorative label in Greek script, and at the bottom right a website watermark reads "www.elia.org.gr".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a riverside row of multi‑storey houses at the foot of a steep, wooded hill. On the hillside is a funicular railway leading up to a large fortress complex on the summit. The word "Seil‑Bahn" appears on the side of a building beside the lower station. At the bottom margin is a printed caption identifying the location, with additional handwritten German text across the image and margins.

Black‑and‑white rural scene showing a man sitting on a simple wooden sled or harrow drawn by a single horse along a dirt track bordered by rows of blooming fruit trees (likely cherry or apple trees). Behind a wooden picket fence stands a small plastered farmhouse with a tiled gabled roof and shuttered windows. The trees are densely covered with blossoms, suggesting springtime in a European countryside.

Black‑and‑white illustrated postcard showing a soldier with a rifle standing on rocky ground, looking out over a body of water with islands or coastline in the distance. Another smaller figure stands further away near the shore. At the top there is printed Swedish text about proceeds for a hometown hospital in Uddevalla, and across the image there is a handwritten date, most likely from 1915. An artist's signature appears in the lower right corner.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a rural half‑timbered inn or guesthouse with a steep tiled roof, garden beds in the foreground, wooden fences, and a horse‑drawn carriage in front. Trees and a wooded background surround the building. The title in red Gothic script appears at the top, and publisher information is printed along the edges.

An illustrated postcard showing a group of medieval-style houses with steep red roofs clustered around an open square or market area. A tall church or town hall spire rises in the background. The drawing is done in pen and light color wash. Along the bottom border there are captions in two languages: one in Estonian on the left and one in German on the right.

Black-and-white postcard showing a two-story school building with a tiled roof, centered at the end of a gravel path lined with young trees. Bicycles are visible by the building, and a flag flies on the left behind trees. Printed caption text appears along the bottom border, along with a photographer/publisher credit and a catalog number.

A black-and-white aerial photograph of a rural village dominated by a rectangular white church with a square tower and spire, surrounded by trees. Farm fields and scattered wooden farmhouses and barns extend into the distance, with narrow country roads winding through the landscape. The overall look suggests an old European countryside scene.

Black‑and‑white view of a cobblestone street leading uphill to a medieval city gate tower with a tall, simple hipped roof and small windows. The arched gateway forms a tunnel through the tower, with a glimpse of trees and houses beyond. On the right side of the street is a row of plastered houses with shop signs and a doorway; on the left are simpler residential buildings. A few people, including children, stand near the archway. The architecture suggests a small Central European town with preserved fortifications.

A black-and-white postcard photograph showing a narrow-gauge railway track running through dense banana and coffee plantations. Several people, including men in hats and traditional clothing, stand along the track amidst tall banana plants. Mountains are faintly visible in the distance. Handwritten-style text along the bottom identifies the scene and location, and there is a photographer's credit on the lower right.

A colorized historical postcard view of a busy European city square. In the foreground stands a large monument with multiple statues and steps, surrounded by café tables and parasols. Old multi‑story buildings with red-tiled roofs and green window shutters line the square. A tram and horse-drawn carriages are visible. In the background, on a hill, there is a fortified structure with a prominent clock tower. Red printed text at the top reads in German: "Graz. Hauptplatz mit Schlossberg."

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a panoramic view of a densely built city with tiled-roof houses and at least one prominent mosque with a tall minaret in the middle ground. Hills and more buildings appear in the background. The printed caption under the image reads "83. SALONIQUE" followed by multilingual text "Un Panorama — A Panorama". At the bottom left is the editor credit "Edit. Koller, Lyon".

Vintage sepia postcard showing a white Gothic‑style church with a tall clock tower and spire on the right side, surrounded by trees and fields. In the foreground is a cultivated field, and in the lower center ornate lettering in a Latin-script language is printed over the image. The general layout and print style suggest an early‑20th‑century European postcard.

Black-and-white panoramic view of a small European village in a hilly rural landscape. The foreground shows a meadow with wildflowers sloping down toward tightly clustered houses with steep gabled roofs, many of them two or three stories and plastered or half‑timbered. A railway line with a small station building and a train runs along the edge of the village. Beyond, patchwork fields, scattered farm buildings, and wooded hills extend into the distance. There is no visible printed caption or handwriting on the image side.

Sepia-toned historical photograph of a packed marble stadium during a formal ceremony. The stands are filled with spectators wearing late‑19th‑ or early‑20th‑century clothing, while officials in dark suits line up on the track. In the infield stands a tall pillar or mast decorated with a wreath or garland. At one side there is a monumental arched entrance set into the tiers of seating. The overall look suggests an antique-style Olympic or ceremonial event.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of an ornate historic spa building with a central pavilion and side arcades, fronted by formal gardens, paths, trimmed bushes, and outdoor seating. The architecture is richly decorated with arches, columns, and a mansard-style roof with small towers. The lower margin carries captions indicating the spa town and the specific building depicted.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view of a European city in a river valley, showing dense late‑19th‑century urban buildings and two prominent Gothic‑revival churches with tall spires and crosses. In the foreground stands a large neo‑Gothic church with pointed windows and buttresses, next to tree‑lined streets and a railway or tram line. Beyond it are rows of multi‑storey townhouses and industrial buildings with a tall factory chimney. In the background, steep hillsides are terraced with vineyards and scattered villas, with a fortress‑like structure on the ridge.

Black-and-white postcard view of a landscaped park with young trees in the foreground, a man walking along a paved street, and in the background the large arched span of a bridge. The scene is framed by dense trees on the left and right. Printed caption text appears along the bottom edge.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a sketched stone city gate set in a wall along a road with trees to the left and a building to the right. The archway has measurement arrows marked with dimensions, and handwritten labels identify directions and locations. Decorative German text in an old‑style script appears at the top, and a printed caption is at the bottom.

A sepia-toned historic postcard showing a coastal village built on a hillside around a calm harbor. Small boats lie along the waterfront and traditional stone houses with tile roofs rise in tiers up the slope. Printed captions appear in French at the top and in Greek at the bottom, and there is a handwritten date in blue ink in the upper right corner.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a large brick railway station building with arched windows and a small tower or cupola on the roof. The scene shows a cobblestone street in the foreground and bare trees framing the image, suggesting late autumn or winter. In the lower left corner, printed caption text identifies the location, and a handwritten number appears in the lower right.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a busy waterfront scene. Numerous small wooden fishing boats are moored side by side along a quay. Women in traditional regional clothing and white bonnets, along with a few men in caps and uniform-like coats, stand on the quay and in the boats handling baskets and fishing gear, suggesting a fish market or landing of the day's catch. In the distance are industrial buildings with tall chimneys and gasworks structures, and further out on the water there is a small building on stilts or a pier and a sailing boat. The overall style and attire evoke an early‑20th‑century Northern European fishing town.

Black‑and‑white view of a cobblestoned town square bordered by 2‑ to 3‑story historic buildings. On the left is a row of houses with shopfronts; in the middle distance rises a church tower with a clock and onion‑shaped spire. On the right side stands a prominent multi‑story civic‑style building with arched windows and decorative stonework, facing the open square. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and stand around the square, and bicycles are visible near the large building. Mountainous terrain appears faintly in the background.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a calm waterfront with a small boat moored along a stone quay, a bridge crossing a canal or inlet, and multi‑story classical buildings and trees in the background. Text is printed along the bottom edge in Swedish, identifying the location as Vänersborg and describing the view from the harbor.

Black‑and‑white photograph of an old Gothic doorway on a narrow cobblestone street. The central pointed‑arch door has wooden panels with tracery, reached by a few worn stone steps. Above it is a large stone relief panel in a Gothic frame showing several kneeling figures around a heraldic shield or religious scene. Flanking the doorway are fragments of elaborate Gothic carvings and another pointed arch to the right. On the left is a small window with metal lattice bars and flower pots. The façade is rough and peeling, suggesting great age. At the very bottom edge, some hand‑written characters appear on the print border.

Colour-tinted vintage postcard view of a coastal promenade with railings and trees on the left and the sea on the right. In the background a large fortified rock with ramparts and buildings stands out, forming a citadel by the water. A small boat is visible in the bay. There is printed caption text in French at the bottom and handwritten notes across the lower margin.

A colorized historical postcard view of a European spa town. It shows a river or canal running through a valley, lined with elegant multi‑story buildings on both sides. On the left is a grand civic building, while promenades and tree‑covered walkways follow the water. People in late 19th‑/early 20th‑century clothing stroll along the embankments and horse‑drawn carriages travel on the street. Forested hills rise in the background. Printed captions in German identify the scene as Karlsbad with specific streets or buildings.

A monochrome winter scene showing a historic European town covered in snow, with a frozen or icy river in the foreground. A multi‑arch stone bridge crosses the river toward a large hilltop complex of Gothic towers and steep‑roofed buildings dominating the right side, likely a castle and cathedral. Snow blankets the roofs and the riverbank. At the bottom left margin in cursive script is the caption "Meissen im Winter."

A black‑and‑white (sepia-toned) view of a slightly sloping street lined with two‑ and three‑story townhouses on both sides. The buildings have steep tiled roofs and traditional German architectural elements. Utility poles and early telegraph/telephone lines run along the street. Small groups of people are walking or standing on the sidewalks. At the top of the image, printed in red Gothic-style script, it reads "Zöblitz i. Erzgeb." on the left and "Johannes-Strasse" on the right.

Colorized, slightly worn card depicting a two‑storey brick and stone public building in a landscaped garden. The structure has large arched windows on the upper floor, pilasters and decorative friezes in a neoclassical style, red brick side wings, a low hipped roof with several chimneys, and a small manicured park with flowerbeds, paths, and trees in the foreground. No visible caption or writing appears on the front.

A vintage black-and-white postcard view showing a small passenger boat or ferry sailing on a body of water in front of a tree‑lined shore with several large buildings. One prominent domed church-like structure with a lantern tower stands on the hill, and to the right there is a large, ornate building with towers. The upper left corner of the card bears printed text in Swedish describing the view of Skeppsholmen in Stockholm.

Colorized vintage view from a terraced garden walkway on a hill looking down over a European city with red-tiled roofs and a river crossed by bridges. On the right, a pergola covered in vines, stone steps, and a woman in a long dress stand at the overlook. At the top of the card there is German text indicating the viewpoint over the city from the Schlossberg in Graz.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view of a European river valley town taken from a high vantage point.
