Additional information suggests it was published by F. Koelbel, Landeck.

A vintage black and white postcard depicting a large Byzantine-style church with a central dome, bell tower, and multiple arched windows. The building is situated near the coast, with a sailing ship visible in the background. The postcard includes printed and handwritten text in French and another script, possibly Ottoman Turkish. The church is labeled as 'Eglise-Cathédrale St-Grégoire.' The upper part features the phrase 'Souvenir de Trébizonde.'

The postcard features an illustrated image of a warship or patrol boat sailing on calm waters, with a coastal city visible in the distant background. The ship is shown from a frontal side, creating a dramatic and dynamic effect. There is text in the upper right corner in a non-English language, specifically Estonian.

A black and white postcard photograph showing a panoramic view of a hillside city. Prominent in the foreground is a large palace complex on a rocky outcrop, with a mountainous backdrop. The French text at the top identifies the site as the 'Palais du Prince' (Prince's Palace) in Monaco and references the 'Tête de Chien' (a distinctive mountain peak whose name means 'the head of the dog'). There is also English text providing a translation.

A vintage black‑and‑white/sepia postcard view of a waterfront settlement. Several small sailing boats are on the water in the foreground. On the shore stand wooden buildings and pavilions, including a long building with a central tower-like roof and a smaller structure on a pier or floating platform. Behind them are trees and a few larger villas on a hill. The caption in red at the top left reads "Uddevalla, Gustafsberg."

Black-and-white image showing a large stone suspension bridge with massive arched towers spanning a wide river. Ornamental lamps line the bridge, and people are walking across it. In the foreground there is a neatly landscaped riverside garden with paths, bushes, and several people strolling or tending plants. Across the river, a grand historic building with twin towers and a dome is visible. The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century European cityscape. No visible printed text is present on the front.

Black‑and‑white view of a central town square with a prominent three‑storey stone building bearing a clock‑tower and small spire. The façade carries the inscription "KOENIGLICHES AMTSGERICHT" (Royal District Court). In front stand leafless, pollarded trees and a decorative street lamp. To the right are adjoining townhouses with shopfronts and signage, including one marked "Hôtel Altenburg". The scene is quiet with no visible people or vehicles, suggesting an early 20th‑century European townscape.

A night-time view of a modern glass pyramid structure shot from below, with the triangular form rising against a deep blue sky. Bright colored light beams or illuminated lines (yellow and red) streak diagonally upward along the dark reflective surface of the pyramid, giving it a futuristic appearance. There is no visible text on the front.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a riverside industrial complex with a tall smokestack in the foreground and a large hill covered in trees behind it. On top of the hill stands a fortified medieval complex with walls, towers, and buildings, identified as Schloss Mildenstein. The scene is reflected in the calm river. Red printed German text appears at the top and along the right edge.

A black-and-white postcard view showing a bridge in the foreground leading into a small town with multi-story buildings and a church-like tower with a spire. Trees and a few lower buildings line the right side, while the left side shows older houses and a street where a cart or vehicle is visible. At the bottom of the image there is a caption printed in German.

Monochrome printed postcard showing a detailed architectural engraving of a richly decorated Baroque church façade with statues and a large dome behind it. A broad exterior staircase with stone balustrades and patterned railings leads up between the church and an adjacent palatial building; several small figures walk on the steps. The image is signed "Kreuzer" at the lower left, and there is a handwritten word resembling a place name centered in the lower margin.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a panoramic view from a wooded hillside looking down onto a small town in a valley, with church spires and scattered buildings surrounded by fields and low hills. Tall tree trunks frame the foreground. The caption in red at the bottom reads "Blick auf Flöha." and in smaller red print along the lower margin it reads "6280 Brück & Sohn, Meissen 1905". The lower part of the card is left blank for writing.

Color postcard view of a historic hilltop complex with a large Gothic cathedral featuring tall dark spires and an attached castle-like palace overlooking a river. Traditional European houses line the riverbank below. A long white paddle steamboat with a side-mounted paddle wheel sails on the river in the foreground under a clear blue sky.

Black‑and‑white landscape view showing a Central European rural valley with scattered houses and small villas surrounded by fields and dense coniferous forest. Dominating the right side is a large sandstone rock massif with vertical grooves and a forested top, reminiscent of a rock city formation. Low, wooded mountains and rolling hills form the distant background; there are no visible captions or borders on the picture side.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large, two‑storey institutional building behind a high wall and decorative fence. The structure has many rectangular windows, a central arched entrance, and a long façade, suggesting a school or asylum. In the foreground is a street with telegraph poles, and a child or small figure standing by the corner of the wall. At the top of the image is printed text: a numbered caption on the left and the publisher's name on the right.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a rural landscape with haystacks in the foreground and a small town in the background. Dominating the town skyline is a church with a tall, pointed steeple and clock tower. Trees and modest town buildings surround the church. At the top left, in red Gothic-style lettering, is the caption 'Lengefeld i. Erzgeb.'

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand corner residential or civic building with ornate facades and a steep roof with a tower-like section. The building stands on a broad tree‑lined square or boulevard. A tram and people are visible on the left side, and the street is otherwise open and spacious. The words "Graz." appear in the upper left, "Schillerplatz." in the upper right, and a small serial number is printed at the bottom left.

Black‑and‑white / tinted postcard view of a river scene with a steam paddle boat named "Pillnitz" docking at a pier on a calm river. On the right is a small pier building on the water, with a few small boats nearby. In the background are terraced hillsides, cliffs, and a village with several houses and trees. At the top in red Gothic-style script is German text identifying the location on the River Elbe at Diesbar and its steamboat landing.

Old monochrome postcard showing a long brick military complex behind an iron fence along a wide cobbled street. The main building is a multi‑storey barracks, with adjoining structures including a more ornate officers' casino. German captions in red identify the scene as the barracks, hospital (lazaret) and officers' casino of the K.S. 13th Infantry Regiment No. 178 in Kamenz. A printer's line appears at the bottom edge.

Colorized historic view of a European city square with a central open plaza lined with young trees and outdoor café tables. Surrounding the square are multi‑story buildings in late 19th–early 20th century style, including a prominent white corner building with ornate gables and towers. A tall column or monument stands in the square, and a green-and-white electric tram runs along the street in the foreground. The distant background shows low hills. At the top center is printed text indicating the city and square name.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a three-story building labeled "Bahnhôtel Bärenstein" with several people standing in front, including men in uniforms, women in dresses, a person with a bicycle, and a horse-drawn cart. Trees, a fence, and a hilly wooded background suggest a rural or small-town railway-hotel setting in the Ore Mountains.

A vintage black‑and‑white photograph of a historic stone courtyard framed by colonnades and arcades. At the center is a large, ancient-looking façade with a pediment and an arched niche, flanked by columns and smaller decorative arches. Steps lead up from the open square in the foreground, and several people in early‑20th‑century clothing walk or stand around the area. Tall buildings with shuttered windows and balconies line the right side, creating an enclosed urban square.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a small railway station or house-like station building in front of a forested hill or mountain. A short train with freight or passenger cars stands on the tracks beside the building. Evergreen trees line the base of the mountain behind. The caption "TABERG." is printed at the bottom left of the image, and there is handwritten cursive text in a Scandinavian language along the right margin and at the top edge.

Black-and-white postcard view of a large brick institutional complex with multiple connected buildings in a simple historicist style. The structures are three to four stories high with steep tiled roofs, chimneys, and arched windows. In the foreground is an open courtyard or parade ground; a small group of uniformed people, likely soldiers or cadets, stand in formation near one entrance. The overall scene suggests a barracks, military academy, or similar government facility. There is no visible printed caption or handwriting on the image side.

A monochrome illustrated street scene labeled at the top. The drawing shows a chaotic event on a town street: people are falling, tumbling, or being blown about, with houses lining the street to the left and trees along the right. The style is humorous or caricature-like. At the top there is handwritten-style text reading "MARSTAL MØLLEVEJ. ANNO 1909."

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a rocky coastal bay with calm water and low, barren islands or skerries. In the foreground are rocks and shoreline; in the water a small rowboat with several people and a distant sailboat can be seen. Simple printed captions appear in the otherwise empty sky area of the image.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a traditional European café or wine tavern. The room is filled with small round and square tables covered with white tablecloths, each with simple chairs and small flower vases. At the far end is a bar counter with shelves of bottles and glasses behind it, and a chandelier hanging from the ceiling. The walls are lined with coat hooks, framed pictures, and decorative plates. At the bottom of the image there is a caption identifying the place as Café Glück and referring to the Meißner Ratsweinprobierstube.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a large three‑storey wooden institutional building on a gentle grassy hill, with trees in the background. The architecture looks early‑20th‑century Scandinavian. Printed text appears along the bottom left and right edges indicating the place name and the photographer/publisher.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large grand hotel complex with multiple wings, turreted corner towers, and numerous balconies, set above terraced gardens and trees. The building has early‑20th‑century architecture and dominates the scene. At the bottom of the image, printed text identifies the place as 'Weltbad Karlsbad. Hotel Imperial'.

A black-and-white postcard view of a rural village road leading uphill toward a church with a tall bell tower on the right, and traditional farmhouses on the left. Stone walls and wooden fences line the unpaved road. At the bottom margin, printed text reads "Chiesa di ANDALO m. 1042" indicating the church of Andalo at 1042 meters above sea level.

A vintage postcard mounted in an album showing the facade of the Kursaal Hotel d'Italia with a balcony and entrance, and printed text advertising the hotel and restaurant. There is also a small portrait medallion of a man with German text indicating he stayed there in 1888–1890. Below on the album page is a separate photograph of a rustic building and telegraph poles in a hilly landscape labeled 'Ruta'. Handwritten notes in French mention Ruta near Portofino on the Italian Riviera.

Color postcard with a white border and a central photograph showing a lively European city square with outdoor cafés, red parasols, historic brick and gabled buildings on the left, more modern buildings on the right, and pedestrians walking across the cobbled plaza. In the background is a tower with a green dome. The bottom of the postcard bears a caption in a script font.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a central market square with several multi‑storey historic buildings. Dominating the right side is a large town hall with a steep tiled roof, dormer windows, and an ornate clock tower topped by a lantern. Smaller bourgeois houses line the left side of the square. A few people are walking across the open plaza. Red printed text at the top reads the place name and subject; the façade of the town hall bears the word "STADTHAUS".

A colorized historic street scene labeled "Karlsbad Marktplatz," depicting a bustling marketplace in a European spa town. The view shows ornate multi‑story buildings, shop awnings, horse‑drawn carriages, and pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing. In the foreground is a sculpted monument or fountain with statues, and behind it hills rise with villas and a towered building. The right margin contains the printer's imprint and the lower right corner notes that it is a hand-colored artist postcard.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large three-story barracks complex with mansard roofs and multiple dormer windows, behind a brick wall and iron fence along a street lined with trees. The printed caption at the top reads "Grimma i. Sa. Husaren-Kaserne". The style and printing suggest an early 20th‑century military facility.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a distant panoramic view of a town built on the slope of a hill, with many small houses clustered together. In the foreground there is a straight tree-lined road or path leading toward the town. The lower margin contains printed captions in Greek and French identifying the place as Levadia in Greece and the view as the city entrance. There are two Greek postage stamps affixed at the upper-right corner and a faint postmark. The website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears across the image.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard view of a small European village with half‑timbered houses and farm buildings, surrounded by trees and gardens. A church with a tall steeple dominates the left side on slightly higher ground. At the bottom margin there is a handwritten-style caption.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a tranquil rural scene with dense trees around a small pond or river. On the far bank stand two red wooden buildings with sloping roofs, partly hidden by foliage. The still water reflects the trees and buildings. At the top of the image there is a printed caption in a reddish font.

A vintage black‑and‑white photograph of a small steamship or passenger ferry sailing on calm water with forested shores in the background. The vessel has multiple decks, circular life buoys along the sides, and a central smokestack emitting a faint plume. At the bottom edge, an embossed mark indicates a Stockholm connection.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large villa with a steep tiled tower roof and balconies on the left, overlooking fenced gardens, open fields, and a small village in the distance bordered by forest. The scene evokes a rural summer retreat near a wooded landscape. At the top, printed in German, is the caption identifying the place as Lausa‑Weixdorf near Dresden.

Old sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi‑storey brick building with many windows, arched main entrance and modest decorative gables. Leafless trees stand in front on an open lawn. The caption above the photo reads "Birkenruh." on the left and "Wenden." on the right. Along the left edge in small type is a photographer/printer line in German.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard depicting a large classical triumphal arch standing on a dirt road, with several uniformed men and townspeople nearby. Low, one‑ and two‑story buildings with hipped roofs line the right side, suggesting a small Russian townscape. Printed text in Russian and French/Latin letters appears in the upper left corner identifying the view as an Omsk city gate associated with the fortress.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing an elevated view of a European town market square with cobblestone streets and rows of 2–3 story gabled houses and shops. A broad, curving street runs through the foreground with awnings over storefronts. In the background, larger buildings and a hilltop complex are visible. Printed caption text at the top right reads "Nossen i. Sa. — Markt". On one corner building a sign reads "Bäckerei & ...", indicating a bakery.

Black-and-white landscape view of a small village nestled in a valley surrounded by dense forested hills. The foreground shows scattered houses, barns, and farm buildings with pitched roofs, arranged along a narrow road. In the midground there is open pastureland with rows of trees and a few larger buildings, one resembling a church or chapel. The background is dominated by continuous evergreen-covered hills under a cloudy sky. Printed caption text appears at the bottom of the image.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing an ornate Baroque building with domes and statues, viewed from a sloping street and stairway in the foreground. The printed caption identifies it as a mausoleum and greets from the city of Graz. Publisher information appears at the bottom.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a large historic complex enclosing an open courtyard. The buildings have steep gabled roofs, decorative façades and dormer windows in a Renaissance/Baroque style. A central gateway arch is visible in the middle building, with a leafless tree dominating the courtyard. On the right stands a clock tower with a domed top and spire. At the lower left of the image, white cursive German text identifies the location as a riding and driving school in Wermsdorf.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing an elevated panoramic view of a town surrounded by hills and cultivated fields. Dense blocks of stone buildings with tiled roofs fill the foreground and middle ground, while the rural landscape stretches into the distance. Printed caption text appears at the bottom margin, along with a small reference number and publisher name, characteristic of early 20th‑century postcards.

A black‑and‑white photograph of a busy industrial harbor with a large cargo ship in the foreground. The ship has two funnels and multiple masts, with smoke rising from its stacks, and is moored alongside heavy quayside cranes and port structures. Smaller boats move across the choppy water in front of it. The name "GINNHEIM" is visible on the bow of the main vessel, with another word starting with "A" near the bow, likely the shipping line or home port. The atmosphere and vessels suggest a mid‑20th‑century European port scene.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a grand riverside building labeled as Café Kaiserpark, nestled in a forested valley. The structure features large arched windows in a long pavilion-like section with ornate domes along the roofline, attached to a taller, turreted historicist villa behind it. Trees frame the scene in the foreground and a river runs along the right side of the building. Printed title text appears in the upper right corner.

Vintage black-and-white postcard showing a large, symmetrical institutional building with a central pedimented section and two long side wings. The foreground features a landscaped garden or park with small trees and paths. The text in red at the top identifies the location as Kamenz in Saxony and names the building as a Barmherzigkeits-Stift (charitable foundation). Additional text is inscribed on the façade above the central entrance.

Sepia-toned postcard view of a large early-20th‑century brick school building labeled "Realgymnasium," fronted by trees and smaller residential houses, all reflected in a calm body of water in the foreground. The scene is tranquil, with no visible people or vehicles, and the text identifying the location appears at the top.

A sepia-toned studio portrait of a young man with wavy hair and a small mustache, dressed formally in a dark suit, white shirt, and white bow tie. The lower part of his torso fades into the light background in a classic cabinet-card or postcard style. Beneath the portrait is printed text with his name and an additional word in parentheses.

An old monochrome postcard-style photograph depicting the ruins of a large stone castle on a low hill by a river or lake. The walls are partially collapsed, with several tall sections of masonry still standing. In the foreground, three men in early 20th‑century clothing stand by and in a small rowboat among rocks in the shallow water. The scene has a calm, reflective surface of water, and the overall image has a greenish tint typical of vintage postcards. In the upper left corner there is printed text identifying the view.

Black‑and‑white vintage street view of a small European town. A gently curving road leads uphill between stone and half‑timbered houses with tiled roofs. A man with a cane walks in the foreground, while a horse‑drawn cart and several people stand further up the street. On the hillside above the houses are trees, the tower and spire of a church with a cross on top, and, slightly behind, the crenellated ruins of a medieval castle. The edges of the image show damage or unexposed film, suggesting an old photographic postcard or plate.

A black‑and‑white photograph of a narrow, old town street with traditional two‑storey houses with overhanging wooden upper floors and tiled roofs. The street is muddy with puddles. A solitary person in dark clothing walks in the foreground. In the background stands a square clock tower with a small cupola on top. At the bottom of the image there is a printed website address indicating archival origin.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a river spanned by a multi‑arched stone bridge, with several people standing by the riverbank. On the far side stands a complex of masonry buildings including a tower with a lantern-like top, smaller adjoining houses, and trees. In the lower margin, printed text labels the scene, and there is cursive handwriting across the bottom.

Monochrome/yellow-tinted image bordered in yellow, showing a broad tree-lined avenue leading to a large stone gatehouse or city gate with an arched passageway. The building has a row of small square windows above the arch and decorative stonework around the central portal. Several pedestrians are visible near the gate; one person stands closer to the camera on the right side of the road. The scene suggests an old fortified entrance to a town or park, photographed in an early-20th‑century style. No visible caption or writing appears on the front.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a circular fountain with a central jet of water in a landscaped park or promenade. The fountain is bordered by a low crisscross wooden fence and surrounded by gravel paths and dense trees. A small group of people can be seen sitting or standing on benches in the background. At the top of the image is a printed caption in German.

An illustrated postcard showing a large hilltop complex of castle‑like buildings with multiple towers and terraced structures rising above dense green trees. The structure stands on a rocky outcrop overlooking a body of water, with mountains and a small settlement visible in the distant background. The style is soft, in muted pastel colors, resembling an early‑20th‑century drawing or watercolor.

Black‑and‑white landscape view of a grassy meadow leading up to a row of large, ornate villas at the edge of a forested hillside. The architecture is early‑20th‑century Central European, with steep, complex roofs, balconies, bay windows, and window shutters. One villa, on the right, has signage on its facade and striped window awnings, suggesting it may be a guesthouse or pension. A narrow path or road runs along the base of the houses. The whole scene has a calm, rural, small‑spa‑town atmosphere.

A colorized illustrated view of a landscaped park with winding paths, lawns, trees, and a pond in the foreground. A woman in period clothing walks along a path. In the background stands a castellated building or tower on a hill, and a few smaller buildings among trees. At the top of the image, printed in red capital letters, is the caption identifying the location as Nijmegen's Hunnerpark.

Colorized historic postcard view of a grand town hall with a tall clock tower topped by an ornate dome and smaller domes, red tiled roofs, and a façade with many windows and decorative gables. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk in the square in front of the building. The printed text identifies the town and the building, and there is a red handwritten note along the right side.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a view through an arched colonnade into a large open courtyard dominated by a tall, square minaret tower with multiple tiers and small windows. Surrounding the courtyard are arcaded walls of a mosque complex. The caption in French at the bottom identifies the scene as the minaret of the Great Mosque in Kairouan.

A hand‑colored historic postcard showing a broad market square lined with two‑ and three‑story traditional buildings with red tiled roofs. Prominent signage includes the 'Hotel zur Tanne' with an entrance arch labeled 'Hall Saal' and another shop labeled 'Gustav Müller'. A few people in early 20th‑century dress stand near the hotel entrance. The foreground is an open cobbled or dirt square. Printed text at the bottom identifies the scene as the market of Neustadt i. S., and credits the publisher Brück & Sohn, Meissen, with an additional note that this is a hand‑colored artist card.

Black-and-white panoramic view over a densely built town with many low houses and a few larger buildings on gently rolling hills. A mostly dry riverbed or stream curves through the left foreground with trees along its banks. The town extends into the distance. Along the lower edge of the image there is printed text in Greek and French, and a web address watermark appears in the bottom right.

A vintage, black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard. The large upper image shows a forest holiday house with a steep tiled roof, surrounded by thin pine trees; several women and a child stand in front. The lower left image shows a group of well‑dressed people standing on a narrow bridge or plank over a pond in a forest. The lower right image shows a quiet forest pond bordered by trees. German captions identify the holiday house of the city of Görlitz in Rauscha and views from the Görlitzer Heide at Ziebelteich.

Black‑and‑white historic postcard showing a large statue of a female allegorical figure (Germania) holding a laurel wreath and sword on a tall pedestal decorated with griffins and coats of arms. The monument stands in a paved urban square surrounded by ornate iron railings, with late‑19th‑century buildings in the background and several people in period clothing in the foreground. The caption and publisher information are printed along the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white view over a European town with a large hilltop castle complex dominating the scene. The fortress has multiple tall, narrow towers with steep gabled roofs and many small windows, surrounded by stone walls and terraced gardens. Below the castle are several 2–3‑story houses with pitched roofs, trees, and cultivated plots, giving a semi‑rural feel. The architecture suggests a historic Germanic castle overlooking a small town.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a riverside industrial yard with moored wooden boats in the foreground and stacks of timber along the shore. A small factory with two tall smoking chimneys stands near the water; on its wall appears German writing. Behind it rises a large baroque or early modern palace-like complex on a hill, with a tall central tower and spire and a long façade of many identical windows. Trees and smaller houses fill the middle ground.

Vintage postcard back with multilingual heading 'Postkarte – Carte postale' and equivalents in many European languages, printed in red. At the upper right there is a red Spanish postage stamp marked 'ESPAÑA' with a value of 10 céntimos, cancelled with a circular postmark. The address is handwritten in blue ink and directed to 'Sr Don Benito Pérez Galdós, Palacio "San Quintín", Santander'. The card has dotted red guide lines for writing.

A black‑and‑white postcard view over a forested mountain valley with a clustered spa village of multi‑story houses and villas. A church or clock‑tower is visible on the left, and scattered buildings sit on the surrounding hillsides. Dense coniferous woods cover most slopes, with some open meadows higher up. The caption in German runs along the bottom white border.

A color illustration of a uniformed officer on horseback, viewed in profile, wearing a white tunic with gold epaulettes and decorations, dark riding boots, and blue trousers with red stripes. The horse is draped with a richly embroidered red and gold saddle blanket bearing an order-like insignia. Several similarly uniformed officers on horseback stand in the background against a hazy tree line. The image has the texture and wear typical of an early 20th‑century printed postcard. No visible text is present on the front.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a formal military ceremony in front of neoclassical buildings. Long rows of uniformed soldiers wearing helmets stand in formation in a courtyard. Civilians and officers observe near the entrance gate. The architecture has arched windows and a central stairway leading into a prominent building. Greek text is printed beneath the image, and there is a vertical caption along the left side listing an edition and photographer.

An old black-and-white postcard view of a forested river valley with steep rocky cliffs on the left and a winding river and road below. A few buildings lie near the river at the bottom right. The style looks early 20th century. Printed German text at the top identifies the scene as Hockstein and the Polenztal valley in Saxon Switzerland.

Black‑and‑white view from a wooded hillside path with tall trees and a seated woman in early 20th‑century clothing on a bench in the left foreground. Through the trees on the right, a spa town with large multi‑storey buildings and scattered houses is visible in a valley. Red printed German text appears in the upper right corner.

Sepia-toned postcard depicting a rural farm scene with a wooden house partly obscured by trees, a picket fence and open gate in the foreground, and wooden farm structures or pens to the right. The style is early-photographic with printed captions in Swedish at the bottom margin.

Tinted historical postcard showing a large red‑brick institutional building with decorative yellow gable trim and a tall chimney on the right. In front of the building is an open yard with leafless trees and many children and a few adults, some in aprons or uniforms, standing or playing. At the bottom is a printed caption in red.

Black-and-white image showing a brick civic-style building with a steep, slate-like roof and a flagpole flying a light-colored flag with a darker edge or band. The façade has arched windows, decorative stonework, and a small balcony. In front of the building is a narrow river or canal with landscaped banks, and a small road bridge crossing it. A horse-drawn carriage and a cyclist are on the bridge. Dense trees and foliage surround the scene, giving it a park-like setting.

Vintage black-and-white postcard showing a long, three-story barracks-type building with a gabled roof and many evenly spaced windows. A small group of people stands on the sidewalk and street in front, near young trees and a low fence. The printed caption at the top in Hungarian identifies the city as Kolozsvár and describes the building as a royal common barracks.

Black‑and‑white view over a small spa or resort town nestled in a forested valley in the mountains. In the foreground there is a wooden bench by a tree beside a hillside path, overlooking the town below. The town consists of several large villa‑style buildings and guesthouses with steep roofs, surrounded by dense coniferous forest. A prominent church with a tall square tower and spire stands slightly left of center. Hills covered with trees rise in the background, with mist softening the distant landscape. There is a small rectangular sign fixed to the tree near the bench and some handwritten numeric markings along the left border of the image, as in an old photographic or postcard print.

A simple religious greeting postcard with black text and a blue handwritten Bible verse on a cream background. In the upper left corner there is a black graphic of a Christian cross rising from an oil lamp with a small flame. The blue handwriting across the top contains a Finnish quotation from the New Testament (2 Corinthians 8:9). Below, in printed Finnish text, the card offers Christian wishes of comfort, grace, and peace to a sick friend at Christmas, invoking Jesus Christ. The sender is identified as the Oulu regional branch of the Christian Association of Finnish Nurses.

Black-and-white vintage view of a harbor with a quay in the foreground, barrels and mooring bollards along the waterfront, rail tracks by the pier, several masted sailing ships and other vessels docked, and a tall harbor crane in the background. Printed text in Swedish identifies the location.

Black‑and‑white image centered on a crowd gathered around a statue on a pedestal in front of a two‑story wooden building with many open windows. People in late‑19th/early‑20th‑century clothing stand formally on both sides of the monument, suggesting an unveiling or ceremony. The building has tall rectangular windows with decorative trim and a hilly, wooded background. There is a faint embossed mark at the lower right, likely the postcard publisher's imprint.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a long row of ornate multi‑story residential buildings along a street. The leftmost corner building has a small tower-like roof and decorative window surrounds. Several people, including women and children, stand or walk on the sidewalk in front. A streetlamp is visible in the foreground on the right, and trees frame the scene. At the top of the card, in red print, is the caption identifying the town and street.

Colored vintage view of a large, tree‑filled urban square surrounded by multi‑storey neoclassical buildings. Tram or street tracks run along the foreground, with pedestrians and carriages visible. Greek text labels the scene at the top left, and French/Latin text appears near the top center-right identifying the square. A Cyprus postage stamp valued at TEN PARAS is affixed in the upper right corner. Handwritten ink notes appear across the upper margin and lower edge.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a wooden street-front of early 20th‑century shops in a Nordic town. Two-storey timber buildings with large display windows line a cobbled or dirt street. Several people in period clothing (long skirts, waistcoats, bowler hats) stand outside. Visible shop signs read 'Iwar Lindstrand. Manufaktur‑klädes & herrekiperingsaffär' above a clothing store and 'C. E. Ramm. Bok- & pappershandel' above a bookstore/stationer. Books and printed items are displayed in the right-hand window.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a small mountain village nestled in a valley, with terraced fields and stone walls in the foreground. Several multi‑story houses line the hillside, and on the right stands a church with a tall clock tower and simple façade. Snow‑topped mountains rise in the background. At the top left in red lettering is the caption "Saluto da St. Orsola".

Monochrome vintage view of a wooded park with a rustic wooden bridge over a small pond and a round gazebo or pavilion raised on a rocky mound among tall trees. Two women in long light-colored dresses and large hats stand on the bridge, while another person sits in the gazebo. The style suggests an early-20th‑century landscaped garden scene.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over an early‑20th‑century European city. In the foreground are cultivated fields or vineyards and a solitary three‑storey house along a country road. Behind it stretch low‑rise residential blocks, gardens and small industrial buildings with several tall smokestacks. In the distance, a hilly ridge frames the city, and on the right side stands a large, ornate institutional building or palace‑like structure. The overall scene mixes farmland at the edge of town with an expanding industrial urban area.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view over a rural town in a valley, surrounded by rolling cultivated hills. In the middle‑distance there are several large institutional buildings set apart from smaller clustered houses, likely a school complex. Trees and fields dominate the landscape. At the bottom margin, white printed text in Romanian identifies the subject.

Sepia-toned photograph of a military parade in a snowy or frosty street lined with low wooden and masonry buildings in a Nordic / Baltic-looking town. Soldiers in dark uniforms and tall boots march in formation, some bearing armbands and a light-colored flag with an emblem. More uniformed men and civilians stand at attention along the side. The architecture features wooden façades with pilasters and multi-pane windows. There is handwritten text along the left margin of the card and a small sign on a building in a language using the Latin alphabet.

A black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a three‑story, rectangular villa with classical detailing, shuttered windows, and a flat roofline. The house is partially covered by climbing vines along a pergola at ground level and is set behind a low fence. Mature trees line a path or quiet street running along the front of the property. There is no visible printed caption or writing on the image itself.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a full-length statue of George Washington on a tall pedestal in a park, with foliage and an eagle sculpture at the base. At the top in red letters there is multilingual text identifying the location in Budapest and describing the Washington memorial in the city park.

Black-and-white/sepia postcard view of a European old town street leading toward a tall medieval/early‑modern city gate tower with a clock, battlements, and a high, intricate spire. At the base of the tower is an archway through which the street passes. To the left is a timber‑framed house; to the right are several multi‑story townhouses with shops and inns at street level. Painted signage on one prominent building reads "Gasthaus zum Bären". People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and stand along the cobbled street.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a large ceremonial street procession in front of an ornate Middle Eastern building with minarets. Soldiers in uniforms, officials on horseback, and crowds escort a richly decorated structure identified as the Holy Carpet. The top of the image has printed caption text, and a website watermark appears across the lower part.

Black‑and‑white view along a tree‑lined riverside promenade. On the left is a shaded footpath under dense foliage, with a low stone wall bordering the path to the right. Beyond the wall is a broad river with a low weir or rapids. On the opposite bank, on a small hill, stands a large villa or small palace with a steep tower and multiple stories, surrounded by trees and a few neighboring buildings. The overall style is early‑20th‑century European. No visible text on the image.

A vintage black‑and‑white studio portrait of a young man in a formal suit with high collar and cravat, shown from the chest up against a plain light background. The lower part of the image fades to white in typical cabinet‑card/postcard style. In the lower right corner, the printed name 'Gunnar Wingård' appears; a small number '838' is printed in the lower left.

Black-and-white postcard view of a residential neighborhood with detached wooden villas, gardens and white picket fences in the foreground, and a large church with a tall spire and clock tower in the background. Printed caption text appears in the lower left, and the photographer/publisher credit appears in the lower right.

Color image with a white border showing a wintry park scene. A woman in a long fur coat stands on a snow-covered path with a small shaggy dog beside her. Bare trees dusted with snow fill the background. On the right side, a classic upright bicycle with a front basket is parked by the low wall that borders the path. The overall mood is quiet and contemplative, with soft winter light.

A sepia-toned image showing a devastated urban street with heavily damaged and ruined buildings. Rubble and debris cover the ground, with roofless walls and chimneys still standing. On the right is a distinctive rounded modern building with many broken windows. The overall scene suggests wartime destruction. Along the bottom margin there is printed Dutch text identifying the location in Nijmegen.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a man in a long coat and hat walking on a barren, sloping ground toward imposing stone fortification walls with towers. The walls dominate the background and stretch along a ridge. Printed French captions and small publisher marks appear at the bottom margin.

Colorized vintage view of an industrial complex, identified as a cement factory, seen across open green fields. Several long, low factory buildings and tall chimneys dominate the skyline, one chimney emitting a long plume of dark smoke. On the right stands a large multi‑storey brick industrial building with multiple roof structures. Printed red text appears along the top edge in German.

Vintage black-and-white postcard showing a quiet street and a courtyard flanked by stone buildings with shuttered windows and arched doorways. In the center background is a plain façade with round and arched architectural details and a small fountain or monument in front. Printed captions identify the view as the barracks of Santa Maria Maddalena in Trento. Margins contain Italian and German text and a photographer's imprint along the left edge; there is a handwritten number near the top right.

A vintage black-and-white postcard showing a canal scene in an old European city. On the left are stepped-gable brick houses in Flemish style, with people walking along the cobbled quay. A small boat with several passengers moves along the canal toward a low stone bridge in the center of the image. Tall trees line the right-hand bank. Handwritten ink at the top shows a date, and printed text at the bottom identifies the view.

Sepia-toned vintage street scene showing a cobblestone road lined with multi‑story buildings. Pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the wet street and sidewalks. At the top center, printed caption text identifies the location as Döbeln – Johannisstrasse. On the left building a large wall sign reads "Vogler A. G." and various smaller shop signs are visible further down the street.

Black‑and‑white view of a late‑19th‑ or early‑20th‑century villa‑style building with striped masonry and steep roofs, signed as a restaurant. It sits along a wide dirt road with a low hedge and simple wooden fences in front. A few small trees line the road and two children stand near the fence. In the background a prominent, steep, flat‑topped mountain rises behind the building, with more hills stretching off to the side. The overall look is of a rural or resort restaurant set in a mountainous landscape.

A monochrome vintage postcard showing a large stone fortress with high, thick walls and a central gate tower. Ruined outer walls and cannon carriages or wagons lie in the foreground. Across the top is printed text in French describing the scene as the Yedi-Koulé fortress in Salonique.

A monochrome/sepia street view showing an old European town with multi‑story houses lining a gently rising road. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk and cycle along the street. Trees and simple railings border the sidewalk on the right. At the top in red print is the caption naming the town and street.

Colorized panoramic view of a small town with red-roofed houses nestled in a forested valley surrounded by high mountains. A prominent church with a tall bell tower and red roof stands on the right side above the town. At the top center, text labels a mountain peak as "PIZZO DI LEVICO". At the bottom right, cursive text reads "Roncegno m. 550 - Panorama". The overall style and colorization resemble a mid‑20th‑century tourist postcard.

Colorized historic postcard showing the courtyard façade of a large Renaissance-style castle with white walls, red tiled roofs, ornate stepped gables and a tall tower. Ivy covers parts of the walls and a formal entrance with a decorated portal stands in the center. Trees and a path are in the foreground. German cursive captions are printed in the lower margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a marble obelisk‑style monument behind an iron fence, with a bell tower and a rocky hill topped with fortifications in the background. The lower margin bears printed captions in Greek and French, and a modern website watermark appears at the bottom.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a broad dirt road leading up to a large, symmetrical three‑storey neoclassical barracks building. The structure has many evenly spaced windows, a central entrance with an archway, a small tower or pediment above, and a flagpole on the roof. Low fences and grassy areas line both sides of the road. Printed French text appears at the top identifying the scene as military barracks in Salonique, and a website watermark is visible at the bottom.

Vintage monochrome postcard view of a town square with a large, ornate civic building labeled as the town hall. The building has a grand arched doorway with decorative stonework, a small balcony above, shuttered windows, and a coat of arms. To the left is a narrow cobbled street lined with multi‑story houses leading toward hills in the background. Several people, including children, stand or walk in the square. Printed captions at the top identify the location as Ala in Trentino and specify that the building is the Municipio (town hall).

Black‑and‑white view across a river toward a European town with 3–4‑storey houses and a prominent large Gothic brick church with a tall, slender spire dominating the skyline. A grass meadow occupies the foreground where a uniformed man and a child stand by the water. On the left, a small boat or ferry with people aboard is near the riverbank. A stone embankment lines the opposite shore with streets and more buildings stretching into the distance. The image has the appearance of an early 20th‑century photographic postcard.

Two black‑and‑white postcard photographs mounted on a decorative album page with clover motifs. The upper postcard shows a cycle-racing track event with cyclists lined up with pacer motorbikes in front of a grandstand crowded with spectators. Advertising banners in German are visible along the track. The caption at the bottom reads in German about a prize of the city of Leipzig. The lower postcard is a promotional/commemorative card printed in German, featuring an illustration of a steep wooden ramp and bridge-like structure used for a bicycle stunt, a small portrait of a man, and handwritten script over much of the card. The printed caption at the bottom names master rider Alfred Schneider and his 'phenomenal death jump'.

Sepia-toned postcard image showing a quiet rural landscape at dusk or dawn. In the middle distance stands a tall, slender church spire with Gothic features rising above trees. In the foreground is a calm body of water with reeds along the bank, reflecting parts of the scene. A crescent moon appears in the sky on the left and a flock of birds flies across the right side. The lower left corner bears the printed artist's name: 'ALLAN BARRAUD.'

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a European town seen from an elevated, tree-framed vantage point. In the foreground are detached houses with steep tiled roofs. In the middle and background stand denser town buildings and a large church or civic building with a tall, pointed spire dominating the skyline. The scene is printed in an old photographic style typical of early 20th-century postcards. In the upper right corner the caption 'Löbau i. Sa.' is printed in a decorative script.

A multi-view color postcard showing a busy seaside resort with long sandy beaches packed with tourists, modern high-rise hotels along a forested hillside, a pier extending into a bright blue sea, small boats and a sailboat in the water, and a terrace area with conical thatched-roof huts surrounded by greenery. The title in Cyrillic script appears at the top right.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a small town in a hilly rural landscape. In the foreground are open fields; beyond them lies a cluster of traditional houses with pitched roofs. Dominating the center is a large church with a tall tower and spire. The town sits in a valley surrounded by terraced or patchwork fields climbing gentle hills. At the top left, red printed text identifies the location.

Color photograph of a dramatic rocky mountain wall rising steeply behind a conifer-covered slope. At the base of the slope is an alpine meadow with several chalet-style buildings, parked cars, and a road, suggesting a small mountain resort or pass. The sky is blue with scattered clouds. The style and colors resemble a mid‑20th‑century tourist postcard.

Black‑and‑white view down a gently curving cobblestone street in a European town. On the right is a row of ornate historic townhouses with arched windows and classical detailing; on the left, leafy trees and simpler houses. At the end of the street stands a massive, steep‑roofed medieval building that resembles part of a castle or fortress complex. There are a few streetlamps and potted plants, but no visible cars, suggesting an early 20th‑century scene.

An old Russian Empire postal card with printed red coat of arms on the left and pre-printed red postage on the upper right, heavily canceled with circular postmarks dated 6 4 05. The heading in red Cyrillic reads "ОТКРЫТОЕ ПИСЬМО" (open letter / postcard). The card is filled with handwritten script in black ink, addressed in German. At the bottom left is a purple business stamp in German giving the address of a bookseller in Riga, with additional small red printed Russian text along the bottom.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large fortified complex with round towers and high defensive walls, labeled as Castello del Buon Consiglio. The castle sits at the edge of a town with a road curving around the base of the walls, a few pedestrians in early 20th‑century dress, tall trees on the right, and mountains faintly visible in the background. Printed captions identify the site and city, and there is a handwritten signature at the bottom margin.

Black-and-white postcard photo of an alpine landscape with dramatic jagged mountains in the background, forested slopes and meadows in the midground, and a large mountain hut or lodge in the foreground behind a rustic wooden fence. The sky is partly cloudy. Along the bottom edge there is an Italian caption describing the hut and surrounding peaks.

Colorized vintage postcard view taken from a pergola terrace high on a hill, with a woman in early 20th‑century dress looking out over a city and a river with several bridges. Large stone columns and creeping vines frame the left foreground, while the right side shows a panoramic view of tightly packed buildings, church towers, and the river running through the city. There is printed red text at the top right reading "Pergola am Schlossberg Graz." and cursive handwriting over the sky area.

Black‑and‑white view of a busy European city square with tram tracks, several trams, early‑mid 20th century cars, and many pedestrians. In the center of the square stands a prominent stone pyramid monument. On the right is a long neoclassical building with arched ground‑floor arcades and the words "BADISCHE SPARKASSE" on its facade. Behind it rises a church tower. The scene is framed like a typical vintage postcard photograph.

Colored postcard illustration of a church with green roofs and onion-shaped spires, surrounded by trees and a grassy churchyard. A separate wooden bell tower with a steep, shingled roof stands to the right. In the foreground, several people in traditional folk clothing pose on the lawn. Handwritten text appears across the sky area at the top, and printed text runs vertically along the right edge.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a large corner commercial building with arcaded ground floor and red-tiled roof. Several people walk or stand near the entrances and a person with a bicycle is in front. Awnings shade the shopfronts. At the top of the image, printed in red, is a caption identifying the location and the firm housed in the building.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large, ornate villa called 'Villa Bergfried' set on a hillside surrounded by dense forest and a meadow in the foreground. The multi‑storey building has steep roofs, gables, balconies and decorative wooden elements, with a few people visible walking or standing near the fence and in the meadow. Printed German text in red appears at the top describing the villa and its location in the Ore Mountains.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a large three-story masonry school building with many tall windows and a central entrance risalit. The façade bears a small pediment and decorative clock or emblem. In front, a street runs along the building with a railing and some trees; a woman pushes a small child in a stroller and a few children stand nearby. At the top of the card is printed German text identifying the location as Geyer in the Erzgebirge region and specifying that the building is a Bürgerschule (civic school).

Colorized view from a path on a hillside looking toward a historic walled city with many trees in the foreground. Several medieval stone towers with red roofs and a tall church spire dominate the skyline, together with a round tower complex and a domed church with an onion-shaped cupola. The sky is lightly clouded with a soft gradient from pink near the horizon to blue above. No printed text is visible on the image side.

A vintage postcard featuring a full‑length illustration of a rural man in traditional winter peasant costume. He wears a fur‑trimmed coat, hat, boots, and carries a walking stick and a bag. Below the figure there is printed bilingual text in Russian and German identifying the costume as Oesel peasant dress ('Oeselsche Bauertrachten – Wolde'). The left margin has a vertical printer's credit, and the lower part contains handwritten greetings and a date.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a round stone tower with a conical dark-green roof, attached to a larger castle-like building with red tiled roofs. In the foreground there is a cobblestone courtyard bordered by lush greenery and trees, with a lamppost and garden beds along a low wall. An arched passageway leads through the building on the right. The caption text at the top reads "Wurzen" on the left and "Partie am Schloß" on the right.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a wooden truss bridge over a river with a person and child standing by the water in the foreground. On the hill behind the bridge stands a tall church with a prominent spire surrounded by trees. Dark, dramatic storm clouds fill the sky. The caption in the lower left corner reads "GAUJ IENA Pirms nega i sa" (with some letters slightly unclear), printed directly on the image.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing an elevated railway station with a train arriving on tracks below. People stand on the platform near the train. Above the tracks is a covered station building spanning the line. Greek handwriting is visible at the top, and printed Greek text appears at the bottom along with a website watermark.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a tree‑lined street with large chestnut trees and a straight avenue stretching into the distance. At the entrance of the street stand two stone gate pillars crowned with sculptures, flanking the roadway. On the right is a villa or mansion with a square tower and ornate roof details behind a wooden fence. A single person stands in the middle of the street. The caption is printed at the top in red text.

Colorized panoramic view over a small town in a hilly, forested landscape. The town has many villas and buildings with red and grey roofs, a prominent church with a tall spire, and lush green trees in the foreground. Printed in red at the top left is the German phrase "Blick auf Bad Elster." The style appears to be that of an early 20th‑century tourist postcard.

A monochrome printed postcard showing a three‑story masonry building identified as the Masonic Temple in Lewiston, Idaho. The structure has arched entrances at street level, upper-story windows, and a balcony. A sign reading "THEATRE" stands on the left, and large trees line the street. Handwritten notes appear at the top and lower right of the image. Printed caption text in red at the bottom credits Henry Fair of Lewiston, Idaho, with a 1905 copyright.

Black‑and‑white image showing a monumental statue of a seated man with crossed legs on a high pedestal, holding a sword. Around the base are sculpted objects such as a large dog seated alertly at the front corner and various military or travel gear (helmet, bags, rope) on the right. The monument stands on a stepped stone plinth, surrounded by an ornate metal fence with spear‑shaped finials. Tall conifer trees fill the background, and the whole scene has the look of an early 20th‑century photograph reproduced as a postcard.

A colorized vintage panoramic view of a town at the foot of a large mountain. The settlement is filled with low traditional houses, several mosque minarets, and domed roofs scattered among trees. At the top left, the caption reads "Salut de Brousse" and at the bottom right there is a printed website watermark "www.elia.org.gr".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large villa named "Waldidylle" in a rural forested setting near Oberbärenburg. The image features a fenced property with a multi‑storey house with balconies on the right and another smaller building on the left, surrounded by tall conifer trees and a dirt path in the foreground. German text is printed in red at the top and bottom of the card.

A monochrome postcard showing a side view of a steam freight locomotive on railway tracks. The locomotive is detailed, with visible wheels, rods, boiler, cab, and tender. At the top of the card there is German text describing the locomotive and its builder, and the locomotive number plate 5446 is visible on the front side.

Vintage sepia postcard view of a wooded valley town. In the foreground stands a large, ornate multi‑storey institutional building. On the wooded hillside above, to the right, is a church with a tall tower and spire. Hills rise in the background. The top caption reads "Tharandt. Forstakademie und Kirche." and the bottom margin credits the publisher "Brück & Sohn, Meissen" along with the number 4515.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a large corner building in an urban street. The structure has a steep tiled roof with dormer windows, tall vertical windows on a prominent hall wing, and a small dome-like tower. Young trees line the sidewalk and a low stone and metal fence surrounds the property. At the corner a street sign is visible, and above the tall windows on the gable end there is German text on the façade indicating the institution housed in the building.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a rocky outcrop in a forest with a long wooden staircase and railings leading to a viewing platform on top of the rock. Tall pine trees surround the formation. Printed captions in German appear at the bottom, including a greeting from Bad Landeck and the name of the rock, Achillesfelsen.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a wide dirt road leading toward a complex of low buildings with East Asian architectural features (curved tiled roofs and gate structures). A flagpole with a flag stands in front of the central building. Other smaller structures and a tree are visible in the background. Printed caption text in Cyrillic and Latin script appears at the top left.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard-style view of a European city street with tram tracks, pedestrians, horse-drawn vehicles, and ornate multi‑story stone buildings on both sides. In the foreground is a canal with a small arched bridge and moored boats. The scene looks like an early 20th‑century urban streetscape. Printed text at the top right reads "Göteborg, Västra Hamngatan."

Black-and-white vintage postcard showing a harbor scene on a river. Several long barges or riverboats with tall masts are moored along the bank, with people visible working on the boats. In the background there is a tree-lined shore and a prominent multi‑storey house or inn on the right. The printed caption at the top reads "Mühlberg (Elbe) – Hafen," indicating this is the harbor of Mühlberg on the Elbe River.

Hand‑tinted postcard scene of a calm river crossed by two long, low ferries with soldiers and sailors on board. The men wear early 20th‑century German military uniforms and white naval-style clothing. Simple masts and cables suggest a cable or flying ferry construction. Low, flat countryside with a few houses is visible on the opposite bank under a pastel orange-and-blue sky. Printed German text appears at the top and lower right of the image.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing two children sitting with their backs to the viewer on a small stone landing by a pond or lake. Across the water is a townscape with a prominent tall church with a spire and another towered building, all reflected clearly in the still water. Trees line the far shore. Printed German text at the top identifies the location.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a large decorative stone archway forming the entrance to a passage between buildings. The arch is richly ornamented with sculpted figures, motifs of horse heads along the curve, and round medallions with animal reliefs. Above the archway the number "16–22" is inscribed. People are visible walking through the passage behind the arch. Printed captions identify the location as "Hippodromen" and the city as Malmö, with handwritten message text along the right side.

Vintage illustrated postcard cover showing a riverside cityscape labeled LYON. In the center is a colored drawing of a bridge over a river with quays, a large church or cathedral on the right bank, and a hill in the background topped by a basilica and a metal tower. Decorative floral motifs frame the image, and large ornate lettering at the top spells 'LYON'. French text at the bottom mentions 'Édition Artistique E.R.' and 'cartes détachables'.

Black-and-white postcard view of a large, light-colored house or guesthouse with a hipped roof and twin chimneys, surrounded by trees and a white fence. In the foreground is a cultivated field or garden; in the background are wooded hills or low mountains. Printed caption text appears at the bottom left and the photographer credit at the bottom right.

Monochrome, printed postcard-style image of a historic European street with tram tracks curving in the cobblestone road in the foreground. On the left stands a long Renaissance/early Baroque brick building with ornate stone window frames, numerous statues in niches above the windows, and circular medallions along the roofline. A high stone base supports the façade. Several pedestrians in early‑20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalk near a prominent arched entrance with steps and a small canopy. Adjacent, narrower houses continue the streetscape; distant spires are visible in the background.

Black‑and‑white printed postcard showing an old cemetery with many upright gravestones and tall, mostly leafless trees, likely cypresses and pruned deciduous trees. In the background are low hills and scattered buildings. The lower margin contains printed captions including a publisher credit and the title indicating it is the Muslim cemetery of Salonique (Thessaloniki).

Sepia-toned photographic postcard showing a woman seated in an ornate armchair by a tiled fireplace in an elegant, richly decorated room. She is reading a book and has a shawl over her lap. Decorative objects such as candlesticks, a clock or figurine, and patterned wallpaper and carpets are visible. At the bottom of the postcard is printed German text identifying her as Henny Porten and indicating the scene is in her home.

A color view of a seaside quay with a red-brick hotel or commercial building to the left, outdoor café tables along the waterfront, and a row of parked 1950s-era cars on the right. Several flagpoles stand near the center flying the Swedish flag, the United States flag, and at least one other flag. In the background are boats, a small harbor, and low rocky islands or coastline under a clear blue sky.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a seafront promenade with traditional multi-story stone houses built along fortified walls descending to the water. A narrow coastal road follows the shoreline, and steps and ramps lead from the town down toward the sea. The architecture is typical of older Greek island settlements. Greek text captions appear below the image, along with a publisher's imprint and a watermark from an archive website.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a meadow path leading into a dense coniferous forest. A girl in a light dress and hat sits beside the path in the foreground. In the distance, above the treeline, a stone observation tower rises. The upper margin has printed German text and red handwritten annotations and numbers.

Color postcard view of a large Gothic church with two tall, ornate towers and a central façade facing an open cobblestone square. The church has pointed spires, intricate stone tracery, and a smaller red-roofed structure projecting from the middle of the front. Mature trees partly obscure the lower section. To the sides are historic multi‑story buildings with steep roofs and dormer windows. A few vintage cars and several pedestrians are visible, suggesting a mid‑20th‑century scene under a clear blue sky.

Vintage sepia postcard with two photographic panels. The left panel shows the damaged interior of a Catholic church: partially collapsed masonry, gothic altar and crucifix, and rubble on the floor with a person standing among the ruins. The right panel shows a town market square with tents and townspeople, and a damaged church visible in the background. Polish captions and title are printed in red around and below the images.

A sepia-toned street scene in a European city, showing a narrow cobblestone street lined with multi‑story buildings full of shop signs. Numerous pedestrians and a few bicycles occupy the street. In the background rises a tall neo‑Gothic church tower with pointed arches and a spire. At the lower right corner there is a small heraldic shield featuring a double‑headed eagle.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view showing a tall, rectangular medieval tower with crenellations (Torre Vanga) beside a canal or old riverbed. People walk and ride in a lightly trafficked dirt road in the foreground, with trees, mountains, and a townscape in the background. A caption in Italian is printed at the bottom margin.

A black‑and‑white aerial photograph of a small, low‑density residential settlement surrounded by fields and forest. The landscape shows detached one‑and‑a‑half‑story wooden houses with steep gabled roofs, each on its own rectangular plot, many with visible vegetable gardens and small outbuildings. Narrow unpaved or lightly paved roads wind through the neighborhood; beyond the houses lie open farmland and dense tree stands. The overall scene suggests a quiet rural or early‑suburban European village in the mid‑20th century.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a two‑storey wooden railway station building beside several train tracks, surrounded by trees. A few people stand on the platform. The architecture is typical early 20th‑century Scandinavian style, and printed text at the top left identifies the station.
