The scene has an early‑20th‑century feel and resembles a typical central‑European historic riverside city.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a coastal view with several small boats in a bay, a long wooden or metal pier extending out over the water, and a small islet in the distance. In the foreground there is a house and some vegetation. The printed captions at the bottom identify the scene as Praia in Cabo Verde and specifically the Ilheu de Santa Maria and a disembarkation bridge.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a herd of wild boars being fed in an open enclosure bordered by trees and a wooden fence. In the background, many well‑dressed people in late‑19th or early‑20th‑century clothing stand behind the fence watching. The lower part of the card is left blank for writing, with printed German captions in red script.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large hilltop castle complex with a tall church-like tower rising above a clustered village in a forested valley. The buildings have steep, tiled roofs and Baroque-style architecture. A road curves along the right side of the image. At the top, in red script, is the caption 'Schloss Weesenstein.' Additional small printer's text appears along the left edge. The lower margin is blank and slightly stained, typical of early 20th‑century postcards.

Black‑and‑white landscape view of a rural village set in a forested valley. A dirt road curves through the foreground with two children standing at the roadside. On the left and center are several timber‑framed houses and farm buildings behind wooden picket fences, with laundry hanging in a yard. Densely wooded hills rise in the background. The image has the composition and border style typical of an early 20th‑century picture postcard. No printed caption or handwriting is visible on the image side.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small park with birch trees, a pond with children playing at the water's edge, and adults sitting on benches. In the background stands a multi‑storey residential building with a tiled roof and awnings. The scene feels calm and suburban. Printed caption text appears along the bottom margin, and a photographer/publisher mark is on the right.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a Swedish Saab J35D "Draken" jet fighter landing or taking off with its drag parachute deployed. The aircraft bears the number 23 on the tail and Swedish roundels on the fuselage. Below the photo there is a white margin with Swedish text giving technical data for the J35D, the crest and wings emblem of the Swedish Air Force, and text identifying the unit Kungl Östgöta Flygflottilj F3 at Malmslätt.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large guesthouse or sanatorium-style building in a forested valley. In the foreground there is a path with a simple railing following a small stream, and a narrow bridge leading to the building. The structure has a tiled roof, timber-framed gable, and several trees and benches in front. Printed German text at the top identifies the place as Bärenfels in the Saxon Ore Mountains and names the establishment "Erholungsheim 'Waldwiese'". A small sign near the bridge also refers to the Erholungsheim.

Sepia-toned vintage view of a large cobblestone town square with people walking and cycling. A long, low market building stands in the center, flanked by historic gabled houses and a taller, more ornate building with a tower-like top in the background. The caption at the top reads "Store Torv. Rønne".

Colorized view from a tree‑lined country road looking toward a small town with red‑roofed houses, factory chimneys, and a prominent church steeple and tower in the distance. A person with a suitcase stands by the roadside in the foreground. The caption in red German text at the top reads "Blick auf Geringswalde."

Colorized vintage postcard showing a large medieval cathedral with a rose window and a tall bell tower with an onion-shaped dome, facing a square with an ornate baroque fountain in the center. Several people in early 20th‑century clothing stand near the fountain. On the right side there is a white vertical panel containing handwritten cursive text, and printed at the top are the words identifying the location.

A black‑and‑white portrait of a young woman and man standing outdoors in front of large leafy plants. The woman wears an ornate traditional folk costume with embroidered apron, blouse, vest, beads, and a large hat. The man wears a light-colored suit with matching trousers and dark shoes. Printed text in Swedish appears at the top of the image.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a partly collapsed stone gateway or arch standing alone in a rough, grassy landscape. The structure is a substantial ruin with large rectangular blocks and an arched opening, identified in the caption as the gate of the Temple of Lysimachus at Ephesus. There is printed text along the bottom margin in French and a small circular stamp-like mark and website watermark.

Sepia-toned panoramic view over a lake with a small island and a town on the opposite shore, seen from an elevated vantage point with rooftops and fences in the foreground. Forested hills rise behind the town. The caption "Bengtsfors från Majberget" is printed at the top left on a plain margin, with no other design elements visible.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a stone bench and wall structure called the 'Zillerbank' along a wooded path in a valley. A woman in early 20th‑century dress and hat stands in front of the curved stone bench, which is built into a hillside and features a central plaque and small gabled top. Bare trees cover the sloping forest behind. Printed captions in German identify the location as Kötzschenbroda–Lößnitzgrund and name the bench Zillerbank, with a publisher credit at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white postcard view from a forested hillside over a valley densely covered with coniferous trees. A winding road and a few buildings are visible in the clearing below. The printed caption along the bottom margin reads in German, indicating the view from Hochechek towards Waldbärenburg in the Eastern Ore Mountains.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style street scene showing a European city intersection with late‑19th‑century multi‑storey buildings. On the left is a corner building with the sign "H. Mehlhose" at street level and an obelisk-like monument in front, bordered by chains. On the right is another ornate corner building with a small tower; shop signs at the ground level include "Drogerie Germania" and a hotel or inn. Cobblestone streets, a few adults, a uniformed man, and several children in period clothing occupy the open square. A gas streetlamp stands on the right foreground.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a landscaped public garden with paths, hedges, and neatly trimmed trees. In the foreground is an ornate metal fence and gate; just inside stands a gardener holding a tool. Behind him are greenhouses and a small house with a steep tiled roof and flower boxes. On the wooded hill in the background stand large, decorative villas or mansions and, on the skyline, a slender lattice observation tower reminiscent of early 20th‑century European iron towers.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a calm coastal landscape with rocky shoreline in the foreground, still sea water, and a sloping mountain or hill to the right. Small buildings and trees line the distant shore. The image has a printed caption near the bottom left and a vertical credit line along the left edge.

Black-and-white postcard showing a rural scene with a large country house partly covered by trees, a fenced garden or entrance in the foreground, and the spire of a church visible behind the trees. The building has shuttered windows and a steep roof. Printed caption text appears beneath the photo area.

Sepia-toned postcard image showing a tall baroque church tower with an onion-shaped dome and cross, a clock on the tower, and an adjacent slender obelisk-like monument in a small fenced square. Surrounding it are 2–3 story historic buildings lining a narrow street. The style suggests a Central or Eastern European town square.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a long, grand neoclassical building on a wide street, with bare trees lining the sidewalk and a horse‑drawn carriage at the far left. The façade has arched windows on the ground floor, rectangular windows above, and a central section with large columns and sculptural figures on the pediment. There is a narrow decorative border around the photograph and handwritten cursive text along the right margin, dated 1904.

A colorized vintage postcard depicting a small neo-Gothic chapel-like structure on a sloping cobblestone street flanked by high walls and trees. The building has pointed arches, decorative pinnacles, and a steep spire with a cross on top. Below, the street descends toward a brighter open area in the distance. Printed captions in red at the bottom read the location and name of the site.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a stone hilltop castle complex with towers and walls (Schloss Tersatto) overlooking a rocky landscape and a distant coastal town. At the bottom is printed German text identifying the view and there is handwritten cursive text and a date on the left.

Black‑and‑white vintage view of a manor house surrounded by trees and landscaped gardens, seen from across a small pond with a narrow path and simple wooden footbridge in the foreground. The building has a classical appearance with a mansard roof and ornamented façade. At the bottom margin there is printed caption text in Dutch identifying the scene.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a riverside scene. In the foreground, three people sit in a wooden boat on a calm river with other small boats nearby. On the opposite bank rises a large Renaissance-style castle complex with white walls, red roofs, and a tall tower. To the right, a metal bridge spans the river. Trees and a gently sloping embankment frame the scene. Printed German text at the top reads "Torgau." on the left and "Blick von der Elbe." on the right, with a handwritten red number above.

Sepia-toned historic street view framed by a red border. A large, ornate 19th‑century stone building stands on the left along a cobblestone avenue lined with young trees and gas lamps. Horse‑drawn traffic and pedestrians appear in the distance. The border text is in multiple languages, and the bottom center credits the photographer/publisher in Helsingfors (Helsinki).

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a wide town square bordered by 3‑ to 4‑story historic buildings. A large tree and fenced sidewalk are on the left, with small shopfronts. In the middle distance there is a simple metal structure for overhead lines and a streetlamp. On the right stands a long, stately building with a central pedimented entrance facing the open square. A few figures and a carriage or cart are visible. The caption in red script at the bottom names the town and square, and a small publisher's line is printed at the lower left.

Color postcard view of a European town square with cobblestone paving and several mid-rise historic buildings with red-tiled roofs and dormer windows. A slender tower with a baroque-style spire rises in the background. Numerous 1950s-era cars are parked around the square, and pedestrians in mid‑20th‑century clothing walk across the open space under a clear blue sky.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a large church or cathedral, focused on an ornate pipe organ mounted above a gallery. The vaulted ceiling is decorated with patterned ribs, and several large crystal chandeliers hang down over long rows of wooden pews. In the upper left corner, the caption reads "Koivisto–Björkö".

Black‑and‑white view of a broad cobbled town square bordered by 3‑ to 4‑story historic buildings with gabled roofs and shopfronts. In the center stands a fountain or well and an ornate lamppost. Horse‑drawn carriages and a few pedestrians appear around the square. Several shop signs in German are visible on the façades, including a market hall and specialty stores.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a busy European urban square with a central garden and fountain in the foreground, surrounded by grand multi‑storey buildings with awnings and shops at street level. In the background a richly decorated baroque church tower dominates the scene. The top margin contains printed titles and handwritten script, and there is small printed text along the bottom edge.

A black‑and‑white, scallop‑edged postcard showing the lavish high altar of a Baroque church interior. The composition centers on a tall altarpiece framed by dramatic sculpted figures, swirling stucco and gilded ornamentation, with a painting in the middle, an ornate tabernacle below, and a bright domed window or oculus above. Wooden communion rails and pews appear in the foreground.

Black‑and‑white image of a massive rectangular stone castle or fortress perched dramatically on a steep rocky cliff above a winding river. The walls are largely unornamented, with a few narrow windows and small towers or turrets at the corners, one with a conical roof. Below the keep are remnants of round defensive works integrated into the cliff. In the distance, a valley with fields and forested hills follows the river. The upper left of the image is partially obscured by a dark triangular area, suggesting damage or cropping. No visible caption or writing appears on the image side.

A vintage black-and-white postcard view of a large, grand hotel building in a neoclassical style with tall columns and multiple stories. In front of the hotel there is a broad terrace filled with tables and people seated outdoors, bordered by decorative balustrades and staircases leading down to a wide open square or street, where pedestrians are walking. Ornate street lamps line the area. The upper left corner of the postcard bears the printed caption 'Hotel Esplanade, Zagreb'.

A monochrome postcard showing an inner courtyard with Baroque and Renaissance architectural elements. Visible are a domed tower-like structure with arched windows, ornate window frames on the adjacent building, an external staircase with an arched entrance, and a decorative well with an elaborate wrought-iron canopy in the courtyard. The borders are light-colored, and there is printed caption text along the bottom edge.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a rocky coastal village with traditional wooden houses scattered among low hills. In the foreground are a tiled‑roof cottage and shrubs; further down a small pier with boats and a boathouse extends into a sheltered bay. More houses dot the rocky shoreline and background hills. The caption text is printed along the bottom left and a small logo with a number appears at the bottom right.

Sepia-tone panoramic view of a small historic town in a hilly landscape, seen from an elevated point behind conifer trees. The town has dense traditional buildings, church towers, and a prominent castle-like complex on a hill to the right. Printed red text at the top identifies the place, and a vertical red publisher imprint appears on the left margin.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a broad open yard in front of several connected barracks‑like buildings with large windows and chimneys. Sparse small trees and bushes stand in the foreground. The architecture is simple and functional, suggesting military or institutional use. Handwritten numbers mark a few buildings. Along the bottom is printed Swedish text identifying the place.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large multi-storey brick school building with many tall windows and decorative stonework, seen from across a fenced street or path. Several small figures stand near the entrance. To the right stands a cylindrical water tower rising above trees. Printed German text appears at the top left identifying the town and the boys' civic school, and a vertical publisher imprint is printed along the right edge.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view over a coastal town with many small houses, a church, docks, and forested areas in the foreground. The sea or a wide bay is visible with low hills in the distance. The word "STENUNGSUND" is printed in the lower left, and a small triangular publisher's logo with the number "7921" appears in the lower right.

Black‑and‑white view of a neo‑Gothic church with a large square tower, pointed roofs, rose windows and an ornate portal opening onto a mostly empty cobblestone square. To the left stands a multi‑storey Gothic‑revival building with many pointed gables and a tall slender spire. A small tree is in front of the church; surrounding buildings appear historic and European. The image is framed like an old photographic postcard, with white borders and some handwritten marks along the bottom edge.

Black-and-white image showing a rural European village scene with half-timbered or steep‑roofed houses along a dirt road, bordered by fields and a low fence in the foreground and a dense forest in the background. Utility poles line the road. The architecture suggests early 20th‑century Central Europe. A small handwritten catalog number appears at the bottom edge.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a panoramic coastal view with a curved bay, cliffs, dense tree cover, and a long pier or jetty extending into calm water. On the hill above the bay stands a large palace-like building. Printed captions in Cyrillic and French at the bottom identify the scene as the royal palace near Varna (Euxinograd).

Black‑and‑white ethnographic postcard showing a barefoot Indigenous Sanapaná man standing outdoors on rocky ground, wearing a draped cloth garment and carrying a net bag and other items over his shoulder. Printed captions in Spanish appear beneath the photograph, mentioning 'Indio Sanapaná, Puerto Casado' and publication details from Buenos Aires.

Colorized early-20th‑century streetscape showing a quiet residential street lined with large villas and fenced gardens. A gently curving road runs into the distance with telegraph poles along the sidewalk and low hills or vineyards in the background. Printed titling at the top identifies the scene as Radebeul, Rosenstrasse. Publisher information appears vertically along the left and right margins.

A monochrome postcard showing historic brick hospital buildings along a canal. The gothic-style windows, arched doorways, stepped gables, and tiled roofs stand directly over the water, reflecting in the canal. Printed French text at the bottom identifies the scene as a view of a hospital in Bruges, looking over the water, with a small reference number at the lower right.

Black‑and‑white view over a small European spa or resort town in a hilly, forested landscape. In the foreground stands a prominent villa-style building with half‑timbered decorative gable and the name "Villa Zipfel" painted on the facade; a woman is visible near the entrance and a fenced garden surrounds the house. Other detached villas and small houses line a curving road leading into the town, with wooded hills and fields in the background.

Color postcard showing a hillside urban landscape. On the top of the hill stands a large, white, modernist terraced hotel or sanatorium surrounded by trees. Below are several mid‑rise apartment blocks with balconies, a curving road with a few cars, and a long zigzagging pedestrian path or stairway climbing the slope. The setting is lush and green under a bright blue sky with large white clouds. No legible printed text is visible on the image side.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a posed indoor group portrait of men, women and children dressed in traditional folk costumes. They are arranged around a table and a spinning wheel in a room with a large window and patterned wall décor. The text at the bottom left reads "Norrbottens folkdräkter."

Vintage monochrome postcard view over a historic European town with steep roofs and stepped‑gabled buildings in the foreground and a large hilltop complex with a cathedral and castle in the background. At the top, in red Gothic-style print, is German text identifying the scene as a view from the city tower toward the royal Albrechtsburg in Meissen.

Black-and-white landscape view of a riverside scene with Bohus Fortress on a hill to the left, boats along the water, forested slopes, and open marshlands in the distance. In the right foreground stands a white wooden house with a tiled roof. Printed captions identify the location and publisher at the bottom of the image.

A vintage Spanish postcard front (address side) labeled 'TARJETA POSTAL – UNION POSTAL UNIVERSAL – ESPAÑA'. It is addressed in red and black cursive handwriting to 'Sr. Don Benito Perez-Galdos'. The original city name 'Santander' is underlined in blue and then redirected to 'Madrid'. There are circular Spanish postal cancellation marks and a red Spanish stamp in the lower right corner. In the lower left corner appears a small printer's mark with the word 'MADRID'. The card shows signs of age and discoloration.

Colorized view of the interior of a historic mosque with white arches, ornate mihrab, hanging brass lamps, and striped prayer rugs on the floor. Caption text in French appears along the bottom margin.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a rural hilly landscape with scattered houses and small buildings clustered in a valley and on surrounding slopes. Greek text is printed at the top left, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

Black‑and‑white industrial scene showing a large overhead loading crane spanning a quarry or open pit with a bucket hanging beneath it. Below and beyond the crane are buildings of a small settlement, and a body of water and low hills in the distance. Printed caption text appears at the bottom of the image in a Nordic-looking language.

A black‑and‑white view over a historic spa town nestled in a forested valley. Dominating the foreground is a Baroque church with twin onion‑domed towers and a central dome, surrounded by tightly packed multi‑story buildings with steep roofs. Hills covered with trees rise in the background. The image is framed by tree branches, and a small caption is printed in the lower left corner.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a hillside landscape dominated by a large Venetian fortress on the top of a hill. Below the fortress are scattered houses and stone ruins in a rocky terrain. The image is framed by printed captions in French and Greek identifying the place as the Venetian fortress of Saint George near Argostoli.

Color image showing a small alpine-style lake with striking reddish-brown water, surrounded by dense coniferous forest. A person in a red top stands on the rocky shore at the left foreground. The background consists of tall evergreen trees and a glimpse of mountains to the far right. No visible printed text appears on the image side.

Colored vintage postcard view of a broad boulevard with tram tracks and several trams, lined with multi‑story buildings on the left and a formal garden square on the right. Dominating the right side is a large neoclassical building with a wide staircase and a colonnaded portico, likely a museum, facing a park with statues and paths. The sky is softly tinted and the card shows aging spots and a central crease. At the top is printed multilingual text identifying the location as Museum Boulevard in Budapest.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a large crowd gathered in front of a neoclassical building with arches and tall windows. Flags are visible above the people, and the scene appears to be a public celebration or political event. Printed captions in French and Greek are overlaid on the image, identifying it as a souvenir from Samos and dating the event to November 1912.

Colorized landscape postcard showing a rural valley town with scattered houses with red roofs, surrounding fields, forested hills, and a prominent multi‑arch stone railway viaduct crossing the scene. The title "Sebnitz. (Sächs. Schweiz.)" appears printed in red at the top, with a small publisher's note at the bottom right.

Vintage tinted postcard view of a street and hill in Lublin, showing a winding dirt road in the foreground and a complex of historic buildings with church towers and a large school building on the ridge. The sky is colorized in pinkish-orange, while the townscape and vegetation are in monochrome. Printed Polish text at the top labels the city, street, church, and a trade school.

Colorized vintage postcard view over a tree‑filled park or garden towards a small town. In the middle distance stands a prominent red‑brick public building with pointed gables and arched windows. Behind it stretches a low skyline of light‑colored houses and a tall clock or church tower. The sky is softly tinted with pastel colors suggesting sunrise or sunset. Printed text at the bottom identifies the location and publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view framed by tree branches, looking across a forested valley toward a large hilltop castle complex. A tall factory chimney and some industrial buildings stand in the lower middle ground. At the top in reddish lettering is a German caption naming the castle and indicating the viewpoint.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a grand spa‑town building complex. On the left is a multi‑storey hotel with a steep tiled roof and dormer windows; on the right is a neoclassical building with a columned portico and a pediment bearing relief sculpture, labeled "KURTHEATER". In the foreground are manicured gardens, steps, and a curved driveway with a few people and an early automobile. At the bottom edge, printed text identifies the location as Bad Elster and names the buildings Sachsenhof and Kurtheater.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a tree-covered hillside with tall pines on the left and a curved road with a railing on the right, leading towards a prominent neo‑Gothic church tower in the distance. Printed caption text appears in the upper right corner.

Colorized historic postcard view of a large corner building with ornate gables and a small tower, labeled as the Schützenhaus (marksmen's hall). The structure houses a restaurant and hotel, with German signage on the facade. A tree-lined street runs in front, with a few pedestrians and a horse-drawn carriage visible, suggesting an early 20th‑century European town scene.

Black-and-white interior view of an early 20th‑century café or Gasthaus with wooden chairs and tables covered in lace tablecloths, floral centerpieces, arched doorways, a bar or counter with display cabinets, wall clock, and decorative geometric ceiling. Small wall posters and a stove are visible. The lower margin of the image bears handwritten-style captions, likely the place name and establishment name.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a riverside or lakeside military swimming school. On the water there are long wooden platforms and a floating building with a shed-like roof where people, likely soldiers, are gathered and swimming. Trees line the far bank, and some swimmers are visible in the water. At the top, in red printed text, is the title of the view in German.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of Athens showing the Acropolis hill with the Parthenon on top, and in the foreground the Corinthian columns of the Temple of Olympian Zeus surrounded by the city's low buildings. Printed captions in Greek and French appear below the image, along with a web watermark.

Colorized vintage view of a low, red‑roofed brick hospital complex with verandas and decorative trim. A white picket fence encloses a small garden with a palm tree and central lamp post in the foreground. Several nurses or staff in white uniforms and a few other figures stand near the building. The caption in red at the top left reads "Hospital – Mildura." The sky is softly tinted blue and pink, typical of early color postcards.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing two substantial masonry school buildings in a sparsely developed landscape. Two men stand on open ground in the foreground. The main left building has the Swedish words "FOLKSKOLA" on its facade. Printed Swedish captions at the bottom identify the institutions and location, and stamped text reads "UDDEVALLA MUSEUM" with a printed date "Feb. 1903."

Color image showing four national flags on tall flagpoles against a cloudy sky. From left to right, the flags appear to be Sweden (blue with a yellow Nordic cross), Denmark (red with a white Nordic cross), Imperial Germany (horizontal black‑white‑red tricolor), and Bulgaria (horizontal white‑green‑red tricolor). The tops of some roof structures or poles are visible at the bottom edge, along with overhead wires, suggesting a public or exhibition area. There is no visible printed caption on the front.

Black‑and‑white photographic postcard showing a densely packed crowd seated in a stadium, many holding white umbrellas. A staircase with railings leads up from the foreground to the stands. The lower margin contains printed Greek text along with some French text, and handwritten signatures. A watermark with the domain "www.elia.org.gr" is visible.

A black-and-white portrait of a middle‑aged man wearing a wide‑brimmed hat, dark suit, white shirt, and patterned tie. The image is closely cropped to his head and upper torso, with a neutral blurred background. At the bottom left there is a caption with the person's profession and name; at the bottom right there is a small imprint or logo.

Black‑and‑white night view of a large illuminated Baroque church with a tall tower and ornate façade, photographed from across a river or open space. Streetlights form a line in the foreground, with light streaks from moving vehicles. Additional historic buildings are visible to the left and right, all dramatically lit against a dark sky. The image has scalloped edges typical of vintage postcards. No visible caption or writing appears on the image side.

Color-tinted historic postcard showing a riverside view of Eilenburg with timber and plaster houses in the foreground, a water edge, and on the hill behind them a complex with towers and large roofed buildings identified as the Schlossberg with the district court. The style is early-20th‑century German litho printing.

A colorized historic postcard showing a round medieval stone tower with a conical roof rising above trees and a wooden fence in the foreground. The tower has small rectangular windows and weathered masonry. At the top of the image the caption reads "Kik in de Kök," and beneath the picture the location is labeled "Reval." The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century printed postcard.

Vintage black-and-white postcard view of a stone city gate and tower beside a canal or moat. The round tower with a conical roof stands in the water, attached to a bridge and city wall. Leafless trees line the banks, and a few people and a horse-drawn vehicle are visible on the bridge. Printed text at the top identifies the scene as a view of Bruges and specifically La Porte Maréchal. A small printer's mark with letters and the word "Glogn" (partially legible) appears near the upper center.

Black‑and‑white postcard reproduction of a late‑medieval Christian painting or panel. It depicts a female saint in rich, somewhat worn robes and veil, with wavy hair and a halo-like patterned background. She holds a tall cylindrical container or tower-shaped vessel in her right hand, and gestures with her left. The image is framed with a wide white margin at the bottom, typical of art‑reproduction postcards. No visible caption or writing appears on the front.

Black‑and‑white aerial or elevated view of a central European small town square bordered by two‑storey historic buildings with sloped tiled roofs. The nearly empty square has a few trees aligned along the facades and a couple of lamp posts or monuments in the middle. Beyond the town stretch open fields and low hills, with an industrial chimney visible in the far distance. The card is framed by a white border typical of early 20th‑century postcards. No printed caption or handwriting is visible.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing ancient ruins: in the foreground and right are low stone walls and a large arch; in the background left stand several tall Doric columns from a classical temple. The caption beneath the image is printed in Greek and French, identifying the scene as the bazaar and Temple of Apollo in ancient Corinth. A web address is faintly visible at the bottom right.

Black‑and‑white view of a large cobblestoned town square bordered by historic buildings. On the right is an ornate town‑hall‑like structure with a tall clock tower, steep gabled roof, statues, and a grand staircase leading up to an arched entrance. Smaller townhouses adjoin it. On the left side stand two simpler, rectangular buildings with hipped roofs and arched doorways; faint lettering is visible on their façades. The square itself is mostly empty except for a few distant figures, suggesting an early‑20th‑century European setting.

Black‑and‑white historic view of a busy market square in a European town. Stalls and horse‑drawn carts fill the open square, with many people in early 20th‑century clothing. On the left stands a large baroque/renaissance town hall‑like building with an ornate façade and a tall church or town‑hall tower topped by a bulbous spire and cross. Surrounding the square are multi‑story gabled houses with steep tiled roofs. On the right are prominent hotels with large painted signs on their façades.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a small tram or streetcar on curved tracks running through a wooded, hilly landscape. To the right is a steep staircase ascending the hill with a person sitting beside it in light clothing and a hat. The scene is tranquil and surrounded by dense trees. At the bottom center of the postcard is a printed caption.

Black‑and‑white image showing a rural lakeside scene with a few wooden houses on a hillside. In the foreground there is a sloping field; behind it stand houses surrounded by trees. A large body of water and forested hills are visible in the background. A flagpole with what appears to be the Norwegian flag flies near the right side. At the bottom left, white text is printed directly on the image.

Sepia-toned street scene showing early 20th‑century urban buildings. At left are multi‑storey residential houses; in the center a straight street recedes into the distance lined with detached houses. Several children and adults walk along the wide road. On the right is a prominent corner building with arched windows and signage for a pharmacy. Handwritten-style text at the top names the location, and the pharmacy sign on the right façade reads "ANKER-APOTHEKE" next to an anchor symbol.

Black‑and‑white view of a large stone castle-like complex on a hill, partially obscured by leafy trees in the foreground. The main structure has steep, tiled roofs, multi‑story rectangular towers with small windows, and an inner courtyard enclosed by walls. A smaller town with houses and terraced gardens lies below the fortification. The central tower has a small spire topped by a cross, indicating a chapel or religious element within the complex. The overall style is Central European and medieval/early modern.

An old sepia-toned postcard showing a rural scene in a stone courtyard: a woman in traditional dress hands something to an older man seated near a well or stone structure. There are geese or ducks on the left side near a small wooden door. The style is early 20th century, with printed captions in Spanish at the bottom.

A hand‑colored vintage postcard showing a panoramic view of a small town in a valley, with half‑timbered houses, red roofs, a prominent white church with a tall steeple, and an industrial building with a tall brick chimney. Rolling hills and fields surround the town. The bottom margin contains red German text, including a greeting from Cunewalde and publisher information.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a tree-lined path densely bordered by tall palm trees in a botanical garden. The scene is framed like an illustration or early photograph. At the bottom, printed text identifies the location as the palm-lined street within the botanical garden in Lisbon.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a grand Neo‑Baroque opera house with a large central dome, ornate pediment, statues on the roof, and a portico supported by multiple columns. Small figures walk in the foreground, and trees and lampposts line the front plaza. The top of the card is printed with the words "GRAZ" on the left and "Opernhaus" on the right.

A black‑and‑white street scene showing a gently sloping road lined with wooden and masonry buildings. People walk along the sidewalks, some with children, while bicycles are parked against a building on the right. In the distance are low hills or mountains under a clear sky. Printed text at the bottom left identifies the scene as a street in Kiruna, and a photographer/publisher credit appears at the bottom right.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a street corner with a large, ornate multi‑story building housing the "Restaurant zu den Linden." People in early 20th‑century dress walk or stand near tram tracks and leafless trees lining wide streets. Printed captions identify the location and publisher.

Black‑and‑white winter view of a snow-covered Alpine valley. A cluster of multi‑storey hotels and spa‑like buildings sits on the valley floor, surrounded by dense coniferous forest. Behind the town rise steep, dramatic mountains with snowy peaks and ridges. The overall look is of an early or mid‑20th‑century mountain resort in winter. No visible caption or printed text appears on the image side.

Colorized view of a landscaped city park with curving gravel paths, lawns, flowerbeds, trees, a yellow bench, and a large stone pedestal topped by a lion statue. A lone person walks in the distance. The lower margin has printed captions indicating the location and the publisher.

A colorized old postcard view of a wide cobblestone street lined with substantial townhouses and brick walls on both sides. There are gas or early electric streetlamps, horse-drawn vehicles in the distance, and a few pedestrians, including two children on the right foreground. The sky is bright blue with scattered white clouds. At the top of the image, printed text identifies the place as 'Limbach i. Sa.' on the left and 'Bahnhofstrasse.' on the right.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped park with paths, benches, trees and flower beds leading toward a large multi‑storey building in the background. On the reverse, it is formatted as a divided back postcard with printed multilingual heading and a green postage stamp. Handwritten text and address are visible, along with a museum/archive stamp label. At the bottom left of the message side appears a caption naming the spa town and park.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large youth brass and drum band posed in front of a building with a balcony. The children wear uniform-style clothing and caps, and many hold musical instruments (trombones, trumpets, drums, cymbals). A flag is held in the center of the group. At the bottom is handwritten or printed text in a Scandinavian language, and in the lower right corner is a dark label with the word "ARBEJDERMUSEET" and a small flag icon.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a hilltop complex of Gothic towers and large historic buildings above a riverside town. The river (the Elbe) is in the foreground with houses and embankment along the shore, framed by trees and foliage. At the bottom is a handwritten-style caption identifying the scene.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a sloping street lined with multi-story townhouses on both sides, leading downhill toward a distant church spire. A few pedestrians and a horse-drawn cart are visible on the street. The caption at the top reads "Apolda — Dornburger Straße".

Colorized historic postcard showing a large Neo-Renaissance / Neo-Baroque public building with ornate façades, statues in niches, and a red tiled roof. The caption in red Hungarian text at the top left reads "Lőcse. Törvényszék." The central gable bears decorative reliefs and the year "1903". Trees stand in front of the building and the sky is softly tinted blue and pink.

Black-and-white postcard showing a rocky hill with a small bell tower or chapel built into the rock, surrounded by lush vegetation. At the base and on the slopes of the hill are stone buildings with tiled roofs, and in the background stand larger multi‑storey structures. The caption text in Bulgarian and French identifies the scene as a view of Plovdiv.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the façade of an early 20th‑century building named 'Hotel Metropole'. The architecture has Art Nouveau details, with large arched windows and decorative floral motifs. A large roof sign reads 'HOTEL METROPOLE' and another sign over the first floor reads 'CAFÉ RESTAURANT'. The ground floor is open to the street, with tables and seated guests visible inside. At the bottom margin of the card is printed text identifying the location as Nijmegen and giving the street address and owners.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard with an ornate floral border. The main image shows a large rectangular building enclosing a parade ground filled with soldiers on horseback and on foot, watched by a crowd of civilians. An inset image at the upper right shows a mounted officer on a horse. Handwritten text appears around the border.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a wide, mostly empty town market square with a central fountain and a street lamp in the foreground. Around the square stand 2–3‑story historic buildings with gabled roofs and shop signs in German on their facades. A church tower with a clock rises behind the row of houses slightly left of center, while a building on the right with a small tower and sign houses a hotel and restaurant. A lone person walks across the square, and a horse‑drawn covered wagon stands on the right edge. At the top left is a caption identifying the place as 'Radeburg. Markt,'.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a broad street lined with large brick and stucco buildings in early 20th‑century architectural style. On the left side are multi‑storey buildings with bay windows, balconies, and a clock on one of the roofs; trees and a low fence line the sidewalk. Further along stands a complex identified as Hospital St. Johannis. People in period clothing walk along the pavement, while horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians move down the road. The caption text in red is printed at the top of the image.

Black-and-white street scene showing a calm town center with low buildings, tree-lined sidewalks, pedestrians, bicycles, and a horse-drawn cart. The perspective looks down a straight street bordered by traditional European-style houses and shops. Text overlays at the bottom identify the place and the photography studio.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a steep rocky cliff covered with scattered trees. On the plateau at the top stands a solitary building. At the top edge of the card there is printed German text identifying the view as a look from the Roßtrappe toward the Hexentanzplatz in the Bode Valley of the Harz Mountains.

Old sepia postcard showing a full-length portrait of a woman in traditional dress carrying baskets and a large woven pack on her back. The style is ethnographic rather than touristic. There is a postage stamp affixed in the upper right corner. At the bottom, printed captions in French identify the subject and send greetings from Constantinople.

A black‑and‑white view of a curving European street lined with tall, ornate late‑19th‑century apartment and hotel buildings featuring balconies, bay windows and steep roofs with small spires. On the right is a grand institutional or hotel building with classical detailing and a landscaped garden in front. A church with a spire is visible further back. People in early 20th‑century dress walk along the pavement and a horse‑drawn carriage stands in the street. There is no visible printed caption or text on the image.

Black‑and‑white photograph postcard showing a large stone Renaissance-style portal in a stucco wall. The arched doorway has heavy rusticated blocks and carved ornament around the frame. Above the lintel is a frieze with decorative reliefs and a circular medallion bearing an emblem or monogram, flanked by sculpted figures. Higher up are three arched openings: two filled, one open, with columns and classical detailing. A man in dark clothing stands partly in the shadow of the passageway. On the right side of the façade is a small rectangular plaque with the number 25.

Colorized historic postcard view of a European city riverfront. A bridge crosses a river with pedestrians on it, and along the opposite bank stand multi‑story buildings with red roofs and shop signs. A tall church tower with a green onion-shaped dome rises on the right. In the background a steep, wooded hill topped with fortifications and a prominent clock tower overlooks the city. The printed title at the top reads in German about Graz, the Schlossberg, two bridges, and the Franciscan church.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a large seaside palace in landscaped gardens, with a tall tower flying a red flag. The foreground features a formal lawn and flowerbeds with a path leading toward the building. In the sky area at upper left, multilingual captions identify the scene and location.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a landscaped park with lush vegetation, palm trees, footbridges, and a stone bridge beside a lake. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along paths, and a horse-drawn carriage travels on a road overlooking the water, where a sailboat is visible. At the very bottom is a printed caption identifying the location.

A black-and-white vintage postcard showing a snowy mountain landscape. In the foreground is a curved, elevated bobsleigh track fenced with wooden railings. In the middle distance stands a large alpine-style lodge or hut on a slope, surrounded by forest. Rolling, tree-covered mountains extend into the background. The caption in German is printed in the lower left margin.

Color postcard view of a historic hilltop complex with a large Gothic cathedral featuring two tall spires and several smaller spires, attached to an extensive castle-like ensemble with red-tiled roofs and a round tower. The buildings rise above a riverside town of smaller houses and warehouses, with barges and boats moored on a broad river in the foreground under a clear blue sky. No visible printed text appears on the image side.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a busy street corner with a grand two‑storey neoclassical building with arcades, balconies, and awnings. People in early 20th‑century attire walk and ride in carriages in front. A green Egyptian postage stamp is affixed in the upper left corner. The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as 'Alexandria – Cook's Corner.'

Colorized vintage postcard view across the Bosphorus showing an ornate waterfront palace with elaborate neoclassical-Ottoman architecture, identified in French as the Beylerbeyi Palace in Constantinople. The building stands behind a long sea wall with the water in the foreground and hilly, tree-covered land in the background. Printed caption text appears at the top, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

Colorized postcard image of an early 20th‑century ocean liner at sea. The ship has two large white funnels with red tops, black hull with a red waterline, and tall masts with rigging. Smoke rises from the funnels. In the upper left, German text identifies the vessel as the motor ship "Monte Sarmiento" of the Hamburg–South American Steamship Company.

Monochrome printed postcard showing a small, old, steep‑roofed house standing alone in a cobbled square, with a horse and cart at its side. The building has a high, tiled hip roof, simple plastered walls, and small windows. Behind it rise taller townhouses and, in the background, the ornate tower and spire of a church or town hall. The style is Northern European and appears to be an architectural illustration rather than a photograph.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a peaceful coastal scene: a wooden barn on the left with a few women in long dresses seated by bushes, a small wooden pier extending into the water, and several sailing boats with tall white sails moored along the shoreline. At the bottom there is printed and handwritten text in Swedish, including the place name "Raahe – Brahestad" and a dated message from 1903.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a tranquil forest pond or small lake. In the foreground is a dirt path and tall trees along the water's edge, with dense coniferous forest on the opposite shore under a yellowish evening sky. At the bottom, ornate cursive German text identifies the location.

A colorized historical postcard view over a coastal town with wooden houses along a harbor, small boats in the water, and a large stone church with a tall tower and steep roof dominating the skyline. A long veranda-style building stands in the foreground, and forested islands are visible in the background. Handwritten-looking red text appears at the top left, and a small vertical serial number is printed along the right edge.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a wooded shoreline with several wooden houses or cottages on a forested hill beside calm water. Small piers and moored boats line the water's edge, and low hills are visible in the distance across the lake or fjord. A printed caption at the bottom left reads "No. 7. Gustafsberg."

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a large hunting lodge and adjacent small chapel-like building on a grassy hillside, backed by dense coniferous forest. The main building is a grand, multi‑storey villa with steep gabled roofs and a corner tower. Printed red text at the top reads "Kgl. Jagdschloss Rehefeld i. sächs. Erzgeb."

A black‑and‑white, slightly grainy photograph of a modernist high‑rise concrete building shot from a low angle. The façade shows vertical slit windows and a long band of small windows near the ground floor. Large Hebrew letters, made of dark material, are mounted high on the wall, indicating the function of the building. The style and framing resemble a vintage architectural postcard.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large wooden country hotel building in a rural valley with mountains in the background. A flagpole with a Scandinavian-style flag stands in front, with a few people and a horse‑drawn cart by the entrance. Decorative text at the bottom identifies the hotel, and along the right edge there is vertically printed holiday greeting text. The design and wear suggest an early 20th‑century postcard.

A sepia-toned historic postcard showing a large multi‑wing institutional building with ornate gables and towers, set in front of wooded hills and open fields. The architecture resembles an early 20th‑century sanatorium or convalescent home. At the bottom, there is a printed German caption identifying the place.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-story brick high school building with a central tower and arched entrance, set along a broad street lined with palm trees and a telephone pole. A smaller house stands to the left, and there are handwritten numbers in red and black ink near the top and left sides. Printed red text at the lower right reads "High School, San Bernardino, Cal."

A black-and-white historical postcard showing a wide cobblestoned market square bordered by multi‑story townhouses with shops on the ground floors. In the foreground stands a small pavilion or kiosk with people gathered around, and a few pedestrians walking across the open square. In the background, behind the row of buildings, a church spire is visible. Printed text at the top identifies the place.

A vintage printed postal card with typed Estonian text dated in Tallinn on 15 February 1934, addressed to Mr. M. Torn. It itemizes amounts owed in kroons and cents, with several sums underlined in red and handwritten annotations in the margins. The card is signed at the bottom and bears no photograph or illustration, only text within a rectangular border.

Black‑and‑white street scene showing two early electric trams (car no. 407 and another behind it) stopped on a cobblestone road in front of ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. Many people in period clothing, including children and uniformed officials, stand around the trams. German shop signs line the façades (for a jeweler, drapery, bicycle shop, etc.). Leafless trees and a decorative street lamp are visible on the right, and a sign for a confectioner hangs on the corner.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a calm canal bordered by vegetation and palm trees, with buildings and a slender minaret in the background. The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as the Mahmoudieh Canal in Alexandria. There is printed vertical text along the left edge and handwritten text in a cursive script along the right margin.

Color photograph of the interior of a large Gothic cathedral, viewed from the nave toward the high altar. The scene shows tall pointed arches, ribbed vaulting, clustered stone columns, and an elaborate stone choir screen with a large crucifix and figures above it. Wooden pews fill the nave, and numerous small hanging lights descend from the high ceiling along both sides.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a Lutheran church with a tall central tower topped by a spire and cross. The church has a tiled, polygonal roof and narrow arched windows, and is surrounded by trees and a wooden fence with masonry posts. In the foreground, a grassy open space with two children and a dog is visible. At the top is printed text in Cyrillic on the left and in German on the right.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing Michelangelo's marble sculpture of the Madonna and Child set in an ornate altar with columns and decorative bases. The printed caption in red at the bottom identifies the work and its location in Bruges.

A monochrome street scene showing a curved tram-lined street bordered by multi‑story shopfronts with awnings and hanging signs, including a prominent C&A sign on the right. Pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalks. In the distance stands a taller historic tower with an ornate spire. The caption at the bottom reads "Nijmegen. Lange Burchtstraat."

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a panoramic industrial view of a port city with rail tracks, warehouses, stacked lumber, and a tall smokestack dominating the middle. In the distance is a large grain-elevator‑type building and a spread of low houses with hills behind. There are two old postage stamps and circular postmarks in the upper right. Russian text is printed at the top left, likely giving the city name and identifying the elevator structure.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a wide, flat lakeshore landscape. In the foreground to the right is a horse-drawn cart with a driver seated on it, facing toward the water. The lake stretches across the horizon under an open sky. At the top of the card, printed in red, are captions in Russian and Latin script.

Black‑and‑white image showing a formal military ceremony at the entrance of a barracks or palace courtyard. Uniformed guards with plumed shakos and ornate cartridge pouches stand at attention, some holding trumpets. A striped guardhouse and iron gate are visible on the right, with steps leading up to a covered entrance. In the background are long, low barracks‑style buildings decorated with wreaths or garlands, and a tall flagpole flying a long, horizontal flag.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a tall neo‑Gothic brick church with a very high spire, clock faces on the tower, and a rose window above the main entrance. The church stands behind trees and a landscaped square or park. At the top of the card, red printed text in German identifies the place.

Colorized vintage postcard view over a European city with a river running through the center, crossed by several bridges. The foreground shows stone columns and a wall, likely part of a castle or fortification on an elevated hill, looking down onto dense urban buildings and distant green hills. At the top, red German text reads "Graz mit Castellaufgang."

A multi-image winter-sport postcard with a blue border showing scenes from a large cross‑country ski race. The top-left image shows a mass start of skiers wearing numbered bibs. The top-right image shows skiers approaching a finish or checkpoint banner amid snowy forested hills. The bottom-left image shows many children and families on skis in a snowy park. The bottom-right image shows a smiling skier in race gear speaking with an older man in winter clothing near red fencing. The central caption reads "TARTU MARATON" and on the right side "WORLDLOPPET"; there are also small logos.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a triptych painting mounted on an ornate interior wall. The central panel depicts the Lamentation over the dead Christ, surrounded by Mary and other figures; numerous small angels appear above. Flanking side panels show donor figures and other religious personages. Decorative inscriptions in Latin or German appear in the upper parts of the side panels. Beneath the image, in cursive German script, is a caption identifying the location and artist.

Color-tinted vintage postcard showing a narrow forested valley with a small cascading stream or waterfall (Steinbachgraben). Dense trees line both sides of the rocky creek, and the water flows toward the viewer. At the bottom edge there is a printed caption in German identifying the location as Steinbachgraben in Rettenbach near Maria Trost.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a large neoclassical two‑storey seaside building with balconies and railings, likely a grand hotel or spa establishment. Several people and possibly carriages are visible in front, with the sea and a low hill in the background. Greek text is printed at the bottom, and a modern watermark with a website URL appears across the lower right.

A black-and-white photograph of a quiet small-town street. On the left is a two-story, light-colored house or inn with steep gabled roof and two chimneys. Trees line the middle of the image, partly obscuring other buildings in the background. The street appears unpaved or lightly paved, and there are power poles and wires to the right. The sky is bright and mostly featureless. There is no clearly legible text visible on the buildings or elsewhere.

Illustrated vintage postcard showing a lush garden and landscaped grounds in front of a long, low building with an ornate, arcaded veranda. At the center stands a prominent statue on a pedestal, framed by trees and shrubs. The image is bordered by a light margin, and printed text beneath the illustration identifies the scene in French.

A black‑and‑white photograph of a small cargo ship or coastal freighter sailing along a narrow river or canal bordered by trees and low vegetation. The vessel has a single mast and a central superstructure with lifeboats mounted on deck. On the stern, the ship's name 'CHRISTA' and a home port starting with 'HAMB…' are visible, suggesting 'HAMBURG'. A small flag flies from the mast. The scene looks like an older documentary or tourist view of a working ship on an inland waterway.

Vintage sepia postcard view of a small town with ornate villas and church spires at the foot of a forested mountain. In the foreground is a landscaped park with paths, lawns, and trees. The printed caption at the top reads "Bad Harzburg. Villen am Burgberge." and a vertical imprint on the left margin shows the publisher's name. The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century German spa resort scene.

A black-and-white photograph of a formal dinner or banquet in an ornate, wood‑paneled room. Several well-dressed men and women in evening attire are seated around a long table set with candlesticks, glasses, and plates. A man in a tuxedo stands giving a toast, while guests seated on both sides of the table raise their glasses and smile. The setting suggests a stately or historic interior, possibly in a mansion, club, or institutional dining hall. There is no visible printed caption or writing on the front.

Black‑and‑white historic postcard showing a large brick railway station complex with arched windows and a long glass‑roofed train shed. A clock tower rises near the center-right of the building. In the foreground is a cobblestone square with several men in late‑19th‑century or early‑20th‑century clothing standing or walking. A bridge or railing runs along the front of the station. At the bottom the caption reads "Centralstationen."

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a winding road carved into rocky coastal cliffs above a body of water. The road curves along the hillside with a simple railing, surrounded by rocks and sparse trees. Printed caption text appears in the upper left.

A monochrome postcard-style photograph showing a large, monumental early‑20th‑century building with steep tiled roofs, small cupolas, tall narrow windows and heavy masonry walls. The architecture is somewhat expressionist or Art Nouveau, with a massive, almost fortress‑like appearance and minimal ornament. In the upper right corner of the card, the number "1597" is written in red ink. No printed caption or other text is visible on the front.

A postcard reproducing the front page of an old Portuguese newspaper titled "O COMBATE". The layout is densely packed text in columns with a bold masthead at the top. Beneath the title, there is a line naming the proprietor and director, Daniel de Lima Trindade, and a dateline indicating Lisbon on Monday, 8 May 1882. The central feature is a decorative double oval portrait framed with ornate foliage, showing two 18th‑century figures in wigs and formal attire, labeled as Dom José I and Marquez de Pombal. The rest of the page is filled with long articles in Portuguese, commemorating Sebastião José de Carvalho e Mello.

Colorized vintage postcard view over a small lake surrounded by lush greenery, with rowboats on the water and a covered pier or boathouse with flags on the right. In the background stands a spa town with ornate buildings and a prominent church tower. The foreground and margins contain printed German text including the place name and publisher details.

A vintage sepia postcard showing a tall church with a multi‑tiered tower topped by a cross. The tower has arched windows and a clock face, and is attached to a baroque-style church building surrounded by trees and a fence. Printed text in German at the top left reads "Libau. Deutsche Kirche".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a river valley with steep wooded hills on both sides. On a prominent rocky cliff above the river stand the ruins of a medieval castle. A steamboat travels along the river in the foreground, and there are scattered houses, fields, and orchards along the banks. German text is printed in red at the top of the image.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a large, three-story urban villa or apartment building with dormer windows and ornate arched window decorations. A central balcony and covered entrance face the street, with bare trees and a low wall with gate in the foreground. The lower half of the card is blank for writing, and there is printed cursive text at the bottom indicating an address.

Black‑and‑white view from a cliffside building with arched windows and awnings, perched dramatically on a rocky precipice. A small open cable car descends on steep cables from near the building toward the valley below. In the distance lies a broad valley filled with a dense town or small city and surrounding agricultural fields, ringed by mountains under a hazy sky. The image has a white border and the aged, slightly speckled look of an early 20th‑century printed postcard. No visible caption or printed text appears on the image side.

Black-and-white postcard showing a three-story neoclassical building at the end of a straight driveway bordered by trees. The facade is symmetrical with arched windows on the second floor and a central doorway. In the lower-left corner there is a printed caption, and in the lower-right corner a small oval publisher mark.

An old sepia-toned postcard showing the ruins of a medieval hilltop castle complex above a river valley and patchwork fields. The foreground features massive stone walls and a partly collapsed gabled structure with arched window openings, while a round tower and additional ruined walls stand further back. In the distant background, a rural landscape with fields and scattered buildings is visible. German printed text appears along the bottom margin.

Monochrome postcard view of a European medieval town with intact city walls and multiple round defensive towers. In the center rises a tall, slender church spire, flanked by massive gate towers and smaller turrets. In the foreground is a park or promenade with trees and several people walking along a path toward the fortified old town. The image occupies the left portion of the card, leaving a blank margin on the right, typical of early 20th‑century postcards.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a rural landscape with a war memorial mound and stone markers in the foreground, and an inset close-up of a commemorative stone. The layout and caption style are typical of historical battlefield or monument postcards.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a shaded Greek courtyard with vines and a seated figure near an arched doorway. The image is framed on the left side of the card. Printed captions in French and Greek identify it as a Greek courtyard in Athens. The top border of the image contains an English phrase, and the bottom margin includes a series number and the Athens-based publisher's name.

Colorized vintage street view of an urban square with a tall column bearing a clock on top in the foreground. Around the square stand multi‑story buildings with enclosed glass balconies typical of northern Spain. One prominent corner building has a sign on the roof reading "PALACE HOTEL" and street‑level awnings. Tram tracks cross the paved square and a few pedestrians walk in the middle distance. At the bottom margin of the image there is printed caption text identifying the scene as a street junction in La Coruña.

Black-and-white postcard depicting a pavilion complex with arched colonnades in the foreground and a tall tower with a dome-like building in the background. The architecture is in a North African / Islamic style, shown as part of a colonial exhibition. A person is walking in the courtyard. Printed French captions describe it as a view of the Algerian pavilion from the official Tunisian pavilion at the Exposition Coloniale Internationale in Paris, 1931.

A vintage, monochrome view of a long Renaissance-style palazzo façade along a city street. The building has arched doorways, rectangular and arched windows with shutters, and fabric awnings hanging from several windows. A few pedestrians stand or walk along the sidewalk in front. At the bottom center of the image, text identifies the location as Palazzo Geremia in Trento.

Black‑and‑white image of a stone church with a steep gabled roof and a tall, slender spire topped with a weather vane. The façade has a round window above a decorated portal with an arched entrance and religious relief, and the side wall shows a series of buttress-like projections with small windows between them. Overhead power or tram lines cross the sky, and a small child stands in the open square in front of the church. The setting appears to be a European town, with a few adjacent buildings partly visible.

Black‑and‑white divided postcard showing two rural scenes. On the left is a tree‑lined path leading to a farmhouse with views over a valley and distant hills; text below labels it as a view toward a meadow and riding area from a guesthouse named 'Landhaus am Waldessaum.' On the right, a young girl sits on a bench beside a tree, with another house and forested hills in the background, labeled as a house with Hochstein. Printed German text at the bottom gives the names and addresses of the properties in Ober‑Schreiberhau in the Riesengebirge mountains.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a damaged windmill on a small hill with several people standing around it. The windmill's tower appears shattered or partially collapsed, with surrounding farm buildings or houses intact in the background. The scene looks like the aftermath of a storm. A caption is printed below the image.

Colorized historical postcard showing a spa or resort building with a pavilion-like Kurhaus set among trees and benches. People in early 20th‑century clothing sit on park benches in the foreground. The caption at the top names the place in Cyrillic and Latin script.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large crowd gathered in a central market square surrounded by multi‑story historic buildings decorated with wreaths and vertical striped flags. Many people wear traditional clothing and hats, forming a procession or festival in the square. Printed caption text appears along the bottom margin and some business signs are visible on the façades.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the interior lobby of an ornate early 20th‑century hotel. The room features large classical columns with decorative capitals, high decorated ceilings with light fixtures, rugs on the floor, and numerous armchairs, rocking chairs, and tables arranged in a spacious seating area. The printed caption at the bottom identifies the scene as the lobby of Hotel Lankershim in Los Angeles, California. A red number "6799." is printed in the upper right corner of the card.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a riverside complex with ornate late‑19th/early‑20th‑century buildings. In the foreground is a river with a stone embankment wall and steps; behind it stands a long, low, richly decorated industrial‑style building with large windows and a small tower, and to the right a taller villa‑like house among trees. The caption in red Gothic‑style type at the top reads "Theresienstadt. Neues Schlachthaus." indicating the new slaughterhouse of Theresienstadt.

Vintage, monochrome postcard depicting a tree‑lined driveway leading to a large hotel building partially visible in the background. There are tall leafy trees, street lamps with overhead wires, benches, and a terrace with tables and chairs in front of the hotel. The scene looks like the entrance area of a grand hotel set in a wooded park. Text is printed in the lower left corner.

Vintage black-and-white postcard view of a small European town in a hilly landscape. In the foreground stands an elegant multi-storey villa or civic building with a mansard roof, central balcony, ivy on the facade, and a clock centered under the roofline. A few people walk on the street in front. Behind this, tightly packed houses and a church with a tower rise up the slope, with wooded hills and terraced fields in the background. At the bottom of the image, red printed text reads "Glashütte i. S." and a smaller publisher credit.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a small rocky seaside harbor with a narrow concrete walkway and stone walls. Several rowboats lie in a sheltered inlet, and a larger sailing boat is moored at a pier where many people are gathered. Low wooded islands are visible in the background. A white wooden building with flags stands on the left. Printed caption text appears in the lower left, and a publisher's mark with a number is in the lower right.

Sepia-toned wartime postcard showing heavily bombed and ruined buildings along a cobblestone street. Rubble fills the foreground, with several people standing among the debris. The printed German caption at the top right identifies the scene as destruction in Mitau, and there is a handwritten correction changing the word 'Kirche' (church) to 'Strasse' (street).

Colorized aerial view of a large institutional complex set amid trees and surrounded by scattered houses and fields. The foreground shows multi‑storey classical buildings with green roofs and a central pedimented façade, likely official or military buildings. In the middle distance is a large rectangular parade ground enclosed by long barracks‑like structures. The landscape behind stretches into gently rolling countryside under a blue sky with a few clouds. Red printed captions in German appear at the top left and top right of the image.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a park-like landscape with tall trees and a calm body of water in the foreground. Across the water stands a richly decorated building with multiple onion domes and towers in Russian Revival style, surrounded by several large villas or hotels with steep roofs and half‑timbered façades. The scene is framed by tree trunks and foliage, giving a picturesque view of the ornate architecture beyond.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a wide landscape view from a forested hillside or cliff down over mixed woodland, fields and a distant lake. The foreground is densely covered with trees on a steep slope at the right, with flatter farmland and additional forest stretching to the horizon and water in the background. At the bottom are printed captions indicating the location and publisher/photographer details.

Color postcard view of a large Gothic church with a tall spire and red-tiled roof facing a spacious central square with formal flowerbeds, lawns and a prominent equestrian monument in the middle. Around the square stand ornate 19th–20th century buildings with domed roofs and a row of parked vintage cars, suggesting a mid‑20th‑century scene. The sky is clear and blue and the area is busy with pedestrians.

Sepia-toned interior view of an ornate hunting or trophy room. Against a high, curtained wall stand two richly carved cabinets with their doors open, displaying elaborate glass and decorative objects. Above each cabinet is a mounted stag head with antlers. In the center is a small table with a mounted bird (a capercaillie). On the floor before the left cabinet is a single antler, and in front of the right cabinet is a pair of intertwined antlers or skulls. At the bottom of the image there are printed German captions identifying the objects.

A black‑and‑white photograph bordered by a white margin showing a calm riverbank scene. In the foreground, a small wooden rowboat is pulled up near the shore. Leafless or sparsely leaved trees line the right bank, with one prominent tree leaning over the water. The left side shows a forested bank and gentle hills in the distance under a cloudy sky. Two small human figures appear further down the shore on the right. There is no visible printed caption or other text on the image side.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a crowded poultry market with numerous plucked birds hanging in rows from the ceiling and stalls. A group of men, likely merchants or customers, stand in front of the hanging poultry. The scene is labeled in French and there is some Greek text and a round stamp on the left. A large website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears across the lower right.

Sepia-toned vintage street scene showing a wide cobblestone avenue lined with multi‑story European-style buildings. People walk along the street and sidewalks; a church spire is visible in the distance. At the top, bilingual text reads in Cyrillic and Latin script. The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century postcard view of an urban center.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing an ornate Moorish courtyard with slender columns, intricate stucco arches and muqarnas decoration. In the center background is the famous fountain supported by lion statues. A light border at the bottom contains printed caption text.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a stone statue of a robed man on a tall pedestal in a formal garden or small square, with evergreen trees and a wall in the background. The base of the statue bears the name "Antonio Rosmini." Printed red captions at the bottom read "Rovereto" and "Monumento Rosmini." There is handwritten cursive text across the lower margin and right side of the image.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a multi‑storey villa with balconies and shuttered windows, surrounded by trees and a picket fence in a hilly, wooded landscape. A sign on the building reads "Unter den Linden". Below the image on the card are printed captions indicating the location and house name, with ample blank space for writing.

A vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a panoramic view over a hillside town and surrounding plain with mountains in the distance. In the middle ground there is a long complex of light-colored buildings with towers or tall sections, possibly part of a monastery or institutional complex. Printed captions in Greek and French identify the place, and handwritten Greek text appears along the bottom margin. The style is typical of early 20th‑century view postcards.

A monochrome cityscape view printed in an old-photographic style. In the foreground a river curves past a stone embankment and a multi‑arch bridge. On the right stands a large brick industrial or civic building with tall arched windows. Across the river are late‑19th‑century townhouses and commercial buildings, with a tall factory chimney and a church spire rising above the roofs. Hills form the hazy background. The title in red Gothic‑style type at the top left reads "Blick auf Aue i. Erzgeb."

Black‑and‑white aerial/raised view over a broad dirt street lined with trees and wooden buildings leading to a central square with market stalls, horses and carriages. At the far end of the axis stands a large church with a tall central spire, backed by forested hills. Below the image, centered in the white border, is the printed caption "LAHTI".

Monochrome postcard-style illustration of a medieval town wall with multiple large round defensive towers topped with conical roofs. The wall runs alongside a street lined with low houses; in the background more towers and a church spire are visible. Trees frame the scene in the foreground. There is a small vertical notation with numbers and letters along the right border.

A black-and-white postcard view of a broad, tree-lined street bordered by early 20th‑century buildings. On the right side is a brick building with a large sign reading "PALLADIUM" above a cinema or theater entrance; pedestrians and bicycles line the sidewalk. The left side shows lower wooden and masonry shopfronts. Benches and a walkway run along the tree row in the center. Printed caption text appears at the bottom left and a photographer/publisher imprint at the bottom right.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard with scalloped edges shows a rural landscape viewed from a shaded uphill road framed by large overhanging tree branches. The road leads down to a narrow bridge crossing a river or valley and continues toward a small settlement of scattered houses and farm buildings in open fields with low hills in the distance. Wooden utility poles line the road. The caption "GAUJIENA." appears in white letters at the lower left of the image, and small initials and numbers ("PM RIGA 187") appear at the lower right.

Black‑and‑white photograph of the interior of a church showing a richly painted altarpiece mural within a large arched apse. The mural depicts Christ and numerous angels and saints in several tiers, with pews in the foreground. Small printed caption text appears along the bottom edge of the image.
