Caption on the image reads "Ljubljana" and "Špitalske ulice." The reverse side has the word "Tiskovina" and a typical divided back for mailing.

Colorized early-20th‑century postcard showing a bustling city square with a prominent statue, tram tracks and a bridge over a river, surrounded by multi‑story buildings. Caption on the front reads in Slovene and German "Ljubljana – Marijin trg / Laibach." The reverse bears an Austro‑Hungarian stamp, a purple censorship mark, handwritten message and an address to Hall in Tyrol.

Colorized view of a central square with the Prešeren Monument (a statue of poet France Prešeren with a muse above) in front of ornate Secession-era buildings. Printed Slovenian captions appear at top left. The reverse shows handwritten message and address in German script with an Austro-Hungarian green 5 heller stamp and a Laibach postmark.

Tinted photograph postcard showing a statue in a central square with ornate late‑19th‑century façades behind it. The caption at top reads "Ljubljana – Prešernov spomenik". The statue base bears the name "PRESEREN". The reverse has the word "DOPISNICA" and blank address lines, with a round Ljubljana stamp impression and a printed note at bottom "Iz zapuščine T. Zupana".

Colorized vintage postcard showing a central square and street scene in Ljubljana with ornate late‑19th‑century buildings, a tram, pedestrians, and Ljubljana Castle on the hill in the background. Caption at top reads "LJUBLJANA – LAIBACH – Stritarjeva ul." The reverse has handwritten message and address with postal markings and a green stamp.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square with the Prešeren Monument and the façade of the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation, surrounded by Secession-era buildings. Handwritten message overlays the image. The reverse side has dense handwriting, the word "Dopisnica," postal marks, and an address.

Vintage black‑and‑white view of a Central European square with a lone statue on a pedestal in the foreground, rows of ornate late‑19th‑century buildings, and a large hilltop castle dominating the background. The reverse side is a divided back with the word "DOPISNICA." at top and a circular library stamp.

Colorized early-20th‑century postcard showing a lively city square with a tram, horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians, lined with ornate Secession-era buildings. A hilltop castle rises in the background. The printed caption reads "Laibach. Stritar gasse." The reverse bears dense handwritten German text, Austrian postmarks and a green 5‑heller stamp.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing central Ljubljana with a view over the Ljubljanica River toward the main square, labeled Marijin trg/Marienplatz. A stone bridge spans the river (the earlier Franz's Bridge, later part of the Triple Bridge). The Franciscan Church is visible on the left and historic buildings line the square. The reverse has a handwritten message, a postage stamp and cancellations.

Tinted photo postcard showing the Prešeren Monument in a city square: a bronze figure of the poet France Prešeren at the base with a muse above on a tall pedestal, surrounded by historic buildings. The reverse has the printed word 'Dopisnica', an Austro‑Hungarian green stamp canceled in Ljubljana, and a handwritten address/message.

Colorized city view over the Ljubljanica River toward a central square. A stone bridge crosses the river and a pink Baroque church with twin towers (Franciscan Church of the Annunciation) stands on the left. Ornate late‑19th‑century buildings line the right bank (including the Kresija building). People and carriages are visible. Bilingual caption on the front reads in Slovene and German, and the divided back shows a library stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the Prešeren Monument in Ljubljana: a statue of the poet France Prešeren with a muse above, on a stepped pedestal. Caption in Slovene appears under the image. The reverse reads "DOPISNICA." with an Austrian 9‑heller stamp, LAIBACH (Ljubljana) and WIEN postmarks dated November 1905, and handwritten message and address.

Colorized view of central Ljubljana showing the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation on the square labeled "Marijin trg," with the Prešeren Monument in front and a bridge over the Ljubljanica River in the foreground. The caption at top reads "LJUBLJANA – LAIBACH – Marijin trg." The reverse has handwritten text, Laibach/Ljubljana postmarks, and an address to Vienna.

Colorized early-20th-century view of Prešeren Square in Ljubljana, showing the Prešeren Monument in the center, the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation behind it, a bridge over the Ljubljanica River in the foreground, and street activity with pedestrians and a tram. The reverse reads 'Dopisnica' and bears an Austro-Hungarian postage stamp with handwritten address.

Sepia view of a central square in Ljubljana labeled 'Marijin trg' with people walking, a prominent statue in the middle (Prešeren Monument), and Ljubljana Castle on the hill in the background. The reverse shows handwritten message, address, Austrian postage and postmarks.

Colorized vintage view across the Ljubljanica River toward Prešeren Square (labeled Marijin trg). The Triple Bridge spans the river; the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation is visible on the left and the Kresija building on the right. The reverse shows a handwritten German message, an Austrian stamp, and a Laibach postmark.

Hand-tinted cityscape showing a central square with ornate late‑19th‑century buildings and pedestrians, with a large hilltop fortress rising above the town. Caption at top reads "Ljubljana (Laibach)." The reverse has a handwritten message, a purple postmark, and an Austrian 10 heller stamp.

Tinted city view showing Prešeren Monument and Stritarjeva ulica with crowds and historic buildings in the foreground, and Ljubljana Castle on the hill behind. The front has bilingual captions in Slovene and German. The reverse is a written correspondence card with an Austrian stamp and postmarks, addressed to Traunstein, Oberbayern.

Colorized view of Ljubljana's central square labeled "Ljubljana — Marijin trg," showing the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation beside the Ljubljanica River, a single bridge, the statue in the square, trams and pedestrians. The reverse has a handwritten message, an Austro‑Hungarian stamp and postmarks.

Sepia photograph of a dense public gathering in a central square before an ornate Secession-era building with shopfronts labeled as a pharmacy. A tall sculptural monument stands to the right side of the square. The reverse shows multilingual 'Carte postale' layout with stamps and handwritten Slovenian/Croatian text, addressed to Ljubljana.

Tinted view of central Ljubljana showing the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation facing a square labeled "Marijin trg," with a round fountain/monument in the middle, the Ljubljanica river in the foreground and the old central bridge. The reverse bears a handwritten message and an Austro‑Hungarian 5 heller stamp with postal cancels.

Colorized view of Ljubljana's central square with the Baroque Franciscan Church of the Annunciation on the left, the Prešeren Monument in the foreground, and ornate Secession-era buildings on the right. The front caption reads "Ljubljana – Marijin trg." The reverse shows handwritten message, an Austrian green stamp with a Laibach (Ljubljana) postmark, and an address to Vienna.

Colorized panoramic postcard showing central Ljubljana: the Ljubljanica River with a stone bridge and, across the square, the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation. The right view is labeled 'Marijin trg' (Mary's Square), depicting the square and surrounding historic buildings. The reverse has two green Austrian 5 Heller stamps and a handwritten message/address.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a central square in Ljubljana with the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation dominating the right side, a statue/monument in the middle of the square, and surrounding fin‑de‑siècle buildings. The reverse has a handwritten message, an Austro‑Hungarian green 5‑heller stamp, and several postmarks.

Colorized view of a central European square with the pink Baroque Franciscan Church facing a statue in the middle of the square. People, a cart, and surrounding historic buildings are visible. The printed caption identifies Ljubljana and the Prešeren monument. The reverse shows a green Austrian stamp, postmarks, handwritten address, and the word DOPISNICA.

Colorized early‑20th‑century view of a European city square with a tram, pedestrians, and ornate buildings around a bridge over a river. The printed caption identifies it as Prešeren Square with the Franciscan Bridge in Laibach (Ljubljana). The reverse shows handwritten address text and Laibach postmarks.

Colorized street scene showing a central European square with a tram, pedestrians, and ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. In the middle stands a monument in Prešeren Square, with the Franciscan Church area and bridge in the background. The caption on the front is in German and labels the view as Laibach (Ljubljana), Prešeren-Platz with the Franciscan Bridge. The reverse has handwritten German text, an Austrian stamp, and a Laibach postmark.

Tinted view of central Ljubljana showing the river Ljubljanica, a stone bridge and the square labeled "Marijin trg," with the prominent Baroque facade of the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation and surrounding buildings. The reverse shows a handwritten message and address with the printed word "Dopisnica," an Austrian 5 Heller stamp and postal cancellations.

Colorized panoramic view of a central square with a stone bridge over a river in the foreground, trams and pedestrians in the square, historic multi‑story buildings around the plaza, and a church façade at the right. The back shows handwritten message, address lines, and a green postage stamp.

Colorized view of a riverside square with a statue in the foreground, tram and pedestrians, and historic buildings along the Ljubljanica River. Printed caption in Slovene and German reads that it is Ljubljana/Laibach and identifies the square and the Prešeren monument. The reverse shows dense handwritten text and postal markings.

Color‑tinted view of central Ljubljana (Laibach) showing the Prešeren Monument on what was then Marienplatz/Marijin trg, beside the Ljubljanica River with a single bridge, a tram and pedestrians. The reverse has handwritten correspondence, an Austrian 10 heller stamp, and Laibach postmarks.

Color-tinted city view showing a baroque pink church on a square beside a river bridge with a tram and pedestrians. The scene is the central square with the Franciscan Church of the Annunciation in Ljubljana, looking over the Triple Bridge area.

Tinted view of a central square with a statue and a tram in the foreground, surrounded by ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. A hilltop fortress (Ljubljana Castle) rises behind the square. The front caption is bilingual and labels the scene as Ljubljana/Laibach, Marijin trg/Marienplatz. The reverse shows a divided back with address lines and a stamp box.

Tinted real-photo postcard showing the bronze Prešeren Monument in front of ornate Secession-era buildings with signs for a pharmacy and a café, in central Ljubljana. The reverse has a handwritten message, an Austrian 10 heller stamp, and postmarks.

Color-tinted view of a central square with an ornate Art Nouveau building crowned by a dome (Grand Hotel Union area) and a statue/fountain in the foreground. The caption on the front reads "Ljubljana — Laibach." The reverse shows handwritten correspondence, an Austrian-era green stamp, a circular postmark, and a purple Ljubljana library stamp.

Tinted view of a central square in Ljubljana with an ornate multi‑story building and a statue/monument in the foreground. Caption on the image reads "Ljubljana — Marijin trg — Laibach." The reverse shows dense handwritten German text, an address, and an Austrian 5‑heller stamp with a Laibach/Ljubljana postmark.

Colorized view of a European city square with an early electric tram, a central monument, and ornate fin‑de‑siècle buildings; the Franciscan church fronts the square and a hilltop castle rises behind. The reverse shows dense German handwriting, a Laibach postmark, and a green Austro‑Hungarian stamp.

Monochrome panoramic postcard showing a rural valley with fields and a village on a hill. A baroque-style church with an onion-dome tower stands prominently, surrounded by scattered farmhouses and forested hills. A small roadside shrine is visible in the foreground. The printed caption at the top reads "St. Georgen b. Völkermarkt."

Monochrome printed view of a small town in hilly terrain. Numerous gabled houses cluster around a hill crowned by a large church with a tall spire and an adjoining multi‑storey building. Caption at bottom left reads "Teinach in Kärnten." and small print at bottom right reads "Nachdruck verboten."

Black‑and‑white postcard with two vignettes: on the left a studio portrait of an elderly clergyman with the caption below, and on the right a panoramic view of a rural village in a valley dominated by a church steeple. Decorative foliage frames the images. Slovene captions appear above and below the village view.

Hand-tinted streetscape showing a grand late‑19th‑century building with green shutters and a shop awning labeled as a department store and café. People stand on a quiet tree-lined street in a resort town setting, with hills in the background.

Colorized view of a multi‑arch stone bridge over a blue-green river with alpine mountains behind. Front caption reads "Tolmin. Most čez Sočo." The reverse says "Dopisnica." and bears an Austro‑Hungarian 5‑heller Franz Joseph stamp with a postmark reading Tolmein; there is a purple library handstamp.

Colorized panorama of a small town in a mountain valley with a prominent church tower; caption reads "Tolmin." Handwritten message across the lower margin. The reverse shows the heading "Correspondenz-Karte / Dopisnica," a green 5 heller Austro‑Hungarian stamp with Tolmin postmark, and a German-language address.

Vintage black-and-white postcard with two photographs of stone ruins on a wooded hill, with several people posing among the walls and an arched opening. The caption at bottom reads "TOLMIN. Stari grad. Kozlov rob." The reverse has the word "Dopisnica," a green Austro‑Hungarian stamp with postmark, a long handwritten message in German, and an address to Klagenfurt. Publisher credit reads "Fotograf Weiss, Gorica."

Early 20th‑century postcard with a small colorized panorama of a town in a valley backed by low mountains, featuring a church steeple. The card bears Austro‑Hungarian postal markings, a green 5‑heller stamp with Emperor Franz Joseph, circular cancellations reading TOLMIN, Slovene printed text such as "Poštna spremnica" and "Dopisnica," a wax seal, and dense handwritten address and message.

Two-view color postcard: the upper view shows a white church with a tall spire beside an official-looking building, captioned in Slovene; the lower view shows a tree-lined street and large buildings in a town, captioned "Pozdrav iz TOLMINA." The reverse reads "DOPISNICA," bears an Austrian 5‑heller green stamp with a TOLMIN postmark, address in cursive Slovene, and a round library stamp.

Early 20th‑century black‑and‑white postcard with a panoramic view of the town of Tolmin and its surrounding fields and hills; a church spire is prominent. Caption reads "Pozdrav iz Tolmina." Publisher credit is printed along the left edge. Handwritten message is on the image front. The back shows an address written in Slovene to Anton Mervic in Povirje pri Sežani, with an Austro‑Hungarian 5‑heller stamp and circular postmarks.

Black‑and‑white postcard labeled "TOLMIN." showing a long multi‑arch bridge crossing a river in a mountainous valley (Soča Valley). The reverse has a green 5‑heller Austro‑Hungarian stamp, a Tolmin postmark, and a handwritten German message addressed to a recipient in Kranj.

Tinted, Art-Nouveau–framed panorama of the town of Tolmin set in a valley with surrounding hills and a prominent church tower. The reverse shows handwritten Slovene text, the heading "Dopisnica," an Austro‑Hungarian green 5‑heller stamp with Emperor Franz Joseph, postal cancels, and a purple circular stamp.

Black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard showing three scenes: a long building along a street, a horse‑drawn carriage with men beside a rocky road, and a panoramic view of a valley town dominated by a conical hill. Caption on the front reads a greeting from Tolmin; handwritten date appears as 1912. The reverse is a standard multilingual 'Postkarte — Carte postale' back with a circular postmark of Tolmin and a receiving/library stamp from Ljubljana, addressed to Trieste.

Tinted view of a river valley with mountains and a multi‑arch stone bridge in the foreground. The caption on the picture side reads "Pozdrav iz Tolmina." The reverse shows the word "Dopisnica," a green 5‑heller Austro‑Hungarian stamp with a circular postmark reading TOLMIN, handwritten message and address, and a small publisher's line.

A vintage multi-view postcard with sepia photographs showing a panoramic view of Tolmin and a couple of notable buildings, plus a small vignette of a hill or forest hut. The front bears the caption in Slovene 'Pozdrav iz Tolmina.' The reverse is a bilingual Austro‑Hungarian correspondence card ('Correspondenz-Karte. Dopisnica.') addressed in black ink, with an Austrian stamp and circular postmarks.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a small Alpine town with scattered houses and fields, mountains in the background, and a prominent church with a tall bell tower on a low hill. The reverse side has a green Austrian stamp (Franz Joseph I), circular postmarks, a purple office mark, and handwritten message/address.

Colorized panoramic view of a small town in a mountain valley labeled "TOLMIN." A white church with a tall bell tower stands near the center, with clustered houses, fields, and forested hills; a river is visible in the background. The reverse shows handwritten message and address, an Austrian 5-heller green stamp with a Tolmin postmark, and a purple library stamp; destination appears to be Trieste.

Historic tinted postcard with Art Nouveau border. The front shows the word 'Tolmin' beneath a white–blue–red tricolor flag and a small vignette of a town park with a circular flowerbed and fountain surrounded by people; a small shield with a castle motif is below. The reverse is an address side labeled 'Dopisnica' with a green 5‑Heller Austro‑Hungarian stamp (Franz Joseph I) and a circular postmark reading 'Tolmein', plus handwritten message.

Colorized vintage postcard. The front shows a mountainous valley with a long multi‑arch stone bridge over a river; the back has the word "Dopisnica.", a green Austro‑Hungarian stamp with postmarks, and handwritten address/message.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the facade of an inn with signs reading P. ACHATZ and Gasthof/ Gasthaus Anton Achatz. People stand at the entrance and lean from windows; a horse stands by a fence. Handwritten German text appears along the top edge, and a printed caption at the bottom identifies the place.

Black‑and‑white historical street scene showing a town center under floodwater. People wade through water between early 20th‑century buildings with striped window awnings. A corner café/bakery is visible, utility poles and overhead wires cross the scene, and the street rises uphill in the distance.

Black‑and‑white view of a long wooden trestle bridge stretching over calm water beside a rocky, pine‑lined shore. A seated person is visible in the foreground. The printed red caption reads "HAMAR BRO," with a small clover logo and the publisher credit at the bottom.

Old black‑and‑white postcard view of a lakeshore with many wooden rowboats pulled up on the bank, looking toward a tree‑covered islet/peninsula across calm water. Caption at bottom reads "HAMAR — TYVEHOLMEN." There is a handwritten holiday greeting across the lower margin.

Vintage black‑and‑white winter view of a hilltop parish church with a tall spire and arched windows, surrounded by bare trees and snow. A small bridge crosses a stream in the foreground. Caption at the bottom reads "Fra Vangs kirke."

Hand-tinted vintage studio photograph of a young woman in Norwegian folk costume (bunad) with a plaid apron and red bodice, carrying two wooden pails. She stands before a painted backdrop of mountains and a fjord. The bottom border bears the photographer/publisher name and a copyright year.

Sepia postcard showing two small boys in fur‑trimmed winter coats and folk caps standing on wooden skis in a snowy landscape. Caption at the bottom reads "Smaagutter paa Ski" with the credit "Wilse." The reverse has a Norwegian 'BREVKORT — CARTE POSTALE' layout, a handwritten Christmas greeting dated 1915, and an address to Einar Johannessen. Publisher imprint reads "A/S B. M. Schönbergs Kunstforlag, Kristiania."

Hand‑tinted winter scene showing a skier using an old single‑pole technique on a snowy slope above two women wearing Norwegian folk costumes (bunad) in a forested, icy landscape. The photographer's mark "Wilse" appears on the front. The reverse reads "BREVKORT FRA NORGE" with a green 5 øre NORGE stamp and a circular postmark.

Black‑and‑white photo postcard showing a powerful waterfall plunging into a steep rocky gorge. Captioned at lower left with the waterfall's name; publishing/photographer credit appears at lower right. The reverse has a divided-back layout typical of early 20th‑century postcards.

Colorized photograph of a wooden birdhouse mounted among leafing, budding branches of a tree against a pastel sky. No identifiable landmark is shown. The reverse has Norwegian postal text, a green Norwegian stamp, and Kristiania postmarks.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over a hilly coastal city and harbor with many small buildings and ships. The caption identifies the scene as a view toward Egersheld in Vladivostok. The reverse bears Russian pre‑reform Cyrillic text alongside French "Carte Postale," a Red Cross emblem of the St. Eugenia community, address lines, and a box for the stamp.

Colorized lithographic postcard showing a neoclassical railway station with a central clock tower, carriages and pedestrians in front. Captions in Russian and French identify it as the Nikolaevsky railway station in Moscow. The reverse bears Imperial Russian UPU headings in Russian and French and an undivided back with address-only lines.

Sepia winter cityscape of Vladivostok showing snow-covered hills, an onion-domed Orthodox church prominently on a slope, nearby buildings, and a slender commemorative column. A frozen waterfront is in the foreground. The front caption is bilingual (Russian/French). The reverse bears pre‑revolution Russian UPU postcard text.

Sepia-toned view of a fortified Chinese city gate with an upper pavilion, ox carts and people passing through a stone arch, captioned in Russian and English: 'Views and types of Manchuria. Girin. The town-gate.' The reverse is a Russian Empire UPU postcard with red pre-1918 Russian orthography, space for a stamp, censorship approval dated 12 March 1903, and the printer 'T-vo Golike i Vilʹborg.'

Sepia photo postcard showing a busy Japanese shopping street with wooden shopfronts, tall utility poles, rickshaws and pedestrians in kimono. Signboards in Japanese hang over the shops. A blue caption at the bottom reads "Isezakicho‑dori Yokohama." The reverse has a blue "POST CARD" heading, a stamp box, and vertical Japanese printing.

Tinted view of the harbor and hillside settlement of Chefoo (treaty‑port era Yantai) with small boats on the water and European‑style buildings along the shore. At lower left is a small vignette portrait of a Chinese woman in traditional dress beside a vase of flowers. Captions include the city name and German publisher credit. The back is a multilingual "Postkarte — Carte postale" layout with dotted address lines typical of early postcards.

Colorized early-20th-century street view postcard showing Tverskaya Street in Moscow. Pedestrians in period dress walk between ornate multi‑story buildings with striped shop awnings; horse-drawn vehicles are visible. The reverse has Russian pre‑reform and French UPU postcard headings.

Sepia image of a Chinese-style stone bridge with a small pavilion on top, spanning water in an imperial garden. The front leaves a large blank area for writing; a faint German caption runs beneath the picture. The reverse reads in German and French with dotted address lines.

Hand-colored postcard showing a yellow Qing imperial dragon flag at left, with a black‑and‑white framed panorama of a coastal harbor and town labeled 'Chefoo'. Publisher imprint at bottom reads 'Verlag von H. Sietas & Co., Chefoo.' The reverse is a multilingual UPU postcard back with address lines.

Colorized street view of a broad avenue with pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing and horse‑drawn carriages. A cast‑iron fence lines a park or garden on the right; historic buildings rise beyond, including a classical structure with a rooftop belvedere. Legends printed below the image read in Russian and French: "Москва - Moscou" and "Знаменка - Rue Znamenka." Publisher credit appears at lower left.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a waterfront view with small boats on a wide river and a tree-lined promenade with colonial-era buildings behind it. Caption reads 'Shanghai. View of the Public Gardens and Bund.' The reverse side is undivided with 'POSTCARD' printed at the top and dotted address lines.

Black‑and‑white real‑photo postcard showing a cobblestoned downhill street leading to a central square. At the far side of the square stands a neoclassical church with a pedimented facade and a tall open bell tower topped by a dome. An early automobile is parked at the curb and a few pedestrians walk along the street. The back is printed in Finnish/French with a Viipuri (Vyborg) photo credit.

Black‑and‑white street view labeled Viipuri, showing a cobbled avenue with tram tracks, pedestrians, and shopfronts with awnings. A vertical sign reads "PARTURI" and, in the distance, the large arched facade of the market hall is visible. The reverse has a divided back with Finnish–Swedish imprint, a penciled/inked catalog number, and the handwritten name "Hugo E. Liljestrand."

Sepia-toned postcard showing a rural school complex: a larger wooden school building with two chimneys and a gabled section with large windows, front steps and porch railings, and a long outbuilding to the left set in a field. The back reads 'UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE / CARTE POSTALE / SUOMI - FINLAND' with Swedish publisher and caption indicating Petsmo.

Vintage real-photo postcard showing a studio portrait of five sailors in double‑breasted pea coats and striped undershirts. Their naval caps have Cyrillic tallies that appear to read "КРОНШТАДТ." The reverse is a divided‑back postcard with dotted address lines and a brief handwritten note dated 18/19.

Sepia studio portrait of a woman in a dark dress and large turban-style hat standing beside a wicker bench with a small child in a lace bonnet and dark outfit. Painted backdrop with trees and a village scene. The reverse has Swedish handwriting with a New Year greeting and an address, plus a circular archive stamp.

Decorative early 20th‑century postcard with an Art Nouveau floral frame enclosing a black‑and‑white photo of a neoclassical city administration building bearing the sign "Городская управа." Hills and adjacent buildings appear in the background. Bilingual captions in Russian and German read "Владивостокъ / Wladiwostok" and "Городская управа. / Stadt‑Verwaltung." The back is undivided with Russian and French UPU headings.

Tinted view of a long neoclassical building with domed pavilions along a riverside embankment, with barges and piers on the water in the foreground. The caption at top reads in Russian and French: 'Москва - Moscou Воспитательный домъ - Maison des Orphelins.'

Tinted view of a large, white Orthodox cathedral with golden domes seen from across a riverside embankment with a wooden walkway and small riverside structures. The captions in Russian and French identify Moscow and the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour. The back bears Russian Empire UPU headings and undivided address lines; card edges are torn.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a line of Chinese men in traditional clothing standing outdoors, likely in a garden or park. A printed caption in Russian and French identifies them as people from Canton (Guangzhou).

Early 20th‑century Russian postcard showing a dusty street lined with Chinese‑style walled compounds and ornate tiled roofs, likely a trading quarter. The front caption in Russian reads "Street in Maimacheng." The reverse has Russian/French UPU headings and a stamp box.

Tinted view of the classical, domed main building of Moscow University with a grand colonnade, seen from the street behind a gated fence. Pedestrians walk along the sidewalk. Titles are printed in Russian and French at the top. The reverse is a Russian Empire UPU postcard back with address-only lines and bilingual Russian–French instructions.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an ossuary chapel attached to a churchyard with a medieval tower and wall. Murals are painted on the chapel façade. Caption at the bottom identifies the site. The reverse has a green Swiss 'HELVETIA' 10‑rappen stamp, a circular MUTTENZ BASELLAND postmark dated 30.XII.27, and a handwritten German message addressed to Basel.

Illustrated postcard showing two early photographers working in a studio with box cameras, chemical trays, and prints. A ribbon reads the names of the photography pioneers Niépce and Daguerre. The artist's signature appears at the bottom. The reverse says CARTE POSTALE and notes it was produced in Paris and sold for the benefit of the Secours National.

A French philatelic postcard featuring a black‑and‑white portrait of (Nicéphore) Niépce with commemorative text for the bicentenary of his birth. There is a French postage stamp and a circular cancel reading "PHOTO ET PHILATELIE 76-ROUEN 9X66." The reverse shows a standard postcard back with the imprint of the Club Philatélique de Rouen et Région / Ciné Photo‑Club.

Sepia postcard showing a small wooden house by the shoreline and a stone pier with people in early 20th‑century clothing. Caption at the top reads "Lilla Ångbåtsbryggan, Gustafsberg, Uddevalla." The reverse has Swedish handwriting, is labeled "Brevkort / CARTE-POSTALE," and bears a red Swedish 10 öre stamp with an early 1910s postmark. Addressed to Fröken Elie Bergman in Kristianstad.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a wooden museum building with ornate gables and a flag flying on the roof. People in early 20th‑century attire stand in front of the building, with other houses and low hills in the background. The card is captioned with the location and date.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing two wooden rural buildings in open countryside. Caption in Swedish reads "Töllås Grufva och Handelsbod" (Töllås Mine and General Store). The reverse has Swedish handwriting, a red 10 öre SVERIGE stamp with a 1919 postmark, and an address.

Sepia postcard showing a crowd with wreaths gathered around the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier beneath the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. Printed bilingual caption at top. The reverse reads "CARTE POSTALE," with a handwritten French message and an address to 52 Rue de Lévis, 17e, Paris. It bears French stamps, including one reading "COTE FRANCAISE DES SOMALIS."

Old sepia postcard. Front: four Serbian soldiers in WWI-era uniforms sit at a café table with a bottle and glasses; civilians stand behind them. French wording is painted on the building façade. A handwritten Cyrillic note runs vertically along the right edge. Back: the card is filled with a long handwritten message in Serbian Cyrillic with an address section on the right.

Vintage sepia photographic postcard showing a seated studio portrait of a man in traditional Serbian dress (vest, wide sash, embroidered socks and opanci sandals) in a wicker chair. Handwritten Serbian Cyrillic text appears on both sides, including a date 10‑IX‑1917 and references to Čačak and Atenica. Address layout with stamp box on the back.

Real photo postcard showing a black‑and‑white portrait of two men in suits. A handwritten message in Serbian runs across the top and left margin of the photo. The reverse has the standard 'CARTE POSTALE' layout with a red Swiss 10 rappen Helvetia stamp, machine cancel and circular postmark from Bern dated 23.VIII.1917. There is a pink censor/transfer handstamp reading FELDKIRCH and the address is written to Serbia.

Handwritten military field postcard in Serbian Cyrillic. The message side is dated 'Тирана, 11-11-1913. године' and contains a long note in purple ink. The address side bears the red coat of arms and the printed heading 'КРАЉЕВИНА СРБИЈА' and 'ВОЈНИЧКА ДОПИСНА КАРТА', with an added note 'са Јадр. мора'. It is addressed to a recipient named Миленко Ракићевић in the village of Губеревац, Serbia.

Two-sided WWI-era postal card. One side is a long handwritten message in Serbian Cyrillic dated 8 March 1918 with the place name written as "Шели" (Šeli). The other side is a French-format back reading "CARTE POSTALE," with French postal instructions, several postal cancellations and a purple censor/office mark. It is addressed in French to a recipient in "Salonique" (Thessaloniki) with military post number "S.P. 216." The sender's address line mentions "à Chebli, Alger." No photograph or landmark is depicted.

Sepia group photograph of several dozen boys and a few adults posing outdoors with shovels and hoes in a garden beside a brick-and-plaster building; early 20th‑century attire (suspenders, flat caps, straw hats). The reverse is a French postcard layout with handwritten notes mentioning dates in 1918 and the place Semur (Côte-d'Or).

Vintage Serbian postcard. The front shows a black‑and‑white studio portrait of a young man in a suit wearing a Serbian šajkača-style cap. The reverse has Serbian Cyrillic print reading 'Србија' and 'Дописна Карта', a purple circular postmark from Vrnjačka Banja dated 24 IX 1913, vertical imprint of a local photo studio, and a handwritten message/address in purple ink.

Vintage sepia photo postcard showing four uniformed soldiers standing outdoors in winter conditions, likely within a POW camp with wooden barracks in the background. The photo bears a blind embossed censor/approval seal and a photographer credit along the edge. The address side carries printed and stamped Serbian Red Cross information for Geneva, German notations referring to a prisoner-of-war sender from Königsbrück (Saxony), and a handwritten addressee.

Sepia photographic postcard showing two children in traditional rural costume with clogs and hats, holding an umbrella, captioned in French. A handwritten Serbian (Cyrillic) note appears on the image margin. The reverse has French "CARTE POSTALE" layout with a long Serbian message dated 16‑VI‑1917, military censor/field‑post markings, and an address written to Salonique (Thessaloniki).

Vintage postcard showing a long row of port warehouses with a large administrative building and street trams in front. Caption at the bottom reads "63 - MARSEILLE - Les Docks - E. L." The reverse says "CARTE POSTALE," carries military postal cancellations dated 13.8.18, a purple boxed "18," and a handwritten address to a military postal sector in Salonique, with a long message in Cyrillic script.

Sepia portrait postcard showing a seated woman in a flowing dress; the image is captioned in French with the performer's name and role from the series title. The reverse bears "CARTE POSTALE," military franchise marks, postal cancellations, a long handwritten message in Serbian Cyrillic, and an address to the Serbian Army in Salonique (Thessaloniki).

Sepia photographic postcard showing a uniformed soldier's studio portrait on the left and, on the right, a Swiss pre-printed red stamp with "HELVETIA 10" and trilingual "Postkarte. Carte postale. Cartolina postale – SCHWEIZ SUISSE SVIZZERA." It bears a GENÈVE postmark and handwritten address to Serbia (Čačak–Guča). The reverse contains a long message in Serbian dated 1‑VII‑1917.

Sepia studio portrait of a World War I-era soldier standing with one hand on his hip, wearing puttees and a tunic with a high collar. The reverse side is a filled-in prisoner-of-war postcard with French handwriting, German printed heading, censor marks, and address lines to France.

World War I prisoner-of-war camp postcard. Bilingual printed headings in German and French indicate it was sent from Kriegsgefangenenlager 2, Münster i. W. (Germany). The message side contains a long handwritten note in French dated 9 June 1918. The address side is to Mademoiselle Fl. Robin, rue du Cimetière, Auvers‑le‑Hamon (La Flèche, Sarthe), France, and bears German censor markings.

Old sepia real-photo postcard showing a studio portrait of a mustachioed man in a French uniform with a side cap, standing beside a chair and holding a pipe. The reverse reads 'CARTE POSTALE' with French cursive message and an address to a recipient in Puy-de-Dôme (Auvergne), France.

Mailed postcard with a printed tramping-themed motif reading "TO 49" beside a tipi and horse, vertical "© FORTYMILE post card." Addressed in Czech with a Czechoslovak 50h stamp bearing the national coat of arms. The reverse contains a handwritten Czech message beginning "Ahoj Jarde!" followed by several signatures.

Tinted view of an ornate, octagonal pavilion over a mineral spring with ivy‑clad cast‑iron columns, set in a spa garden. People in early 20th‑century attire stroll and sit on benches. Caption at top reads "Bad Pyrmont. Hauptquelle." The reverse shows a museum stamp, publisher imprint from Munich, a card number, and pencil notations.

Sepia-tone postcard showing the interior of an entertainment hall with ornate columns, hanging lamps, wicker seating around tables, a piano, framed paintings, and decorative busts. Caption on the front reads 'Unterhaltungssaal' and 'Richters Pension, Bad Pyrmont'. The back is a divided postcard with a museum stamp reading 'MUSEUM IM SCHLOSS BAD PYRMONT' and some penciled catalog numbers.

Sepia photo postcard showing a large baroque-style church facade with a small belfry and cross, attached to a multi‑windowed hospital building on a town square. A handwritten X marks one window. The printed caption reads "LÜGDE" at left and "Krankenhaus" at right. Reverse has German handwriting, a green Deutsches Reich 6‑pfennig stamp and a cancellation, and the printer's line for Lügde. Also printed is "Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont."

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard depicting a large colonnaded spa hotel with trees and planters in front. Printed caption at top right reads "Bad Pyrmont. Fürstl. Kurhotel." The image side is overlaid with handwritten German text. The reverse shows a green "Deutsches Reich" postage stamp with a Pyrmont postmark, a handwritten address, and a blue museum stamp reading "MUSEUM IM SCHLOSS BAD PYRMONT."

Sepia real-photo postcard showing six people posed outdoors in a garden: three men in Imperial German military uniforms with Iron Cross decorations, one man in civilian suit and hat, and two women in Edwardian-era dresses and broad hats (one with a white fur stole).

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a vine‑covered pergola walkway in a lush park. Caption reads "Bad Pyrmont. Rosengang am Schloßteich." The reverse has German handwriting, the printed line "Deutschlands schönster Kurpark," a blue cachet "MUSEUM IM SCHLOSS BAD PYRMONT," and a green 6‑Pfennig Deutsches Reich stamp. Dated 19.5.39 in pencil.

Sepia studio portrait of a young man in a suit with a high detachable collar and tie. A caption strip below reads "Dr George Altman." The reverse shows a divided-back postcard layout and a black stamp for a museum in Bad Pyrmont, Germany.

Chromolithographic multi-view postcard with the caption 'Gruss aus Bad Driburg', showing a panoramic view of the spa town, a vignette of 'Logirhäuser' (lodging houses), and the 'Brunnenhalle' with strolling visitors. The reverse reads 'Postkarte' and bears a green 5 Pfennig REICHSPOST stamp cancelled in Driburg (Westfalen); addressed to Bielefeld and stamped with a blue archive mark 'Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont'.

Vintage black‑and‑white illustrated collage postcard with a ribbon caption reading "Gruss aus Pyrmont." It shows the 'Neues Kurhaus' (a grand spa house with a flag on top), a tree‑lined 'Haupt Allee,' and a small inset view labeled 'Der Brunnenplatz.'

Sepia-toned postcard showing a Romanesque church with three apses and a small bell gable, captioned "Barsinghausen – Kirche." The reverse reads "POSTKARTE," bears a green 5‑Pfennig Deutsches Reich stamp with a Hannover-area cancel, is addressed in German to Welsede near Pyrmont, and has a later blue museum stamp from Bad Pyrmont.

Black‑and‑white view of a grand spa complex with a long colonnaded facade and mansard roof lined with dormer windows. A terrace with café tables sits before broad stairways; mature trees frame the scene and a person stands in the foreground. Printed greeting text appears in the top right. The reverse shows German handwriting, a green 'Postkarte' imprint, a Deutsches Reich stamp canceled in Pyrmont, and a purple museum stamp.

Sepia-toned view of a neoclassical spa complex with a domed pavilion and long colonnades. People sit on white benches in an open forecourt. The caption at the bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont - Wandelhalle."

Sepia postcard showing a lively spa scene under a pavilion with columns and garlands in front of ornate late‑19th‑century buildings. Many visitors in Edwardian clothing gather around a fountain. Caption at the bottom reads "BAD PYRMONT - Stahlbrunnen." The reverse has German handwriting, a 5‑pfennig Deutsches Reich stamp, a Pyrmont postmark, the publisher credit, and a purple archive stamp.

Black‑and‑white group portrait of dozens of women (and a few men) in 1920s attire posing in front of a building with large columns and decorative lattice panels. The reverse has museum marking and handwritten date.

Sepia postcard showing a three-arched curved gateway set among trees, identified at the bottom as the main portal of the spa park in Bad Pyrmont. The reverse has German handwriting, an 8‑pfennig green Deutsches Reich stamp, a BAD PYRMONT postmark dated 17.7., and an address to Eisenach. Publisher credit printed vertically.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a grand spa hotel with a mansard roof, a long colonnaded veranda, twin balustraded staircases and a cascading fountain leading to a round basin. Caption in red at top left reads "Bad Pyrmont – Kurhotel."

Vintage divided-back postcard with a black‑and‑white photo of a seated statue titled 'Denkmal der Königin Luise' in a garden setting before large windows. The reverse bears a German handwritten message, an address to a young woman, a green 8‑Pfennig Deutsches Reich stamp, a BAD PYRMONT postmark, the printer credit 'Adolf Frost, Bad Pyrmont', and a blue cachet 'Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont'.

Black‑and‑white postcard view over a residential area with steep‑gabled houses lining a broad street, trees, and low wooded hills in the distance. Caption at the bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont – Untere Hauptallee." The reverse has German handwriting and a blue tourism stamp reading that the Weser air is the best medicine, with "Bad Pyrmont" alongside.

Monochrome view over a calm pond with three swans, dense trees, and a small classical pavilion/rotunda on an island. Caption in German at top identifies Bad Pyrmont and the view toward the Schlossinsel from the pergola. The reverse shows divided back, German handwriting dated 1916, publisher credit, and a museum stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a tree‑lined avenue leading toward a grand spa building. The caption at the bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont – Klosterallee und Kurhaus." The reverse is a German divided‑back with "Postkarte," printer credit, and a museum stamp from Bad Pyrmont.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a landscaped promenade lined with palm trees in large planters, potted plants and benches along gravel paths. Caption at the bottom reads in German about the new installations in the spa park at Bad Pyrmont. The back shows a German publisher credit and a museum stamp from Bad Pyrmont.

Hand‑tinted real‑photo postcard of a lush palm garden with flowering beds, white benches and a pergola/colonnade. The printed German caption at the lower right reads "Bad Pyrmont, Partie im Palmengarten." The reverse shows "Echte Photographie," the publisher imprint of Ernst Herrmann (Bad Pyrmont), and a museum stamp.

Sepia collage of oval studio portraits arranged like a family tree on an oak tree, depicting members of Germany's imperial family in military and court dress. Two shields appear, including the German imperial eagle. The title reads "Deutschlands Kaiserhaus," with a Berlin publisher imprint and a serial number.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a lakeside promenade with balustrades and a vine‑covered pergola in front of two grand villas among leafless trees. Printed caption at the bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont. Villa Königin Louise." There is cursive handwriting across the sky on the picture. The reverse has German handwriting, a green 5‑Pfennig Germania stamp, a circular BAD PYRMONT postmark, and a large stamp mark of the local museum.

Black‑and‑white postcard view over a spa complex with a long colonnade and a domed pavilion opening onto an open square filled with benches. A church spire and townhouses rise in the background. German captions along the lower border read "Bad Pyrmont" and "Brunnenplatz mit Wandelhalle." The reverse has German publisher details and a museum mark from Bad Pyrmont.

Colorized view of a manicured palm garden with flowerbeds, a large pedestal planter full of pink flowers, white benches, trimmed hedges and a white lattice fence. A seated person reads on a bench. The reverse has German handwriting, a green 8‑pfennig Deutsches Reich Beethoven stamp, and a Bad Pyrmont postmark indicating the spa town.

Black-and-white postcard view of a moated baroque palace with a stone terrace, arched bridge over water with swans, and a large mansion-like building behind trees. Caption on the front reads "Bad Pyrmont" and "Fürstl. Schloss."

Sepia panoramic view of a spa town nestled between low hills, with a long tree-lined main avenue and a central square featuring a pavilion. Caption at the front reads "BAD PYRMONT" and "GESAMTANSICHT." The reverse has German printing and a museum stamp.

Black‑and‑white photo postcard showing a large turn‑of‑the‑century villa with a tiled roof and multiple dormers. The facade features a two‑story semicircular portico with columns, balconies with scalloped awnings, and many windows. It sits in a landscaped garden with a palm, curved gravel drive, shrubs, and a white curved bench. No caption on the front. The divided back bears a stamp reading "Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont" and handwritten inventory numbers.

Colorized early 20th‑century postcard showing a villa with a round tower at the edge of farmland and a densely forested hill. Front caption reads "Bad Pyrmont" and "Königsberg." The reverse has German handwriting, the word "Postkarte," a circular postmark from Bad Pyrmont dated 18.5.16, and a blue archive stamp "Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont."

Multiview chromolithographic greeting postcard titled "Gruss aus Pyrmont," showing scenes from the spa town of Bad Pyrmont: the Fürstliches Schloss beside water and an arched bridge, the Brunnenplatz with the Trinkhalle pavilion full of promenading visitors, Café-Haus Reusch on the Hauptallee under large trees, and the Bahnhof (railway station). Floral decoration and a handwritten German message appear on the front; the reverse is a Deutsche Reichspost card with 5 Pfennig stamp and Hameln postmark.

Sepia postcard showing a grand hotel with a mansard roof and balconies along a wide, tree‑lined promenade. Benches and tall trees frame the avenue. Caption at the bottom identifies Bad Pyrmont and the Hotel Kaiserhof with the Hauptallee. The reverse has a divided back, a publisher's imprint, a museum stamp, and handwritten numbers.

Sepia-toned view of a spa-town square with a long colonnade and garden in the foreground and a tall neo‑Gothic church with a spire in the background. Caption at top reads "Bad Pyrmont – Partie am Brunnenplatz."

Sepia photo postcard showing a lake with two swans, an arched stone bridge, and the castle complex partly hidden by trees. Caption on the front reads "Bad Pyrmont. Schloss." The reverse has dense handwritten German text, a German Beethoven stamp, a Bad Pyrmont postmark, and a purple museum stamp.

Vintage photographic postcard with a studio portrait of a woman in a dark dress with a white bow at the waist, looking left. The front bears the printed caption "TILLA DURIEUX." and a small photographer credit "Aura Hertwig, Phot." The reverse is a multilingual universal-postal-style back headed "Postkarte – Carte postale" with dotted address lines and no message divider.

Divided-back German postcard with two black‑and‑white views. The front shows a brick school building titled "Schule in der Georg Victoria-Strasse" with children standing outside, and a second view titled "Emmerbrücke" showing an arched bridge over a river in a rural landscape. The caption at bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont-Oesdorf." The reverse reads "Postkarte" and carries a green 5‑pfennig Deutsches Reich stamp canceled "PYRMONT" with date 22.7.08, address lines, and later archive stamps of "Museum Schloss Bad Pyrmont."

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a long pergola/colonnade covered with climbing plants in the spa garden of Bad Pyrmont. A few people stroll under the columns. Caption at bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont – Säulengang im Kurgarten." The reverse has green "Postkarte," a Deutsches Reich stamp postmarked 26.5.11, an advertisement for Café‑Restaurant Knierim on the Hauptallee, a handwritten message and an address to Goslar, plus a museum stamp.

Sepia postcard showing a long pergola-lined walkway along the castle pond, with trees, a railing, and people strolling; swans are visible in the water. Caption at front reads "Bad Pyrmont – Rosengang am Schloßteich." Reverse has German handwriting, a postmark from Bad Pyrmont, an 8 Pf 'Deutsches Reich' Beethoven stamp, and a printed logo "Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont." Addressed to Herbert Herzog in Schmiedeberg i. Erzgebirge.

Black-and-white studio portrait of a young woman wearing a large brimmed hat and jacket. Soft-focus style. Printed captions at the bottom read the subject's name and title and the photographer/publisher in Dresden, along with a small catalog number.

Black‑and‑white view of a concert hall with large arched arcades and tall windows, seen from a landscaped park with trees, paths, benches, and a lamppost in the foreground. German caption printed at lower right identifies the scene.

Sepia postcard view of a leafy park scene with many people in early 20th‑century attire sitting on benches and strolling. A decorative bandshell/bandstand stands in the background. Caption on the front reads "Bad Pyrmont – Konzertplatz." The reverse has German handwriting in purple ink, a green Deutsches Reich stamp, and a circular postmark from Pyrmont dated 4.9.13, addressed to a woman in the Celle area.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing the ornate Kurhaus (spa house) in Pyrmont with a grand façade, terrace, stairways, fountain and benches in a landscaped park. The printed caption at top reads "PYRMONT – Kurhaus."

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a leafy park with a pond and swans, an arched multi‑span bridge, and the baroque palace partially visible among trees. Caption at top reads "Bad Pyrmont – Schloß." The reverse shows a divided back with the publisher line and a large museum imprint for the castle museum in Bad Pyrmont.

Colorized view of a leafy spa park with a small pavilion beside a path, benches and promenading visitors in early 20th‑century dress. Caption reads "Bad Pyrmont – Helenenquelle." The reverse has a divided back, a printed publisher line from Bad Pyrmont, and a museum stamp from the local Schloss museum.
Black‑and‑white postcard view of a neoclassical arcaded building with a long colonnade and steps, trees and shrubs in front. The caption on the front reads "Bad Pyrmont" and "Arkadenbau."

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a leafy riverside/pond scene with reflections in the water. A terrace with tables and a sun umbrella sits in front of a building bearing the sign "Hamborner Mühle." Caption at the bottom reads "Hamborner Mühle b. Bad Pyrmont."

Tinted view of a large timber‑framed hotel in a wooded setting with a rooftop sign reading "KÖNIGIN EMMA." Caption at bottom reads "Friedensthal bei Bad Pyrmont. Hotel u. Pension Königin Emma." The address side has "Postkarte," two green 5‑Pfennig Deutsches Reich stamps cancelled "LÖWENSEN 28.7.04," a receiving postmark "AMSTERDAM 29.7.04," publisher line "Verlag: Richard Borek, Braunschweig," a collection stamp "MUSEUM IM SCHLOSS BAD PYRMONT," and a handwritten address to Amsterdam.

Monochrome view of a landscaped square with an urn on a pedestal and hedged beds in the foreground, surrounded by leafy trees and elegant houses with shutters and vine-covered balconies. The bottom captions read "Bad Pyrmont" and "Altenau-Platz." The reverse has divided address lines, a vertical publisher credit, and a printed museum mark reading "MUSEUM IM SCHLOSS BAD PYRMONT."

Sepia postcard showing two high-ranking military officers in field uniforms standing in a courtyard with arched buildings behind them. A printed German caption at the top states the photo was taken by Her Majesty the Empress and Queen in July 1915. At the bottom are cursive lines including a signature and the place/date "Posen 1915." Publisher credit appears as Rotophot A.G. Berlin. The reverse has a Red Cross emblem, pricing, and charity note.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large sanatorium complex with a villa in the foreground. Printed captions at the bottom read "Bad Lippspringe" and "Kaiserin Auguste Victoria‑Stift." The reverse has German handwriting, an address to a Fräulein, a red "Deutsches Reich" stamp, a vertical publisher line, and a blue museum stamp.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a curved street lined with leafy trees and grand villas in a spa town. The printed caption reads "BAD PYRMONT Schloßstraße." and a handwritten note labels one villa as "Villa Reiling." The reverse has a handwritten German message, two Deutsches Reich Germania stamps (5 Pf and 2½ Pf) canceled in Bad Pyrmont, an address to Richard Müller, and a blue archive stamp from the Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont.

Sepia portrait postcard showing a woman in a white dress holding a decorated hat, standing beside a man in a Prussian officer's uniform with medals, outdoors. A German caption is printed at the top. Publisher and photographer credits appear at the bottom. The reverse is a divided-back postcard with a museum stamp from Bad Pyrmont.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-wing building with a small tower and gabled roofs set among trees and a path. Caption at the bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont   Helenen-Kinderheim." The reverse has a divided back and a blue museum logo reading "MUSEUM IM SCHLOSS BAD PYRMONT," along with penciled notations and a small printer's code.

Colorized postcard view showing a busy spa pavilion covered with garlands in a park-like setting, labeled "Bad Pyrmont – Stahlbrunnen." A tall church spire rises in the background and townspeople in period dress gather around the octagonal wellhouse. The reverse has a green 6‑pfennig Deutsches Reich stamp with a BAD PYRMONT postmark, an advertising cancel for spa cures, a museum cachet, publisher information, and handwritten message in German.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of the grand Kurhaus in Bad Pyrmont, a spa complex with a long veranda, mansard roofs, ornate lamp posts and many white benches set around a park square in the foreground. The printed caption at top right reads "BAD PYRMONT. Kurhaus."

Colorized view of a grand spa-hotel building with a mansard roof and long veranda (Kurhaus). White benches and flowerbeds line a forecourt framed by large trees. The reverse shows a divided-back layout with a publisher line and a blue stamp from the local museum.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large spa/kurhaus building bordered by gardens and a tree‑lined path, with a person walking in the foreground. Caption at the bottom reads "Bad Pyrmont" and "Staatl. Kurhaus." The reverse has standard address lines, the German printing note "Echte Kupfertiefdruckkarte," a blue stamp "Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont," and a small oval printer's mark from Dortmund with a serial number.

Vintage German postcard with a green 5 Pfennig REICHSPOST stamp, postmarked in Pyrmont on 19 Aug 1896 and received in Hannover the same day. The address side bears the logo 'Museum im Schloss Bad Pyrmont.' The picture side shows Schloss Pyrmont with a multi-arch stone bridge over the water, captioned 'Das Schloss' and dated 'Pyrmont 29.8.96,' with a handwritten note.

Color lithographic postcard showing a tree‑lined avenue in a landscaped park with a round flowerbed in the foreground and an arched arbor in the distance. Right margin bears a handwritten German message. Caption reads "Gruss aus Pyrmont." The reverse has a 5‑pfennig German Reichspost stamp, postmarks, and an address to Berlin.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped park with a pond, dense trees and shrubs, and a small white balustraded bridge; hills rise in the background. The reverse has the publisher mark, an address line for a Bad Pyrmont business, and a blue stamp from the local museum.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a landscaped spa garden with palm trees, trimmed hedges and multiple circular fountains. The front caption reads "Bad Pyrmont" and "Kurpark." The reverse shows a German postcard back with the printer's line and a blue museum stamp.

Color printed 'Oilette' postcard showing a painted scene of a broad, tree‑lined promenade with benches and café tables, many people in Edwardian dress strolling beneath rows of linden trees. Caption at bottom reads "PYRMONT, HAUPTALLEE." Reverse side is a Tuck's Postkarte with German description and publisher details.

A vintage black‑and‑white street scene in a European spa town. Grand multi‑story historic buildings line both sides of a broad street with shopfronts at ground level, including arched windows and signs. Trees form an avenue in the middle distance, beyond which bath and spa buildings rise against a wooded hillside. People in early 20th‑century fashion stroll along the sidewalks and street. Red printed caption text at the top right reads "Karlsbad Eingang zur Alten Wiese."

A stylized illustration showing a white-faced female figure with flowing hair and a long patterned dress, seemingly falling or flying beside a dark, demonic silhouette. The dress contains fiery, hellish imagery reminiscent of medieval religious art. The background is blue with faint script text, and at the bottom-left a large decorative white letter 'E' appears above the name 'Mariken van Nieumeghen'. The overall design resembles a modern art or literary-themed postcard.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a broad market square lined with multi‑story historic townhouses. The buildings have steep gabled roofs and ornate façades with shops at street level. A tall decorative streetlamp stands near the center foreground. Small groups of people gather in front of the buildings. Printed in red at the top left is the caption identifying the location as the old market. Additional German shop signs are visible on the right‑hand buildings.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a village scene with a prominent church on the left, featuring a tall spire and clock tower, and a large two‑story school building on the right. Both are surrounded by trees, gardens, fences, and small paths. The printed caption at the bottom identifies the location and the buildings, and a printer's credit line appears below the caption.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a wide grassy field in front of a forested hillside. Scattered groups of children and adults are sitting and standing on the lawn. In the background there are several small identical cottages with red roofs lined up, and on the right side a larger two‑storey building with a red roof. At the top left there is Cyrillic text.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large hilltop castle complex with a tall tower and multiple attached buildings, identified in German as Schloss Weesenstein. The castle overlooks a small river or stream running through a valley, with trees, fields, and a few houses in the foreground. A small steam train with smoke from its chimney is visible on tracks beside the river. The printed caption at the top reads "Schloss Weesenstein i. Müglitztale."

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large house or villa with a steep roof, partly obscured by trees, set in a landscaped park with an open lawn in the foreground. A person stands on the grass to the left. At the bottom of the image there is printed German text indicating the location is a park-restaurant in Klettenberg, along with an old-style telephone number.

Colorized vintage view of a small town scene with a central Gothic‑revival style church featuring a tall green spire, pointed-arch windows, and an arched entrance. To the right stands a red-and-white corner townhouse with a mansard-like roof and turret. Trees and wooden fencing surround the area, and a few people are visible near the fence. The sky is softly tinted, suggesting sunset or sunrise. At the bottom left margin of the image, cursive text is printed.

Black‑and‑white view of a European hillside residential district with late‑19th/early‑20th‑century apartment villas. A broad, bright street runs from the foreground into the background, flanked by multi‑storey stone townhouses on the right and freestanding mansions on the left. In the center, a steep stairway or funicular line climbs between buildings up a terraced slope planted like vineyards, with larger villas at the top of the hill. There is a handwritten white label partly covering the bottom left of the image and some small handwritten marks along the bottom edge.

Black-and-white postcard showing a small bay and beach with several small boats anchored near the shore. Whitewashed houses are clustered along the waterfront and scattered on the rocky hillside. The scene is a coastal village nestled in a rugged cove. Greek text is printed along the bottom margin in purple, and a web address watermark appears across the lower right of the image.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a large neo‑Gothic church, looking down the central aisle toward an ornate pipe organ on the rear gallery. Tall pointed arches, clustered columns, wooden pews, chandeliers and a cross above the entrance arch are visible. Caption text in Latvian is printed along the bottom margin.

Vintage tinted postcard showing a lively urban street scene. Multi‑story buildings with balconies and enclosed galleries line a sloping square filled with people in early 20th‑century clothing, horse‑drawn carts, and kiosks. On the right side margin, in red script, it reads "Vigo Puerto del Sol" and there is a purple round stamp from a public library. Additional small red vertical text appears along the right edge near the bottom.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a tree‑filled parish park with people walking and sitting on benches. In the background stands a church with a tall bell tower and clock. At the top of the image is printed text identifying the location, with an additional handwritten note.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a large, elegant café or coffee house with rows of square tables and bentwood chairs arranged symmetrically along a central carpeted aisle. There are tall coat racks, wooden columns, and a mezzanine gallery with railings above. At the far end is a counter or bar with illuminated signs and a clock on the wall. The image caption at the bottom reads "Kaffee Nordmeier Essen," indicating the name of the café and its location.

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a tall monument with a statue of Dante standing on top of a multi-tiered pedestal surrounded by sculptural reliefs. The monument is set in a park with benches, trees, and mountains visible in the background. An ornate streetlamp stands to the right. The caption at the bottom reads in Italian: "TRENTO - Monumento a Dante".

A sepia-toned postcard showing a general view of a Romanesque church complex in a rural valley, surrounded by stone walls and fields. The main building has a simple façade with an arched doorway, small bell tower and attached cloister-like arcade. Low hills and scattered houses are visible in the background. Printed caption text appears at the top and along the right edge.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a large rectangular Baroque-style building with three visible stories, a hipped roof with dormer windows, and a small central tower or cupola. The building stands in a landscaped garden or park area with trees and bushes in the foreground. In the lower left corner there is a short caption printed in a serif font.

Sepia-toned historic street scene showing a row of two‑story buildings with shops at ground level and wooden facades above. Soldiers and civilians stand or walk along the street; one soldier is on horseback. A hanging sign and flags mark a building identified as a soldiers' home. The printed caption at the top reads "Mitau – Soldatenheim".

Black-and-white postcard view of a cobblestone street with tram tracks running along it, lined with stepped-gable Flemish houses and dominated by a large brick Jesuit church with a tall square tower. Handwritten messages appear at the top right and across the bottom. Printed caption at the bottom identifies the scene in French.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of an ornate Russian Orthodox church with multiple onion domes and a tall bell tower, surrounded by forested hills. In the lower right corner there is white printed text in German identifying the location.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a wide view of a makeshift refugee camp on bare ground, with many small huts or shacks in the background and several people walking in traditional dress in the foreground. Printed captions in French and English at the top read "SALONIQUE — Vue générale du Camp des réfugiés / SALONICA — General view of a refugee camp," and a publisher line appears at the bottom left. A modern website watermark (www.elia.org.gr) is superimposed across the lower right.

Sepia-toned aerial view over a historic European town with dense tiled roofs. A large Gothic-style church with pointed windows and a steep roof dominates the left foreground. In the middle distance is a small market square surrounded by multi-storey buildings. Trees and a flat horizon line with industrial chimneys are visible in the background. Printed German captions appear at the top.

An old sepia-toned postcard view of a large ivy‑covered manor or small castle with a central arched gateway and many rectangular windows. In front of the building is a circular driveway with a round basin and fountain in the middle, surrounded by neatly kept gardens and trees. The caption in German is printed in red at the top left.

A black‑and‑white wartime postcard showing a fortified hill with stone walls and a large round tower on top, overlooking a rocky slope with a few small buildings. The style is early 20th century. French printed captions at the bottom reference the First World War and identify the view as the Ciceron (Cicéron) Tower at Salonique (Salonica). There is a handwritten note in French at the top and a small printer's mark at the bottom.

A vintage black‑and‑white view over a dense cluster of multi‑story historic buildings along a hillside, bordered by forest. The architecture is typical of Central European spa towns, with ornate facades and steep roofs. At the top left in red print is the caption "Karlsbad. Andreasgasse." indicating the location.

Color photograph of a lively European square with people walking, cycling, and sitting at café terraces under green umbrellas. Historic narrow townhouses with tiled roofs line the background. A large tree stands on the right, and street signs and a traffic sign (3.5t) are visible. At the bottom center, the white caption "NIJMEGEN" is printed on a dark border.

An old black‑and‑white postcard view across a wide river toward a hilly urban neighborhood. In the foreground a long paddle steamer with a central smokestack sails along the river; the ship's side bears the name "WETTIN." On the opposite bank stands a stone embankment and a bridge entering from the right. Above the river rise several tiers of late‑19th‑century houses and villas, and on the hilltop there are large institutional buildings, possibly schools or administrative complexes, with steep roofs and small towers. The photograph shows some physical damage and abrasions along the lower edge.

Sepia-toned photograph of a formal park path leading to a tall monument. The monument consists of a rocky pedestal with a sculpted bust or figure in the middle and, on top, a winged female figure holding a laurel wreath aloft. Decorative multi‑globe street lamps flank the walkway. At the bottom of the image are three postage stamps, each cancelled with round postmarks.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a cobblestoned street in a small European town, lined with 2‑ to 3‑story plastered houses with steep tiled roofs. Several shopfronts with large painted signs face the street. A few women and children stand on the sidewalks. The scene looks early‑20th‑century, with no cars and simple wooden shop windows. The signs are in German, advertising a plumbing shop, men's clothing and underwear shops, and a business named Adolf Zippel.

A black‑and‑white riverside view of a European city. In the foreground a long, low river steamer with the name "PIRNA" on its side travels along a wide river. Along the opposite bank stands a row of multi‑storey 19th‑century townhouses and small buildings. Behind them rises a wooded hill, sparsely covered with leafless trees, and on its summit is a small church or chapel with a steep spire and several associated buildings. The sky is blank and light, giving the photograph a vintage appearance typical of old postcards.

Vintage Spanish postal card with light blue background, printed heading 'UNIÓN POSTAL UNIVERSAL / UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE / ESPAÑA' and a red Spanish stamp depicting a profile bust. The card is filled in with handwritten address text in Spanish, including a street and the city Madrid. At the bottom there is printed bilingual text in Spanish and French indicating that this side is reserved for the address.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard view of a sparse settlement in an arid landscape. Several low colonial‑style buildings with verandas stand on open ground with little vegetation, surrounded by hills or mountains in the distance. Simple walls and a small house-like structure appear in the right foreground. Printed captions at the top read "Mindelo" on the left and "S. Vicente C. V." on the right.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a hillside town with many houses nestled among trees. On the upper slope is a prominent castle-like building labeled 'Kaiser Wilhelmsburg'. At the bottom, printed text identifies the location as Bad Kösen on the Saale River. Publisher information and a date (1905) appear in small print in the lower left.

Black-and-white vintage postcard showing a brick cloister or portico with arched arcades and ornate columns, including a central twisted column. The architecture is clearly historic and Italianate. In the lower left corner there is printed caption text indicating the location and subject, and in the upper right there is a circular mark with the letters "M.C.T.".

A colorized landscape view of a rural valley with green fields, orchards, and a backdrop of wooded hills and mountains. On the left stands a castle‑like villa with four corner towers; in the middle a tall rectangular villa with a tower; on the right a small village with a church featuring a steeple. The image has a printed caption at the top in Italian.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large pavilion‑like building with arched arcades, steep roofs and small tower elements, set among trees and a landscaped park. Benches and garden furniture are visible in the foreground along a wide path. Red printed German text appears at the top of the card.

Vintage monochrome postcard depicting the elaborate Gothic façade and large pointed-arch window of a church or cathedral entrance, framed by trees, wrought-iron fencing, a small fountain, and a streetlamp in the foreground. The roof behind is steep and covered with small dormer windows. Printed red text at the top reads "Freiberg i. S Goldene Pforte," indicating the subject. Additional vertical publisher text appears along the right edge.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a lakeside pier framed by trees in the foreground. A small passenger steamboat named "ÅRAN" is docked at the pier, with several people standing on the boat and on the dock. An early 20th‑century automobile is parked on the wooden pier. Across the water, forested hills and scattered lakeside buildings are visible. Handwritten or printed caption text appears along the bottom right edge.

Sepia-toned photograph of a commemorative stone in an open field or meadow. The stone bears the number "1345" painted in white on its face and is decorated with wreaths or garlands of foliage and evergreen branches draped over and around it. In the background are gently rolling fields with scattered trees and a young, newly planted tree supported by stakes to the right. The scene is rural and somber, suggesting a memorial or historical marker.

Black‑and‑white postcard view over a river with a long bridge in the foreground and a paddle steamer on the water. On the hill behind the bridge stands a large castle complex with prominent Gothic church towers, overlooking a town of dense historic buildings. The card has decorative, slightly scalloped edges and a caption in German at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white view of a cloistered courtyard with a garden, seen through a dark foreground arch and railing. The main building has two levels of arcaded galleries with rounded arches, tile roofs, and a large domed church rising behind, topped with a lantern and cross. The architectural style suggests a Mediterranean or Latin monastic complex.

Sepia-toned interior view of a large late‑Gothic church nave with very tall clustered pillars, elaborate ribbed and net vaulting, high narrow stained-glass windows, wooden pews, and richly carved galleries. At the far end stands a monumental multi‑tiered altarpiece and an ornate pulpit to the right.

A black‑and‑white street scene in a European town, likely from the late 19th or early 20th century. Cobbled streets run between rows of 3–4 storey masonry townhouses with neoclassical detailing. A woman in a long dress and hat walks in the foreground, a horse and cart stand in the center, and another cart with a large covered load is partly visible on the right. On the corner building to the right, shop signage with German text can be seen. The overall appearance suggests a quiet bourgeois town street rather than a famous monument.

Sepia-toned studio photograph showing two women in traditional rural-style dresses and two uniformed soldiers with rifles and pickelhaube spiked helmets. One soldier is holding hands with the central woman while the other soldier, smiling, touches his comrade's helmet. The second woman stands to the left, apparently crying into a cloth near a rustic wooden fence and broom. The painted backdrop suggests a countryside setting. There is no visible printed text on the image side.

A monochrome postcard showing a wooden pavilion-style building with a long veranda and columns, set among tall trees in a park or garden. A person stands on the steps at the entrance. The image is bordered by a white margin, and Russian text is printed vertically along the right side with a small number indicating it is part of a series.

A vintage, tinted night‑view postcard showing a large Romanesque cathedral with two prominent towers and an ornate multi-tiered fountain in the foreground. The moon and clouds are visible in the sky. The scene is framed by a light border, and a caption is printed below the image.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a wide view over a calm body of water, seen from a wooded foreground hillside. On the opposite shore lies a small settlement with scattered houses and a prominent white church with a tower, backed by densely forested hills. A few small boats are visible on the water. Printed white caption text appears along the bottom left, and a small publisher's logo with the number 7809 is at the bottom right.

Color-tinted vintage postcard showing a large fortified complex with high walls, a prominent round tower and a long palace-like building behind it. Trees and a broad walkway with a few pedestrians appear in the foreground. The bottom margin bears a printed caption identifying the castle and handwritten script; there is also a vertical strip of handwriting on the right edge.

A vintage black‑and‑white street scene showing a busy urban square with tram tracks, pedestrians, bicycles, and multi‑story brick and stone buildings. In the foreground a colorful illustrated gnome or elf carrying a tray has been added over the photo. The caption at the top identifies the view as Järntorget in Gothenburg, and museum information and an archive code appear along the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white historic postcard view of a cobblestone street lined with multi‑story townhouses and small shops. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalks. The printed caption at the top in red German text reads "Grossenhain. Meißner Straße und Kgl. Amtsgericht." indicating the street and the royal district court in the town of Großenhain.

Black‑and‑white printed postcard showing a detailed bird's‑eye view drawing of a large industrial factory complex with multiple long brick buildings, tall chimneys emitting smoke, internal roads, and some smaller houses or offices at the front. A tree‑lined embankment runs along a river in the foreground where a small steamship is depicted. Below the image there is a German caption identifying the factory and its date.

Color postcard showing a multi-level sanctuary complex built on a rocky spur in a forested mountain valley. The buildings have light-colored walls, red-tiled roofs, small arched windows, and a prominent church with a tall, steeply pitched roof and bell tower. In front is a lower building with a central arched entrance, a crucifix and statue niche above the doorway, flower beds, and a wooden fence bordering a grassy path where visitors walk. The image is framed by a decorative border with gold vertical segments on the sides and a broad purple band at the bottom containing the caption 'SAN ROMEDIO' in large gold letters.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a rural village scene with two women in traditional dress and a dog in the foreground.
