Black-and-white postcard showing a grand historic theatre building in an urban setting, with elaborate neo-baroque architecture, twin towers topped by statues, and a large arched entrance. Trees, gardens and a street with vehicles appear in the foreground. Printed caption at the top left reads "CLUJ – Teatrul National", and above the main entrance the inscription "TEATRUL NATIONAL" is visible.

Sepia-toned photograph showing a walled historic town with a prominent church tower and very tall, slender spire at the center. The spire is topped with scaffolding or an ornate structure. In the foreground is a garden or park path framed by bushes. To the left is a round medieval tower integrated into the town wall; additional stone buildings with tiled roofs stand behind the wall. The overall look is early 20th‑century European.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a rural church with a tall, narrow steeple rising above trees beside a pond. In the foreground is a traditional wooden well sweep by the water. The scene is quiet and pastoral. At the top of the card is printed text in Estonian identifying the church and region.

Black‑and‑white view of a walled hilltop church complex with a tall, narrow bell tower (campanile) rising above surrounding agricultural fields. Behind the church are forested slopes and a high mountain ridge with some snow patches. The architecture is Romanesque/early‑Renaissance in style, typical of southern European mountain regions.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a panoramic cityscape dominated by a tall neo‑Gothic church with a slender spire rising above surrounding low buildings. There is a column-like monument on the left and rooftops in the foreground. Printed red text labels the scene and the city; handwritten notes appear along the right margin. The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century European postcard.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing an old harbor or shipyard with sailing ships and industrial buildings along the shoreline, with low hills in the background. Beneath the image are several printed and stamped Swedish texts indicating a company in Uddevalla and that the item belongs to Uddevalla Museum, dated February 1903.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a tranquil park scene with a small rustic wooden bridge over a pond or stream surrounded by trees, reeds, and lush vegetation. The image is framed by printed captions in German, including the town name at the top and a description of the location at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a rural mountainous landscape with forested hills, scattered farmhouses, and village buildings in a valley. The scene shows the countryside framed by trees in the foreground and rolling hills in the background. A printed caption in German appears along the bottom border.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a landscaped park with a central round medieval tower beside a waterway, tree‑lined paths, and a large mansion or villa in the background. The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as Kronenburger-park in Nijmegen. There is printed publisher information along the left edge and handwritten ink on the lower part of the card.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a tree-lined promenade with wooden pavilions or kiosks on both sides, likely in a spa or resort park. Several well‑dressed women in long dresses and hats walk along the path, while men stand near the shopfronts. A sign hangs above one shop entrance reading "Josef Staab," and there is a large German text poster on the left building. The number "1328" and the word beneath it, which looks like a place name, are handwritten along the bottom edge of the image.

A black‑and‑white (tinted) historic postcard showing an elevated view of a large castle complex with multiple towers and steep roofs next to a church with a tall clock tower. The buildings sit above terraced gardens and trees, with a town and hilly landscape in the background. At the top in red Gothic-style print is a German caption identifying the scene.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a tall white minaret and adjoining religious complex seen from a narrow street lined with low stone houses. At the top it bears multilingual text identifying it as a souvenir from Salonique (Thessaloniki) and naming the Church of Saint Catherine, which was later used as a mosque (Mosquée Ski Cherrifé). The sky is softly tinted blue and pink, and there is a small website attribution at the bottom.

A vintage black‑and‑white panoramic view over a wooded valley and a small spa town nestled among forested hills. A curving tree‑lined road leads through meadows toward a cluster of buildings and church spires in the distance. The landscape is dominated by rolling hills and dense conifer forests. A printed caption in German appears at the bottom edge of the image.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a long ox-drawn wagon train crossing an arid plain. At the front left is a covered wagon with large wooden wheels and a driver; a span of many oxen stretches across almost the entire width of the image. The landscape is flat and barren with low hills on the horizon. The bottom portion of the card is blank for writing, with red printed captions: the word 'Mossamedes' on the left, 'Carro de Boers' on the right, and a small publisher credit along the lower edge.

Black-and-white photograph showing a formal garden with symmetrical paths and manicured shrubs leading toward a low neoclassical building with a central pediment and colonnade. Tall trees frame the scene, and two wooden posts with box-like structures stand in the foreground on each side of the main path.

Monochrome postcard showing a riverside industrial facility surrounded by forest. In the foreground there is a brick building with a tall chimney and stacks of cut timber. A smaller structure with a hipped roof stands near the riverbank where people appear to be working. Along the water's edge several small piers or floating platforms extend into a wide river. In the background are scattered wooden houses and dense trees. Printed Russian text appears in the upper right corner.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi-story industrial brick factory building with many evenly spaced windows. The facade bears a long painted company name in German. In the foreground there is an unpaved road and piles of material, likely wood. The caption at the top right reads "Brand-Erbisdorf i. Sa." indicating the town, and the building inscription reads "Erzgebirgische Holzindustrie Act. Ges."

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a multi‑storey brick institutional building seen behind leafless trees and a snowy garden or park. The architecture is late‑19th/early‑20th‑century, with symmetrical wings and many windows. Printed text in the upper left corner identifies the place.

A philatelic postcard or first day cover commemorating the XXVI Summer Olympic Games. On the right is a large block of three Estonian postage stamps featuring Olympic themes: a medal, a victorious athlete with raised arms, and a swimmer on the starting block. Above them are five interlinked Olympic rings and text. There are cancellation marks dated 25.IV.1996 from Tallinn. On the left is a triangular pattern of small blue human figures forming a stylized tree, with text below referring to Atlanta 1996 and FDC. An Olympic logo and Estonian text with the date and Tallinn are also printed near the top, with a handwritten signature in the middle.

Black-and-white view of a large two-storey school building with a central entrance and symmetrical wings, surrounded by a fenced yard with trees. Groups of children and adults stand in front of the building. The bottom edge bears printed text identifying the school and the photographer/publisher.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small village set against a densely forested hillside. In the foreground is an open grassy field bordered by a simple fence and a few utility poles. Behind it stand several traditional half‑timbered houses and farm buildings partly obscured by trees. The image caption is printed along the bottom white margin.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a two-story school building behind trees and a picket fence. In the foreground is a small square with a fenced monument or statue on a pedestal, and several children and people standing or sitting nearby. The words "Wermsdorf." and "Schule." are printed at the top of the image.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small wooden mountain railway station building labeled "Åre Fjällbana" with surrounding hills and conifer forests. A flagpole with a Scandinavian‑style flag stands in front, and people are seated on a bench by the entrance. There are train tracks in the foreground and a mountain slope rising behind the station.

Black‑and‑white postcard view taken from inside old stone ruins on a hill, looking out over dense forest toward a coastal town and harbor with sailing ships and buildings by the sea. The foreground shows thick, weathered castle walls and openings; in the distance a sailboat is visible on the water. Caption text is printed along the bottom edge in Swedish.

Multiview postcard showing a dramatic mountain ridge with a winding road leading along green slopes and rocky cliffs, a small mountain lodge beside a hairpin road, and a terrace café with tables and chairs overlooking a deep blue lake surrounded by steep mountains.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a stone wall with a bronze relief panel showing a central winged female figure with draped garments, flanked by several soldiers or historical figures holding flags or spears. To the right of the relief is a rectangular commemorative plaque fixed with four round bolts. In front of the wall is a densely planted flowerbed, and above the wall are parked cars and the façades of older multistory buildings, suggesting a European city street.

Black-and-white panoramic view over a lakeside town with many early 20th‑century buildings and a wooded hill across the water. In the foreground stands a substantial brick building with a steep tiled roof, seen above treetops. Printed white text at the bottom identifies the scene as a view of Östersund from the town hall and credits the photography company A/B Almquist & Cöster from Hälsingborg, along with a small oval logo reading "ÄKTA FOTOGRAFI".

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a bustling cobblestone street lined with late‑19th‑century multi‑story buildings with awnings over the shopfronts. Many well‑dressed pedestrians, men in suits and hats and women in long dresses with umbrellas, stand and stroll along the street. A young girl poses in the foreground. At the top in red letters it reads "Lobositz" and "Dr. Kubitschka-Gasse". A sign on the left building reads "Kirchen‑Gasse". The overall look suggests an early 20th‑century Central European town scene.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large villa or mansion on a wooded hilltop, surrounded by trees and overlooking cultivated fields and gardens in the foreground. In the upper left, red German text reads "Waldheim. Blick nach der 'Goldenen Höhe'." The overall style and printing suggest an early 20th‑century Central European postcard.

A monochrome (sepia-toned) postcard image showing a rural forest landscape. A dirt path winds through dense coniferous and deciduous trees along the side of a hill. A lone person stands near the edge of the path on the right side. At the top center, printed in red, is the caption 'Nossen i. S. Steinmetzruhe.' The rest of the card is blank sky above the wooded slope.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a mountain village nestled in a wide alpine valley beneath dramatic, jagged peaks. Snow patches remain on the steep rock faces, while dense forests and open meadows surround a clustered group of multi‑story hotels and buildings in the foreground. Printed captions identify the scene and key peaks: the settlement of S. Martino di Castrozza at 1444 meters above sea level, with Cima Val di Roda (2800 m) and Sass Maor (2816 m) towering above.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a row of uniformed soldiers standing on the steps of a brick building, likely a barracks. They wear spiked helmets (Pickelhaube) and dress uniforms with sabers. On the right, one soldier stands apart, blowing a bugle. The scene appears ceremonial and is printed with red caption text at the bottom.

A colorized historical postcard view of an elegant spa-town street lined with ornate multi‑story buildings and trees, with a wooded hill and a villa on the ridge in the background. The scene is titled "Marienbad. Marienbader Mühle." and additional small print credits the publisher and notes that it is a hand‑colored artist card.

Black‑and‑white landscape view taken from an elevated vantage point, showing a densely forested area with coniferous trees, several lakes or river bends winding through the valley, and scattered houses or small buildings along the shoreline. A tall pine tree dominates the right foreground, with rolling forested hills extending to the horizon under a partly cloudy sky. There is no visible printed caption or text on the image.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard with scalloped edges showing a low-angle view of a circular colonnaded monument with tall columns and an open sky behind. At the bottom border, an Italian caption identifies the scene.

Old sepia-toned postcard showing a busy port with sailing ships moored beside a quay. There are cranes, wagons, and people working on the pier, with mountainous terrain in the background. Printed caption text at the lower left indicates the location and publisher, and there is handwritten Spanish text across the bottom front.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a small marina with several moored sailboats in the foreground and calm water reflecting them. Behind the quay is a stone wall, trees, and a large seaside hotel building with multiple gables and balconies. Another pointed‑tower villa appears to the left. The scene has a tranquil, early‑20th‑century seaside‑resort atmosphere. Swedish text is printed along the bottom edge, identifying the boat harbor and the Strand Hotel in Borgholm, as well as the publisher/photographer.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing a busy stone quay with sailing boats moored in the foreground and people working on the docks. Behind them stands a long façade of multi‑story buildings with characteristic enclosed glass balconies (galerías) and an arcade at ground level. Printed captions appear along the left side margin and at the bottom front of the card.

Colorized postcard view from the sea toward a coastal town with multi‑story buildings lining the waterfront and a fortification or citadel on a small hill in the background. A steamship with two masts and a central smokestack sails in the foreground. The sky is lightly clouded and the water appears calm. In the upper left corner is the caption 'Korfu.' and along the lower right edge is a printed website watermark.

A black‑and‑white historical postcard showing a broad open green field bordered by a wooden fence and bare trees in the foreground, with a row of early 20th‑century town buildings in the background. The architecture includes multi‑storey houses with gabled roofs and decorative facades, set against a forested hillside. Printed caption text appears at the lower left.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a domed building with arched windows and a tall slender minaret, identified as the former Hagia Sophia mosque in Salonica (Thessaloniki). The foreground contains bare trees and low ruined walls, giving the scene a somewhat desolate appearance. Printed captions in French and English describe the site.

Sepia-toned historic street view showing a row of ornate late‑19th/early‑20th‑century townhouses with decorative facades, bay windows, and a tall pointed tower. Trees line the sidewalk and a few people stand on the street. At the top in red Gothic-type lettering is the caption indicating the town and street name.

A monochrome postcard showing the ornate Gothic façade of a large town hall with tall spires, pinnacles, and rows of statues between high arched windows. The text at the top identifies it as the town hall in Bruges. Printer information and a series number appear at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a rural valley landscape with traditional half‑timbered houses surrounded by trees and fields, set against forested hills. Printed red text at the top identifies the location as Lerbach in the Harz region and describes the scene. Vertical text along the left edge credits the publisher located in Lerbach i. Harz.

Color postcard with a central photograph bordered by a white margin. The photo shows a busy outdoor market street crowded with people, lined with flowering trees and stalls. In the background are historic towers and church spires, alongside modern commercial buildings with a prominent vertical rainbow-colored sign for the C&A store. At the bottom margin of the postcard, the word 'NIJMEGEN' is printed.

Illustrated view of a narrow cobblestone street lined with tall medieval stone and plaster houses with steep red-tiled roofs. A horse-drawn cart travels along the street. In the background rises a large church tower with a square base and a very tall, slender spire topped by a finial, flanked by small corner pinnacles. A leafy tree stands on the left near a cylindrical advertising column that bears a small poster. The sky is grey and overcast. The style is that of an early-20th‑century color lithograph.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large ancient stone aqueduct with multiple tiers of arches set in a hilly, vegetated landscape. The structure is in ruins but largely standing. Greek and English captions are printed in the lower margin, along with a publisher credit on the right.

The image shows the reverse side of a written postcard lying on top of a notebook and other cards. The postcard has blue handwritten text in Finnish, an oval postal or ship stamp in blue ink, and a Finnish postage stamp depicting seals and labeled 'SUOMI • FINLAND'. The top has the printed logo 'SILJA LINE', a well‑known ferry company in the Baltic Sea. The notebook page underneath also contains handwritten Finnish text.

Colorized vintage view over a river with a stone bridge leading into a small European town. The riverside is lined with trees and houses with red-tiled roofs, and church towers rise above the town skyline. In the foreground on the grassy riverbank, there appear to be laundry or textiles laid out to dry. The sky is blue with scattered clouds. The printed caption in the upper left reads "Rochlitz i. Sa."

A black‑and‑white postcard view over a small Alpine town nestled in a valley, framed in the foreground by a large tree and grassy slope. In the middle stands a prominent church with a tall bell tower rising above clustered houses. Mountain ranges surround the valley in the background. At the bottom border is a printed Italian caption identifying the scene, and at the lower right there is a handwritten date.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a narrow street scene with people in traditional dress, a laden donkey, and Ottoman‑style houses. At the end of the street rises a tall mosque minaret. Printed captions at the bottom identify the view as the Eshidjéouma (Eshidjeuma) Mosque in Salonique. The domain "www.elia.org.gr" is overprinted on the image.

Sepia-toned historic view of a European town square labeled 'Trento. Piazza delle Erbe.' The scene shows a market with people in early 20th-century clothing, wooden stalls, and carts. On the left is a neoclassical building with the sign 'BANCA COOPERATIVA'. To the right are multi-story buildings with shutters and awnings. In the background a tower rises above the roofs, with mountains visible further behind.

Black‑and‑white image of a central European town hall on a cobbled square. The three‑story building has a steep tiled roof, a clock in a baroque gable, and a small open belfry with a weather vane. Leafless pollarded trees line the façade. In front, a group of boys and a man stand on the square. German text is visible on the façade and on side buildings.

Black‑and‑white aerial view of a European town square with a Gothic-style church featuring a rose window and tower at the center-right. The square is bordered by multi‑story townhouses with steep roofs and shop signs on the ground floors. A wide, mostly empty street runs diagonally, lined with small trimmed trees near the church. In the distance are more buildings and a large palace-like complex on a hill, with gentle hills or low mountains beyond. Visible shop signs on the closest corner buildings are in German, including business names and words like "Restauration".

Black‑and‑white landscape view across an open meadow toward a small town with a prominent church tower rising above low houses. Trees frame the foreground on both sides. The bottom-left corner has the caption "NORA" and the lower-right corner includes a publisher credit mentioning Uppsala.

A colorized vintage view of a stone multi‑arched bridge crossing a river with reflections in the water. On the left is a large building with a tall minaret, suggesting a mosque, and beyond the bridge lies a low town spread across a plain with hills in the distance. Greek text at the top left and English text at the top right identify the location as Larissa in Thessaly. The domain 'www.elia.org.gr' is printed across the lower part of the image.

A vintage black-and-white postcard-style photograph showing a dense medieval town with steeply roofed houses in the foreground and a large Gothic cathedral complex dominating the hill above. The cathedral has two very tall, ornate spires side by side and additional spires and towers around it, attached to a castle-like ensemble of historic buildings and fortifications. The image has slightly irregular white borders, typical of early to mid‑20th‑century postcards. No visible printed caption or handwriting appears on the front.

A black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph showing a historic European town dominated by medieval fortifications. In the foreground are vineyards or cultivated fields, descending to houses clustered below massive stone walls built on rocky outcrops. Prominent in the middle is a tall round stone tower with a crenellated top, attached to the fortification line. To the left stands a large Gothic church with steeply pitched roof and an attached square bell tower with a slender spire. To the right and in the background rise additional towers and spires above dense, old-town buildings. The scene has no visible printed caption or other text on the image side.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a hilly town with dense trees and multiple multi‑story houses with steep roofs nestled in a valley. On the slopes above the town stand a few prominent villas or large houses. The foreground shows a cluster of older buildings, while the background is dominated by wooded hills. Printed red text at the lower right reads "Ober-Tharandt." and at the very bottom appear publisher details in smaller type.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view of a small European town nestled among forested hills and farmland. In the foreground there is a sloping harvested field leading down to several simple, plastered houses with steep gabled roofs and small chimneys. Further back, more elaborate late‑19th/early‑20th‑century villas and town buildings appear among dense trees; one large villa stands prominently on a hillside, and another cluster of larger houses or small hotels lies to the right. The background shows rolling hills covered with woods and patchwork fields. The image edges are irregular, as if from an old photographic print used on a postcard. No printed caption or legible writing is visible on the image.

A black‑and‑white aerial photograph of a small rural settlement surrounded by forests and fields. The scene shows scattered detached houses with steep gabled roofs, some with small outbuildings and gardens, laid out along curving unpaved or lightly paved roads. Dense coniferous woods border the village, and open farmland stretches beyond. There are no visible tall landmarks, coastline, or urban high‑rises; the overall impression is of a quiet northern European countryside in the early or mid‑20th century.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small town square with a prominent church tower featuring a clock and onion-shaped spire. To the right, partially visible behind trees, is a castle-like building with round towers. At street level there are a few pedestrians and cyclists, and a shopfront on the left. The caption at the bottom identifies the scene as the church and castle in Nossen, Saxony.

A colored illustrated postcard showing a panoramic view over a city along a winding river, seen from an elevated terrace with a stone balustrade. In the right foreground stands a bronze lion monument on a large stone pedestal. Several figures in early 20th‑century clothing look out over the cityscape and surrounding hills. At the top of the card there is German text identifying the scene.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large, three-storey classical building with a hipped roof, central entrance and symmetrical windows, fronted by trees and a broad open square. Behind it lies a river or lake with forested hills on the opposite shore. The caption at the bottom left reads "Residenset, Vänersborg".

A black‑and‑white panoramic coastal town view taken from a rocky hill. In the foreground are sloping rocks and trees, then densely packed wooden and masonry houses with steep gabled roofs, some with dormers and small gardens. Beyond the town lies a calm harbor with piers, low industrial buildings, and a breakwater extending into the sea. In the distance are rocky islands and a hilly shoreline across the water. The overall style suggests a small Northern European seaside town, likely mid‑20th century. There is no visible printed or handwritten text on the image side.

A sepia-toned photograph showing a weathered stone statue of a robed, possibly ecclesiastical figure standing on a small pedestal against a high rough-stone wall. The figure's face and some details are eroded, and it appears to be holding an object in front of its chest. The statue is set beside a descending stone pathway or stair with a handrail. In the distant upper left background faint outlines of hills or mountains are visible. There is no visible printed caption or text on the image side.

Colorized historical street view labeled "Königsbrück. Schlossstrasse." showing a slightly curving town street lined with two‑story buildings with red tile roofs. Shops with German signage occupy the ground floors, and people in late‑19th/early‑20th‑century clothing walk or stand along the street. On the right foreground is a stone monument topped with stacked cannonballs, partly obscured by trees.

A black‑and‑white landscape view showing a broad grassy field in the foreground and, across a fence and tree line, a row of sizeable late‑19th/early‑20th‑century villas or townhouses. Behind them is a wooded hillside. On the right, a well‑dressed man holding a cane stands beside a tree, raising his arm as if pointing or greeting someone. The buildings feature steep gabled roofs, dormer windows, and one has a small spire or turret, giving the scene a Central European small‑town feel. There is no visible title or caption on the image side.

Black‑and‑white view of a cobblestoned town square bordered by 18th–19th‑century two‑storey buildings with steep tiled roofs. In the foreground are several 1930s–1940s style cars parked near a kiosk. A main street runs along the right side where pedestrians walk by shops. A road sign on a pole points toward another locality. The central building at the far side of the square has a slightly grander façade with decorative gables, suggesting a town hall or similar civic building.

A postcard-style card with two main images on a cream background. On the left is a historical drawing of a stone castle with multiple round towers capped by red roofs, standing on a small island surrounded by water. The image is labeled with letters on the castle walls. On the right is an ornate Orthodox-style icon of the Virgin Mary holding the Christ Child, both with golden halos and framed in a richly decorated metal riza. At the top of the card are printed institutional and location details, and a reference number at the upper right.

Sepia-toned vintage street view of a small European town. The scene shows a gently curving road lined with two‑ and three‑story houses and shops. On the right side a shop sign reads "Max Gössel" and the buildings have arched doorways and shuttered windows. On the left side is an older house with a wooden fence and a small garden area. In the distance, higher on a hill, stands a large building with a dome or tower. Printed text at the top right reads "Frauenstein i. Erzgeb."

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a rural road curving past a large three‑storey villa with decorative gables, labelled 'Villa Ida'. The house stands on the right side of the image with fields and a few outbuildings, while a dense forest borders the road on the left. Hills of a wooded mountain range rise in the background. Printed German text appears at the top identifying the location in the Ore Mountains of Saxony.

A colorized vintage street scene showing a wide cobblestone road lined with low, colonial-style buildings with tiled roofs and balconies. People in early 20th‑century clothing, including several in white suits, walk and stand along the sidewalks; a horse‑drawn carriage is visible in the middle distance. The view looks straight down the street toward trees and more buildings. Printed caption text appears at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white view of a European city square with landscaped gardens in the foreground, a fenced path where a woman in light-colored dress walks, and a tall column in the center topped by a winged female figure holding a wreath. Surrounding the monument are ornate late‑19th‑century buildings with steep roofs and decorative facades. The scene has the look of an old photographic postcard, though no border text or caption is visible.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a wooden mountain lodge built on a rocky hilltop, with stone foundations and a steep roof. To the left stands a tall wooden lookout or observation tower. A stairway climbs up along the right edge. The foreground is covered with shrubs and rocks. In the lower left corner there is a printed caption in German.

A monochrome vintage view of a tree‑lined urban park or public square. Numerous evenly spaced trees and lawns create a shaded avenue with benches, on which a few people sit and relax. In the background are low, indistinct buildings. In the foreground, there is a triangular lighter area on the ground, over which the numbers "2932" in black and "8328." in red are printed.

Black‑and‑white image showing a dynamic modernist bronze statue of a running figure holding a large, wing‑like form above its head, mounted on a sculpted concrete pedestal in a grassy park. In the background is a road and a large steel arch bridge crossing a river, with light poles and a few vehicles.

Black‑and‑white image of a large, light‑colored manor‑like building with a steep, tiled roof and simple neo‑classical/Scandinavian revival details. A tall flagpole with a Nordic-style flag (dark with a light cross) stands in front of the central gable. The foreground is filled with an orderly garden or orchard and a straight path leading toward the entrance. No printed captions or handwritten text are visible.

A vintage, monochrome panoramic view of a mountain town nestled in a valley, with numerous clustered buildings and several prominent church towers in the foreground, surrounded by forested slopes and snow-covered peaks in the background. At the bottom margin, printed text identifies the location as Cavalese in the Fiemme Valley.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a wide, elegant city street lined with multi‑story European‑style buildings. Horse‑drawn carriages and pedestrians move along the street, which is bordered by iron railings and balconies. The scene appears early 20th‑century. Printed caption text at the bottom identifies the location and street name, and a website watermark is overlaid on the lower right.

Color postcard showing a monument built into a grassy mound with side staircases. At the center is a large arched entrance in stone, above which is the inscription "VLADISLAO VARNENSI" flanked by heraldic shields. A tall white column with a cross on top rises from the top of the mound, and trees and lawn surround the structure under a blue sky with clouds.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a formal outdoor gathering in a tree‑lined public garden. Numerous men in military and naval uniforms and a few women in white dresses are seated or standing in rows, as if for an official group portrait. Flags hang among the trees. At the top a date is handwritten, and across the bottom there is a long handwritten message in Greek. Printed French text near the bottom left identifies the place, and a modern Greek website watermark appears on the right.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view over a rural landscape with fields, trees, a lake and distant hills. A village with scattered houses and a prominent church with a tall spire appears on the right side. A road with fences runs in the foreground. Printed text along the bottom reads a location name and a photographer credit.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a lakeside scene framed by tree branches. Across the water stand several buildings, including a villa-like structure and a timbered house by a wooded hill. In the distant background, industrial chimneys or mining towers rise on a hill. Red printed German text at the top reads "Freiberg i. S." and "Kreuzteich und Schwanenschlösschen." The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century tinted lithographic postcard.

Black‑and‑white river panorama taken from an elevated viewpoint. A paddle steamer travels along a broad river that curves through a town. On the left bank, closely packed houses rise up a hill crowned by a long rectangular building with a tall tower or steeple. In the middle distance are two bridges: one appears to be a suspension or chain bridge, and behind it a long multi‑arched stone or masonry railway viaduct. On the right, steep rocky cliffs rise directly from the river, with a small building or chapel visible at the cliff top. The distant background shows low mountains or large hills. The foreground is framed by tree branches and a railing, emphasizing the scenic overlook. No printed text is visible on the image side.

Color-tinted historical postcard showing an inner courtyard surrounded by arcaded Renaissance-style buildings. The courtyard has three stories of open arches with balustrades, a red-tiled roof with dormer windows, and a small round tower-like structure with a green domed roof on the left. There is also an ornate well in the courtyard. At the top of the image, blue printed text reads the place name and location.

Black-and-white postcard showing a church in winter, largely obscured by leafless trees. The building has a tall tower with arched windows and an ornate belfry topped by a spire. The long nave with simple rectangular windows extends to the right. In the lower left corner, the caption reads "Skuttunge Kyrka."

Vintage sepia postcard view of a large formal square with trees, lampposts, people walking, and a prominent fountain with sculpted figures in the foreground. Dominating the background is an ornate, historic building with a central clock tower and elaborate façade, surrounded by multi‑storey city buildings lining the square.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a large church with a tall, pointed spire topped by a cross. The church has high pitched roofs, arched windows and a square tower base. Trees and low fencing surround the building, and a tall streetlamp stands in the foreground. The printed caption at the top reads "Norberg. Kyrkan."

Colorized historical postcard showing French soldiers unloading goods from a ship or train onto a dock crowded with sacks and crates. The men wear military uniforms and red fez-style caps. It appears to be a busy harbor scene in the early 20th century. Printed French text is at the top, and there is a handwritten message across the sky area.

Black‑and‑white streetscape of a wide, unpaved main street lined with two‑ to three‑story commercial buildings. Horse‑drawn carriages stand along both sides, and numerous wooden utility poles with cross‑arms and wires run down the street. On the left is a sign for a 'New York Bakery' and an 'Elite Restaurant.' On the right are brick storefronts and a neoclassical bank‑like building with tall columns. In the distance stand taller towers or domes, possibly a courthouse or civic buildings. The overall style suggests a North American town in the late 19th or early 20th century.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a sandy beach with dunes and grasses in the foreground, a wooded shoreline and calm water with a small sailboat in the background. Numerous people are sunbathing on the sand. White caption text in Swedish is printed along the bottom of the image, together with a small photographer/publisher imprint.

Colorized historic postcard view of an ornate town hall building with a tall clock tower topped by a spire and weather vane. The architecture has elaborate decorative gables and red tiled roofs. In front of the building stands a sculpted fountain or monument in an open square. The sky is blue with a few clouds. Printed text at the top identifies the location and the building.

A black‑and‑white postcard photograph of powerful river rapids with foaming water crashing over rocks. Forested hills and a few scattered buildings and power lines are visible in the background. The lower left corner bears a caption with the place name, and a small publisher's imprint appears in the lower right.

A black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a four‑storey urban villa or small palace on a broad, unpaved street. The building shows late 19th–early 20th century eclectic architecture with strong neoclassical influence: columned corner loggias, balustraded balconies, ornate cornices, and a steep, partly mansard roof with finials and railings. People in early 1900s clothing stand on the sidewalks, balconies, and entry steps. The façade has small street-level signs near the doors but they are too small to read clearly. Adjacent buildings in a similar historicist style are visible in the background.

A monochrome postcard showing a formally posed portrait of a high‑ranking Qing dynasty woman seated indoors on an ornate throne. She wears elaborate imperial robes with intricate patterns and holds a round fan. Behind her is a richly decorated backdrop with large flowers and drapery. On both sides stand tall pedestals bearing trays piled with fruit and decorative objects; a peacock figure is visible above on the right. Across the upper portion of the image hangs a horizontal Chinese inscription on a scroll.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a waterfront panorama of a small town with a prominent church on a hill, several wooden houses and boats along the shoreline across a calm river or bay. The lower part of the card contains printed and handwritten Swedish text.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large, symmetrical brick building with steep tiled roofs and dormer windows, enclosed by an iron fence with a central gate. A gas-style street lamp stands near the entrance, and leafless trees suggest winter. The printed captions at the top identify the location as an orphanage in Brielle.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a riverside scene. In the foreground three boys sit and fish from a grassy bank beside a calm river. Across the water there is a line of tall trees and behind them a small town with tiled roofs and walls. The style and coloration suggest an early 20th‑century printed postcard. In the upper left corner is German text giving the place name and location by the river.

A colorized postcard view of a tranquil waterfront scene in a small village. There is a calm bay or river in the foreground with two small wooden boats, one with a sail and one with several people on board. On the opposite shore stand light-colored stone houses with red-tiled roofs surrounded by tall trees and greenery. The scene is peaceful and rural, with soft pastel tones. Printed text at the top left names the location, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a two‑story neoclassical railway station building with people standing and sitting on the platform in front of it. Train tracks run across the foreground. The facade has arched and rectangular windows, and a central entrance with a small portico. The building bears the name "DZĒRBENE," and the word "LATVIJA" appears in the lower left corner of the postcard. In the lower right corner the place name "DZĒRBENE" and a number are printed along with a small emblem.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a hilly rural village with tightly clustered houses. Many buildings are traditional half‑timbered structures with steep gabled tile roofs and plaster infill, surrounded by trees and small gardens. Narrow roads wind between the houses, and wooden and masonry facades dominate the foreground. There are telephone or power poles but no visible cars or modern signage.

Black‑and‑white waterfront view of a historic European city. In the foreground are several steam-powered boats and small ships on a broad river or canal. On the right bank stand narrow gabled merchant houses and warehouses. In the background rise large brick churches with tall towers typical of North German / Baltic architecture. The overall look is early‑20th‑century harbor life in an old Hanseatic city.

A vintage monochrome postcard depicting a woman standing indoors wearing an elaborate traditional folk costume, including a long embroidered dress, apron, and head covering. There is ornate furniture and a column or pedestal behind her. Along the right edge appears printed caption text in French and English, and a circular stamp-like emblem is visible on the left side. A website watermark 'www.elia.org.gr' appears at the bottom.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a studio photograph of a marble bust of a bearded man in a suit. The bust stands on a pedestal inscribed with the name of the person portrayed. Printed captions along the bottom identify the sitter and the sculptor in a non‑English language.

Black‑and‑white street scene in a historic European town. Cobblestone road lined with multi‑storey shops and townhouses curves gently toward an ornate building with turrets and a high, steep roof at the end of the street. People in early 20th‑century dress walk along the sidewalks and a horse‑drawn wagon travels up the street. On the right corner is a shop with a large projecting clock and signage for "Paul Richter"; on the left is a shop with an awning carrying the name "Julius Fritsch". The right‑hand shop window advertises various goods such as coffee, sugar, cocoa, tea, cigars, wine, and spirits, described as "Kolonialwaren" (colonial goods) and "Drogen". The overall view resembles a commercial street captured for a postcard.

A black‑and‑white street scene showing a European city around the early 20th century. The view looks down a cobblestone street lined with four‑ to five‑story masonry buildings, many with ornate window frames and dormer roofs. On the right side are shopfronts with awnings, including one with large display windows and signage above. Several pedestrians, including children and women in long skirts and hats, walk along the street. Horse‑drawn vehicles are absent, and there are no automobiles visible. The overall composition and framing resemble a historic postcard photograph.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a European riverside town with a large bridge crossing the river in the foreground. On a hill above the town stands a vast castle‑like complex and a Gothic cathedral with multiple tall spires. Traditional buildings fill the lower town, and blossoming tree branches frame the right side of the image. Caption text is printed along the bottom margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the exterior of a large Romanesque cathedral with an apse, heavy stone walls, and a tall central tower topped with a cross. In the foreground there is a small fenced area and an ornate portal; adjoining buildings are visible on the right. The lower margin of the card contains printed captions in red and black, and the rest of the front is filled with handwritten cursive text.

A vintage monochrome postcard view of a broad town square lined with trees and surrounding buildings, with groups of people standing and children playing in the open space. In the background rises a church complex with a tall clock tower and spire. The caption at the bottom reads in German that this is the parade ground with church in Torgau, and the printing credit notes Brück & Sohn, Meissen, 1904.

Black‑and‑white view of a cobblestoned town square lined with traditional gabled houses. On the right are two-story buildings with shop and restaurant signs; in the distance on the left rises a large church with a tall tower and pointed spire. A few pedestrians stand in the mostly empty square. The scene has an early‑20th‑century European small‑town atmosphere.

Colorized vintage view over a small European town surrounded by green fields and forests. The scene shows clustered houses with red and green roofs and a prominent church with a tall spire on the right. At the bottom border there is a caption printed in a cursive script.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a tall, rectangular tower with an open balustraded viewing platform (belvedere) at the top, set among trees. A wooden bridge with brick posts leads toward the tower, and several children in early 20th‑century clothing stand on the bridge. Printed captions at the bottom identify the scene, with additional handwritten notes over the margin.

A monochrome postcard showing a tall sculpted monument with a statue of Dante Alighieri standing on top of a multi-tiered pedestal adorned with reliefs and seated figures. Mountains form the backdrop, and part of a church or bell tower is visible to the right. At the bottom border of the image, printed text identifies the subject and location.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the courtyard of a modernist school building with large rectangular windows and a rounded glass stairwell or bay on the facade. In the landscaped yard there are benches where several people sit. Prominently in the foreground stands a bust of a man on a tall stone pedestal. Text in Swedish is printed in the lower left and right corners.

A sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a mountain village scene. In the foreground stands a three-story hotel building with the words "ALBERGO CENTRALE" on its facade. The structure is set at a road junction, with trees and smaller buildings around it. In the background are forested hills and cultivated fields typical of an Alpine valley. At the bottom margin, printed text identifies the location as S. Orsola at 950 meters above sea level and describes it as a bathing/health resort.

Black‑and‑white view of a wooded park lake crowded with small rowboats carrying people in early‑20th‑century clothing. In the background is a pavilion or lakeside building with a terrace, set among tall trees. Along the shoreline more people are gathered near railings and a small bridge. Printed caption text appears at the bottom.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a panoramic view of a hillside cityscape with several large institutional buildings and a prominent round tower and walls on the ridge in the background. The foreground has gardens and smaller buildings. Greek text is printed at the upper left, and French text identifying the place as an Ottoman hospital in Salonique appears at the upper right. A website watermark (elia.org.gr) is overprinted at the bottom right.

Black‑and‑white aerial or elevated view of a rural town surrounded by farmland and fields. Rows of small detached houses are visible, along with trees and cultivated plots. In the distance stands an industrial area with chimneys and smoke plumes. At the bottom left, the word "VARGÖN" is printed, and at the bottom right there is a small triangular publisher's logo with the number 4945.

Black‑and‑white view of a broad tree‑lined street in a European city, showing horse‑drawn carriages, a few pedestrians, and late‑19th‑/early‑20th‑century buildings. On the left and right foreground are classical portico structures with columns and lanterns. In the background rise a large multi‑towered Gothic church or cathedral and, to its right, a Baroque‑style building with ornate roofline and a tall tower with an onion‑shaped dome. The scene is quiet and largely unmotorized, evoking a pre‑automobile era.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a festive street parade in a city center. People in traditional folk costumes march beneath a decorative archway resembling a stone gate, while crowds line the sidewalks and watch from building windows and balconies. Many commercial shop signs in Cyrillic script are visible on the façades. The large horizontal banner hanging from the arch is dated 1937 and other Cyrillic inscriptions appear on storefronts and placards.

Black‑and‑white view down a broad formal avenue lined with very tall, tightly clipped conical hedges leading toward a large Baroque palace with three main pavilions, the outer ones crowned by onion-shaped domes and lanterns. The scene is symmetrical and framed like a classic tourist photograph of a grand European residence and its gardens.

Black‑and‑white historical view of a cobbled town square with people, mostly children, standing and walking in the open space. On the right is a large, two‑storey building with a clock‑tower cupola; the facade bears the signage "Hotel" and "Rathskeller." suggesting it serves as a town hall/inn. On the left, a row of attached houses and shops lines the street, one with the sign "Gustav Bierkamp." A horse‑drawn wagon stands at the far right edge. The architecture and clothing indicate an early 20th‑century Central European small town.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a detailed model of the polar exploration ship "Fram" displayed in a glass case inside a museum. The model sailing vessel with multiple masts and sails fills most of the foreground, with reflections of windows and other ship models in the background. Text is printed along the bottom edge in Norwegian, and there is a small printer/publisher mark at the lower right.

Colorized vintage view over a small spa town nestled among wooded hills. In the foreground is a dark field with a light fence; behind it are many 19th‑century townhouses and larger spa buildings among trees. On the right stands a prominent church with a tall, slender spire and nearby historic-looking civic buildings. The sky is softly tinted in pastel colors. At the top left the place name 'BAD ELSTER' is printed, and on one of the right-hand buildings the word 'ASTREA' is visible.

A colorized panoramic view of a small European village with scattered houses, winding roads, fields, and a prominent church with a tall spire on the right side. The scene is seen from an elevated, wooded vantage point. At the top, printed in red text, it reads "Mohorn i. Sa. Oberdorf."

A black-and-white postcard view of a small hillside village surrounded by dense coniferous forest. Traditional gabled houses and pensions are scattered on the slope, with fields and meadows in the foreground. At the bottom edge there is a printed caption in German indicating the place and elevation.

A monochrome vintage postcard view over a wide river with a side‑wheel steamship in midstream. In the foreground are several large residential villas surrounded by trees on a slope. Across the river lies a town with industrial buildings and church towers, and behind it rolling hills with scattered houses and fields. The caption in red at the top reads "Meissen. Blick vom Bergschlösschen".

Colorized image of a historic multi‑story townhouse or small hotel with ornate stone façade and many green window shutters. Two small balconies with decorative wrought‑iron railings face a tree‑lined street and a garden terrace enclosed by a balustrade. Ivy climbs an adjacent building. Behind the houses rises a steep, forested hillside. The style evokes a Central European spa or residential district.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a large motor ship named "Ciudad de Cadiz" moored in a harbor. Smaller boats and masts are visible in the background along with a misty shoreline and port facilities. The vessel dominates the scene, photographed in profile from the water. A white border surrounds the image, and printed captions appear below the photograph.

An old colored postcard showing two steamships moored side by side in a harbor at sunset. Both ships fly tricolor flags of Romania (vertical stripes of blue, yellow, and red). The name "Constanţa" appears at the upper left, and the ships bear the names "Traian" (or "Împ. Traian") and "România" on their sterns. There is printed text in Romanian at the upper right and faint handwritten text across the lower part of the image.

Black-and-white postcard showing an ornate Baroque/rococo-style palace façade with high windows and shutters, elaborate stucco decoration, and a garden path lined with large classical statues on pedestals in the foreground. Leafless trees suggest late autumn or winter. The right margin bears printed vertical text indicating the subject and location.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing an ornate, richly decorated small palace or pavilion in an eclectic Ottoman/Baroque style, surrounded by trees. The façade is heavily ornamented with reliefs, columns, and an elaborate central entrance reached by side stairs. The card is filled with handwritten script across the margins and over the image. Printed captions include the place name in French and in English/Latin script.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large historicist-style corner building with elaborate façades, columns, and a central tower-like roof feature. People in late 19th–early 20th century clothing walk along the cobblestone street, and a horse-drawn carriage stands in front of the building. Printed German captions identify the building as the imperial and royal post and telegraph office and send greetings from Graz. A circular archival stamp and the printed year 1903 appear at the bottom.

Colorized vintage postcard showing a steep glacial cirque in high mountains with lingering snowfields on the rocky slopes and a small dark pond at the bottom. On the distant ridge there appears to be a small building or shelter. At the bottom edge, a German caption is printed.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a dirt street lined with simple thatched huts or shelters on both sides, with groups of people standing along the road. The scene is labeled as a workers' camp in Léopoldville, in the former Belgian Congo. On the right side of the card, in large cursive script, are the words "Meilleurs Souvenirs."

Black‑and‑white interior view of an old-fashioned restaurant or inn. The room has neatly set tables with white tablecloths and wooden chairs. The walls are crowded with decorative items: clocks, framed pictures, plates, hunting tools, saws crossed in an X, and rustic household objects. Lace trim runs along the top of a long bench. In the background a doorway reveals another similarly furnished room. The style suggests a Central European, possibly Alpine, guesthouse or tavern.

Sepia-toned street scene showing a crowded bazaar beneath a monumental stone gateway with two tall, slender Ottoman-style minarets rising above it. The foreground is filled with people, animals, and carts in a narrow street lined with old multi‑story buildings. At the bottom edge there is a printed caption identifying the view.

Black‑and‑white postcard view over a rural village set in a valley with fields and forested hills in the background. In the foreground is a grassy slope with trees on the right side. Scattered houses and farm buildings are visible among trees in the middle distance. Printed caption text appears at the bottom left reading "Sohland/Spree – An der Obersohlmlede" and a small code "K37155 B" appears in the bottom right.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard with two vignette photographs. The left vignette shows a rural inn or farmhouse with wooden buildings, a fenced yard and a horse‑drawn carriage; it is labeled "Gasthof von Fr. Erdnüss." The right vignette presents a general view of a small village in hilly countryside with scattered houses and a church with a tower; it is labeled "Gruss aus Birnbach." Handwritten German script text surrounds the images on the top and bottom margins.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view over a broad river with several moored and passing boats. In the foreground are tree‑covered banks; a long pier or jetty extends into the water with barges alongside. In the distance a large arched bridge crosses the river and low buildings and fields lie beyond. Printed text at the top left reads in Dutch: "Nijmegen. Panorama vanuit Lent gezien."

Illustrated color postcard showing a Baroque church façade and surrounding buildings in an urban square. The church has ornate sculptural decoration, a central portal, and a small tower with a bulbous dome. Multi‑story townhouses with red roofs and shuttered windows flank the church. Trees and a few small human figures appear in the foreground. Handwritten cursive text runs vertically along the right side. Printed captions in German are at the top and bottom edges.

Black‑and‑white image of a landscaped park with curving paths and dense trees framing a large, ornate stone monument. The monument features a central standing female figure on a tall pedestal, with seated allegorical figures around the base and circular medallions or reliefs. Behind the trees, a church or town‑hall–like building with a clock on its tower and a tall spire rises in the background. The scene is formal and symmetrical, typical of an early 20th‑century city park postcard. Any inscriptions on the monument are too small and blurred to read.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of large early‑20th‑century spa or hotel buildings along a curved street, with a park or grassy slope and trees in the foreground. In the distance a church or tower rises above other town buildings. At the top in red German text it reads "Karlsbad Kurhaus zum Goldenen Kreuz."

Colorized vintage postcard view of a riverside scene at sunset or dawn. A wooden footbridge with many posts crosses a calm river, reflecting the bridge and surrounding trees in the water. On the far bank stands a two‑story building with a red roof labeled as a restaurant, surrounded by dense trees and garden structures. Printed caption text appears at the upper left.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the interior of a richly decorated historic room with swirling painted patterns covering the walls and ceiling. There is a large wooden table in the center, carved furniture, a tiled or painted stove in the back, and an open doorway leading to another room. Printed caption text appears in the lower‑right corner.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped spa square with low, manicured hedges, benches, and flagpoles in the foreground. A long colonnaded walkway runs across the middle of the scene, leading to a multi‑storey historic building with arched windows and a clock on the gable. Large trees form a backdrop. The caption "Bad Elster. Badeplatz" is printed at the bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white panoramic view taken from a field toward a small European town nestled in a valley. In the foreground is a cultivated field, then a few detached houses along a lane. Farther back stand several large institutional buildings with mansard or steep roofs and a prominent multi‑storey wing on the left. Near the center‑right of the town is a church with a tall spire; other church‑like buildings with towers appear nearby. The town is surrounded by forested hills in the background. There is no visible printed caption or handwriting on the image side.

Vintage sepia postcard with three photographs showing traditional rural life and people in folk costumes. The large right-hand image depicts a couple in traditional Greek dress standing in a doorway, apparently engaged or being married. Two smaller images on the left show villagers: one outside a stone house, another inside a room with a loom or weaving apparatus. On the right side of the postcard there is printed French text indicating Greece, the Peloponnese region, and the town of Andritsaina.

A black‑and‑white historical postcard showing a panoramic view of a city district heavily damaged by fire. Many buildings are roofless or burned out, streets are filled with debris, and the overall scene depicts widespread destruction. Printed captions in French and English describe the scene as a general view of the city after the fire of 18–19–20 August. The word "Salonica" appears prominently, along with French "Salonique". A small number "20" appears at the start of the caption, and there is a publisher mark or logo on the lower right.

Black‑and‑white view of a cloister-like courtyard of an ivy-covered college building. The image is framed by stone columns with ornate capitals in the foreground, opening onto a formal garden with paths, trimmed bushes, and a central statue on a tall pedestal. Large multi-pane windows line the surrounding walls. At the bottom of the image, in a decorative script, appears the caption "Canisius-College."

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a stone fountain in a small European square. The fountain has a tall, decorated pedestal with lion-head spouts and a seated female figure on top, posed in a contemplative manner. Surrounding it are old multi‑story buildings with shuttered windows and cobblestone pavement. Along the bottom border, handwritten-style text identifies the location.

Black-and-white postcard view of a large, classical-style three‑storey building partly obscured by mature trees, seen from across a broad street. A low stone wall runs along the front, with pedestrians and benches visible on the sidewalk. The building has a simple but formal façade, with rows of rectangular windows and a central section bearing a crest and flagpole. In the lower left corner of the image, printed text reads "VÄNERSBORG. Residenset." and a small number "35124" appears in the lower right corner.

A vintage, colored postcard view of a broad cobblestone street with tram tracks, lined with multi‑story historic buildings and shops. Many pedestrians in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalks and street. A distinctive corner building with a tall, steep roof and decorative façade dominates the center-right. At the top left of the postcard, multilingual text names the city and the street.

Colorized historic postcard showing a large Gothic church with a polygonal apse, tall pointed windows, and a steep red roof with a slender spire in front of a taller tower with a bulbous Baroque dome and clock. In the foreground there is an open-air market with rows of stalls under white canopies in a town square. Printed captions at the bottom identify the place and publisher.

Black‑and‑white view of a long, grand colonnade with rows of Corinthian columns and ornate ceiling coffers and hanging lamps. People in early-20th-century clothing—men in long coats and bowler or top hats, women in long dresses and hats—stroll or sit along the corridor. The perspective looks through the colonnade toward large arched openings at the far end. There is no visible printed caption or handwriting on the image side.

Reverse side of an old postcard with printed multilingual wordings for 'postcard' across the top, a vertical dividing line, handwritten purple ink message on the left and address on the right. There is a green 5 pfennig stamp of the Deutsches Reich cancelled with a circular postmark that reads 'DRESDEN'. Along the left edge is a printed publisher credit in German mentioning 'Dresdner Kunstverlag Gustav Schmidt, Dresden A.27'.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard with an ornate dark border framing an oval photograph of a town. The view shows densely packed tile‑roofed houses and several church towers rising above them, set against a barren hillside in the background. The style and print quality suggest an early 20th‑century postcard. There is printed caption text below the image and a faint circular stamp on the left. A website watermark (not original to the card) appears across the lower right of the image.

A colorized, painted panoramic view of a European town nestled in a lush, green valley, surrounded by low, rolling hills or small mountains. In the foreground and middle ground are many trees and villas with red-tiled roofs and white facades. Toward the center is a hill rising above the town, topped by a small structure or tower, with more town buildings spreading out beyond it. The distant background shows layered hills under a partly cloudy sky. There is no visible printed caption on the front.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view over a snowy, sparsely vegetated landscape with a small industrial complex and scattered town buildings in the middle distance. Low hills surround the settlement, one of which is prominent on the left. In the foreground there is a solitary house partly covered in snow. Printed white text at the bottom left reads "Kiruna med Luossavaara."

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a church with a tall central tower topped by a lantern and cross. The building has a classical facade, arched windows, and a staircase leading up from a tree‑lined forecourt. Several small figures are visible near the entrance. At the bottom of the image, printed in red text, are the words "Carl Johans Kyrka." on the left and "Göteborg." on the right.

The image shows the reverse side of an old postcard or postal card with handwritten German text in black ink. The card has a small round hole punched near the top edge and printed text along the bottom margin. The handwriting is cursive and fills most of the card. At the top right there is a place and date written, starting with "Leipzig" followed by a date in 1918. The card is displayed against a dark background.

A black‑and‑white historical postcard view of a European city boulevard with tram tracks and several pedestrians. On the right stands a large, ornate neoclassical building with a central dome and mansard roofs, facing a landscaped triangular park with paths, trees, and low hedges. In the distance are more multi‑story buildings and church spires under a hazy sky. The image appears slightly faded and worn, typical of early‑20th‑century postcards. No clear caption or title is visible on the front.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a low, rectangular neoclassical building with arched windows and a central arched entrance labeled "RECORDS" on the frieze above the doorway. The building is surrounded by trees and shrubs, with a dirt road in the foreground and a larger multi‑story civic structure visible behind it. Printed red text at the top identifies the location, and there are bold handwritten cataloging numbers and notes across the sky area.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a small settlement with wooden houses and a prominent large white church-like building with a tower on the right. In the foreground is an open grassy field; behind it run a road and telephone poles. Trees and additional houses are visible in the background under a cloudy sky. Text identifying the place appears at the bottom left, and a small logo of the photographer/printer appears at the bottom right.

A colorized panoramic postcard view of a historic European spa town nestled in a narrow valley surrounded by forested hills. The town is densely packed with multi‑story buildings, many with red roofs and ornate 19th‑century facades. A wooded hill rises steeply on the right. At the top left in red and black Gothic script appears a German caption identifying the scene as a view toward the Schlossberg and the Hirschensprung in Karlsbad.

Black‑and‑white view of a substantial villa or guesthouse with a tiled roof and large glassed‑in veranda, set in a wooded valley. Terraced gardens and cultivated beds occupy the foreground. A tall chimney stands behind an adjoining lower wing. On the hillside road to the right there is a signboard reading "Grundmühle". Some partially visible wall text on the building suggests it may be an inn or restaurant.

A sepia-toned postcard showing a grand stone building with a large arched entrance, heavy rusticated lower walls, and classical columns above. Sculptures and decorative reliefs adorn the façade, with a balustraded roofline and a sculptural group on top. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk in front of the building. In white script at the bottom left, the caption reads "The Municipal Art Gallery Bristol."

Black-and-white postcard view of a small wooden railway station building labeled "HALLSTA" on two signs. People in early 20th‑century clothing stand on the platform beside railway tracks. There are posters on the station walls, a tall telegraph/flag pole in front, and dense forest in the background. The caption at the bottom reads "HÅLLSTA JERNVÄGSSTATION."

The image shows the back of an old postcard with printed multilingual headings such as "Carte postale", "Postkarte", "Cartolina postale", and others, indicating it follows the Universal Postal Union format. A red 10-cent stamp is affixed in the upper right corner, partially cancelled with a circular postmark. The rest of the card contains handwritten address text in Spanish, directing the card to a recipient in Seville. The card has aged yellow paper with some stains and wear.

Black-and-white postcard view of a rural road lined with fences and stone posts, leading toward a tall church with a slender spire on the left (Ringsaker Kirke). On the right are large wooden houses with steep roofs and multiple windows, and several telegraph poles with many wires. Leafless trees and forested hills appear in the background. Printed captions in Norwegian identify the scene and the photographer/publisher, dated 1922.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a wooded landscape with a narrow path running through a forested hillside. A solitary figure, likely a farmer or wood-gatherer, walks along the path carrying a large bundle on their back and holding a walking stick. At the top right of the image there is printed red text in Dutch referencing a nearby hotel and locality near Nijmegen.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large multi‑story mill complex beside a river. A stone bridge with several arches crosses the water in the foreground, with many people standing along its railing. The mill buildings and bridge are reflected clearly in the calm river. Trees form a backdrop behind the structures. Printed caption text in German appears at the top right.

A vintage monochrome postcard depicting a walkway between long arcaded stone walls, likely former fortifications, with several people standing and walking along the path. At the far end is a large arched gateway built into an earthen rampart, with trees visible above. The lower margin bears printed captions in red Gothic-style script that identify the scene as a location in Graz and specify 'Schloßberg-Casematten.'

A multi-view postcard showing a night panorama of a coastal city with illuminated harbor and waterfront, two interior views of a modest restaurant or dining hall with wooden tables and red accents, and a daytime scene of a rocky hilltop with a stone lookout tower and a nearby wooden building surrounded by pine trees. The word 'SUNDSVALL' is printed vertically in large black letters between the views.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a calm river scene. In the foreground a small ferry boat with several people and a ferryman stands on the water. In the background a rural riverbank with a path leading up to a modest building with a red roof and large tree beside it, with fields and scattered houses further back. The sky is lightly clouded. German text is printed at the top of the image.

A monochrome panoramic view of a small town with wooden houses and fences in the foreground and larger masonry buildings and churches with tall steeples in the background. The image is bordered like an old postcard, with the word "Kotka" printed at the lower left and a publisher line in a small serif font along the bottom.

Sepia-toned postcard view of an iron arch bridge crossing a river, with ornate railings and lampposts. Multi‑storey historic buildings line the far riverbank, and a wooded hillside rises on the right. Printed caption text at the top reads "GRAZ, Kaiser Ferdinands-Brücke."

Black‑and‑white view of a tree‑lined avenue in front of a large late‑19th‑century villa with elaborate window frames and a steep hipped roof. Behind it rise terraced, largely bare hillsides that appear to be vineyards. Scattered on the slope are several detached villas and, on the hilltop, a pavilion or small mansion. There is no visible printed caption or writing on the image.

A black‑and‑white vintage view of a large European city square with tram tracks, pedestrians, and classical stone buildings. A canal or basin crosses the right side of the square, bordered by railings. In the center distance is a prominent neoclassical building with arched windows and columns, and around the square are several multi‑story buildings. The image has printed captions in Swedish at the bottom identifying the place and publisher.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a panoramic waterfront view with a long pier or jetty extending into the sea, low buildings along the shore, and hills in the background. It includes printed titles in both Greek and French and a large handwritten signature across the lower part.

Sepia-toned historical postcard showing a waterfront quay lined with masted sailing ships. In the foreground and middle distance there is a long column of soldiers on horseback moving along the cobbled street beside the harbor. On the right, civilian pedestrians walk along the sidewalk and telephone poles line the road. At the top right is printed text reading "SALONIQUE – Le Quai." A web address "www.elia.org.gr" appears at the bottom.

Vintage, lightly colorized postcard showing a stone gate tower on the left leading into a road that curves past trees toward a dramatic cityscape built on cliffs. The skyline features church spires and historic buildings overlooking a deep valley. Printed captions at the bottom identify the scene as Luxembourg and specifically the Porte de Trèves, with publisher details in small type.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a hilly rural village with scattered houses, fields, and dense trees. A church or chapel with a clock tower and dome stands prominently in the lower right area. The village stretches across the slopes with farm buildings and winding paths visible. At the upper left, the printed caption reads "Oberkipsdorf", and across the top center there is a large handwritten red number.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a large industrial brewery complex at the base of rocky cliffs, with multiple long factory buildings, chimneys, rail tracks and sidings in the foreground, and wooded hills behind. The caption in red German text appears below the image, with a printer's mark and number at the bottom and a handwritten red number at the top right.

Color-tinted vintage postcard showing a white church with a tall spire and large arched windows, viewed from slightly below behind trees, a stone wall, and a white wooden fence. Handwritten cursive text covers the sky area and the lower margin. The printed caption under the image reads "Vangs Kirke," indicating the name of the church.

Black‑and‑white view of a large Gothic church with a massive square tower surmounted by a multi‑tiered Baroque spire. In front of the side façade there is a landscaped square with small trees and flowerbeds, as well as a statue on a pedestal standing between two small turreted chapel‑like structures. Residential buildings with steep roofs appear in the background. The image has rough white masking around the tower area and handwritten numbers along the bottom border, suggesting an old photographic postcard or plate.

Black‑and‑white historic street scene showing a European city square with ornate late‑19th‑century buildings, shops with striped awnings at street level, and people in Edwardian‑era clothing walking across a broad plaza. A decorative cast‑iron streetlamp stands prominently in the foreground. Large painted wall advertisements in German are visible on the side of a building, and a monument or fountain is faintly visible deeper in the square.

A monochrome postcard view of an ornate pedestrian bridge leading through a decorative wrought‑iron gate flanked by stone pillars into a tree‑lined park. Three figures walk away from the viewer toward buildings visible beyond the gate. The caption at the bottom identifies the location as the entrance to Valkhof in Nijmegen. Printer and copyright information are also printed along the lower margin.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a church with a tall, slender spire rising from an onion‑shaped dome atop a square tower. The church façade has narrow arched windows and simple plastered walls, with a gabled nave and a modest entrance partly obscured by trees. The street in front is unpaved and there is an early 20th‑century vehicle or shed structure at the left edge, suggesting a small European town setting. No printed caption or visible writing appears on the image side.

Colored lithographic view over a small European town nestled in a valley with forested hills and vineyards in the background. The foreground shows streets lined with 19th‑century houses and public buildings, with a few pedestrians. Church towers are visible among dense trees in the middle distance. The style is typical of late‑19th‑ or early‑20th‑century German picture postcards. Text in German appears at the bottom and top of the image.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a quiet curved beach with a small boat near the shore, gentle waves, and a mostly undeveloped coastline backed by low wooded hills. A few isolated white buildings stand on the slopes above the bay. Greek text is printed in the lower border, along with a website watermark over the image.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a long, straight city street lined with tall leafy trees on the left and ornate multi‑storey buildings on the right. Tram tracks run along the middle of the cobbled street, with a few pedestrians visible. The scene is captioned at the bottom with the city name and the street name in decorative script.

Color-tinted landscape view of a terraced hillside with a small village at its base. Scattered white houses, a church with a bell tower, cultivated fields and low stone walls fill the foreground. Greek and Latin-character captions are printed at the top, and a website watermark appears at the bottom.

Vintage sepia postcard with a central oval photograph showing a rural landscape near a village: rocky ground, dense vegetation including cacti, trees, and a distant mountain.
