Behind the railway lies a dense cluster of houses and industrial chimneys, rising up a hillside toward larger buildings and a prominent church or tower on the hilltop. The caption in the upper left reads "Nossen i. Sa.", printed in an old-style serif font.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a countryside inn named "Gasthof zum Erbgericht" in a rural, hilly landscape with orchards, a path in the foreground, and additional farm buildings in the background. Two men in early‑20th‑century attire stand on the grassy slope. Printed German text identifies the place as Hartmannsbach near Bad Gottleuba, and the card credits a Meissen-based printer/publisher.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a panoramic view of a large complex of rectangular, multi‑storey barracks-style buildings with inner courtyards, laid out in a grid in an urban setting surrounded by smaller houses. Trees line some paths and streets. The lower margin contains printed captions in red identifying the scene, while the rest of the card is filled with handwritten cursive text.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a landscaped park with a large reflective pond or lake in the foreground. A fountain rises from the center of the water, with a small building or pavilion at the far shore. Dense trees surround the water, and on the distant hilltop the ruins and towers of a castle can be seen. There is a small bridge on the right bank. Printed text at the top reads "WENDEN Schloss-Park".

A black‑and‑white postcard shows a large villa or guesthouse in a rural, hilly landscape. The building has two stories with dormer windows and a long glazed veranda on the right side. The word "Germaniabaude" is prominently written on the veranda. In the foreground there is an open field; to the right, trees line a path or road. Low forested hills rise in the misty background. Printed caption text appears at the bottom margin.

Black-and-white landscape postcard showing a panoramic view over forested hills and patchwork fields towards a small town with many detached houses and a prominent church spire. The caption at the bottom reads in German about Auersberg and Eibenstock, indicating a mountainous area at 1020 meters. The style and print suggest a mid-20th‑century European postcard.

Colorized vintage view over a heavily forested valley with a row of townhouses at the bottom and, above the trees, a large castle complex and towers on a hill. The caption in red German text at the top reads "Nossen i. S. Schloss und Talstrasse." indicating the castle and valley street of the town of Nossen.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a small historic town seen through tree branches in the foreground. The town has dense traditional houses with pitched roofs, a church with a tall spire rising above the rooftops on the right, and two prominent ruined stone towers on a wooded hill to the left. The single printed word "Kohren" appears in the upper left of the image.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a harbor scene with a large sailing ship moored beside a covered pier and customs buildings. People are visible under the metal canopies along the waterfront. The caption at the top is printed in French and Greek, identifying the location as the customs square in Argostoli. A modern website watermark appears at the bottom.

A monochrome image showing a Gothic stone façade with two large crowned statues of royals or saints set in niches high on the wall. Each figure stands on a carved console beneath an ornate canopy of miniature pinnacles and arches. Below them is a pointed, richly moulded Gothic doorway with tracery and a heavy studded wooden door. The architectural style is late medieval/early Renaissance Central European Gothic.

Sepia-toned vintage view of a mosque complex with an arched portico, masonry walls, ornate metal fence, and a tall minaret rising behind trees. The lower margin bears printed captions identifying the site and city, and there is a website watermark added later by an archive.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard view of a canal or river curving through a town set against mountains. Leafless trees line the embankment and a small bridge crosses the water. Prominently visible is a medieval-looking round tower attached to a building. At the bottom margin, printed captions read the city name and the specific landmark.

A black‑and‑white aerial view of a small town surrounded by dense coniferous forest. The settlement has detached wooden houses with steep gabled roofs, light facades and darker roofs, arranged along a few intersecting roads. One larger, darker building that could be a public hall or school stands prominently to the left. Gardens and small fields are visible between houses, and the general layout suggests a planned but sparsely populated settlement in a northern, heavily forested region.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style photograph of a large Renaissance / Baroque town hall dominating a market square. The building has a steep gabled roof with multiple stepped gables, dormer-like upper windows, a small turret with a spire in the center, and elaborate window framing. A columned balcony/portal marks the main entrance reached by stairs. In the foreground are townspeople in early-20th‑century clothing, a kiosk or advertising column, small market stalls, and a horse-drawn carriage. Shops line the ground floor of adjacent buildings around the square.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large ornate historic building complex facing an open square or park. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along wide streets with lampposts in front of the building. The card is heavily overlaid with handwritten script. Printed captions at the bottom identify the view and the publisher.

A black‑and‑white commemorative military postcard arranged as a collage. At the top center is a portrait of Kaiser Wilhelm, flanked by other uniformed officers and German imperial symbols. Beneath them are small photographs of barracks buildings, a guardhouse, landscapes, and regimental scenes, each labeled in German. At the bottom is a stag's head with crossed rifles and a banner containing German text marking the 100‑year anniversary of a Jäger (rifle) battalion from Hirschberg in Silesia.

Sepia-toned panoramic view over fields and trees toward a small town on a hill. A church with a tall spire rises above the houses, and on the right stands a prominent hilltop fortress or castle complex. At the top center of the image is the printed caption "Stolpen i. Sa."

Black‑and‑white view of a European town square dominated by a large equestrian statue of a military figure wearing a pickelhaube helmet and cloak, mounted on a tall stone pedestal surrounded by a low fence. Around the square stand multi‑storey buildings with shops on the ground floor. Large painted signs in German advertise various businesses such as clothing, colonial goods, mineral water, and a local newspaper. A few pedestrians are visible in the otherwise quiet cobbled square.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a dramatic rocky landscape along a large river. A single‑track railway line runs through tall, narrow basalt rock spires, one of which has a lone tree growing from its top. Telegraph poles follow the tracks. On the right is an open riverside plain sloping down to the broad river, with more isolated rock pinnacles scattered across it. Forested hills and headlands fade into the mist in the distance. Handwritten notes appear along the right margin in cursive script.

A sepia-tone postcard showing a panoramic view over open fields and distant low hills, seen from a wooded, bushy foreground. At the top there is a German caption printed in black, identifying the viewpoint as Duivelsberg at the German border and referring to the post office of Cranenburg.

Sepia-toned art reproduction postcard showing a Renaissance-style painted portrait of a noblewoman identified as Dona Maria, Infante of Portugal. She wears an elaborate dark dress with puffed white sleeves, pearl jewelry and headpiece, and holds a small folded paper or letter in her hands. Below the image is a printed caption in French referencing Chantilly and the Musée Condé, noting that this is a Spanish-school portrait.

Black-and-white vintage postcard showing a historic square lined with ornate Flemish-style gabled buildings. People are scattered around the open space, and a statue on a pedestal is visible to the right. Printed captions at the bottom read the place name and publisher information.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard with two photographs side by side. The left image shows an old stone church facade with arches and a smaller dome behind, labeled as St. Dimitrion in Mistra. The right image shows a balcony or loggia with several people standing and sitting, supported by stone arches below, looking out over a landscape. Printed French text at the top right identifies the location as Greece, Peloponnese, Mistra.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a neoclassical mansion set within a lush garden. The building has a flat roof, symmetrical façade, balcony with balustrade, and a central portico with columns. Trees and dense foliage frame a curved driveway leading to the entrance. Decorative printed text and a round stamp-like mark appear on the left in red ink, and additional red text appears at lower right. A modern website watermark "www.elia.org.gr" is overprinted across the bottom.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a town square with a canal or river in the foreground, stone embankment, and several trees framing a central obelisk monument. Behind the monument stands an ornate historic town hall building with a tall spire and clock, flanked by other classical town houses. Parked vintage cars from the early 20th century line the street on the right. Printed captions in Swedish appear at the lower left and lower right edges.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a small chapel with a tall steeple and cross, surrounded by leafless trees and a nearby building. At the bottom in red script it reads "Pensionat-Hauskapelle. Feldhof bei Graz." There is a purple circular stamp on the lower right reading "STEIERM. LANDES-ARCHIV" and the year "1903" printed beside it. Along the left border is a vertical imprint with the name and address of a printer in Graz.

An old sepia-toned waterside scene showing a small ornamental pavilion or birdhouse on a pond with a large white bird (likely a swan or goose) standing on a ramp. Behind the water is a low stone embankment and terrace covered with creeping plants, with stairs leading down to the water. Above the terrace stands a long, single‑storey building with a tiled roof and wooden veranda, next to older multi‑storey houses with steep gabled roofs and chimneys. The upper part of the image is stained and partially faded, consistent with an aged photographic postcard. No visible printed caption or handwriting appears on the front.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a richly decorated Eastern Orthodox church. The image shows a large iconostasis filled with icons, ornate chandeliers hanging from a wooden ceiling, and tall columns framing the nave. The photograph is printed with Cyrillic text along the bottom margin, including the place name Bansko and a note about the Holy Trinity church built in 1835.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a mid‑20th‑century cargo ship named M/S FIDRA underway on calm water, with a low wooded shoreline in the background and a partly cloudy sky. The ship has a single funnel marked with an 'S' and two masts. Printed captions appear in white text at the lower left and lower right edges of the image.

Black-and-white postcard view of a large Baroque hunting lodge with four round corner towers and domed roofs, situated on an island in a lake. The castle is seen across the water from a shaded, tree-lined shore in the foreground. The text "Jagdschloß Moritzburg" is printed in white at the lower right corner of the image.

Black‑and‑white portrait postcard showing a man in profile wearing an ornate metal helmet with feathers and richly decorated armor or costume, suggesting a theatrical or historical role. The lower margin contains printed text with the name of the person and the photographer's studio location.

Colorized vintage view of a large square with a neoclassical opera house in the background and an equestrian statue on a high pedestal in the foreground. Palm trees and low buildings surround the square. The caption at the top is in French, and a website watermark appears at the bottom right.

Black‑and‑white postcard view from a garden with paths, hedges and flowering bushes looking out over a body of water toward forested hills. A road and fence run along the shoreline in the middle distance. In the lower left corner there is a printed caption in Swedish and a small publisher's logo with a number in the lower right.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a residential city street with a railway bridge crossing above a sunken cobblestone road. In the foreground is the underpass, with a lone pedestrian walking below the bridge. Rail tracks run across the image on top of the bridge, with telegraph poles and wires alongside. On the left stands a large early‑20th‑century townhouse or apartment building with steep, tiled roof and dormer windows; commercial signs are mounted on or near the building. A tree‑lined avenue extends straight into the distance on the right side, bordered by more residential buildings and dense trees.

A black‑and‑white studio portrait of a man with short hair, a prominent mustache and small goatee, wearing a dark suit jacket, high-collared shirt and patterned bow tie. The figure fades softly into a light background in a classic cabinet-card or postcard style. At the bottom border, ornate studio-imprint text appears, including a photographer's name and the word "STOCKHOLM."

Colorized vintage postcard showing a busy sandy beach scene with many people in early 20th‑century swimwear. In the background there is a large pavilion or beach building with the word "LIDO" written in Latin and Cyrillic letters on the roof, surrounded by trees. A flag flies over a wooden structure with swings or gym equipment. The caption in the upper left reads "Zemun. Plaža".

A monochrome vintage postcard showing a serene park lake with people rowing small boats. Along the far shore is a tree‑lined promenade with benches, a pavilion or kiosk, and a classical-looking lakeside building visible through the trees. In the foreground there is a grassy slope with benches and a large ornamental planter on a pedestal overlooking the water. The caption at the top left reads "Graz. Hilmteich."

Black-and-white panoramic view of a small European town seen from fields in the foreground. The skyline is dominated by a large historic church with a tall tower and onion-shaped spire. Around it are dense, steep-roofed houses and a few larger brick buildings. In the distance, there are factory chimneys and gently rolling farmland, suggesting a mixed industrial and rural setting. The image has the style and framing typical of early 20th‑century picture postcards. No visible text appears on the image side.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a harbor scene with several warships sailing out to sea. The foreground features a large battleship with masts and smoke stacks, while additional vessels and a low, built-up shoreline are visible in the distance. There are printed German captions describing the departure of the German war squadron from Port Said, as well as printed text indicating greetings from Egypt and the publisher's details. Handwritten signatures and a date are visible across the lower portion of the card, and postal cancellation marks appear at the top.

Sepia-toned panoramic view of a small town nestled in a hilly, rural landscape. The town is composed of dense rows of multi-story houses, church towers, and a few taller chimneys, surrounded by fields and forested hills. At the top-left of the image, text reads "Olbernhau i. Erzgeb." indicating the place shown.

Hand-colored postcard view of a historic railway station building labeled "Kötzschenbroda. Bahnhof." A large, ornate multi-story station with mansard roof stands to the left, with people walking in front and a clock mounted on the façade. To the right are stairs leading up to the tracks behind a high retaining wall, and a fenced area and advertising column in the foreground. The sky has a soft gradient suggesting sunset or sunrise.

Black‑and‑white view of a forest path beside a calm body of water. Tall tree trunks and branches frame the bright lake or river in the background. The scene looks tranquil and natural, with printed caption text along the bottom edge.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing a group of wild boars being fed in an open sandy enclosure bordered by forest. In the background there is a rustic wooden building with people standing or sitting nearby behind a fence. The scene is rural and appears to be part of a game park or hunting estate. Decorative script text is printed along the bottom margin.

A black‑and‑white winter street scene showing a snowy road lined with wooden houses on both sides. An early 20th‑century bus or car is parked to the left, and a few pedestrians walk along the snow-covered street. Wooden fences and telegraph poles are visible. At the top left of the image there is printed text in Swedish.

Illustrated vintage postcard showing the Mosque of Muhammad Ali inside the Citadel of Cairo. The scene depicts the large domed mosque with tall minarets rising above massive fortress walls. In the foreground are people in traditional clothing, one riding a camel along a path, others standing or sitting near stone walls, with a stylized cityscape in the distance. The sky is rendered in warm sunset tones. The front contains printed French text naming the city and mosque, along with handwritten script at the bottom.

A vintage black-and-white postcard showing a riverside scene with dense trees and evergreens on the far bank. In the foreground, two figures in early 20th‑century clothing stand on the grassy shore of a calm river. Printed catalog numbers appear in the upper right, and a red caption at the bottom identifies the location as Necanicum in Seaside, Oregon.

Vintage monochrome view of a rural church with a square tower and spire, arched windows and a low churchyard wall, partly obscured by large trees. A dirt road curves in the foreground. The caption in the upper-right reads "Söderåkra kyrka."

Monochrome postcard with selective red coloring on the lower hull of an enormous ocean liner being launched from a shipyard, surrounded by tall cranes and a large crowd. A printed caption appears along the bottom edge.

Black‑and‑white photo postcard showing a close-up of a richly carved Gothic cathedral portal with elongated jamb statues of saints and kings, dense archivolts filled with small figures, and patterned colonnettes. A cursive "YVON" photographer's mark appears at lower right.

Black-and-white view from the water of a large manor-like house with a steep hipped roof and a central balcony/portico, set among trees on a shoreline with a stone edge. Caption text in Swedish appears at the lower left.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a grand neoclassical theatre building with arched windows and a pedimented roofline. Groups of people in early 20th‑century clothing stand in front. The caption at the bottom reads "TEATERN, KALMAR."

Back of a vintage divided-back postcard with the British royal coat of arms and the heading POST CARD. Printed British usage instructions appear on the left, a vertical publisher credit for Raphael Tuck & Sons is present, and the address is handwritten to Miss Christine Anderson, to Mrs Raymond, Strawberry Hill, Stamford. A green U.S. 1¢ Franklin stamp is affixed at the top right.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a distinctive central-plan church with a tall spire and small corner turrets. The church stands by a fence-lined road and a small bridge, with wooden rural houses in the background. The caption at the top right reads "Örsjö Kyrka."

Monochrome postcard showing a large square‑rigged sailing ship on choppy seas with another vessel behind it and a shoreline featuring a castle with tall spires in the distance. Printed artist credit appears at the lower left. A handwritten Swedish message is written across the bottom margin.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a landscaped park with curving gravel paths, newly planted trees, and benches beside a body of water. In the background, a striped cylindrical water tower and low buildings are visible. A Swedish caption is printed at the top.

Hand-tinted view of a harbor with steamships and small boats moored along a long quay. People stroll on the promenade beside a large waterfront building. Printed caption at top left reads "Sundsvall, Hamnen." One vessel bears the name "TURISTEN."

Black‑and‑white aerial postcard showing a lakeside industrial area with a sawmill/box mill complex, a smoking chimney, railway tracks, and large stacks of timber floating or piled by the shore. The scene overlooks a forested lake with islands and peninsulas. Captioning and publisher info are printed along the bottom edge.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a person in a small rowboat among reeds on a calm river. Across the water stands a village with a prominent church tower rising above trees. A Swedish caption is printed along the bottom margin.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing the ocean liner named Drottningholm underway at sea. The ship's name "DROTTNINGHOLM" is painted on the bow. Printed caption at lower left reads "T. S. 'Drottningholm'." and a publisher credit at lower right reads "FÖRLAG 'NORDISK KONST' STOCKHOLM."

Back side of an early 20th‑century postcard with multi‑language 'post card' headings. It bears a Swedish red 10 öre stamp reading 'SVERIGE' with a circular postmark that reads 'BODA' and date '20/3'. Handwritten address to the United States (Stamford, Conn). Additional transit/date marks are faint, including '1905'.

Vintage black‑and‑white view of a cobbled main square with pedestrians, a multi‑story brick building with a tower on the left, and shops along the right side flying Nordic‑cross flags. Printed caption at the top reads "Stortorget. Kalmar." A storefront sign on the right advertises books, music, and paper goods.

Black‑and‑white aerial view of a small Northern European town: straight main road lined with detached wooden houses, scattered farms and fields around the settlement, a larger institutional block near the center and a brick church-like building with stepped gables. No vehicles or modern high‑rises visible.

Black‑and‑white real‑photo postcard showing a side profile of a steam tank locomotive with two crewmen in the cab. The engine carries large side lettering reading "THE HIGHLAND RAILWAY." A round cab plate appears to read "HIGHLAND RAILWAY 23." In the railyard background a wagon marked "HR 34" is visible. A small negative number "4105" appears at the lower left.
Sepia-toned vintage view of a grand Baroque cathedral on a cobbled square with pedestrians and a bicycle; printed caption at the top left reads 'Domkyrkan, Kalmar.'

Vintage black‑and‑white town view showing a tree‑lined open street or square with wooden villas (one with a small turret), gardens and fences; a lone pedestrian is visible. A printed caption at the top reads "Motiv från BERGA."

Color-tinted photo card showing three small spaniel-type puppies perched on a little wooden raft or platform floating among reeds on a calm lake. A printed caption at the bottom reads "Three Dogs on a Boat." Handwritten message and date appear across the lower margin.

Vintage monochrome view of a cobblestoned town square with low buildings and striped awnings. Pedestrians and a horse-drawn cart are visible. The printed caption at the top reads "Larmtorget. Kalmar." Storefront signs include "Bröderna Carlssons Klädeshandel" and "Conditori & Café."

Black‑and‑white aerial view of a lakeside industrial town with floating timber rafts, lumber stacks, a long factory with a smokestack, scattered wooden houses, and dense forest beyond. Caption at the bottom reads about box mills and timber yards at Sommen; publisher credit in Swedish appears at lower right.

Sepia-toned postcard showing the stone ruins of a small chapel with a pointed arch and a narrow window slit, surrounded by vegetation. A Swedish caption strip at the bottom identifies the site and provides historical notes, with printing marks including "ÖLAND 19," "STF," and the photographer credit.

Black‑and‑white winter scene of a small stone arch bridge with metal railings over an icy canal or river. Five people stand on the bridge. In the center of the railing there is a round medallion depicting a castle with three towers above wavy water lines. Snow and telegraph poles are visible in the background.

Sepia-toned vintage view of a two‑story wooden pavilion in a landscaped city park. The building has large windows, an open upper veranda with people standing, and a tall flagpole flying a Nordic cross flag. A circular flowerbed and lawns fill the foreground, with trees framing the scene. Printed captions at the top read the place and city.
Sepia-toned winter view of a grand villa with a round corner tower seen through leafless trees. The caption is printed vertically along the right edge, with a publisher credit above it.

Color postcard showing an illustration of a 19th‑century side‑wheel paddle steamer with three masts and a red‑and‑black funnel, black hull with ornate gold scrollwork, sailing on a calm blue sea. A small red ensign flies at the stern; no coastline or other features are visible.

Black‑and‑white aerial photo of a farm estate with large barns, a main house with a formal garden, and surrounding crop fields. Swedish captions are printed along the bottom, including the site name and a publisher/credit line.

Black‑and‑white aerial view of a bustling town square filled with market stalls and crowds, surrounded by wooden houses; handwritten message along the lower margin. Printed caption at lower left indicates the square's name and publisher.
Vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a small church with a tower and spire behind a low stone wall and leafless trees. The caption in the upper left reads "Alböke Kyrka."

Vintage black‑and‑white street view showing a corner of multi‑storey stone buildings with mansard roofs and ornate gables. In the foreground is a landscaped green/park area and a broad street; smaller houses are visible in the background. The caption printed at the top left reads "Kalmar - Bremerlyckan."

Color postcard view of a multi-spired church with a tall central tented spire topped by a cross, surrounded by trees and seen from a small bridge or road with railings in the foreground. The white-walled building has smaller pointed corner turrets and a dark metal roof under a blue sky.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a rustic timber cottage with a turf roof, flower beds and benches outside. A tall flagpole flies a Scandinavian cross flag. Two people in early 20th‑century attire stand by the doorway. Printed caption at the top right reads "Borgholm – Kaffetorpet."

A multi-view vintage postcard with the Swedish caption "Hälsning från Emmaboda." It shows four scenes: the main street Storgatan with shops and cars; a park lake with a fountain labeled "E. R. sjön"; a small red timber cottage with turf roof labeled "Ryggasstugan Hembygdsgården"; and a memorial stone in a clearing labeled "Mobergstenen," commemorating author Vilhelm Moberg.

Two-image postcard showing a beige church with a square tower partly hidden by trees and parked vintage cars outside; the lower image shows the church interior with long pews, chandeliers, and an ornate altar. Center caption reads "Ålems Kyrka."

Sepia-toned reproduction of an old painting showing huge crowds picnicking and celebrating on a hillside with parasols and carriages, beside a river, with a panoramic view of a large historic city on the far bank. A framed, black‑and‑white studio portrait of a seated woman in early 20th‑century attire with a long pearl necklace. A white printed caption appears along the lower edge of the image, and smaller photographer/publisher credits are faintly visible.

Color view of a large white ocean liner named HAMBURG entering a busy harbor, escorted by tugs. A German flag flies atop the ship. In the background are waterfront buildings and the tall baroque tower of St. Michael's Church rising over the Port of Hamburg.

Black‑and‑white aerial view of a rural settlement with scattered houses, fields and forests. Swedish caption at lower left reads 'Flygfoto över Förlösa.' At lower right are publisher and photographer credits: 'Ensamrätt: A/B Flygtrafik Stockholm Foto: Liljeqvist.'

Colorized early 20th‑century street view showing a tall red‑brick water tower with white bands and a flagpole, next to an arched city gate. People walk near historic buildings. New Year greeting and captions are printed on the front.

Black‑and‑white photo postcard showing a multi‑masted sailing ship (schooner) on calm water with low, rocky shores in the background. A Swedish caption appears at the lower left, and a small publisher mark with the number 630 is at the lower right.

Back side of an old postcard with multilingual Universal Postal Union headings, a green 1¢ Benjamin Franklin U.S. stamp, circular cancellations including one reading GLENBROOK (Conn.), and a purple MIS SENT handstamp. Addressed in cursive to a Miss … Anderson at Strawberry Hill, Stamford, Conn., c/o Mrs. H. Raymond.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view across a waterway with bare trees and a cobblestone street and railing in the foreground. A tall cylindrical brick water tower with decorative bands rises on the right. Printed caption at top left reads "Vattentornet, Kalmar."

Black‑and‑white real‑photo postcard showing an elevated view over a waterfront city with islands and inlets. In the foreground is a large school complex inside a walled block, with bridges, quays and a canal-like basin nearby. Swedish text is printed along the bottom left and a publisher imprint appears in an oval at bottom right.

Black‑and‑white aerial postcard showing a moated castle complex with a formal parterre garden, wooded grounds and nearby water. The main building forms an L‑shape with a round corner tower; outbuildings and a drive are visible in the foreground. Swedish caption and publisher credits are printed in white on the image.

Black‑and‑white aerial view of a waterfront city with canals and islands. At center is a large school complex of several connected, light‑colored buildings around an open courtyard. Rooftops and a towered building appear in the foreground; trees, fields, and the sea with islets are in the distance. The lower left caption reads "Kalmar läroverk." A publisher line at bottom right mentions a bookstore in Kalmar and there is an oval mark reading "AKTA FOTOGRAFI."

This is a vintage sepia postcard featuring a large, stately academic-style building surrounded by trees and a balustrade, with people walking in front. The building is labeled in both Bulgarian and German as the 'Varna Handelakademie' (Trade Academy of Varna). One side of the card has handwritten text in Bulgarian, with a Bulgarian stamp, postmark, and address. There are also Cyrillic inscriptions about the sender and recipient.

The front side of this postcard displays a colorized photograph of a coastal landscape with a rocky shoreline, a sandy beach in the foreground, and a prominent building with a dome and spire on the hill overlooking the sea. The background text is in three languages: Bulgarian, Russian, and French, identifying the location. The card has handwritten notes and postal marks including a stamp from Varna. The reverse side has handwritten text in Cyrillic, indicative of communication, a postal stamp from Varna, and recipient details.

The postcard features a sepia-toned image of a large Orthodox cathedral with prominent domes crowned with crosses, set in an urban landscape surrounded by historical buildings. Text framing the bottom of the front side provides context in Bulgarian, French, and transliterated English, identifying the location and landmark. The reverse features handwritten text in Bulgarian, an old Bulgarian postage stamp, and postal markings indicative of authentic correspondence.

The postcard shows an old photograph depicting a palace-like building on a coastal cliff. The structure is prominent and appears luxurious, with a flag flying on top of a tower. The foreground features a large body of water, suggesting the palace is near the sea. The bottom of the front side presents text in Bulgarian and French, identifying the building as the Palace of Euxinograd in Varna. The reverse side of the postcard contains handwritten text in Cyrillic script, Bulgarian postage stamps, and publication information, all confirming its Bulgarian origin.

A sepia-toned historical city square scene with early 20th-century cars parked along the street and people dressed in period attire walking or standing around. The bottom edge contains Cyrillic script giving the location as 'Varna, Musalla Square (Nezavisimost)' with a number, suggesting this is a vintage postcard. The reverse has handwritten notes in Cyrillic (Bulgarian language) with 'CARTE POSTALE' printed at the top.

This is a vintage postcard depicting a broad avenue lined with trees and stately buildings, likely from the late 19th or early 20th century. The foreground features an obelisk or small monument and a prominent multi-story building with classical architectural elements. The caption on the image is in Bulgarian, English, and French, translating as 'Varna. Rue Vladislav.' The reverse side features handwritten Cyrillic script covering most of the card, a purple stamp, and printed text referencing a bookseller from Varna.

The postcard features a sepia photograph of a large, ornate building with soldiers and guards standing in front of the entrance, some under a canopy. Crowds and a parade-like scene are visible. The text on the front is in both Bulgarian and French: 'Поздравъ отъ Варна. Souvenir de Varna.' and 'Посрѣщането на рускии адмиралъ М. Николаевичъ' which translates to 'Greeting from Varna. Souvenir of Varna.' and 'Reception of Russian Admiral M. Nikolaevich.' Handwritten notes in Bulgarian are also present. The reverse side is a typical divided-back for addresses and contains handwriting in Bulgarian.

The front side of the postcard features two historical black-and-white images: the upper image shows a grand European-style mansion labeled as 'Двореца Евксиноградъ' (Euxinograd Palace); the lower image depicts partially ruined stone walls with several people, labeled as 'Стара Турска Крепость Кадиръ баба' (Old Turkish Fortress Kadir Baba). Both images have handwritten notes in several languages. The top of the card carries the text 'Gruss von Varna' and its Bulgarian equivalent, meaning 'Greetings from Varna.' The reverse side has printed address lines and postage markings, with Cyrillic text and a Bulgarian stamp dating from the early 1900s. It is addressed to Sofia, Bulgaria.

The postcard features a black-and-white photograph of a wide street lined with early 20th-century buildings, with shops, pedestrians, a vintage car, and a horse-drawn carriage. The lower left corner in Cyrillic and Latin reads 'VARNA - STR 6 SEPTEMBER', identifying the street and city. The reverse side has handwritten Cyrillic script, a red postage stamp from Bulgaria, postal marks, and an official purple stamp with 'VARNA' visible.

The postcard's front features a black-and-white photograph of a pier or quay covered in thick ice and snow, with dramatic icicles encasing railings, structures, and two tall utility poles. The back of the postcard has handwritten Cyrillic text, a Bulgarian postage stamp, postal markings, and a purple stamp with the name 'Ярослав В. Гочев' and 'Варна'.

A vintage black-and-white postcard shows an entrance to a garden or park, framed by stone pillars and lush trees. The bottom of the postcard contains printed text in Cyrillic and French, referencing 'морската градина', 'Varna', and 'Vue du jardin maritime'. The reverse of the card contains handwritten text in Bulgarian and an official purple stamp mentioning 'Ярослав В. Гочев ВАРНА'.

This is a black and white postcard featuring a fountain with sculpted children and a decorative water basin, surrounded by a landscaped garden with banana trees. The image is taken in a public park, with the sea visible in the background. The text on the front is in Bulgarian and German, and the back is filled with handwritten Cyrillic text, stamps, and a postmark from Varna. The message is addressed to Sofia.

The postcard features a sepia-toned photograph of a large formal garden or park with a variety of trees, palm-like plants, and landscaped flower beds. There is a decorative fountain or planter in the center of the image. The photo caption at the bottom is written in Bulgarian Cyrillic and German, identifying the place as a park in Varna. The reverse side contains handwritten text in blue ink, an address, and a sender's name, as well as a stamp in Cyrillic script.

The image shows an old, black-and-white photograph of a landscaped garden area with ornamental plants arranged in a circular pattern and a prominent agave or similar large-leafed plant in the center. Trees and shrubs make up the background. At the bottom of the postcard, text is visible in multiple languages.

The postcard shows a sepia photograph of a monument surrounded by sparse trees and some bushes. The structure is built on a raised platform with stairs leading up to it, and it features a large bird—likely an eagle—on the top, suggesting it is a memorial. The caption at the bottom is in Cyrillic script and appears to mention 'Orlov,' possibly referring to the eagle ('Орлова') and 'Памятникъ' meaning 'monument' in Russian or Bulgarian.

The postcard displays a sepia-toned photograph of a beach scene taken from a shaded viewpoint under trees. In the foreground, a person is sitting on the sand looking towards the sea and a wooden pier. On the right, there is a horse and carriage. Hills and more trees are in the background. The front lower edge contains text in Cyrillic. The reverse side showcases handwritten text in Cyrillic (Bulgarian), postal markings, and a faded stamp.

The postcard features a sepia-toned photograph of a port with a stone breakwater extending into the water, several ships and boats anchored in the harbor, and a distant view of the coastline and hills. The upper part of the card includes text in both Cyrillic and French, and a title identifying the scene as a port. The reverse side shows a typical divided-back layout for address and correspondence, postal markings, and an address written in a mix of Cyrillic, Latin, and French.

The front side of the postcard shows a stone lighthouse or beacon structure at a breakwater, with several people, including adults and children, dressed in old-fashioned clothing. The reverse side has handwritten correspondence in Bulgarian, some French text ('Union Postale Universelle', 'Carte Postale'), postal markings, and several stamps and addresses, including one for Varna.

The postcard features an early 20th-century colored photograph of seaside bathhouses on stilts in Varna, Bulgaria, with a wooden structure extending out into the sea and labeled for men's and women's sea baths. The reverse includes handwritten correspondence and postmarks from Varna dated 1910, as well as printed information about the publisher.

The postcard depicts a black-and-white photograph of a busy beach scene with many people swimming and playing in the waves. The reverse side features handwritten text, a red Bulgarian stamp commemorating 1888–1938, and a postmark from Varna. The address is written to someone in Prague, Czechoslovakia (now Czechia).

The postcard features a sepia-toned photograph of a popular seafront bathhouse and beach. The structure extends along the sand with many people enjoying the sea and sun, some under sun umbrellas. The postcard shows a black-and-white photograph of a landscaped terrace with balustrades, stairs, and lush trees, overlooking a bay with ships in the water. Printed text in both Cyrillic (Bulgarian) and German identifies the city as Varna (Warna) and describes the subject as 'the steps near the baths.'

The postcard features a colored photograph of a busy port scene with a large steamship docked, people working on the quay, and various cargo or luggage items scattered around. This is a vintage postcard featuring a black-and-white photograph of a harbor at sunset, with a large steamship docked, several people standing by the water, warehouses, and a visible clock tower in the distance. The photo caption is in Bulgarian and French, indicating the view is of Varna at sunset. The reverse side contains handwritten Bulgarian text, a Bulgarian postage stamp from the Kingdom era with a portrait of Tsar Boris III, and postmarks. There is also a printed stamp advertising Varna as a sunny beach resort in German ('BESUCHET WARNA SONNIGSTEN BADESTRAND').

The image shows a black-and-white (or sepia-toned) postcard, featuring a long wooden building with several windows and a slightly gabled entrance section. The building appears to be situated in a semi-rural, possibly northern European environment, with a wooden fence in the background and several other detached houses on a hill. The postcard is mounted on a textured surface, possibly for display or preservation. The top left of the postcard includes text.

The postcard consists of two sides. The first side shows handwritten text in Swedish, an address, and a Swedish stamp marked 'SVERIGE' with a value of 10 öre. The postmark is dated '1926'. The recipient is 'Fröken Elsa Ekström', addressed to Sandviksgatan, Luleå, Sweden. The postcard consists of two sides. The front side features a black-and-white photograph of a young child sitting on a fur rug, wearing a dress and a brimmed straw hat, in an oval vignette—typical of early 20th-century studio portraiture. The word 'SVERIGE' on the stamp indicates Sweden.

The front side of the postcard shows four uniformed men (likely police or military officers) standing on a wooden staircase outside what appears to be a wooden building and a train car. The setting is wintery, with snow or frost visible on the ground. The reverse side of the postcard contains handwritten text in Swedish and an address section with a green Swedish stamp featuring a portrait of a monarch.

The image is an illustrated postcard showing an El Al Cargo Boeing 747 aircraft being loaded with cargo at an airport. A black-and-white aerial photograph of a small village or settlement surrounded by forest. The postcard has some printed Swedish text on it, including a caption describing a flyfoto (aerial photo) of Anundgård, and there is a photo credit in the margin.

A black and white photograph of a rural landscape with meadows and scattered wildflowers in the foreground. There are two clusters of traditional Scandinavian-style buildings, one closer and one further away, partially surrounded by forest. The word 'Ånungård' appears in the bottom left of the image. A black-and-white vintage postcard view of a cobblestone street in Bruges, Belgium, taken from a small bridge with stone lion statues on either side. Traditional brick houses line the street, and in the distant background a tall medieval tower, likely the Belfry of Bruges, rises above the rooftops. The printed caption at the top identifies the scene as 'Bruges. - Le Pont des Lions', with a small printer's credit 'L. L., Brux.' beneath.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing a tree-lined street with a Catholic church featuring a tall, slender spire and simple façade. Adjacent buildings line the street, and another tower is visible in the background. Printed captions in German identify the location and publisher, with a date of 1904.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a tall Gothic church tower connected to a long fortified building. The tower has an ornate spire and detailed tracery, and the roof of the adjoining structure has a patterned design. Printed red text at the top identifies the place and location in German.

A vintage printed card from an insurance company with decorative black‑and‑white graphics at the top, including industrial scenes, a coat of arms and ornate lettering. Below is preprinted Finnish text with some handwritten insertions in blue ink. The layout and back‑printing style resemble an early‑20th‑century business postcard or payment reminder rather than a touristic view.

Black‑and‑white landscape view across a calm lake bordered by forest and scattered houses in the distance. In the foreground there is a large haystack on a grassy shore framed by tree trunks and overhanging branches. At the lower left, a cursive caption reads "Elwa."

Vintage colorized postcard showing a seaside promenade with metal railing and a lamppost in the foreground, where a few people stand looking out over the water. Across the bay is a fortified rocky hill with substantial fortifications and long buildings at its base, identified in the caption as a citadel. The image is printed in an oval frame on a beige card. A watermark with the website 'www.elia.org.gr' appears over the lower right part of the image.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a large hilltop castle complex with towers and a church spire, overlooking a riverside town with small houses, industrial buildings, lumber stacks, and a riverbank in the foreground. The main caption in red at the bottom identifies the view as Meissen and specifically the royal Albrechtsburg castle. Additional German printing appears along the left edge and bottom margin.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing the ornate brick façade of a historic Renaissance-style school building with arched decorative niches, statues between the windows, shuttered lower windows, and a steep tiled roof with a dormer. In front of the entrance are a couple of bicycles and large stone blocks. A caption printed in Dutch appears in the bottom margin.

Colorized illustrative postcard view of a large hilltop castle complex rising above a riverside town. The multi‑storey stone buildings with red tile roofs and towers sit on a high embankment with defensive walls, surrounded by trees and lower houses in the foreground. A calm river runs along the bottom edge. In the upper right corner, printed text reads "Schloß Colditz i. Sa." against a pale sky.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a chapel structure with an onion-shaped dome and adjacent arched walkway in a cemetery setting, surrounded by trees and gravestones. A curved path leads through the grass toward the buildings. Printed German text at the bottom identifies the scene and the publisher, with a small date.

Sepia-toned historical postcard depicting a large market square framed by arcaded townhouses on the left and a prominent town hall with a tall clock tower on the right. People are walking and standing in the open square, with trees lining part of the right side. German text is printed at the top left identifying the scene as the arcades of the market and the town hall in Hirschberg.

Sepia-toned postcard view of a Baroque church with two ornate towers and a richly decorated façade, standing beside a row of shops and houses along a street. People are walking in front of the buildings and a horse-drawn carriage is visible. At the top of the image, printed text reads "Graz Pfarrkirche Mariahilf." Storefront signs with German words appear along the ground floor of the adjacent building.

Colorized vintage view of a zoological park with a pond full of swans and other waterfowl in the foreground, surrounded by trees and landscaped paths. In the background stands a large domed aviary or pavilion structure. The image has printed red caption text at the bottom indicating it is from Lima, Peru, and refers to the zoological park and its lagoon.

Vintage monochrome postcard view of a riverside town on the Elbe, with a long paddle steamer labeled "PILLNITZ" on the water in the foreground. Behind the quayside stand several ornate multi‑story buildings, including a large church with a tall spire and smaller towers, and a prominent hotel-like building with the words "Dampfschiff-Hotel" on the façade. The overall style is late 19th to early 20th century Central European.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a large clock tower on a hill above a city. The tower has a steep, shingled roof with wooden balconies and large clock faces with Roman numerals on its stone base. Trees and a path frame the foreground, with a person in a hat standing near the edge overlooking the densely built city below. Printed text at the top identifies the location in German.

A black‑and‑white panoramic view of a historic European spa town nestled in a wooded valley. In the foreground are multi‑story buildings with steep metal roofs and painted signage, including the clearly visible 'HOTEL NEW‑YORK' and a smaller house marked 'LONDON'. Behind them lies a large landscaped park with paths, lawns, and mature trees. Beyond the park rises a dense cluster of grand 19th‑century spa and hotel buildings in ornate historicist styles, set against a forested hillside. A prominent large spa or bathhouse complex with towers and a clock is visible near the center‑right, and more palace‑like hotels stand higher on the slope. The overall scene suggests a fashionable Central European spa resort of the early 20th century.

Colored vintage postcard view of a harbor with sailing boats and small vessels in the foreground, several people standing on the quayside near a lamppost, and a fortified hill or citadel dominating the background. The image is captioned in French at the bottom and has handwritten text across the lower margin.

Black‑and‑white panoramic industrial scene showing a large factory complex with tall smokestacks emitting dark smoke, set against rocky hills and wooded slopes. In the foreground are tram tracks with electric streetcars, several horse‑drawn wagons, and people walking along a fenced street. The mid‑ground has multiple industrial buildings, rail sidings and freight cars. The sky and upper border show heavy damage or overpainting from age or reproduction. One horse cart bears a sign on the side.

A color image of a small-town central square with a landscaped park in the foreground, featuring paths, lawns, flowerbeds, and a white statue on a pedestal. Around the square are low, tiled-roof buildings and two-story houses with balconies, surrounded by trees and greenery. In the background, forested hills and mountains are visible under a clear sky. A few people are walking or standing in the open paved area.

Vintage monochrome postcard view over a river valley with a railway line, freight wagons, boats moored along the riverbank, and a truss bridge crossing the river. A town with dense buildings lies along the water, backed by steep, wooded hillsides. On a hilltop there is a prominent church-like building. Red printed German text appears at the top identifying the view.

Black-and-white postcard showing a large modernist railway station building with cubic volumes and grid-like window façades. A clock is visible above the main entrance. In front of the station is a busy square with people walking, cyclists, a tram or bus, cars, and lampposts. Low vegetation occupies the foreground. Printed text at the bottom left reads "Meißen a.d. Elbe - Bahnhof".

A vintage monochrome postcard showing a classical, light‑colored pavilion building surrounded by trees and landscaped garden paths. The building has large rectangular windows, a flat roof with a balustrade, and an attached wing with tall arched windows. Printed text at the top identifies the location as Stockholm and names the building Haga Lustpaviljong.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing an artillery exercise in a forested area beside a body of water. Several large field guns are lined up, with soldiers in early 20th‑century uniforms operating them amid clouds of gun smoke. Tall trees frame the scene. Handwritten cursive text covers the upper part of the image and runs along the edges, suggesting it was used as a correspondence postcard.

Black‑and‑white interior view of a large neoclassical salon with high ceiling, crystal chandeliers hanging on long cords, tall windows with sheer curtains, and rows of ornate chairs and sofas along the walls. A piano stands at the far end of the room, and two framed portraits hang on the wall. At the bottom of the image there is a caption identifying the location as Gustafsbergs Societetssalong in Uddevalla.

Black-and-white postcard showing a striking modernist concrete church building in a snowy landscape. The church has a tall, open-frame pyramidal tower with a cross at the top and bells partway up. The lower part of the structure has large rectangular windows. In the foreground there is snow-covered ground, a road with a car, street lamps, and a smaller adjacent building. Printed caption text appears in the lower left corner.

Vintage divided-back postcard with handwritten Spanish text on the left and address on the right. The printed heading at the top right says "Postkarte – Carte postale – Weltpostverein – Union postale universelle" followed by the word for postcard in many languages. There is a red stamp with a circular cancellation mark and a postmark. The card is addressed in blue ink to Sr. D. Benito Pérez Galdós at Hotel S. Quintín, La Magdalena, Santander. The left side contains a personal message in neat cursive handwriting signed "Alfredo Guadalupe".

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a brick Catholic church with a steep tiled roof and tall spire behind a brick wall and iron gates. Trees partially obscure the church façade. Two children stand on the street in the foreground. In the distance to the right, another tower rises above nearby buildings. Printed German captions at the top read the town name and indicate that the building is a Catholic church.

Black-and-white postcard view of a rural village set in gently rolling fields and surrounded by forest. A row of traditional gabled houses stretches across the midground; in the foreground are meadows and low stone or shrub borders. Tall conifer trees frame the right side of the image. At the bottom margin, handwritten-style text reads "Sohland / Spree. Neusorge".

A monochrome postcard view of a large neoclassical building with a colonnaded central portico facing an open cobblestone square. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk or stand in the foreground, with horse‑drawn carts and bicycles visible. At the top, printed text reads "Helsingfors - Helsinki" on the left and "Universitetet - Yliopisto" on the right.

Sepia-toned postcard image showing a large traditional Dutch windmill behind a fenced yard and a low brick-roofed house. The mill has four sails and a broad, tapered wooden body on a brick base. Printed white text at the bottom reads "DE KOKER – ZAANDAM".

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a wooded landscape with a manor-like building partly hidden by trees on a hill. In the foreground there is a small waterway or pond with a low dam and stone walls, as well as some outbuildings and stacked wood. Printed red text at the top identifies the location as Klingenberg near Dresden and mentions a Rittergut (manor estate). On the left edge, vertical publisher information is printed.

Black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a general view of the village of Rochefort-Montagne in a hilly rural landscape. In the foreground are clustered stone houses with tiled roofs and a prominent church with a square bell tower. The village is surrounded by fields, trees, and hills in the background. Text is printed at the top and bottom margins in French, giving the title and publisher information.

Sepia-toned vintage postcard showing a panoramic view of a small village nestled in a hilly, forested landscape. Scattered houses, farms, and a church with a tower sit on the slopes below a densely wooded hill. Handwritten red numbers appear at the top right, and a printed cursive caption runs along the bottom border in German.

Vintage black-and-white panoramic view over central Budapest, taken from the slopes of Gellért Hill looking toward the Danube River. A busy city square and streets with horse-drawn carriages and early trams are visible in the foreground, along with ornate historic buildings. In the background, the Chain Bridge spans the Danube and the dome of the Hungarian Parliament Building appears on the right. At the far left on the hilltop stands the large palace-like complex of the Royal Palace/Buda Castle. Red printed text in Hungarian and German is at the top of the postcard.

A color-illustrated street scene in a European city, showing a broad avenue or square lined with multi‑story historic buildings and trees. At the center background stands a tall Baroque-style church tower with an ornate spire. People walk and gather along the street, and storefronts with awnings line the ground floors. The image is framed by a white border, typical of printed postcards. A small, painterly signature appears in the lower right corner.

Vintage black‑and‑white multi‑view postcard with three horizontal photographs. The top image shows a large old manor complex with a tower and outbuildings, labeled in script. The middle image is a wide rural landscape view of a village with fields and trees, also labeled. The bottom image shows a fenced building that looks like a village school next to trees and a half‑timbered house, with a caption beneath. The captions are in German.

Hand‑tinted studio portrait of a smiling couple in early 20th‑century fashion. The man in a dark suit and tie leans affectionately toward the woman, who wears a pink jacket or dress adorned with large daisies and a pearl necklace. The background is softly blurred in pastel tones. In the lower left corner is a small imprint with the studio name and location.

A vintage black‑and‑white studio portrait of a seated woman in early 20th‑century dress. She wears a dark outfit with white lace cuffs and a hat decorated with a large flower, and she smiles toward the camera while sitting sideways on an ornate upholstered chair. Text at the bottom identifies her name and the Stockholm-based publisher/photographer.

Vintage sepia-toned postcard showing three Chinese street musicians standing outdoors in front of a simple plastered building with a window. They wear traditional clothing and hold musical instruments (a flute and stringed instruments). Russian captions are printed in red at the top and bottom of the card, with a small number '12.' at the upper right.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard view of a large European town square labeled 'Altmarkt' with the city name 'Dresden'. The scene shows Dresden's historic Old Market Square filled with pedestrians, horse‑drawn carriages, and early electric trams. Surrounding the square are multi‑story historic buildings with ornate facades, shops, and cafés. A tall church tower rises prominently on the right side, and a large monument with a statue stands in the center of the square.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style print showing a wide, busy city street lined with multi‑story Haussmann-style buildings. People in early 20th‑century clothing walk along the sidewalks and roadway, with horse-drawn vehicles and early motor traffic visible. French shop signs are visible on the facades. Beneath the image is a caption in Russian that identifies the location.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large ceremonial procession crossing an ornate bridge. Mounted soldiers ride in formation, followed by uniformed groups, while dense crowds line both sides of the street and bridge. The bridge entrance is flanked by tall stone pylons topped with seated allegorical statues and lion sculptures at their bases. Period clothing (top hats, bowler hats, long dresses) suggests an early 20th‑century event. Some people hold placards, and there are lampposts and substantial stone embankments in the background.

Black‑and‑white postcard showing two stone lighthouse towers and an adjacent house behind a low stone wall in a flat grassy landscape. In the foreground stands a wooden tripod structure with a metal bowl or signal apparatus on top. The image has printed caption text in the lower left and a small triangular publisher's logo with a number in the lower right.

A colorized vintage postcard view of a canal lined with historic brick buildings and towers. The scene shows the picturesque waterfront with reflections in the water, trees on the left, stepped-gable and turreted houses on the right, and a tall tower in the background. At the top is printed text identifying the location, and there is a small printer's mark in the upper-right corner.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a damaged multi‑story brick building with missing windows and rubble in front, likely a war‑damaged urban street scene. The printed caption at the top reads "Mitau - Lettische Bank," indicating the Latvian Bank building in Mitau. Other faint wall inscriptions appear on the right‑hand building but are not clearly legible.

Black‑and‑white view of a quiet town square with half‑timbered and plastered houses. In the foreground left is a large, ornate half‑timber building with a steep slate roof and dormers. Further back, centered, rises a baroque-style church tower with a bulbous helmet roof and lantern. Gabled houses frame the square, and a few small figures stand in the street. One building at right appears to bear the partially visible word 'Restaurant' on its facade. The overall style suggests an early 20th‑century European village scene.

Vintage sepia postcard showing a portrait of a uniformed military bandmaster in the upper left, and a large military band posed in front of and on an ornate octagonal music pavilion/bandstand in a park. The structure is richly decorated with carved wood or cast-iron elements and flags on top. The captioning and labels are printed in red Hungarian text around the images.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a statue of Crown Prince Rudolf standing on a large stone pedestal in a park. Rudolf is dressed in hunting attire, holding a rifle, with trees in the background. The top of the postcard bears red printed text in Hungarian and German identifying the monument in Budapest; a small red number is printed vertically along the right edge. The pedestal is inscribed with the name 'RUDOLF' and there is a wreath or floral arrangement at its base.

An old sepia-toned panoramic postcard showing a broad, mostly empty grassy square bordered by low houses and trees. The buildings look like late 19th- or early 20th‑century wooden or brick town houses. At the top center is the caption 'Lubescher Platz.' At the bottom in decorative script is the phrase 'Gruss aus Walki.' The card is vertically creased and worn, suggesting age.

A black‑and‑white historic view down a wide cobblestone street lined with two‑ to three‑storey townhouses. At the end of the street stands a large brick Gothic church with a tall, square tower bearing a clock, stepped gables and a steep roof. A few people, including children and a man with a handcart, walk along the nearly empty street. German shop signs are visible on the left‑ and right‑hand buildings.

Vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a cobbled bridge leading to an arched gatehouse with a small religious statue above the arch. To the left is a row of old brick houses with tiled roofs and many windows; to the right is a railing along the bridge. Printed captions in French at the bottom identify the view as the entrance to the Beguinage in Bruges.

A black‑and‑white postcard showing a mountainous, forested landscape with a mining ropeway (aerial tramway) in the foreground. Wooden support towers carry cables with suspended ore buckets moving along the line. Below, scattered buildings and mining structures sit on a rocky slope, with wide hills and valleys in the distance. White caption text is printed along the bottom edge of the image.

A sports-themed postcard featuring a close-up action photograph of cross-country skier Andrus Veerpalu competing at the Winter Olympics. He wears a white racing suit, red bib with Olympic rings, and skis in snowy conditions. The Olympic rings logo appears at the top left, his printed name at the top right, and his black autograph near the top. At the lower left is an attached commemorative postage stamp with his portrait, flowers, Olympic rings, Estonian text, and postal cancellation marks.

Black‑and‑white postcard-style image showing a large villa beside a small ornamental pond and garden. The house has a distinctive onion-shaped dome with a cross on top, timber-framed gables, and wraparound wooden balconies. Leafless trees suggest early spring or late autumn. In the left background, several people in early 20th‑century clothing walk along a path. Another residential building stands farther back on the right, and low hills are faintly visible in the distance.

Sepia-toned postcard view over a small European town with tiled-roof houses and prominent church architecture. In the foreground stands a large Gothic-style church with a tall spire topped by a cross; in the background another towered building, likely the town hall, rises above the trees. At the top of the card the printed caption reads "Dahlen i. Sa."

Black-and-white postcard showing a river in the foreground with a stone-lined bank, a large light-colored building with many windows on the right (the Upplands museum), and behind it a grand Gothic cathedral with three tall spires (Uppsala Cathedral). Trees surround the buildings, and light clouds fill the sky. Printed caption text appears at the bottom edge, along with publisher information.

A black‑and‑white vintage postcard showing a Dutch Renaissance-style civic building on a town square. The large brick building has ornate gables, many shuttered windows, and an external staircase leading up to a main entrance. Surrounding it are narrow townhouses typical of historic Dutch city centers. Printed captions at the top identify the scene as Nijmegen and the Grote Markt. A small publisher's credit appears at the bottom.

Colorized vintage view over a river with a paddle steamer in the foreground and small boats moored along the bank. On the opposite bank lies a town of gabled houses climbing a hill dominated by a large Gothic cathedral and castle complex. The sky is tinted yellow at the horizon, suggesting sunset. Decorative cursive German text is printed in the upper left.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a traditional two‑storey inn with a steep tiled roof and dormer windows, fronting a cobblestone street. Flower boxes and parasols line a terrace behind a low wall. Trees rise behind and to the side of the building. Printed caption text appears along the bottom edge in German, identifying the spa town and the guesthouse. Additional text is faintly visible on the facade above the entrance.

Black‑and‑white photograph of a wooden railway station building with a tiled gable roof. A sign on the facade reads "LANDVETTER". Three people sit on a bench on the platform in front of the building. Bicycles and a small kiosk appear to the left, and railway tracks run in the foreground. Text at the bottom identifies the scene as the Landvetter railway station, and a small publisher's mark with a number appears in the lower right.

An old private mailing card with a red postage stamp and circular postmark from Havana, Cuba. The card is addressed in Spanish handwriting to Spain, specifically to a person in Santander. Printed text includes multilingual indications that it is a private mailing/postal card and a note that the side is exclusively for the address.

A black‑and‑white view of a cobblestoned town square bordered by Baroque and Renaissance-style townhouses with arcades on the ground floor. The building in the foreground has three arches with signs above them and dormer windows in the tiled roof. Farther along the row are ornate facades with stucco decoration and a church tower with an onion dome and clock rising behind them. A few pedestrians stand or walk in the square, which is mostly empty.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a fast‑flowing river or stream surrounded by dense trees and rocky banks. The image is framed by a white border. At the top it reads in French 'La Macédoine Pittoresque'. At the bottom, in French, it is captioned 'VERRIA — Vue sur l'Axa Doré'.

Colorized vintage street view showing a gently curving road lined with multi‑story townhouses, horse‑drawn carriages, and pedestrians. Church spires rise in the background. The scene is labeled at the top with the town name and the street name in German. Publisher information is printed at the bottom left and a short note appears at the bottom right.

Black‑and‑white vertical postcard view of a quiet European village street leading toward a tall church with a distinctive baroque-style tower and onion-shaped dome topped by a cross. On the right are steeply tiled roofs with flagpoles and a hanging round sign on one building, possibly an inn or shop. Trees line the street and partially obscure the church and adjacent houses. A torn edge is visible on the lower right of the card.

A color photograph of a compact village with red-tiled roofs scattered on green, terraced slopes in a steep alpine valley. A church with a light-colored facade and tall bell tower stands near the center. The surrounding landscape features lush meadows, scattered trees, and dramatic rocky mountains rising sharply in the background under a clear blue sky. The style and colors suggest a mid‑20th‑century printed postcard. No visible text appears on the image side.

Black‑and‑white postcard view of a wooded, hilly spa town with scattered villas and guesthouses nestled among trees. In the foreground is a prominent multi‑storey building labeled "Falkenhorst" with similar buildings nearby. Farmland and forests cover the surrounding hills. At the bottom margin appears a printed caption in German identifying the place and its elevation.

Vintage monochrome postcard showing a canal-side street with multi‑story classical buildings and a domed synagogue in the background. A railing lines the waterside promenade and trees frame the scene. Red printed captions identify the location and subject.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a coastal view of a town on a hilly shoreline, with many small buildings and boats along the waterfront. The scene is framed by a tree and rocky shore in the foreground, looking across the water toward the settlement. Printed caption text in French appears at the top and bottom of the image.

Colorized photograph of a war memorial set along a tree-lined path in a park or cemetery. At the center is a stone statue of a soldier in uniform, bowing his head, with several figures at the base, mounted on a pedestal surrounded by flowers. On both sides are long stone walls or tablets inscribed with many names. The image has a cream border, and at the bottom in cursive script it reads the location and the title of the monument in German.

Tinted historical postcard showing a tall church with a high, slender spire rising above a tree‑lined street and fenced churchyard. The image has a sepia tone with a blue sky and clouds above. Printed captions in Russian and German at the top identify the location and the church as Evangelical Reformed.

Black-and-white postcard showing a long indoor corridor with arched ceilings, large hanging lamps and a staircase at the far end. Below the photograph there is printed Dutch text identifying the scene as a corridor in Canisius College in Nijmegen, along with publisher information and handwritten date and signature.

Black‑and‑white wartime postcard showing a large steamship with two funnels anchored in a bay or harbor, with small boats alongside apparently used for disembarking soldiers. Low shoreline with buildings is visible in the background. The bottom margin contains printed captions in French and English referring to the Balkan front in the 1914–1915 war, and a publisher/series note.

A vintage black‑and‑white postcard showing a wooded landscape with tall trees and a winding path or stream running through the forest. In the foreground there is a simple wooden railing or fence curving along the edge, suggesting a viewpoint or walking path. The lower part of the card has printed German text identifying the location and the publisher.

Colorized panoramic view of a European city with dense mid-rise buildings and red-tiled roofs, surrounded by greenery and hills in the background. A prominent church tower rises near the center. At the top left of the image there is printed German text identifying the view as Graz, III. Bezirk, seen from Rainerkogel.

A color illustration viewed from an elevated garden with flowering plants in the foreground, looking down over the red‑tiled roofs of a European city. Dominating the center is a richly ornamented yellowish building with a large central dome flanked by several corner towers with spires, resembling a 19th‑century town hall or administrative palace. Church towers with baroque and gothic spires rise among densely packed buildings, and a river meanders through the distant background.

Sepia-toned postcard showing a large multi‑storey sanatorium-style building with balconies, set on a landscaped hillside surrounded by fields and forest. At the top of the image there is a printed German caption identifying the building and its location.

Old black‑and‑white postcard view of a baroque church with a tall tower topped by an onion dome and cross, featuring a clock on the tower. In front of the church there is a tall obelisk monument in a small square, with surrounding low buildings and a cobbled street. Red printed Hungarian captions appear at the top.

A black‑and‑white postcard view of a curving road descending between rocky outcrops toward a coastal inlet or bay. In the middle distance are fields, a shoreline with small buildings and piers, and low forested hills under a partly cloudy sky. The caption at the bottom left identifies the scene as Uddevalla, Skeppsviken. A small logo and publisher credit appear in the lower right corner.

A black‑and‑white view of an elegant 19th‑century urban park with a circular flowerbed in the foreground and a tree‑lined promenade and street beyond. On the right stands a richly ornamented neo‑Gothic/neo‑Renaissance mansion with pinnacles, gables and statues in niches; to the left are more bourgeois townhouses. Several blurred figures, likely pedestrians or cyclists, move along the street, suggesting a long exposure typical of early photography. The scene conveys a refined European city environment.

Colorized vintage postcard view of a large medieval clock tower on a hill, with a steep shingled roof and wooden gallery. The tower's prominent clock face with Roman numerals overlooks a cityscape of red-roofed buildings spread out in the valley below. Trees and greenery frame the foreground. Printed caption text appears at the top, and a handwritten date is visible in the upper left.

Black‑and‑white landscape view taken from an elevated vantage point over a wide river with a gentle bend. At the inner bank runs a long embankment or promenade with a narrow strip of beach. Small houses with steep gabled roofs line the river at the foot of wooded hills and cliffs; the opposite bank is more rural with open fields. On the river a side‑wheel or paddle‑steam boat travels upstream or downstream, while a small rowboat is in mid‑river and a bundle of timber logs is lashed together near the foreground. The scene looks like an early‑20th‑century European river valley, possibly the Elbe or a similar Central European river. There is no visible printed caption or writing on the image.

Black‑and‑white harbor scene showing many steamships and boats moored along a busy waterfront quay. People walk and work on the cobblestone pier with tram or rail tracks, carts, and early motor vehicles. Industrial cranes and docks line the opposite shore, with low hills in the distance. Text printed along the bottom mentions the view from Skeppsbron and a local publisher in Gothenburg.

Sepia-toned historic postcard showing extensive ancient ruins along a stone-paved street running in a valley at the foot of a rocky hillside. Numerous fallen columns, blocks and arches line the way, with excavation materials visible. Printed caption text in Greek and French appears at the top.

A black-and-white nighttime photograph showing fireworks bursting above a lit hilltop monument, the Acropolis. The Parthenon and surrounding structures are illuminated while arcs of fireworks rise and fall against the dark sky. At the bottom is a white border containing printed text in Greek and French, and a website watermark "www.elia.org.gr" is visible across the lower right portion of the image.

A vintage, monochrome postcard view of a European town square. Along the left side are multi‑story townhouses with steep gabled roofs and dormer windows. One bears a sign for the "Hotel zur goldnen Kugel." On the right stands a large church with a tall tower topped by an onion-shaped spire. The open square in the foreground is sparsely planted with young trees. At the top of the postcard, printed in red, is the caption "Grossenhain. Hauptmarkt."

Sepia-toned photograph of an ornate Renaissance or early Baroque wall monument mounted between church columns. The structure is elaborately framed with scrollwork and foliage motifs, topped by the date 1524. In the lower panel a kneeling figure in prayer faces a relief of Christ or a saint above an inscribed plaque. The architecture and sculptural style suggest a Central European Catholic church interior. There is also a red handwritten signature or note along the lower right edge.

Vintage illustration-style New Year or festive postcard showing a bottle of sparkling wine labeled "CONCORDIA," two champagne flutes, an old-fashioned wooden mantel clock showing midnight, green fir branches, several four-leaf clovers, and a small red-and-white spotted mushroom (a fly agaric), arranged on a light-colored table. The right half of the card is blank for writing a message.

A sepia-toned postcard showing the front façade of a long brick building complex on a quiet street. The left section resembles residential or institutional housing with multiple windows and dormers under a tiled roof, while the right section has a taller gabled hall with large vertical windows and decorative brickwork. A simple sidewalk, lamppost, and low brick-and-metal fence run along the street. The caption at the bottom reads "Voorgevel, Vermeerstraat."

Colorized panoramic view of a spa town nestled in a wooded valley, with densely packed multi‑story buildings with red roofs on the slopes and a long neoclassical colonnade with many arches in the foreground. Rolling forested hills and open countryside surround the town. Printed red text at the top identifies the location and vantage point in German.

A colorized vintage view over a European city with a river running through the middle, crossed by several metal bridges. Historic multi‑story buildings with red and yellow facades line both banks. On the right, a wooded hill rises above the city, topped with fortification‑like buildings and a clock tower, labeled "Schlossberg".
